```6502
    LDA trigger_flags, Y
    ORA #PUZZLE_OFF
    STA trigger_flags, Y
    RTS

; Trigger action 6, PUZZLE_MOVE_MONSTER (it sets which way a monster moves):
; monster X / 4 goes direction A; MONSTER_GONE or more takes it off the map,
; for 26 points (score_monster). X = &10 means all four, but only
; monster 3 gets A: set_monster_direction leaves A changed, and the loop
; passes the next monster its predecessor's X, so monsters 2 and 1 get 12 and
; 8 (gone) and monster 0 gets 4, stuck going left, which it soon moves out
; of. (No trigger in the shipped mission asks for all four.)
.action_set_monster
    JSR sound_trigger
    JSR trigger_arguments
    CPX #MONSTERS * MONSTER_BYTES       ; all of them?
    BEQ set_all_monsters
.set_monster_direction
    LDY monster_direction, X            ; its old direction
    STA monster_direction, X
    TYA
    EOR #MONSTER_GONE                   ; was in play and now gone?
    AND monster_direction, X
    CMP #MONSTER_GONE
    BCC set_monster_done
    STX work4
    JSR empty_monster_cell              ; off the map...
    JSR score_monster                   ; ...for 26 points
    LDX work4
.set_monster_done
    RTS
.set_all_monsters
    DEX                                 ; monsters 3 to 0
    DEX
    DEX
    DEX
    JSR set_monster_direction
    TXA
    BNE set_all_monsters
    RTS

; Trigger action 9, PUZZLE_SWAP_NEXT: the cell in front changes from type A
; to X, or X to A.
; In: Y = the trigger * 4.
.action_toggle
    INY
    LDA work5                           ; the cell in front
    CMP trigger_args - 1, Y             ; A?
    BEQ action_toggle_set
    DEY
    CMP trigger_args + 1, Y             ; X?
    BEQ action_toggle_set
.action_toggle_fails
    JMP trigger_fails
.action_toggle_set
    JSR sound_trigger
    LDA trigger_args, Y                 ; the other
    PHA
    LDX front_x
    LDY front_y
    PLA
    JMP set_cell_and_draw

; Trigger action 4, PUZZLE_THROW_OBJECT: throw object A (carried) Y cells,
; from the empty cell in front, and stop the player's step.
.action_launch
    LDA work5                           ; the cell in front must be empty
    BNE action_toggle_fails
    JSR trigger_arguments
    JSR find_carried                    ; carried?
    BNE action_toggle_fails
    STX work0                           ; its slot
    TAX
    JSR launch_object                   ; throw it
    BCS action_toggle_fails
    LDA #ACTION_STOP                    ; no step
    STA action
    LSR A                               ; noise 5
    LDX #ENVELOPE_TONE
    JMP sound_effect

; Trigger action 8, PUZZLE_TELEPORT: put the view's top left at cell (X, Y),
; and so the player at (X + 4, Y + 4), which is also where the level restarts
; after a life is lost, with a flash; and stop the player's step.
.action_teleport
    LDA #ACTION_STOP
    STA action
    JSR trigger_arguments
    JSR place_player                    ; move the view and the player
    LDX #ENVELOPE_BEEP
    LDA #2
    JSR sound_effect                    ; a sound...
    LDA #2                              ; ...two flashes, 4 frames a colour...
    LDX #4
    JSR flash_palette_times
    JSR clear_screen                    ; ...and the view redrawn
    LDA #0
    LDX #ENVELOPE_BEEP
    JSR sound_effect_pitch
    JMP redraw_view

; Look at the cell in front, preserving Y.
; Out: front_cell; the carry set if it's the exit or off the map.
; Clobbers: A, X, cell_x, cell_y, map_pointer, cell_low_nibble.
.front_blocked
    TYA
    PHA
    JSR look_at_front
    PLA
    TAY
    RTS

; Trigger Y / 4's arguments.
; Out: A, X and Y = its first three arguments.
.trigger_arguments
    LDA trigger_args, Y
    PHA
    LDA trigger_args + 1, Y
    TAX
    LDA trigger_args + 2, Y
    TAY
    PLA
    RTS

; Monster X / 4's map cell.
; Out: X, Y.
; Clobbers: A.
.monster_cell
    LDY monster_y, X
    LDA monster_x, X
    TAX

; Character position (X, Y) to map cell (X, Y).
; Clobbers: A.
.to_cell
    TXA
    LSR A
    LSR A
    TAX
    TYA
    LSR A
    LSR A
    TAY
.monster_think_done
    RTS

; Decide where a monster goes next. If its fire cell has gone (something's
; been put there, or the level's map never had it: level 2's monster 0 goes
; at the first call of think), it's gone, for 26 points. Otherwise it tries up
; to four ways, each a 2-bit field of monster_turns (the lowest first)
; picking a row of the turns table: back, ahead, clockwise or anticlockwise
; from the way it was going. It goes into an empty cell or an
; object's; if the cell is what it eats (monster_food) it turns that into
; what it leaves, and is gone. If it can't go anywhere it's stuck.
; At the map's edge the way off it is lava (cell_at), so a monster that eats
; lava, as in all four of the shipped mission's levels, eats its way out
; when its turns come to that way: the lava past the edge stays (set_cell
; writes only on the map), its own cell is emptied, and it's gone for 26
; points as for any food. To a monster that eats anything else the edge is
; a wall. No shipped level's monster goes that way unless the player changes
; its path (docs/notes/game.md).
; In: work0-work3 = its x, y, direction and turns; work4 = its number.
; Clobbers: everything.
.monster_think
    LDA work2
    CMP #MONSTER_GONE
    BCS monster_think_done              ; gone: nothing to decide
    AND #3                              ; stuck or not, the way it was going
    STA work2
    LDA #DIRECTION_NONE                 ; its own cell
    JSR cell_beside_monster
    CMP #CELL_FIRE                      ; still fire?
    BNE monster_gone
    LDA #%11                            ; the first field
    STA work5
.monster_try_turn
    LDA work5
    LDY #0
.monster_turn_field
    INY                                 ; find the field...
    LSR A
    BCC monster_turn_field
    LDA work5                           ; ...and take it
    AND work3
.monster_turn_shift
    LSR A
    DEY
    BNE monster_turn_shift
    ROL A                               ; back, ahead, clockwise, anticlockwise...
    ASL A                               ; ...* TURN_ROW
    ASL A
ASSERT TURN_ROW = 4
    ADC work2
    TAY
    LDA turns, Y                        ; the way to try
    PHA
    JSR cell_beside_monster             ; what's there
    BEQ monster_set_direction           ; empty: go
    CMP #CELL_OBJECT
    BEQ monster_set_direction           ; an object: go
    EOR monster_food                    ; food?
    AND #&0F
    BEQ monster_eats
    ASL work5                           ; the next field
    ASL work5
    PLA
    BCC monster_try_turn                ; none left?
    LDA work2                           ; stuck
    ORA #MONSTER_STUCK
    PHA
.monster_set_direction
    LDA work4
    ASL A
    ASL A
    TAX
    PLA
    STA monster_direction, X
    RTS
.monster_eats
    LDA #&66                            ; a sound
    JSR sound_tone
    PLA
    TAY
    JSR step_from_monster               ; the cell it eats...
    LDA monster_food                    ; ...becomes what it leaves
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    JSR set_cell_and_draw               ; (off the map: nothing)
    LDA work4
    ASL A
    ASL A
    TAX
    JSR empty_monster_cell              ; and the monster's cell empty
.monster_gone
    LDA #MONSTER_GONE
    PHA
    JSR score_monster                   ; 26 points
    JMP monster_set_direction

; What's in the cell beside the monster (work0, work1) in direction A
; (DIRECTION_NONE: its own).
; Out: A, Z and carry as cell_at.
; Clobbers: as cell_at.
.cell_beside_monster
    JSR step_from_monster
    JMP cell_at
.step_from_monster
    PHA
    LDX work0
    LDY work1
    JSR to_cell
    PLA

; One step in direction A from map cell (X, Y).
; Out: X, Y.
; Clobbers: A.
.step
    STY step_y                          ; (a spare byte in the stack page)
    TAY
    TXA
    CLC
    ADC direction_dx, Y
    TAX
    LDA step_y
    CLC
    ADC direction_dy, Y
    TAY
    RTS

; Add points to the score, in BCD: score_monster 26 (25 was surely meant),
; add_points X + 1 (with X = 0, 257), add_point 1. add_points runs into
; add_point after its loop, hence the one more.
; Clobbers: A, X.
.score_monster
    LDX #25
.add_points
    JSR add_point
    DEX
    BNE add_points
.add_point
    SED                                 ; BCD
    LDA score
    CLC
    ADC #1
    STA score
    LDA score_high
    ADC #0
    STA score_high
    CLD
    RTS

; L on the title screen: ask for a mission file name (up to 12 characters, in
; a box between arrows) and load it. Fails on a B with Econet (see
; load_mission's service calls).
.ask_for_mission
    JSR draw_title_screen
    JSR print_inline
    TEXT_AT 6, 11
    EQUB VDU_COLOUR, COLOUR_BACKGROUND + 1, VDU_COLOUR, 2
    EQUS "Filename ?"
    TEXT_AT 30, 15
    EQUS "<"                            ; "<" at the right...
    EQUB VDU_BACKSPACE, VDU_BACKSPACE   ; ...back past it and blank the box
FOR n = 1..FILENAME_LENGTH
    EQUB VDU_DELETE                     ; (in colour 1) leftwards...
NEXT
    EQUB VDU_BACKSPACE, VDU_BACKSPACE
    EQUS ">"                            ; ...">" at the left...
    EQUB VDU_RIGHT                      ; ...and the cursor at the box's start
    NOP
    LDA #OSWORD_READ_LINE
    LDX #LO(read_line_block)
    LDY #HI(read_line_block)
    JSR OSWORD
    JSR load_mission                    ; load it
    JMP title_screen

; Load the mission file named at mission_filename (":0.$.IO" unless the
; player has asked for another) to io_start. The game has taken the DFS's
; workspace at &0E00-&10FF (and the NMI area and extended vectors), so first
; swap SWAP_START to SWAP_END out of the way into the screen, put an RTI
; where the NMI handler goes, put back the extended vectors the loader saved,
; and ask the filing systems to claim their workspace again (service calls 1
; and 2), then *DISK. Output is turned off while the file loads, then the game
; is swapped back. The display is off throughout.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, work0-work3.
.load_mission
    JSR blank_display
    STA furthest_level                  ; A = 0: no starting late on a new mission
    JSR swap_memory                     ; the game's code out of the way
    LDA #OPCODE_RTI
    STA MOS_NMI_ROUTINE                 ; NMIs are ignored until the DFS sets them up
    LDY #&100 - LO(MOS_EXTENDED_VECTORS) - 1
.load_mission_vectors
    LDA saved_extended_vectors, Y       ; the extended vectors back
    STA MOS_EXTENDED_VECTORS, Y
    DEY
    BPL load_mission_vectors
; On a B with Econet, these claims also wake the NFS, which takes NETV back
; through the extended vector entry at &0DD5. Once the game is swapped back,
; its code fills that entry, so the next OSWORD 0 (ask_for_mission's, which
; calls NETV after the line) jumps into the game and ends on its error screen;
; title-screen L can never load a mission there (docs/notes/loaders.md has
; the evidence). Without Econet the NFS stays asleep.
    LDA #OSBYTE_SERVICE_CALL
    LDX #SERVICE_CLAIM_ABSOLUTE
    LDY #&0E                            ; (the page the claims start from)
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDX #SERVICE_CLAIM_PRIVATE
    LDY #&10
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDX #LO(disk_command)
    LDY #HI(disk_command)
    JSR OSCLI                           ; *DISK
    LDY #osfile_block - osfile_block_template - 1
.load_mission_block
    LDA osfile_block_template, Y
    STA osfile_block, Y
    DEY
    BPL load_mission_block
    LDA #VDU_DISABLE                    ; no output...
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDX #LO(osfile_block)
    LDY #HI(osfile_block)
    LDA #OSFILE_LOAD
    JSR OSFILE
    LDA #VDU_ENABLE                     ; ...output again
    JSR OSWRCH

; Swap SWAP_START to SWAP_END with as much of the screen from SCREEN.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, work0-work3.
.swap_memory
    LDY #0
    STY work0
    STY work2
    LDA #HI(SCREEN)
    STA work1
    LDA #HI(SWAP_START)
    STA work3
    LDX #SWAP_PAGES
.swap_memory_loop
    LDA (work0), Y
    PHA
    LDA (work2), Y
    STA (work0), Y
    PLA
    STA (work2), Y
    INY
    BNE swap_memory_loop
    INC work1
    INC work3
    DEX
    BNE swap_memory_loop
    RTS

; What runs while the game's swapped out must be outside the swap, and what
; error_handler looks at to tell inside it.
ASSERT load_mission >= SWAP_END AND osfile_block_template >= SWAP_END AND error_handler >= SWAP_END
ASSERT flash_palette_cycle >= SWAP_START AND flash_palette_cycle < SWAP_END

; OSFILE's parameter block: the file name's address, the load address
; io_start, an execution address of 0 (whose low byte 0 says to load at that
; address) and the rest unused; copied to osfile_block before each load
; since OSFILE writes into it.
.osfile_block_template
    EQUW mission_filename
    EQUD io_start, 0, 0, 0
.osfile_block
    SKIP osfile_block - osfile_block_template

; The mission file's name, and OSWORD 0's block for reading another into it:
; up to FILENAME_LENGTH characters, from space to &FF.
.mission_filename
    EQUS ":0.$.IO     ", CR
ASSERT P% - mission_filename = FILENAME_LENGTH + 1
.read_line_block
    EQUW mission_filename
    EQUB FILENAME_LENGTH, ' ', &FF
.disk_command
    EQUS "DISK", CR

; BRKV: an error (from the filing system, loading a mission). If it happened
; while the game's code was swapped out (a sample of it isn't where it
; should be), swap it back; then show the error and "Press SPACE:" on the
; title screen, and start again from the title.
.error_handler
    LDA flash_palette_cycle             ; LDX #COLOUR_WHITE here means the code is in place
    CMP #OPCODE_LDX_IMMEDIATE
    BNE error_handler_swap_back
    LDA flash_palette_cycle + 1
    CMP #COLOUR_WHITE
    BEQ error_handler_message
.error_handler_swap_back
    JSR swap_memory
.error_handler_message
    JSR flush_buffers
    JSR draw_title_screen
    JSR print_inline
    TEXT_AT 4, 15
    EQUS "Press"
    EQUB VDU_RIGHT
    EQUS "SPACE:"
    TEXT_AT 2, 11                       ; the error message
    NOP
    LDY #1                              ; past the error number
    LDA MOS_ERROR_PTR
    STA work0
    LDA MOS_ERROR_PTR + 1
    STA work1
.error_handler_print
    LDA (work0), Y
    BEQ error_handler_done
    CMP #' '                     ; spaces as cursor movement, control codes left out
    BCC error_handler_next
    BNE error_handler_char
    LDA #VDU_RIGHT
.error_handler_char
    JSR OSWRCH
.error_handler_next
    INY
    BNE error_handler_print
    INC work1
    BNE error_handler_print
.error_handler_done
    JSR wait_for_space
    LDX #&FF                            ; the stack's no use after an error
    TXS
    JMP new_game

; The triggers' actions, by the low nibble of their flags (PUZZLE_*), called
; by trigger_fires.
.trigger_actions
    EQUW action_set_cell
    EQUW action_move_cell
    EQUW action_set_front
    EQUW action_set_clock
    EQUW action_launch
    EQUW action_explode
    EQUW action_set_monster
    EQUW action_move_monster
    EQUW action_teleport
    EQUW action_toggle
    EQUW action_enable
    EQUW action_disable
    EQUW action_recharge
    EQUW action_set_pushes
    EQUW action_push
    EQUW action_swap_keys
ASSERT P% - trigger_actions = 2 * (PUZZLE_ACTION + 1)

; The player's actions, by action number (ACTION_*): nothing, P, D, M, CTRL,
; T, Return, the four directions, and nothing again when a trigger has
; stopped the player. player_turn jumps to them (jump_to) with Y = the action
; * 2, and they clobber everything.
.action_table
    EQUW clear_keys_down
    EQUW pick_up
    EQUW drop
    EQUW map_screen
    EQUW backpack_screen
    EQUW throw
    EQUW use
    EQUW move
    EQUW move
    EQUW move
    EQUW move
    EQUW clear_keys_down
ASSERT P% - action_table = 2 * (ACTION_STOP + 1)

; For each move action, the opposite one: a pipe turns the player back.
.reverse_moves
    EQUB ACTION_RIGHT, ACTION_LEFT, ACTION_DOWN, ACTION_UP

; Each trigger's place, x and y, copied in by setup_level over what was here:
; bytes left in the file, not code (the start of a strip of LDATA's picture:
; see leftover). Their arguments (trigger_args) follow, past the end of what
; the loader copies, up to IO.
.trigger_places
    EQUB &0C, &0C, &19, &F0, &C0, &80, &33, &77
    EQUB &FF, &FF, &FF, &00, &00, &FF, &FF, &FF
    EQUB &CC, &88, &88, &00, &00, &FF, &FF, &FF
    EQUB &33, &11, &11, &0F, &03, &01, &CC, &EE
    EQUB &EE, &FF, &FF, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &70
    EQUB &70, &30, &30, &F0, &F0, &F0, &E0, &C0
    EQUB &C0, &91, &C0, &E0, &80, &11, &77, &FF
    EQUB &FF, &FF, &FF, &00, &00, &FF, &FF, &FF
.main_code_end
ASSERT main_code_end = trigger_args AND trigger_args + 4 * PUZZLES = io_start
ENDSECTION

; Past the end of what the loader copies: leftovers, never used. From
; trigger_places on, the file's last &93 bytes (file offsets &206D-&20FF) are
; LDATA's bytes at the same offsets: a strip of the Level Designer's title
; picture, character row 18, columns 13-31 of its 64, through the tops of
; "esig" in "Designer". The hidden files went onto the disc a whole number of
; sectors each from one buffer, which had held LDATA: H.GAME's own bytes end
; at offset &206C, and the rest of its last sector is what LDATA left there.
; H.GRAPH, next, ends with H.GAME's last bytes and the same strip, and
; H.LEVDES, last, with H.GRAPH's.
.leftover
    EQUB &88, &88, &88, &00, &00, &FF, &FF, &FF, &00, &00, &00, &00, &00, &FF, &FF, &FF
    EQUB &00, &00, &10, &F0, &70, &30, &98, &30, &70, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0
    EQUB &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &E0, &E0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &C0, &80, &33, &77, &77
    EQUB &33, &33, &33, &10, &10, &CC, &EE, &EE, &EE, &EE, &EE, &F0, &F0, &F0, &70, &70
    EQUB &70, &70, &70, &00, &00, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &FF, &FF, &F0, &E0, &C0
    EQUB &C0, &91, &91
}
ENDSECTION
```

`src/hidden_graphic.6502`:

```6502
; H.GRAPH: the PIPELINE Graphics Designer, option 3 on the disc's menu.
;
; It edits a graphics set: every picture the game draws, and the names of the
; objects the player can pick up. A set is &F34 bytes, kept at &4000 while the
; designer runs; DEFAULT, on the disc, is the set the game comes with
; (sprites.6502inc has the layout, default.6502inc the pictures). It can also
; load and save the copy of a set inside IO, the mission file that the
; Mission Generator (MISSION) builds and the game loads (io.6502inc).
;
; How it's reached: MENU, the BASIC menu the disc boots into, runs the GRAPHIC
; stub (*/GRAPHIC), a small loader in the disc's catalogue. The stub reads
; this program to &1AB0 from sectors &145-&165, a run of sectors that no
; catalogue entry mentions, so that copying the disc's files leaves it behind
; (hidden_loader.6502inc has the details), and jumps to start (&2BAE).
; H.GRAPH is only the build's name for those sectors. Escape offers to leave:
; on disc that runs /MRUN, a small program that undoes the designer's changes
; to the OS and runs the boot file again to bring the menu back; on tape it
; resets the machine.
;
; Words used throughout:
;   slot     a sprite's place in the graphics set, &00-&28. &10-&1F are small
;            sprites, the rest large. sprites.6502inc's SLOT_* say what the
;            game uses each for.
;   sheet    every sprite at once, on the right of the screen, where the
;            cursor keys move the selection.
;   sprite number  how the code names a sprite: its position on the sheet,
;            which isn't its slot (see "Sprite numbers" below); or, while
;            by_slot is set, a slot.
;   object   one of the 15 kinds of thing the player can pick up. Small slots
;            &10-&1E are their icons; each has a 12-character name, which the
;            designer numbers 1-15. Small slot &1F is the icon the game draws
;            for the exit, and has no name.
;   floor    slot 0, the picture of the map's floor (cell type 0).
;   window   a pop-up box over the screen: a menu, a prompt or an error.
;   frame    the border round a window or the editing grid; but in Animate, one
;            picture of an animation.
;   on tape  the filing system is tape (or ROM), numbered below FS_DISC: no
;            random access, so no single-sprite loads and saves (see disc_fs).
;
; The screen is MODE 5 at &5800. On the left, the editing grid: the selected
; sprite magnified four times, each pixel a cell (four MODE 5 pixels) wide and
; four lines tall. Under it, the current colour and, for an object, its number
; and name. On the right, the sheet: a 5x5 grid of large sprites (16x32
; pixels) and under it a 4x4 grid of small ones (8x16), then the PIPELINE
; logo. Windows keep what they cover at &5000 and put it back when they close.
;
; Keys: Z and X move the pixel cursor left and right, : and / up and down;
; 0-3 pick a colour (4 is 0 again); Return plots a pixel in that colour and
; Delete clears it to colour 0. The cursor keys move the selection on the
; sheet. f0-f3 open the menus (OptionsA, OptionsB, Environment and the
; credits), and CTRL with a key is a shortcut for a menu item. Escape asks
; whether to leave.
;
; Memory, besides the screen:
;   &1AB0-&3ADB  this program; the rest, to &3BAF, is whatever was in memory
;                after it when it was saved (see leftover)
;   &3E00, &3E80 two sprite buffers: Animate's frames
;   &3F80        the undo copy of the sprite being edited
;   &4000-&4F33  the graphics set, with "Finish Block" after it (see
;                finish_block; start clears &4000-&4FFF the first time)
;   &5000-&537F  what a pop-up window covers (the biggest is &380 bytes)
;   &50-&65      zero page: pointers, counters and scratch
;   &70-&7E      zero page: the editor's state (the selection, the pixel
;                cursor, the colour)
;
; The file, in order:
;   names        keys, window text, windows, sprite numbers, the screen, the
;                graphics set and IO, zero page
;   &1AB0        data: the logo, slot_of_position, the font (&1D00), the
;                windows' places and sizes
;   &2054        windows (open_window, close_window), keys (key_pressed), text
;                (print_char), menus (menu)
;   &22BB        sprites: finding their bytes (sprite_address), drawing them
;                in the editing grid (draw_grid) and on the sheet
;                (draw_sheet_sprite, sheet_address)
;   &2595        the Escape event, the screen's furniture, the window texts
;   &2A53        showing the sheet, the selection (show_selection) and the
;                colour; three unused routines
;   &2B4E        start-up state, error_handler, start (&2BAE), main_loop and
;                command_table
;   &2DFE        the commands: OptionsA and OptionsB (cmd_*,
;                pick_second_sprite, combine_sprites), Def. Colour, Animate
;   &334B        moving the selection and pacing the main loop
;                (select_sprite), and the pixel cursor (toggle_cursor)
;   &3503        files: the Environment menu's loads and saves, IO's pieces;
;                Obj name and its line input (input_line)
;   &387F        painting (edit_pixels) and the pixel primitives (plot_pixel,
;                read_pixel)
;   &3A41        reading a command (read_command, shortcut_keys)
;   &3ADC        leftover bytes, not part of the program
;
; Routine headers say what a routine is for, then In:, Out: and Clobbers:,
; leaving out a line with nothing to say. "Clobbers: everything" means the
; registers and whatever zero page and workspace the routines it calls use.
; Pictures (the logo, the font) are written as pixels, two characters to a
; pixel, in sprites.6502inc's mode5_pictures notation.

INCLUDE "os.6502inc"
INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"
INCLUDE "io.6502inc"                    ; and sprites.6502inc, the graphics set's format

; In shortcut_keys, an entry below &80 isn't a key (any INKEY_TEST() value is
; &80 or more).
NO_KEY = &57

; While a menu runs, f0 gives KEYCODE_F0 (set with OSBYTE_FUNCTION_KEY_BASE)
; and f1-f9 the codes after it. menu takes any code from FUNCTION_KEY_CODES
; up as a function key.
KEYCODE_F0         = &E0
FUNCTION_KEY_CODES = &C8

; Window text: a flag byte (MENU makes the lines after the first a list to
; pick from), then lines ending in CR, then TEXT_END.
TEXT_END = &FF
MENU     = &FF
PLAIN    = 0

; Windows, numbered as window_address and window_size list them. A menu's
; window number is also its function key's number.
WINDOW_OPTIONS_A   = 0
WINDOW_OPTIONS_B   = 1
WINDOW_ENVIRONMENT = 2
WINDOW_CREDITS     = 3
WINDOW_PICK        = 4          ; "Select sprite to...", and Animate's
WINDOW_QUESTION    = 5          ; Escape?, Exists, the palette
WINDOW_INPUT       = 6          ; file and object names; "insert disc"
WINDOW_ERROR       = 7
WINDOWS            = 8

; Sprite numbers. On the sheet, &00-&0F and &20-&28 are the large sprites'
; places in reading order (slot_of_position gives the slot each shows), and
; &10-&1F the small ones, which show their own slots. While by_slot is set,
; the code takes sprite numbers as slots instead.
FIRST_SMALL = FIRST_SMALL_SLOT
LAST_SMALL  = FIRST_SMALL + 15
AFTER_SMALL = MORE_LARGE_SLOT   ; the first large place after &0F
LAST_SPRITE = LAST_SLOT
SMALL_WIDTH = SMALL_SPRITE_WIDTH / 4    ; in bytes, as sprite_width holds it
LARGE_WIDTH = LARGE_SPRITE_WIDTH / 4
ASSERT SLOT_EXIT = LAST_SMALL

; The sheet: 5 rows of 5 large sprites, then 4 rows of 4 small ones.
LARGE_COLUMNS = 5
LARGE_ROWS    = 5
SMALL_COLUMNS = 4
SMALL_ROWS    = 4

; Sprite numbers beyond the sheet: the two buffers Animate shows frames in.
SPRITE_FRAME_A = &57
SPRITE_FRAME_B = &58
UPSIDE_DOWN    = &80            ; in animation_frames: show the frame turned over

; The screen: MODE 5, where a character row is 40 cells of 8 bytes, each cell
; four pixels (a byte) across and eight lines down. A MODE 5 text character
; is two cells wide; the designer's own font is one.
SCREEN = MODE5_SCREEN
CELL   = 8
ROW    = MODE5_ROW_BYTES
ASSERT ROW = 40 * CELL

SECTION graphics_set, org=SET_LOAD_ADDRESS, virtual=TRUE
.graphics     SKIP SET_NAMES - LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE    ; the graphics set
.slot_28      SKIP LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE                ; the last slot, stored apart in IO
.object_names SKIP SET_SIZE - SET_NAMES
.graphics_end
ENDSECTION

; Where the set's pieces are in an IO file (see io_segments).
IO_SLOT_28_OFFSET  = io_no_object_picture - io_start
IO_NAMES_OFFSET    = io_object_names - io_start
IO_GRAPHICS_OFFSET = io_graphics - io_start
IO_LENGTH          = IO_END - io_start
ASSERT LO(IO_SLOT_28_OFFSET) = LO(slot_28 - graphics)
ASSERT LO(IO_NAMES_OFFSET) = LO(SET_NAMES)
ASSERT IO_GRAPHICS_SIZE = slot_28 - graphics

SECTION sprite_buffers, org=&3E00, virtual=TRUE
.frame_a      SKIP LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE    ; Animate's frames: sprite number SPRITE_FRAME_A...
.frame_b      SKIP LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE    ; ...and SPRITE_FRAME_B
ENDSECTION
SECTION undo_sprite, org=&3F80, virtual=TRUE
.undo_buffer  SKIP LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE    ; the sprite being edited, as it was when selected
ENDSECTION
SECTION window_backing, org=&5000, guard=SCREEN, virtual=TRUE
.window_store SKIP &380                 ; what the open window covers (the biggest's size)
ENDSECTION

; Places on the screen.
edit_grid     = SCREEN + ROW + 2*CELL           ; each pixel a cell, two sprite rows to a character row
colour_swatch = SCREEN + 19*ROW + 1*CELL        ; two cells of the current colour
name_box      = SCREEN + 19*ROW + 4*CELL        ; an object's number and name
large_sheet   = SCREEN + 20*CELL                ; 5 sprites across, each 4 cells by 4 rows
small_sheet   = SCREEN + 20*ROW + 21*CELL       ; 4 across, 4 cells apart, each 2 cells by 2 rows
frame_preview = SCREEN + 23*ROW + 9*CELL        ; Animate's frame, in its window
logo_screen   = SCREEN + 28*ROW + 18*CELL       ; the logo, at the bottom right
; Two bytes of the editing grid's frame that tell whether it is drawn for a
; large sprite or a small one: the small frame's top right corner, and the
; top of the large frame's right edge. Each is &08 (a pixel of colour 1 at
; the cell's left) only when that frame is drawn.
grid_frame_top   = SCREEN + 10*CELL + 7
grid_frame_right = SCREEN + ROW + 18*CELL

; Zero page.
SECTION zero_page, org=&50, virtual=TRUE
.screen_ptr SKIP 2              ; where on the screen to draw
.data_ptr SKIP 2                ; a sprite's bytes; window text
.save_ptr SKIP 2                ; where a window's background is kept; a line of its text
.pixel_x SKIP 1                 ; the pixel pixel_address is finding
.pixel_y SKIP 1
.aux_ptr SKIP 2                 ; a glyph; a window's corner; a second sprite
    SKIP 6
.line_count SKIP 1              ; lines of window text, less one
.temp SKIP 1
.count_x SKIP 1
.count_y SKIP 1
.item SKIP 1                    ; the highlighted menu line, from 0; also scratch
.mask SKIP 1                    ; one pixel's bits in a byte; also window text's flag byte
    SKIP 10
.sprite_width SKIP 1            ; in bytes: 4 large, 2 small; the height in pixels is 8 times it
.sprite SKIP 1                  ; the selected sprite
.old_sprite SKIP 1              ; the selection before select_sprite moved it
.cursor_x SKIP 1                ; the pixel cursor, in the sprite's pixels
.cursor_y SKIP 1
.old_cursor_x SKIP 1            ; where it was before edit_pixels moved it
.old_cursor_y SKIP 1
.colour SKIP 1                  ; for plotting, 0-3
.repeat_delay SKIP 1            ; the pixel cursor's key repeat, shortening as it repeats
    SKIP 1
.last_column SKIP 1             ; the last column of the selected sprite's row in the sheet
.by_slot SKIP 1                 ; bit 7 set while sprite numbers are slots, not sheet places
.border_ptr SKIP 2              ; where a window's frame is being drawn
.escape_latch SKIP 1            ; bit 7 set once SHIFT-Escape is pressed
ENDSECTION

SECTION hidden_graphic, filename="H.GRAPH", org=&1AB0

; the screen a band at a time. mode5_pictures turns each band into bytes in

LOGO_BAND = 22*CELL

        },
        ; x y z { | } ~ DEL
        {
            "............................33....33......33....33..............",
            "..........................33......33......33......33............",
            "33..33..33..33..333333....33......33......33....33..33..........",
            "33..33..33..33......33..3333................33......33..........",
            "..33....33..33....33......33......33......33....33..33..........",
            "33..33..333333....33......33......33......33......33............",
            "33..33......33..333333......33....33......33....33..............",
            "........333333.................................................."
        }
    })

; Bit 7 set while each window is open (and what it covers is saved). start
; clears all twenty bytes, though only the first WINDOWS are used.
.window_open
    SKIP 20

; The screen address of each pair of pixel rows of the editing grid.
.grid_row_address
    EQUW edit_grid + (0..15) * ROW

; Each window's top left corner on the screen...
.window_address
    EQUW SCREEN                     ; OptionsA
    EQUW SCREEN + 8*CELL            ; OptionsB
    EQUW SCREEN + 16*CELL           ; Environment
    EQUW SCREEN + 24*CELL           ; credits
    EQUW SCREEN + 21*ROW + 4*CELL   ; pick a sprite; Animate
    EQUW SCREEN + 22*ROW + 4*CELL   ; questions
    EQUW SCREEN + 22*ROW + 2*CELL   ; names
    EQUW SCREEN + 14*ROW + 12*CELL  ; errors

; ...and its width in bytes less one, and its height in character rows.
.window_size
    EQUB 8*CELL-1, 8
    EQUB 8*CELL-1, 8
    EQUB 11*CELL-1, 8
    EQUB 16*CELL-1, 6
    EQUB 14*CELL-1, 7
    EQUB 8*CELL-1, 6
    EQUB 16*CELL-1, 7
    EQUB 16*CELL-1, 6
ASSERT window_size - window_address = 2 * WINDOWS

; Point at a window.
; In:  A = window number (only bits 0-2 count)
; Out: screen_ptr and aux_ptr = its corner on the screen, save_ptr =
;      window_store, count_x = width in bytes less one, count_y = height in
;      rows, Y = window number * 2
; Clobbers: A
.window_setup
{
    AND #WINDOWS - 1
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDA #HI(window_store)
    STA save_ptr+1
    LDA window_address, Y
    STA screen_ptr
    STA aux_ptr
    LDA window_address+1, Y
    STA screen_ptr+1
    STA aux_ptr+1
    LDA #LO(window_store)
    STA save_ptr
    LDA window_size, Y
    STA count_x
    LDA window_size+1, Y
    STA count_y
    RTS
}

; Open a window and write its text in it. Any open window is closed first,
; so they never overlap; what the window covers is kept at window_store, and
; it is filled with colour 1 for the title row and colour 3 below, then
; print_window_text writes the text and draws the frame.
; In:  A = window number (bit 7 ignored), X/Y = its text (see TEXT_END)
; Out: screen_ptr = just after the text's last character, line_count =
;      lines in the text less one, mask = the text's flag byte
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, data_ptr, save_ptr, aux_ptr, border_ptr, count_x,
;      count_y
.open_window
{
    STX data_ptr
    STY data_ptr+1
    AND #&7F
    PHA
    LDA #WINDOWS - 1

    ; Close every window, the last first.
.close_others
    PHA
    TAX
    JSR close_window
    PLA
    SEC
    SBC #&01
    BCS close_others
    PLA
    PHA
    TAX
    ORA #&80                        ; bit 7 set: open
    STA window_open, X
    JSR window_setup
    LDX #mode5_byte("1111")         ; the title row in colour 1
.fill_row
    LDY count_x
.fill_byte
    LDA (screen_ptr), Y
    STA (save_ptr), Y
    TXA
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL fill_byte
    LDX #mode5_byte("3333")         ; and the rest in colour 3
    JSR next_window_row
    DEC count_y
    BNE fill_row
    LDA aux_ptr
    STA save_ptr
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA aux_ptr+1
    STA save_ptr+1
    STA screen_ptr+1
    PLA
}

; Write a window's text (open_window's second half), exclusive-ORing it on
; in colour 3, so that writing it again rubs it out; then draw the window's
; frame in colour 2: a line down its right edge below the title row, and
; along its bottom.
; In:  A = window number, data_ptr = the text, screen_ptr and save_ptr = its
;      corner, count_x = its width in bytes less one
; Out: screen_ptr = just after the text's last character, line_count =
;      lines less one, mask = the flag byte
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, data_ptr, save_ptr, aux_ptr, border_ptr, count_y
.print_window_text
{
    PHA
    LDY #&FF
    STY line_count
    INY
    LDA (data_ptr), Y
    STA mask
.next_char
    INC data_ptr
    BNE read_char
    INC data_ptr+1
.read_char
    LDY #&00
    LDA (data_ptr), Y
    CMP #TEXT_END
    BEQ frame
    CMP #CR
    BEQ new_line
    CLC
    JSR print_char_advance          ; carry clear: exclusive-OR the glyph on
    BNE next_char                   ; always: the pointer's last change left it non-zero
.new_line
    INC line_count
    LDA save_ptr                    ; save_ptr holds the start of the line
    CLC
    ADC #LO(ROW)
    STA save_ptr
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA save_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(ROW)
    STA save_ptr+1
    STA screen_ptr+1
    BCC next_char

    ; The frame: the rightmost pixel of each row, then the bottom line.
.frame
    PLA
    AND #WINDOWS - 1
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDA window_address, Y
    STA border_ptr
    LDA window_address+1, Y
    STA border_ptr+1
    LDA window_size+1, Y
    SBC #&00                        ; carry clear from the ASL, so count_y = rows - 1
    STA count_y
.frame_row
    LDY count_x
    LDX #&07
    LDA border_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #LO(ROW)
    STA border_ptr
    LDA border_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(ROW)
    STA border_ptr+1
.frame_right
    LDA (border_ptr), Y
    AND #mode5_byte("333.")         ; pixel 3 becomes colour 2
    ORA #mode5_byte("...2")
    STA (border_ptr), Y
    DEY
    DEX
    BPL frame_right
    DEC count_y
    BNE frame_row
    LDY count_x                     ; the bottom line of each cell of the last row
.frame_bottom
    LDA #mode5_byte("2222")
    STA (border_ptr), Y
    TYA
    SEC
    SBC #CELL
    TAY
    BCS frame_bottom
    RTS
}

; Step both of a window's pointers down a row: save_ptr past the bytes
; just kept, screen_ptr to the next character row. Also entered at
; next_screen_row to step screen_ptr alone.
; In:  count_x = the window's width in bytes less one
; Clobbers: A
.next_window_row
{
    LDA save_ptr
    SEC
    ADC count_x
    STA save_ptr
    BCC next_screen_row
    INC save_ptr+1
.next_screen_row
    LDA screen_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #LO(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    RTS
}

; Close every window.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr, save_ptr, aux_ptr, count_x, count_y
.close_all_windows
{
    LDX #WINDOWS - 1
.loop
    TXA
    PHA
    JSR close_window
    PLA
    TAX
    DEX
    BPL loop
    RTS
}

; Close a window, if it is open, putting back what it covered.
; In:  A = window number (bit 7 ignored)
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr, save_ptr, aux_ptr, count_x, count_y
.close_window
{
    AND #&7F
    PHA
    TAY
    LDA window_open, Y
    BMI open
    PLA
    RTS
.open
    PLA
    PHA
    JSR window_setup
.row
    LDY count_x
.byte
    LDA (save_ptr), Y
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL byte
    JSR next_window_row
    DEC count_y
    BNE row
    PLA
    TAX
    LDA #&00
    STA window_open, X
    RTS
}

; Is a key pressed?
; In:  X = INKEY_TEST() of the key
; Out: A = X = &FF and N set if it is, 0 and N clear if not
; Clobbers: Y
.key_pressed
{
    LDA #OSBYTE_INKEY
    TAY                             ; Y >= &80: scan for one key
    JSR OSBYTE
    TXA
    RTS
}

; Wait until a key is released, so one press does one thing.
; In:  X = INKEY_TEST() of the key
; Clobbers: A, Y
.wait_key_release
{
    TXA
    PHA
    JSR key_pressed
    TAY
    PLA
    TAX
    INY
    BEQ wait_key_release
    RTS
}

; Draw a character and step screen_ptr on to the next cell.
; In:  A = character, carry set to store it, clear to exclusive-OR it
; Out: Z clear
; Clobbers: A, aux_ptr
.print_char_advance
{
    JSR print_char
    LDA screen_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #CELL
    STA screen_ptr
    BCC done
    INC screen_ptr+1
.done
    RTS
}

; Draw a character from the font at screen_ptr, filling one cell.
; In:  A = character (a control code draws a space), carry set to store it
;      (in colour 3 on black), clear to exclusive-OR it with the screen (on
;      a window, so drawing it again rubs it out)
; Clobbers: A, aux_ptr
.print_char
{
    PHP
    STY saved_y
    STX saved_x
    LDY #&00
    STY aux_ptr+1
    LDX #&00
    CMP #' '
    BCS printable
    LDA #'!'                 ; a control code: with carry clear, '!' - ' ' - 1 = 0, the space
.printable
    SBC #' '                 ; aux_ptr = font + 8 * (A - " ")
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ROL aux_ptr+1
    ASL A
    ROL aux_ptr+1
    TAX
    LDA aux_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(font)                   ; the font starts a page
    TAY
    STX aux_ptr
    STY aux_ptr+1
    PLP
    LDY #&07
.row
    LDA (aux_ptr), Y
    BCS store
    EOR (screen_ptr), Y
.store
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL row
    LDX saved_x
    LDY saved_y
    RTS
.saved_x
    EQUB &00
.saved_y
    EQUB &00
}

; Open a window and let the user pick from it: a menu. While it runs, the
; cursor keys give codes and the function keys KEYCODE_F0 up; leaving with Space,
; Escape or another function key puts the function keys back to strings, but
; picking with Return doesn't.
; In:  A = window number, X/Y = its text; if the text's flag is MENU the lines
;      after the title are a list to move along with the cursor keys
; Out: A = X = the line picked with Return (1 = the first after the title,
;      0 if the text has no list), or &FF if left with Space, Escape or
;      another menu's function key
; Clobbers: Y, item, and as open_window
.menu
{
    PHA
    JSR open_window
    PLA
    PHA
    AND #WINDOWS - 1                ; count_y = this window's number, for the function key test
    STA count_y
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDA window_address, Y
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA window_address+1, Y
    STA screen_ptr+1
    JSR next_window_row.next_screen_row
    LDA #&FF
    STA item
    BIT mask
    BPL no_list
    JSR invert_menu_row
    INC item
.no_list
    LDA #OSBYTE_CURSOR_EDITING      ; the cursor keys give codes
    LDX #CURSOR_KEYS_CODES
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDA #OSBYTE_FUNCTION_KEY_BASE   ; f0-f9 give KEYCODE_F0 up
    LDX #KEYCODE_F0
    LDY #&00
    JSR OSBYTE
.read_key
    LDA #OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS       ; empty the keyboard buffer
    LDX #&00
    JSR OSBYTE
    JSR OSRDCH
    BCC got_key
.cancel
    LDA #OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE  ; if there was an Escape
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDA #OSBYTE_FUNCTION_KEY_BASE   ; function keys back to strings
    LDX #FUNCTION_KEYS_STRINGS
    LDY #&00
    JSR OSBYTE
    PLA
    JSR close_window
    LDX #&FF
    TXA
    RTS
.got_key
    CMP #FUNCTION_KEY_CODES         ; a function key (f4-f9 repeat f0-f3)...
    BCC not_fkey
    AND #&03
    CMP count_y                     ; ...other than this menu's own closes it
    BNE cancel
.not_fkey
    CMP #' '
    BEQ cancel
    CMP #CR
    BEQ chosen
    BIT mask
    BPL read_key
    CMP #KEYCODE_DOWN
    BEQ down
    CMP #KEYCODE_UP
    BNE read_key
    LDA item
    BEQ read_key
    JSR invert_menu_row
    DEC item
    LDA screen_ptr                  ; carry is set from the CMP
    SBC #LO(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    SBC #HI(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    BCS highlight                   ; always
.down
    LDA item
    CLC
    ADC #&01
    CMP line_count
    BEQ read_key
    JSR invert_menu_row
    INC item
    JSR next_window_row.next_screen_row
.highlight
    JSR invert_menu_row
    JMP read_key
.chosen
    PLA
    JSR close_window
    LDA #OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS       ; empty the keyboard buffer
    LDX #&00
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_RETURN)
    JSR wait_key_release
    LDX item
    INX
    TXA
    RTS
}

; Highlight or unhighlight a line of a window by exclusive-ORing colour 1
; into every pixel (red and yellow, black and blue change places), then
; put back the frame's right edge, which that changed too.
; In:  screen_ptr = the line, count_x = the window's width in bytes less one
; Clobbers: A, X, Y
.invert_menu_row
{
    LDY count_x
.invert
    LDA (screen_ptr), Y
    EOR #mode5_byte("1111")
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL invert
    LDY count_x
    LDX #&07
.border
    LDA (screen_ptr), Y
    AND #mode5_byte("333.")         ; pixel 3 becomes colour 2
    ORA #mode5_byte("...2")
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    DEX
    BPL border
    RTS
}

; A sprite's size from its number.
; In:  A = sprite number
; Out: sprite_width = SMALL_WIDTH for the small sprites (&10-&1F), else
;      LARGE_WIDTH; data_ptr = graphics (where sprite_address starts from)
; Clobbers: X
.sprite_class
{
    LDX #LO(graphics)
    STX data_ptr
    LDX #HI(graphics)
    STX data_ptr+1
    LDX #LARGE_WIDTH
    CMP #FIRST_SMALL
    BCC store
    CMP #AFTER_SMALL
    BCS store
    LDX #SMALL_WIDTH
.store
    STX sprite_width
    RTS
}

; Find a sprite's bytes.
; In:  A = sprite number: a sheet position (see slot_of_position), or a slot
;      while by_slot has bit 7 set; SPRITE_FRAME_A and SPRITE_FRAME_B (with
;      or without bit 7) are the two frame buffers
; Out: data_ptr = its first byte, sprite_width = its width in bytes, A = Y =
;      the sprite number
; Clobbers: X
.sprite_address
{
    TAY
    JSR sprite_class
    CMP #SPRITE_FRAME_A             ; a frame buffer
    BCS frame
    TAY
    AND #&10                        ; &10-&1F: small
    BNE small
    TYA
    BIT by_slot
    BMI slot
    CMP #AFTER_SMALL                ; positions &20-&28 follow &00-&0F in the table
    BCC mapped
    SBC #AFTER_SMALL - FIRST_SMALL
.mapped
    TAX
    LDA slot_of_position, X

    ; Large slots &00-&0F are at graphics + slot * LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE, half a
    ; page each; &20-&28 the same from SET_MORE_LARGE.
.slot
    CMP #MORE_LARGE_SLOT
    BCS high_slot
    LSR A
    TAX
    LDA #&00                        ; an odd slot starts half a page in
    ROR A
    STA data_ptr
    TXA
    ADC data_ptr+1
    STA data_ptr+1
    TYA
    RTS
.frame
    AND #&7F
    CMP #SPRITE_FRAME_B             ; carry set for the second buffer...
    LDA #&00
    ROR A                           ; ...the half page after the first
    STA data_ptr
    LDA #HI(frame_a)
    STA data_ptr+1
    TYA
    RTS
.high_slot
    AND #&0F
    TAX
    LDA data_ptr+1
    CLC
    ADC #HI(SET_MORE_LARGE)
    STA data_ptr+1
    TXA
    JMP slot

    ; Small slots are at graphics + SET_SMALL + (slot AND &0F) *
    ; SMALL_SPRITE_SIZE.
.small
    TYA
    PHA
    LDA data_ptr+1
    CLC
    ADC #HI(SET_SMALL)
    STA data_ptr+1
    PLA
    ASL A                           ; times SMALL_SPRITE_SIZE (the &10 bit falls off)
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    BCC small_done
    INC data_ptr+1
.small_done
    CLC
    ADC data_ptr
    STA data_ptr
    TYA
    RTS
}
ASSERT LO(graphics) = 0 AND LO(frame_a) = 0
ASSERT LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE = &80 AND SMALL_SPRITE_SIZE = 1 << 5
ASSERT LO(SET_SMALL) = 0 AND LO(SET_MORE_LARGE) = 0

; The offset of the last byte of a sprite of sprite_width.
; In:  sprite_width
; Out: Y = LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE - 1 or SMALL_SPRITE_SIZE - 1
; Clobbers: X
.sprite_last_byte
{
    LDY #LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE - 1
    LDX sprite_width
    CPX #SMALL_WIDTH
    BNE done
    LDY #SMALL_SPRITE_SIZE - 1
.done
    RTS
}

; The byte that fills four MODE 5 pixels with each colour, 0-3.
.colour_byte
    EQUB mode5_byte("...."), mode5_byte("1111"), mode5_byte("2222"), mode5_byte("3333")

; How far draw_grid steps back on the screen after a column of sprite bytes:
; up to the top of the grid and four cells (pixels) right. Indexed by
; sprite_width: small, then large.
.grid_back_step
    EQUW SMALL_SPRITE_HEIGHT/2 * ROW - 4*CELL
    EQUW LARGE_SPRITE_HEIGHT/2 * ROW - 4*CELL

; Draw a sprite magnified in the editing grid: each pixel a cell wide and
; four lines tall, two sprite rows to a character row. Then draw the grid's
; frame, unless the frame for this size is there already.
; In:  A = sprite number, bit 7 set to copy the sprite to undo_buffer first
;      (a new sprite to edit)
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr, data_ptr, temp, count_x, count_y, item,
;      mask, sprite_width
.draw_grid
{
    ASL A
    PHP
    LSR A
    JSR sprite_address
    PLP
    BCC draw
    JSR sprite_last_byte
.keep
    LDA (data_ptr), Y
    STA undo_buffer, Y
    DEY
    BPL keep
.draw
    LDA #LO(edit_grid)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA #HI(edit_grid)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    LDA sprite_width
    STA count_x
.column
    LDA sprite_width                ; count_y = the column's bytes, one for each sprite row
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA count_y
.byte
    LDY #&00
    LDA (data_ptr), Y
    STA temp
    LDX #mode5_byte("3...")         ; the first pixel's bits
    STX mask

    ; Shift this pixel's two bits down to make its colour, 0-3.
.pixel
    LDA mask                        ; item: a copy of mask to shift
    STA item
    LDA temp
    AND mask
.find_bit
    LSR item
    BCS got_bit
    LSR A
    BCC find_bit
.got_bit
    LSR A
    PHP
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    PLP
    ROL A
    TAX
    LDY #&03                        ; the top four lines of the character row...
    LDA #&01
    BIT count_y
    BEQ block
    LDY #&07                        ; ...or, for every second sprite row, the bottom four
.block
    LDA colour_byte, X
    LDX #&03
.block_line
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    DEX
    BPL block_line
    LDA screen_ptr                  ; carry clear from the ROL
    ADC #CELL
    STA screen_ptr
    BCC next_pixel
    INC screen_ptr+1
.next_pixel
    LSR mask
    BCC pixel
    LDA screen_ptr                  ; carry set from the LSR: back to this byte's
    SBC #4*CELL                     ; first cell
    STA screen_ptr
    BCS pixel_done
    DEC screen_ptr+1
.pixel_done
    LDA #&01                        ; after a bottom half, down a row
    AND count_y
    BEQ next_byte
    LDA screen_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #LO(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr+1
.next_byte
    INC data_ptr
    DEC count_y
    BNE byte

    ; Up to the top of the grid, one column of sprite bytes to the right.
    LDX sprite_width
    LDA screen_ptr
    SEC
    SBC grid_back_step-2, X
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    SBC grid_back_step-1, X
    STA screen_ptr+1
    DEC count_x
    BEQ frame
    JMP column

    ; The frame: a large sprite's grid is 16 cells by 16 rows, a small one's
    ; 8 by 8 in the top left of that, with the rest blanked. A byte of each
    ; frame tells which one is on the screen already.
.frame
    LDA sprite_width
    CMP #LARGE_WIDTH
    BEQ large
    LDA grid_frame_top
    CMP #mode5_byte("1...")
    BNE to_small
    RTS
.to_small
    LDA #LO(SCREEN + 10*CELL)       ; blank the large grid's right half...
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA #HI(SCREEN + 10*CELL)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    LDA #18                         ; rows 0-17: the large grid and its frame
    JSR clear_rows
    LDA #LO(SCREEN + 9*ROW + CELL)  ; ...and the rest of its left half
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA #HI(SCREEN + 9*ROW + CELL)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    LDA #9                          ; rows 9-17
    JSR clear_rows
.large
    LDA sprite_width
    CMP #LARGE_WIDTH
    BNE draw_frame
    LDA grid_frame_right
    CMP #mode5_byte("1...")
    BNE draw_frame
    RTS

    ; The top line, the left edge, the bottom line, then the right edge, in
    ; colour 1.
.draw_frame
    LDA #LO(SCREEN + CELL)          ; the row above the grid, a cell left of it
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA #HI(SCREEN + CELL)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    LDY #&07                        ; its last line
    JSR grid_frame_line
    LDA #mode5_byte("...1")         ; the top left corner
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    JSR down_a_row
    LDA sprite_width                ; count_y = the grid's rows
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA count_y
.left_column
    LDA #mode5_byte("...1")         ; the left edge
    LDY #&07
.left_line
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL left_line
    JSR down_a_row
    DEC count_y
    BNE left_column
    LDA #mode5_byte("...1")         ; the bottom left corner, on the row's first line
    INY
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    JSR grid_frame_line
    JSR width_times_32              ; across to the cell after the grid
    ADC #CELL
    ADC screen_ptr
    STA screen_ptr
    BCC right_side
    INC screen_ptr+1
.right_side
    LDA sprite_width
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA count_y
.right_column
    LDA screen_ptr                  ; up a row
    SEC
    SBC #LO(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    SBC #HI(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    LDY #&07
    LDA #mode5_byte("1...")         ; the right edge
.right_line
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL right_line
    DEC count_y
    BNE right_column
    RTS
}

; Draw a horizontal line of the editing grid's frame in colour 1: the corner,
; a pixel at the left of the cell after the grid, then back along every cell
; over (or under) the grid.
; In:  Y = the line within the character row, screen_ptr = the row, at the
;      cell left of the grid
; Out: Y = that line in the cell left of the grid
; Clobbers: A, X, temp
.grid_frame_line
{
    STY temp
    JSR width_times_32              ; the cell after the grid
    ORA temp
    ADC #CELL
    TAY
    LDX #mode5_byte("1...")         ; the corner first...
.loop
    TXA
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    LDX #mode5_byte("1111")         ; ...then the line
    TYA
    SEC
    SBC #CELL
    TAY
    CMP #CELL
    BCS loop
    RTS
}

; Move screen_ptr down a character row.
; Clobbers: A
.down_a_row
{
    LDA screen_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #LO(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    RTS
}

; sprite_width times 32: the editing grid's width in bytes, 128 for a large
; sprite (16 cells), 64 for a small one.
; In:  sprite_width
; Out: A = the result, carry clear
; Clobbers: nothing else
.width_times_32
{
    LDA sprite_width
    LSR A
    ROR A
    ROR A
    ROR A
    RTS
}

; Blank nine cells (72 bytes) of each of A character rows from screen_ptr.
; It has no RTS of its own: it runs on into divide_by_5, which does no harm
; (it divides whatever is left in A, changing only A and X), and returns from
; there.
; In:  A = rows, screen_ptr = where
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr, count_y
.clear_rows
{
    STA count_y
.row
    LDY #9*CELL-1
    LDA #&00
.byte
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL byte
    JSR down_a_row
    DEC count_y
    BNE row
}

; Divide by five: a large sprite's row and column in the sheet.
; In:  A = an index into slot_of_position (a position &00-&0F, or &20-&28
;      less &10)
; Out: X = A DIV 5, A = A MOD 5
; Clobbers: nothing else
.divide_by_5
{
    LDX #&00
.loop
    CMP #LARGE_COLUMNS
    BCC done
    INX
    SBC #LARGE_COLUMNS
    BCS loop
.done
    RTS
}

; Draw a sprite in its place on the sheet, copying its bytes straight to the
; screen a cell (eight bytes of a column) at a time. Also entered at
; at_screen_ptr, with data_ptr, sprite_width and screen_ptr set, to draw one
; somewhere else.
; In:  A = sprite number
; Out: carry clear
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr, data_ptr, count_x, count_y, sprite_width
.draw_sheet_sprite
{
    JSR sprite_address
    JSR sheet_address
.at_screen_ptr
    LDX sprite_width
    STX count_y
.row
    LDX sprite_width
    STX count_x
.column
    LDY #&07
.byte
    LDA (data_ptr), Y
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL byte
    LDA sprite_width                ; the same eight rows of the next column
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ADC data_ptr
    STA data_ptr
    BCC next_screen
    INC data_ptr+1
.next_screen
    LDA #CELL
    CLC
    ADC screen_ptr
    STA screen_ptr
    BCC next_column
    INC screen_ptr+1
.next_column
    DEC count_x
    BNE column

    ; Back to the first column, eight rows down; on the screen, down a row.
    LDA sprite_width
    LSR A
    TAX                             ; 1 small, 2 large
    LDA data_ptr
    SEC
    SBC column_rewind-1, X
    STA data_ptr
    BCS next_row
    DEC data_ptr+1
.next_row
    LDA screen_ptr
    CLC
    ADC row_step-1, X
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(ROW - SMALL_WIDTH*CELL) ; the same for both
    STA screen_ptr+1
    DEC count_y
    BNE row
    RTS
; After a row of cells, how far draw_sheet_sprite steps back through the
; sprite's bytes (column_rewind), and the low byte of how far it steps on
; through the screen to the start of the next row (row_step). Each is indexed
; by sprite_width / 2, from 1: small, then large.
.column_rewind
    EQUB SMALL_SPRITE_SIZE - CELL, LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE - CELL
.row_step
    EQUB LO(ROW - SMALL_WIDTH*CELL), LO(ROW - LARGE_WIDTH*CELL)
    EQUB 0                          ; unused
}
ASSERT HI(ROW - SMALL_WIDTH*CELL) = HI(ROW - LARGE_WIDTH*CELL)

; Where a sprite goes on the screen.
; In:  A = sprite number: a sheet position, or a frame buffer (which shows
;      in Animate's window)
; Out: screen_ptr = the top left of its place, Y = the sprite number (and A
;      too, except for a small sprite)
; Clobbers: X
.sheet_address
{
    TAY
    LDX #&00
    STX screen_ptr+1
    CPY #FIRST_SMALL
    BCC large
    CPY #AFTER_SMALL
    BCC small
    SBC #AFTER_SMALL - FIRST_SMALL  ; (carry set) an index into slot_of_position...
    CMP #SPRITE_FRAME_A - (AFTER_SMALL - FIRST_SMALL)   ; ...unless a frame buffer
    BCS preview

    ; Large sprites: 5 to a row, each 4 cells by 4 rows.
.large
    JSR divide_by_5
    LSR A                           ; the column times 32: four cells
    ROR A
    ROR A
    ROR A
    ADC #LO(large_sheet)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(large_sheet)
.add_rows
    DEX
    BMI done
    ADC #HI(LARGE_SPRITE_HEIGHT/8 * ROW)    ; a row of sprites
    BCC add_rows                    ; always
.done
    STA screen_ptr+1
    TYA
    RTS

    ; Small sprites: 4 to a row, each 2 cells by 2 rows, 4 cells apart.
.small
    AND #&03                        ; the column times 32
    LSR A
    ROR A
    ROR A
    ROR A
    STA screen_ptr
    TYA
    LSR A
    LSR A
    AND #&03
    TAX                             ; the row
.small_rows
    DEX
    BMI small_base
    LDA screen_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #LO(SMALL_SPRITE_HEIGHT/8 * ROW)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(SMALL_SPRITE_HEIGHT/8 * ROW)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    BCC small_rows                  ; always
.small_base
    LDA screen_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #LO(small_sheet)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(small_sheet)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    RTS
.preview
    LDA #LO(frame_preview)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA #HI(frame_preview)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    TYA
    RTS
}
ASSERT LO(LARGE_SPRITE_HEIGHT/8 * ROW) = 0

; An RTS nothing uses.
.stray_rts
{
    RTS
}

; The event handler, for Escape (event 6). With the event enabled the MOS
; leaves setting the Escape flag to the handler (it sets it itself only
; when the event is disabled), so this sets it; and when SHIFT is held, the
; latch too. A menu or prompt that sees the Escape acknowledges it, so plain
; Escape there just cancels; the latch makes SHIFT-Escape cancel and then
; offer to leave as well. Other events aren't passed on.
; In:  A = event number
; Clobbers: nothing
.escape_event
{
    PHP
    CMP #EVENT_ESCAPE
    BNE other_event
    ROR MOS_ESCAPE_FLAG             ; carry is set from the CMP, so this sets bit 7
    TXA
    PHA
    TYA
    PHA
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_SHIFT)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL not_shift
    STA escape_latch                ; A = &FF
.not_shift
    PLA
    TAY
    PLA
    TAX
    LDA #EVENT_ESCAPE
.other_event
    PLP
    RTS
}

; VDU codes for the screen's furniture: clear it, and draw boxes in blue
; round the colour swatch and the name box under the editing grid.
; LAYOUT_END ends the list.
LAYOUT_END = &EA
.screen_layout
    EQUB VDU_RESET_WINDOWS, VDU_CLS
    EQUB VDU_GCOL, 0, 1                             ; draw in colour 1
    EQUB VDU_PLOT, PLOT_MOVE : EQUW 24, 380         ; round the colour swatch
    EQUB VDU_PLOT, PLOT_DRAW_RELATIVE : EQUW 0, 36
    EQUB VDU_PLOT, PLOT_DRAW_RELATIVE : EQUW 72, 0
    EQUB VDU_PLOT, PLOT_DRAW_RELATIVE : EQUW 0, -36
    EQUB VDU_PLOT, PLOT_DRAW_RELATIVE : EQUW -72, 0
    ; Text only in the top 18 rows, so that the CLS on tape (for the filing
    ; system's messages) leaves these boxes and the logo alone.
    EQUB VDU_TEXT_WINDOW, 0, 17, 19, 0
    EQUB VDU_PLOT, PLOT_MOVE_RELATIVE : EQUW 96, 4  ; round the name box
    EQUB VDU_PLOT, PLOT_DRAW_RELATIVE : EQUW 0, 32
    EQUB VDU_PLOT, PLOT_DRAW_RELATIVE : EQUW 488, 0
    EQUB VDU_PLOT, PLOT_DRAW_RELATIVE : EQUW 0, -36
    EQUB VDU_PLOT, PLOT_DRAW_RELATIVE : EQUW -488, 0
    EQUB LAYOUT_END

; The names of the physical colours, eight characters each, for the palette
; window (it shows seven of each).
.colour_names
    EQUS "Black   Red     Green   Yellow  Blue    Magenta Cyan    White   "

; The palette window: show_palette writes the colour names into the blank

PALETTE_LINE = 8
.text_palette

    EQUS "Colour ", CR
.palette_lines

    EQUB TEXT_END

.text_exists

    EQUS "Exists", CR, "Cancel", CR, "Replace", CR
    EQUB TEXT_END
; The prompts for a file name (whole files and single sprites alike) and an
; object's name; input_line echoes the reply after the colon.
.text_load_name

    EQUB TEXT_END

    EQUB TEXT_END

    EQUB TEXT_END

    EQUB TEXT_END
; error_handler copies the error's message into the error window's text,
; breaking its lines and ending it. Before the first error, the spaces run on
; to text_escape's flag byte, MENU, which is the same value as TEXT_END and so
; ends the text. (A message too long for the buffer would run on over
; text_escape; the filing systems' are short.)
.text_error
    EQUB PLAIN
    EQUS "E  R  R  O  R  !", CR, CR
.error_message
    EQUB REPEATED(61, ' ')
.text_escape
    EQUB MENU
    EQUS "Escape?", CR, "No", CR, "Yes", CR
    EQUB TEXT_END
.text_insert_disc
```
