```6502
    EQUS " Return to menu", CR, " Please insert", CR, " Pipeline disc", CR, "and press SPACE", CR
    EQUB TEXT_END

; Draw every sprite in the sheet, from the last position down to 0 (the
; small sprites, &10-&1F, among them).
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr, data_ptr, count_x, count_y, sprite_width
.draw_sheet
{
    LDA #LAST_SPRITE
.loop
    PHA
    JSR draw_sheet_sprite
    PLA
    SEC
    SBC #&01
    BCS loop
    RTS
}

; Mark the selected sprite in the sheet with a box in colour 2, drawn over
; the sprite (drawing the sprite again removes it); and under the editing
; grid show its number and name if it is an object (a small sprite), or
; blank them if not. The exit's "name" is the "Finish Block" that start
; writes after the names.
; In:  A = sprite = the selected sprite (the name comes from sprite)
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr, data_ptr, aux_ptr, count_y, sprite_width
.show_selection
{
    JSR sprite_class
    JSR sheet_address
    LDY #&00
    JSR selection_edge
    LDA sprite_width
    STA count_y

    ; Down each character row: the rightmost pixel of the last cell, the
    ; leftmost of the first.
.column
    LDA sprite_width
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDX #&07
.right_edge
    DEY
    LDA (screen_ptr), Y
    AND #mode5_byte("333.")         ; pixel 3 becomes colour 2
    ORA #mode5_byte("...2")
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEX
    BPL right_edge
    LDY #&07
.left_edge
    LDA (screen_ptr), Y
    AND #mode5_byte(".333")         ; pixel 0 becomes colour 2
    ORA #mode5_byte("2...")
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL left_edge
    DEC count_y
    LDA count_y
    BEQ bottom
    LDA screen_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #LO(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    BCC column
.bottom
    LDY #&07
    JSR selection_edge
    LDA sprite_width
    CMP #SMALL_WIDTH
    BEQ small
    TXA                             ; X is 0 here: blank the name box
    LDY #NAME_BOX_CELLS*CELL-1
.clear_name
    STA name_box, Y
    DEY
    BPL clear_name
    RTS

    ; An object: its number, 1-16 (the small sprite less &0F), then ":" and
    ; its name.
.small
    LDA #LO(name_box)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA #HI(name_box)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    LDX #' '                 ; objects 1-9: no tens
    LDA sprite
    CMP #FIRST_SMALL + 9
    BCC tens
    LDX #'1'
.tens
    SEC
    TXA
    JSR print_char_advance
    LDA sprite
    SEC
    SBC #FIRST_SMALL - 1
    CMP #10
    BCC units
    SBC #10
.units
    SEC                             ; carry set: store the characters
    ORA #'0'
    JSR print_char_advance
    LDA #':'
    SEC
    JSR print_char_advance
    JSR name_offset
    LDX #OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH - 1
.name
    LDA object_names, Y
    SEC
    JSR print_char_advance
    INY
    DEX
    BPL name
    RTS
}
NAME_BOX_CELLS = 3 + OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH     ; "16:" and the name

; Draw a horizontal edge of the selection box in colour 2: line Y of each
; cell across the sprite.
; In:  Y = the line within the character row, screen_ptr = the row
; Out: X = 0
; Clobbers: A, Y
.selection_edge
{
    LDX sprite_width
.loop
    LDA #mode5_byte("2222")
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    TYA
    CLC
    ADC #CELL
    TAY
    DEX
    BNE loop
    RTS
}

; Where an object's name is in object_names. Also entered at of_a with the
; sprite in A.
; In:  sprite = the small sprite
; Out: A = Y = (sprite AND &0F) * OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH
; Clobbers: nothing else
.name_offset
{
    LDA sprite
.of_a
    AND #&0F
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA times_4
    ASL A
    ADC times_4
    TAY
    RTS
.times_4
    EQUB &00
}
ASSERT OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH = 12

; Unused copies of down_a_row, width_times_32 and clear_rows: nothing
; calls these three. This clear_rows has its RTS.
.unused_down_a_row
{
    LDA screen_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #LO(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(ROW)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    RTS
}

; Unused: as width_times_32.
.unused_width_times_32
{
    LDA sprite_width
    LSR A
    ROR A
    ROR A
    ROR A
    RTS
}

; Unused: as clear_rows.
.unused_clear_rows
{
    STA count_y
.row
    LDY #9*CELL-1
    LDA #&00
.byte
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL byte
    JSR unused_down_a_row
    DEC count_y
    BNE row
    RTS
}

; Fill the colour swatch, two cells, with the current colour.
; In:  colour
; Clobbers: A, X, Y
.show_colour
{
    LDX colour
    LDA colour_byte, X
    LDY #2*CELL-1
.loop
    STA colour_swatch, Y
    DEY
    BPL loop
    RTS
}

; The stack pointer when the designer first started, for the main loop to
; reset the stack to. It starts 0; the stack pointer start finds is always
; &80 or more, so bit 7 set also says it has been saved.
.stack_pointer
    EQUB &00

; Bit 7 set once the graphics area has been cleared (and on disc DEFAULT
; loaded), so starting again after an error keeps the user's work.
.graphics_loaded
    EQUB &00

; Bit 7 set if the filing system is numbered FS_DISC or more (disc, or
; network), clear on tape or ROM: what the comments call "on tape".
.disc_fs
    EQUB 0

; The physical colours for logical 1-3 (blue, yellow, red); 0 stays black.
.palette_colours
    EQUB COLOUR_BLUE, COLOUR_YELLOW, COLOUR_RED

; The graphics set to start with, and the command that goes back to the menu.
.default_name
    EQUS "DEFAULT", CR
.mrun_command
    EQUS "/MRUN", CR

; BRKV points here: show the error's message in the error window, wait for
; a key, close any open files and start again.
; In:  MOS_ERROR_PTR = the error, as the OS leaves it
; Out: doesn't return: it runs on into start
.error_handler
{
    LDY #&00
    LDX #&00

    ; Copy the message, breaking it into lines: a CR after the first 14
    ; characters, then after every 15.
.copy
    INY
    INX
    TXA
    AND #&0F
    CMP #&0F
    BNE store
    LDA #CR
    STA error_message-1, X
    INX
.store
    LDA (MOS_ERROR_PTR), Y
    STA error_message-1, X
    BNE copy
    LDA #CR
    STA error_message-1, X
    LDA #TEXT_END
    STA error_message, X
    JSR close_all_windows
    LDX #LO(text_error)
    LDY #HI(text_error)
    LDA #WINDOW_ERROR
    JSR open_window
    LDA #OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS       ; empty the keyboard buffer
    LDX #&00
    LDY #&00
    JSR OSBYTE
.wait
    JSR OSRDCH                      ; wait for a key, acknowledging any Escape
    BCC restart
    LDA #OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE
    JMP wait
.restart
    JSR close_all_windows
    JSR close_files                 ; and fall into start
}

; The entry point, from the GRAPHIC stub, and where errors start again. The
; first time (BRKV still pointing into the ROMs) it takes over BRKV and the
; event vector, keeping the old ones in IND1V and IND2V (vectors the OS
; leaves spare) to put back on leaving, and enables the Escape event. Unless the screen is in MODE 5
; already (as it is after an error, so a changed palette survives), it sets
; MODE 5 and the palette. Then it draws the screen, the first time clears
; the graphics area and (on disc) loads DEFAULT, and draws the sheet and the
; first sprite; main_loop follows.
; Out: doesn't return
.start
{
    LDA #OSBYTE_CURSOR_EDITING      ; the cursor keys give codes
    LDX #CURSOR_KEYS_CODES
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDA BRKV+1                      ; BRKV still pointing into the ROMs (&8000 up):
    BPL installed                   ; not ours yet
    LDX #LO(error_handler)
    LDY #HI(error_handler)
    LDA EVNTV
    STA IND2V
    LDA EVNTV+1
    STA IND2V+1
    LDA BRKV
    STA IND1V
    LDA BRKV+1
    STA IND1V+1
    LDA #LO(escape_event)
    SEI
    STX BRKV
    STY BRKV+1
    STA EVNTV
    LDA #HI(escape_event)
    STA EVNTV+1
    CLI
    LDA #OSBYTE_ENABLE_EVENT        ; enable the Escape event; storing the call
    STA escape_latch                ; number (bit 7 clear) also clears the latch
    LDX #EVENT_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE
.installed
    LDA #OSBYTE_READ_CHAR_AND_MODE  ; the screen mode, into Y
    JSR OSBYTE
    CPY #5
    BEQ setup
    LDA #VDU_MODE                   ; MODE 5
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDA #5
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDA #&03                        ; logical colours 3 to 1
.palette
    PHA
    TAX
    LDA palette_colours-1, X
    JSR write_palette
    PLA
    SEC
    SBC #&01
    BNE palette
.setup
    LDA #OSBYTE_WRITE_SHEILA        ; no cursor
    LDX #LO(CRTC_ADDR)
    LDY #CRTC_CURSOR_START
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDY #CRTC_CURSOR_OFF
    INX                             ; LO(CRTC_DATA)
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDA #OSARGS_READ_FS             ; the filing system's number
    TAY
    JSR OSARGS
    CMP #FS_DISC                    ; carry set for a disc filing system
    LDA #&00
    STA by_slot
    TAY
    ROR A                           ; the carry into bit 7, for disc_fs
    STA disc_fs
    BMI opt
    INY
.opt
    LDA #FSCV_OPT                   ; *OPT 1,Y: messages off on disc (Y = 0), on for tape
    LDX #&01
    JSR fscv
    JSR reset_timer
    TSX
    BIT stack_pointer
    BMI saved_sp
    STX stack_pointer

    ; Draw the screen's furniture.
.saved_sp
    LDY #&FF
.layout
    INY
    LDA screen_layout, Y
    CMP #LAYOUT_END
    BEQ layout_done
    JSR OSWRCH
    JMP layout
.layout_done
    LDX #20-1                       ; all twenty bytes of window_open
    LDA #&00
.clear_windows
    STA window_open, X
    DEX
    BPL clear_windows
    LDA #CRTC_CURSOR_START          ; the cursor off again, after the CLS
    STA CRTC_ADDR
    LDA #CRTC_CURSOR_OFF
    STA CRTC_DATA
    LDA #LO(logo)                   ; not needed: the copy below is indexed
    STA data_ptr
    LDA #HI(logo)
    STA data_ptr+1
    LDY #&00
.logo_copy
    LDA logo, Y
    STA logo_screen, Y
    LDA logo + LOGO_BAND, Y
    STA logo_screen + ROW, Y
    LDA logo + 2*LOGO_BAND, Y
    STA logo_screen + 2*ROW, Y
    INY
    CPY #LOGO_BAND
    BCC logo_copy

    ; The first time only: clear the graphics area and, on disc, load DEFAULT
    ; into it.
    BIT graphics_loaded
    BMI redraw
    LDA #&00
    TAY
    STA screen_ptr                  ; A is 0 for the low byte and to clear with
    LDX #HI(graphics)
    STX screen_ptr+1
    LDX #&10                        ; 16 pages, to &4FFF
.clear
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    INY
    BNE clear
    INC screen_ptr+1
    DEX
    BNE clear
    DEX
    STX graphics_loaded             ; X = &FF
    LDA disc_fs
    BMI load_default

    ; On tape nothing is loaded: the set starts empty. The name is made ""
    ; (the next file on the tape) first, but nothing reads it after this.
    LDX #6                          ; the seven letters of DEFAULT
.tape_name
    STA default_name, X             ; A = 0
    DEX
    BPL tape_name
    LDA #'"'
    STA default_name
    STA default_name+1
    BNE redraw                      ; always
.load_default
    LDA #LO(default_name)
    STA osfile_block
    LDA #HI(default_name)
    STA osfile_block+1
    LDA #OSFILE_LOAD                ; &FF, as graphics_loaded wants too
    STA graphics_loaded
    JSR osfile_graphics

    ; Redraw everything, with the selection back at position 0: also where
    ; the file commands come back to.
.redraw
    BIT disc_fs                     ; on tape, clear away the filing system's messages
    BMI cls_done
    LDA #VDU_CLS
    JSR OSWRCH
.cls_done
    LDX #LEN(FINISH_BLOCK) - 1
.mark_end
    LDA finish_block, X
    STA graphics_end, X
    DEX
    BPL mark_end
    JSR draw_sheet
    LDA #&00
    STA sprite
    JSR show_selection
    LDA #&00                        ; the pixel cursor to the top left
    STA cursor_x
    STA cursor_y
    SEC                             ; carry set: take an undo copy too
    JSR redraw_grid
    LDA #&03                        ; start in colour 3
    STA colour
    JSR show_colour
}

; The main loop. Each pass moves the selection, paints, runs a command picked
; from a menu or by a CTRL shortcut, and on Escape (or a latched SHIFT-Escape)
; asks whether to leave. A pass starts at least two centiseconds after the
; last (select_sprite waits for that, unless CTRL is held) and ends by waiting
; for a vsync. It starts by resetting the stack to where start found it, so a
; command can give up from any depth with a plain JMP to main_loop or
; command_done.
; Out: doesn't return (leaving the designer, it runs /MRUN or resets)
.main_loop
{
    LDX stack_pointer
    TXS
    JSR close_all_windows
    LDA #&00                        ; move the selection
    JSR select_sprite
    BMI edit                        ; nothing moved (or CTRL held)
    LDX cursor_x                    ; the grid was drawn again: put the pixel
    LDY cursor_y                    ; cursor back on it
    JSR toggle_cursor
.edit
    JSR edit_pixels
    LDA colour                      ; commands may use colour as a scratch value
    STA saved_colour
    JSR read_command
    ASL A                           ; &FF (bit 7 set) means no command
    BCS command_done
    TAY
    LDA command_table, Y
    STA dispatch+1
    LDA command_table+1, Y
    STA dispatch+2
.dispatch
    JSR &1234                       ; the command, written in above (&1234 is the original's)
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_RETURN)     ; so a menu choice made with Return doesn't plot too
    JSR wait_key_release
.command_done
    LDA saved_colour
    STA colour
    LDA #OSBYTE_WAIT_VSYNC          ; wait for the vsync, which leaves A = &13...
    JSR OSBYTE
    STA by_slot                     ; ...so by_slot bit 7 is clear again
    LDA MOS_ESCAPE_FLAG             ; Escape, or SHIFT-Escape latched
    ORA escape_latch
    BPL loop
    LSR escape_latch
    LDA #OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE
    JSR close_all_windows
    LDX #LO(text_escape)
    LDY #HI(text_escape)
    LDA #WINDOW_QUESTION
    JSR menu                        ; Escape? No/Yes
    CMP #2                          ; Yes
    BNE loop
    LDX #LO(text_insert_disc)
    LDY #HI(text_insert_disc)
    LDA #WINDOW_INPUT
    JSR open_window
    LDA #OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS       ; empty the keyboard buffer
    JSR OSBYTE
.wait_key
    JSR OSRDCH                      ; wait for a key, acknowledging any Escape
    PHP
    LDA #OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE
    PLP
    BCS wait_key

    ; Leave: put the vectors back and return to the menu.
    LDA IND1V
    STA BRKV
    LDA IND1V+1
    STA BRKV+1
    LDA IND2V
    STA EVNTV
    LDA IND2V+1
    STA EVNTV+1
    LDA #OSBYTE_CURSOR_EDITING      ; X = 0 from the last OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE (no
    INX                             ; Escape was pending), so this is OSBYTE 4,1 and the
    JSR OSBYTE                      ; cursor keys stay codes; MENU sets that anyway
    LDA #OSBYTE_FUNCTION_KEY_BASE   ; function keys back to strings
    LDX #FUNCTION_KEYS_STRINGS
    JSR OSBYTE
    BIT disc_fs
    BMI run_mrun
    LDA #OSBYTE_BREAK_EFFECT        ; on tape there's no /MRUN: *FX200,3 makes
    LDX #&03                        ; BREAK clear memory...
    JSR OSBYTE
    JMP (CPU_RESET_VECTOR)          ; ...and this resets the machine as BREAK does
.run_mrun
    LDX #LO(mrun_command)           ; */MRUN, which goes back to the menu
    LDY #HI(mrun_command)
    JMP OSCLI
.loop
    JMP main_loop
}

; Written after the graphics set in memory, at graphics_end, which is where
; the exit's name would be (SET_NAMES + 15 * OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH): so the
; name box shows the exit as "16:Finish Block".
FINISH_BLOCK = "Finish Block"
.finish_block
    EQUS FINISH_BLOCK
ASSERT LEN(FINISH_BLOCK) = OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH
ASSERT graphics_end = object_names + (SLOT_EXIT - FIRST_SMALL_SLOT) * OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH

; The colour, kept while a command runs.
.saved_colour
    EQUB &00

; The commands, by read_command's number: a menu item is menu * 8 + item
; (items from 1), a CTRL shortcut its place in shortcut_keys plus one.
; Numbers with no command go to the main loop's own tail, command_done,
; which is harmless to call because the main loop resets the stack. A
; command takes the selected sprite from `sprite`, and may clobber every
; register and most of zero page.
.command_table
    EQUW main_loop.command_done     ; 0: none (the credits)
    EQUW cmd_flip_x                 ; OptionsA
    EQUW cmd_flip_y
    EQUW cmd_delete
    EQUW cmd_undo
    EQUW cmd_animate
    EQUW cmd_obj_name
    EQUW main_loop.command_done
    EQUW main_loop.command_done
    EQUW cmd_swap                   ; OptionsB
    EQUW cmd_copy
    EQUW cmd_overlay
    EQUW cmd_underlay
    EQUW cmd_remove
    EQUW cmd_backing
    EQUW main_loop.command_done
    EQUW main_loop.command_done
    EQUW cmd_load_sprite            ; Environment
    EQUW cmd_save_sprite
    EQUW cmd_load_file
    EQUW cmd_save_file
    EQUW cmd_def_colour
    EQUW main_loop.command_done
    EQUW main_loop.command_done
    EQUW main_loop.command_done

; OptionsA Delete (CTRL-Delete): clear the sprite to colour 0, and an
; object's name to zeros. Drawing the sprite again after show_selection
; rubs out the selection box, which stays off until the selection moves.
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_delete
{
    LDA sprite
    JSR sprite_address
    JSR sprite_last_byte
    LDA #&00
.clear
    STA (data_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL clear
    LDX sprite_width
    CPX #SMALL_WIDTH
    BNE redraw
    LDA sprite                      ; the exit has no name to clear
    CMP #SLOT_EXIT
    BEQ redraw
    JSR name_offset
    LDA #&00
    LDX #OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH - 1
.name
    STA object_names, Y
    INY
    DEX
    BPL name
.redraw
    LDA sprite
    JSR show_selection
    LDA sprite
    JSR draw_sheet_sprite
    LDA sprite
    JMP redraw_grid
}

; Draw the selected sprite in the editing grid and put the pixel cursor
; back on it.
; In:  sprite, carry set to take an undo copy of the sprite first
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, and as draw_grid
.redraw_grid
{
    LDA sprite
    BCC draw
    ORA #&80                        ; bit 7 set: take an undo copy
.draw
    JSR draw_grid
    LDX cursor_x
    LDY cursor_y
    JMP toggle_cursor
}

; OptionsA Flip X (CTRL-X): mirror the sprite left to right, pixel by pixel,
; swapping each pixel in the left half of a row with its opposite. colour
; carries the pixels across (main_loop puts it back).
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_flip_x
{
    LDA sprite
    JSR sprite_address
    LDA sprite_width                ; item = pixels in half a row
    ASL A
    STA item
    ASL A                           ; aux_ptr = the last pixel's x
    STA aux_ptr
    ASL A                           ; count_y = the last row
    STA count_y
    DEC aux_ptr
    DEC count_y
.row
    LDA #&00
    STA count_x
.pixel
    LDA aux_ptr
    SEC
    SBC count_x
    TAX
    LDY count_y
    STX mirror_x
    STY mirror_y
    LDA sprite
    JSR read_pixel
    PHA
    LDX count_x
    LDY count_y
    LDA sprite
    JSR read_pixel
    STA colour
    LDX mirror_x
    LDY mirror_y
    LDA sprite
    JSR plot_pixel
    LDX count_x
    LDY count_y
    PLA
    STA colour
    LDA sprite
    JSR plot_pixel
    INC count_x
    LDA count_x
    CMP item
    BCC pixel
    DEC count_y
    BPL row
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_X)          ; the shortcut, to wait for

    ; Show the sprite as changed, then wait for the key in X to be released so
    ; a shortcut acts once.
.redraw
    TXA
    PHA
    LDA sprite
    PHA
    JSR draw_sheet_sprite
    PLA
    JSR redraw_grid                 ; carry is clear from draw_sheet_sprite: no undo copy
    PLA
    TAX
    JMP wait_key_release
}

; Flip X's mirrored pixel: its x and y.
.mirror_x
    EQUB &00

.mirror_y
    EQUB &00

; The OSGBPB block for moving sprites and names to and from files: the
; handle, the address in memory, the byte count, the pointer in the file;
; then three spare bytes, which check_filing_system clears with it.
.gbpb_block                         ; the handle
    EQUB 0
.gbpb_address
    EQUD 0
.gbpb_count
    EQUD 0
.gbpb_pointer
    EQUD 0
    EQUB 0, 0, 0

; OptionsA Flip Y (CTRL-Y): turn the sprite upside down.
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_flip_y
{
    JSR flip_vertically
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_Y)
    JMP cmd_flip_x.redraw
}

; Turn the selected sprite upside down, by reversing each column of bytes.
; In:  sprite (Animate uses this on its frame buffers)
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, data_ptr, count_x, count_y, sprite_width
.flip_vertically
{
    LDA sprite
    JSR sprite_address
    LDA sprite_width
    STA count_x
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA count_y                     ; a column's bytes
.column
    LDY count_y
    DEY
.swap
    LDX #&00
    LDA (data_ptr, X)
    PHA
    LDA (data_ptr), Y
    STA (data_ptr, X)
    PLA
    STA (data_ptr), Y
    INC data_ptr
    BNE next
    INC data_ptr+1
.next
    DEY
    DEY
    BPL swap
    LDA count_y                     ; on to the next column
    LSR A
    CLC
    ADC data_ptr
    STA data_ptr
    BCC next_column
    INC data_ptr+1
.next_column
    DEC count_x
    BNE column
    RTS
}

; OptionsA Undo (CTRL-U): swap the sprite with the copy taken when it was
; selected, so a second Undo puts the changes back.
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_undo
{
    LDA sprite
    JSR sprite_address
    JSR sprite_last_byte
.swap
    LDX undo_buffer, Y
    LDA (data_ptr), Y
    STA undo_buffer, Y
    TXA
    STA (data_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL swap
    LDA sprite
    JSR draw_sheet_sprite
    LDA sprite
    JSR show_selection
    CLC
    JSR redraw_grid
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_U)
    JMP wait_key_release
}

; OptionsB Underlay (no shortcut): put this sprite under another - fill the
; other's colour 0 pixels from this one.
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_underlay
{
    LDX #LO(text_underlay)
    LDY #HI(text_underlay)
    JSR pick_second_sprite
    STX combine_test
    CLC
    JMP combine_sprites
}

; OptionsB Backing (CTRL-B): fill the sprite's colour 0 pixels from the
; floor (sheet position 0). No second sprite to pick: it goes straight on.
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_backing
{
    LDX sprite
    STX combine_test
    LDA #&00                        ; the floor
    CLC
    JMP combine_sprites
}

; OptionsB Overlay (CTRL-O): put this sprite over another - copy its
; pixels other than colour 0 onto the other.
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_overlay
{
    LDX #LO(text_overlay)
    LDY #HI(text_overlay)
    JSR pick_second_sprite
    STA combine_test
    SEC
}

; Combine two sprites a pixel at a time, then show them both again
; (redraw_pair).
; In:  X = the sprite to change, A = the sprite to take pixels from,
;      combine_test = the sprite whose pixels decide, carry set to copy
;      combine_test's pixels where they aren't colour 0 (overlay), clear to
;      copy A's pixels where combine_test's are colour 0 (underlay, backing)
; Clobbers: everything
.combine_sprites
{
    STX combine_target
    STA combine_source
    LDA #&00                        ; combine_over = the carry, in bit 7
    ROR A
    STA combine_over
    LDA sprite_width                ; count_x = the last pixel across
    ASL A
    ASL A
    SBC #&00                        ; (carry clear from the ASL)
    STA count_x
.column
    LDA sprite_width                ; count_y = the last row
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    SBC #&00                        ; (carry clear from the ASL)
    STA count_y
.pixel
    LDA combine_test
    LDX count_x
    LDY count_y
    JSR read_pixel
    BIT combine_over
    BPL under                       ; overlay: copy the pixel where it isn't 0
    CMP #&00
    BEQ next
    BNE plot
.under
    CMP #&00                        ; underlay: where it's 0...
    BNE next
    LDA combine_source              ; ...copy the source's
    LDX count_x
    LDY count_y
    JSR read_pixel
.plot
    STA colour
    LDA combine_target
    LDX count_x
    LDY count_y
    JSR plot_pixel
.next
    DEC count_y
    BPL pixel
    DEC count_x
    BPL column
    LDA combine_source
    JMP redraw_pair
}

; Combine's sprites: the one to change, the one to take pixels from, the
; one whose pixels decide, and bit 7 set to overlay rather than underlay.
.combine_target
    EQUB &00

.combine_source
    EQUB &00

.combine_test
    EQUB &00

.combine_over
    EQUB &00

; OptionsB Remove (CTRL-R): take this sprite from another - clear to 0 the
; other's pixels that match this one's.
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_remove
{
    LDX #LO(text_remove)
    LDY #HI(text_remove)
    JSR pick_second_sprite
    STX combine_target
    STA combine_source
    LDA sprite_width                ; count_x = the last pixel across
    ASL A
    ASL A
    SBC #&00                        ; (carry clear from the ASL)
    STA count_x
.column
    LDA sprite_width                ; count_y = the last row
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    SBC #&00
    STA count_y
.pixel
    LDA combine_target
    LDX count_x
    LDY count_y
    JSR read_pixel
    STA temp
    LDA combine_source
    LDX count_x
    LDY count_y
    JSR read_pixel
    EOR temp                        ; the same colour in both...
    BNE next
    STA colour                      ; ...becomes 0
    LDA combine_target
    LDX count_x
    LDY count_y
    JSR plot_pixel
.next
    DEC count_y
    BPL pixel
    DEC count_x
    BPL column
    LDA combine_source
    JMP redraw_pair
}

; OptionsB Copy (CTRL-COPY): copy this sprite onto another.
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_copy
{
    LDX #LO(text_copy)
    LDY #HI(text_copy)
    JSR pick_second_sprite
    PHA
.copy
    LDA (aux_ptr), Y
    STA (data_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL copy
    PLA
    JMP redraw_pair
}

; OptionsB Swap (CTRL-S): swap this sprite with another, and two objects'
; names with them (unless one is the exit, which has none).
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_swap
{
    LDX #LO(text_swap)
    LDY #HI(text_swap)
    JSR pick_second_sprite
    PHA
.swap
    LDA (data_ptr), Y
    PHA
    LDA (aux_ptr), Y
    STA (data_ptr), Y
    PLA
    STA (aux_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL swap
    LDA sprite_width
    CMP #SMALL_WIDTH
    BNE done
    CPX #SLOT_EXIT
    BEQ done
    PLA
    PHA
    CMP #SLOT_EXIT
    BEQ done

    ; Swap the names: data_ptr and aux_ptr hold the two names' offsets now.
    JSR name_offset
    STA data_ptr
    PLA
    PHA
    JSR name_offset.of_a
    STA aux_ptr
    LDX #OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH - 1     ; count the name's bytes in data_ptr+1
    STX data_ptr+1
.names
    LDY aux_ptr
    LDA object_names, Y
    LDY data_ptr
    LDX object_names, Y
    STA object_names, Y
    LDY aux_ptr
    TXA
    STA object_names, Y
    INC aux_ptr
    INC data_ptr
    DEC data_ptr+1
    BPL names
.done
    PLA
}

; Show both sprites of a two-sprite command as they are now and close the
; picking window. The selection stays on the second sprite, the one picked.
; In:  A = the first sprite (for Backing, the floor), sprite = the one picked
;      (for Backing, the sprite backed)
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, and as draw_grid
.redraw_pair
{
    JSR draw_sheet_sprite
    LDA sprite
    JSR draw_sheet_sprite
    LDA sprite
    JSR show_selection
    LDA sprite
    CLC
    JSR redraw_grid
    LDA #WINDOW_PICK
    JMP close_window
}

; Ask for the second sprite of a two-sprite command: show the question with
; a picture of this sprite, and let the selection move until Return. If the
; two are different sizes it says "Wrong Types"; then, as on Escape (or
; f0-f3), it abandons the command and goes back to the main loop.
; In:  sprite, X/Y = the question
; Out: sprite = X = the sprite picked, A = the first one, data_ptr = the
;      picked one's bytes, aux_ptr = the first one's, Y = the offset of
;      their last byte, carry set
; Clobbers: everything else
.pick_second_sprite
{
    LDA #WINDOW_PICK
    JSR open_window
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_RETURN)     ; the Return that chose the command
    JSR wait_key_release
    LDA sprite
    PHA
    JSR sprite_address
    LDA data_ptr
    STA first_address
    LDA data_ptr+1
    STA first_address+1
    LDA window_address + 2*WINDOW_PICK      ; the picture goes on the right, two rows down
    CLC
    ADC #LO(2*ROW + 8*CELL)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA window_address + 2*WINDOW_PICK + 1
    ADC #HI(2*ROW + 8*CELL)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    JSR draw_sheet_sprite.at_screen_ptr
    LDA sprite_width
    STA first_width
.select
    LDA #&01
    JSR select_sprite               ; move the selection; f0-f3 raise an Escape
    BIT MOS_ESCAPE_FLAG
    BMI abandon
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_RETURN)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL select
    LDA sprite
    JSR sprite_address
    JSR sprite_last_byte
    LDA first_address
    STA aux_ptr
    LDA first_address+1
    STA aux_ptr+1
    LDX sprite
    LDA sprite_width
    CMP first_width                 ; the same size?
    BNE wrong_type
    PLA
    RTS
.wrong_type
    LDA #WINDOW_ERROR
    LDX #LO(text_wrong_types)
    LDY #HI(text_wrong_types)
    JSR open_window
    LDA #OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS       ; empty the keyboard buffer
    LDX #&00
    JSR OSBYTE
.wait_space
    JSR OSRDCH
    BCS close
    CMP #' '
    BNE wait_space
.close
    LDA #WINDOW_ERROR
    JSR close_window
.abandon
    PLA                             ; drop the first sprite and the return into the command
    PLA
    PLA

    ; Give up a command: also where input_line goes on Escape.
.abandon_command
    LDA #WINDOW_PICK
    JSR close_window
    LDA #OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE
    JMP main_loop.command_done
}

; Show an error in the error window until a key other than Escape is
; pressed, then go back to the main loop.
; In:  X/Y = the error's text
; Out: doesn't return
.show_error
{
    STX error_text
    STY error_text+1
.show
    LDA #OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDA #WINDOW_ERROR
    LDX error_text
    LDY error_text+1
    JSR open_window
    JSR OSRDCH
    BIT MOS_ESCAPE_FLAG
    BMI show
    JMP main_loop
}

; pick_second_sprite's first sprite: its address and width.
.first_address
    EQUB &00, &00

.first_width
    EQUB &00

; show_error's text, kept while it waits.
.error_text
    EQUB &00, &00

; Read the palette.
; In:  A = logical colour
; Out: A = the physical colour it shows
; Clobbers: X, Y, osfile_block
.read_palette
{
    STA osfile_block
    LDX #LO(osfile_block)
    LDY #HI(osfile_block)
    LDA #OSWORD_READ_PALETTE
    JSR OSWORD
    LDA osfile_block+1
    RTS
}

; A menu with nothing in it: the palette window opens empty and
; show_palette fills it.
.empty_text
    EQUB MENU, TEXT_END

; Environment Def. Colour (CTRL-C): change the palette. Up and down pick a
; logical colour, left and right step its physical colour through the eight;
; Return, Space, Escape or a function key finish. The change lasts while the
; designer runs: start sets the palette only when it has to set MODE 5, which
; it doesn't when restarting after an error.
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_def_colour
{
    LDA #WINDOW_QUESTION
    LDX #LO(empty_text)
    LDY #HI(empty_text)
    JSR open_window
    LDA #OSBYTE_CURSOR_EDITING      ; the cursor keys give codes
    LDX #CURSOR_KEYS_CODES
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDA #OSBYTE_FUNCTION_KEY_BASE   ; f0-f9 give KEYCODE_F0 up
    LDX #KEYCODE_F0
    LDY #&00
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDA #OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS       ; empty the keyboard buffer
    LDX #&00
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDA #&00
    STA item
    JSR palette_highlight
.redraw
    JSR show_palette
.read_key
    JSR OSRDCH
    BCC got_key
    LDA #OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE
.done
    JMP show_palette.done
.got_key
    LDY item
    CMP #KEYCODE_F0
    BCS done
    CMP #CR
    BEQ done
    CMP #' '
    BEQ done
    CMP #KEYCODE_DOWN
    BNE not_down
    LDX item
    CPX #&03                        ; logical colours 0-3
    BEQ not_down
    INC item
.not_down
    CMP #KEYCODE_UP
    BNE moved
    LDX item
    BEQ moved
    DEC item
.moved
    PHA
    JSR palette_highlight.toggle    ; off the old line, on the new (or the same)
    JSR palette_highlight
    PLA
    LDX #&01                        ; right: the next physical colour
    CMP #KEYCODE_RIGHT
    BEQ change
    LDX #&FF                        ; left: the one before
    CMP #KEYCODE_LEFT
    BNE read_key
.change
    STX colour_step
    LDA item
    JSR read_palette
    CLC
    ADC colour_step
    AND #&07
    PHA
    JSR show_palette                ; rub out the old names...
    PLA
    LDX item
    JSR write_palette
    JMP redraw                      ; ...and show the new
}

; Set the palette.
; In:  X = logical colour, A = physical colour
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, osfile_block
.write_palette
{
    STA osfile_block+1
    STX osfile_block
    LDX #LO(osfile_block)
    LDY #HI(osfile_block)
    LDA #OSWORD_WRITE_PALETTE
    JMP OSWORD
}

; Def. Colour's step through the physical colours: 1, or -1 (&FF).
.colour_step
    EQUB &00

; Write each logical colour's physical colour's name into the palette
; window's text, then exclusive-OR the text onto the window again without
; opening it: so one call shows the names and the next rubs them out, and
; Def. Colour calls it before and after each change.
; In:  the palette window open, so count_x = its width less one
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr, data_ptr, save_ptr, aux_ptr, border_ptr,
;      count_y, osfile_block (its first byte counts the colours)
.show_palette
{
    LDA #&03                        ; logical colours 3 to 0
    STA osfile_block
    LDA #LO(palette_lines + 3*PALETTE_LINE)
    STA save_ptr
    LDA #HI(palette_lines + 3*PALETTE_LINE)
    STA save_ptr+1
.entry
    LDA osfile_block
    JSR read_palette
    ASL A                           ; eight characters to each name...
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ORA #PALETTE_LINE - 2           ; ...of which a line takes seven
    TAX
    LDY #PALETTE_LINE - 2
.name
    LDA colour_names, X
    STA (save_ptr), Y
    DEX
    DEY
    BPL name
    LDA save_ptr
    SEC
    SBC #PALETTE_LINE
    STA save_ptr
    BCS next
    DEC save_ptr+1
.next
    DEC osfile_block
    BPL entry

    ; Write the window's text again, without opening it.
    LDA window_address + 2*WINDOW_QUESTION
    STA save_ptr
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA window_address + 2*WINDOW_QUESTION + 1
    STA save_ptr+1
    STA screen_ptr+1
    LDX #LO(text_palette)
    LDY #HI(text_palette)
    STX data_ptr
    STY data_ptr+1
    LDA #WINDOW_QUESTION
    JMP print_window_text
.done
    RTS
}

; The parameter block for OSFILE: the filename's address, then the load and
; exec addresses, the start address (from OSFILE_READ_INFO, the length) and
; the end address (the attributes), four bytes each; then two spare bytes.
; The palette routines use its first two bytes for OSWORD's block, and
; show_palette its first as a counter.
.osfile_block                       ; the filename's address
    EQUW 0
.osfile_load
    EQUD 0
.osfile_exec
    EQUD 0
.osfile_start                       ; or the length
    EQUD 0
.osfile_end                         ; or the attributes
    EQUD 0
    EQUB 0, 0

; Where each line of the palette window is, from its corner.
.palette_row_offset
    EQUW 1*ROW, 2*ROW, 3*ROW, 4*ROW

; Highlight the palette window's line for a logical colour. Also entered at
; toggle, to highlight or unhighlight the line highlighted last.
; In:  item = the logical colour, 0-3
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr
.palette_highlight
{
    LDA item
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDA palette_row_offset, Y
    CLC
    ADC window_address + 2*WINDOW_QUESTION
    STA highlight_address
    LDA palette_row_offset+1, Y
    ADC window_address + 2*WINDOW_QUESTION + 1
    STA highlight_address+1
.toggle
    LDA highlight_address
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA highlight_address+1
    STA screen_ptr+1
    JMP invert_menu_row
}

; The palette line highlighted.
.highlight_address
    EQUB &00, &00

; The selection, kept while Animate runs.
.animate_sprite
    EQUB &00

; How long Animate shows each frame, in vsyncs.
FRAME_VSYNCS = 6

; OptionsA Animate (CTRL-A): preview how the game animates a picture, a
; frame every six vsyncs, in the animation window and the editing grid,
; until Space or Escape (f0-f3 count as Escape). The monster (slots &0E and
; &0F) alternates its two pictures; the player facing left or right (&20,
; &21) alternates with itself upside down; facing up or down, &22 alternates
; with &23 upside down, and &23 with &22 upside down. Nothing happens for
; other sprites. The frames are copied to frame_a and frame_b first, so
; turning them over leaves the set alone.
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_animate
{
    LDA #&FF
    STA by_slot                     ; sprite numbers are slots from here
    LDA sprite
    STA animate_sprite
    TAX
    AND #&10                        ; small sprites don't animate...
    BNE none
    TXA
    JSR slot_index
    TAX
    LDA slot_of_position, X
    CMP #SLOT_ALTERNATE             ; ...nor do slots &24-&28
    BCS none
    CMP #SLOT_PLAYER
    BCS player
    CMP #SLOT_MONSTER
    BEQ flames
    CMP #SLOT_MONSTER + 1
    BEQ flames
.none
    RTS
.flames
    PHA
    AND #&FE                        ; copy both pictures, from the first
    BNE copy_pair                   ; always
.player
    PHA
.copy_pair
    CMP #SLOT_PLAYER + 2            ; up and down copy both, from the first;
    BCC copy_from                   ; left and right copy themselves (and the next)
    AND #&FE
.copy_from
    JSR sprite_address
    LDY #&00
.copy
    LDA (data_ptr), Y               ; two sprites' worth: this slot and the next
    STA frame_a, Y
    DEY
    BNE copy
    LDA #WINDOW_PICK
    LDX #LO(text_animation)
    LDY #HI(text_animation)
    JSR open_window
    LDA sprite
    JSR slot_index
    TAX
    LDA slot_of_position, X
    CMP #&10                        ; the monster's slots are below, the player's above
    BCS player_frames
    LDA #monster_frames - animation_frames
    BNE chosen                      ; always
.player_frames
    AND #&03                        ; the player's: a pair of entries for each slot
    ASL A
.chosen
    STA frame_index
.show
    TAX
    LDA #FRAME_VSYNCS
    STA frame_delay
    LDA animation_frames, X
    STA sprite
    BPL draw                        ; UPSIDE_DOWN: turn the buffer over first
    JSR flip_vertically
    LDA #FRAME_VSYNCS
    STA frame_delay
.draw
    LDA sprite
    AND #&7F
    STA sprite
    JSR draw_grid
    LDA sprite
    JSR draw_sheet_sprite
.wait
    JSR menu_keys_escape
    BIT MOS_ESCAPE_FLAG
    BMI stop
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_SPACE)
    JSR key_pressed
    BMI stop
    LDA #OSBYTE_WAIT_VSYNC
    JSR OSBYTE
    DEC frame_delay
    BNE wait
    LDA frame_index
    TAX
    EOR #&01
    STA frame_index
    PHA
    LDA animation_frames, X         ; back the right way up before it's shown again
    BPL other_frame
    JSR flip_vertically
.other_frame
    PLA
    JMP show
.stop
    PLA                             ; drop the slot pushed at the start
    LDX animate_sprite
    STX sprite
    LDA #OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDA #WINDOW_PICK                ; by_slot bit 7 clear: sheet positions again
    STA by_slot
    JSR close_window
    JMP redraw_grid                 ; carry clear from close_window: no undo copy
}

; Turn a sheet position into an index into slot_of_position: positions
; &20-&28 follow &00-&0F. It borrows repeat_key's RTS.
; In:  A = a large sprite's position
; Out: A = the index
; Clobbers: nothing else
.slot_index
{
    CMP #FIRST_SMALL
    BCC repeat_key.done
    CMP #AFTER_SMALL
    BCC repeat_key.done
    SBC #AFTER_SMALL - FIRST_SMALL
    RTS
}

; Animate's place in animation_frames, and its countdown to the next
; frame.
.frame_index
    EQUB &00

.frame_delay
    EQUB &00

; Animate's frames, a pair for each animated slot: SPRITE_FRAME_A or _B,
; with UPSIDE_DOWN to show it turned over.
.animation_frames
    EQUB SPRITE_FRAME_A, SPRITE_FRAME_A + UPSIDE_DOWN    ; &20, the player facing left
    EQUB SPRITE_FRAME_A, SPRITE_FRAME_A + UPSIDE_DOWN    ; &21, facing right
    EQUB SPRITE_FRAME_A, SPRITE_FRAME_B + UPSIDE_DOWN    ; &22, facing up
    EQUB SPRITE_FRAME_B, SPRITE_FRAME_A + UPSIDE_DOWN    ; &23, facing down
.monster_frames
    EQUB SPRITE_FRAME_B, SPRITE_FRAME_A                  ; &0E and &0F, the monster

; The selection's auto-repeat, in passes of the main loop: a press moves it
; at once, then after REPEAT_DELAY passes, then every REPEAT_RATE.
REPEAT_DELAY = 20
REPEAT_RATE  = 5

; Read one of the cursor keys that move the selection, with auto-repeat.
; In:  X = INKEY_TEST() of the key
; Out: Y = &FF (N set) to move now, else 0
; Clobbers: A, X
.repeat_key
{
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL not_now
    STX key_held                    ; a key is held this pass
    LDY repeat_count                ; 0 means it's time to repeat
    BEQ move
    STY key_repeating
    CPY #REPEAT_DELAY               ; a fresh press
    BEQ move
.not_now
    LDY #&00
.done
    RTS
.move
    LDY #&FF
    RTS
}

; The selection's auto-repeat countdown: REPEAT_DELAY while no key is held.
.repeat_count
    EQUB &00

; The main loop's pace: a pass takes at least this long.
PASS_CENTISECONDS = 2

; Move the selection with the cursor keys, and pace the main loop: unless
; CTRL is held, it waits until PASS_CENTISECONDS have passed since the
; last call. If the selection moves, the old sprite is drawn again without
; its box, and the new one boxed and drawn in the editing grid (with an
; undo copy).
; In:  A = 0 from the main loop; non-zero while picking a second sprite, when
;      f0-f3 also raise an Escape
; Out: N set if nothing moved (or CTRL is held: then nothing is done)
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, and as draw_grid
.select_sprite
{
    STA select_mode
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_CTRL)
    JSR key_pressed
    BMI repeat_key.done             ; CTRL held: return N set (repeat_key's RTS)
    LDA sprite
    STA old_sprite
    LDA #&00
    STA key_held
    STA key_repeating
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_RIGHT)
    JSR repeat_key
    BPL left
    JSR sheet_column                ; the last column of the row?
    CMP last_column
    BEQ left
    INC sprite
    LDA sprite
    CMP #FIRST_SMALL
    BNE wrap_right
    LDA #AFTER_SMALL                ; after &0F comes &20
.wrap_right
    STA sprite
.left
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_LEFT)
    JSR repeat_key
    BPL left_done
    JSR sheet_column
    CMP #&00
    BEQ left_done
    DEC sprite
    LDA sprite
    CMP #LAST_SMALL
    BNE wrap_left
    LDA #FIRST_SMALL - 1            ; before &20 comes &0F
.wrap_left
    STA sprite
.left_done
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_DOWN)
    JSR repeat_key
    BPL down_done
    JSR sheet_row
    CPX #LARGE_ROWS + SMALL_ROWS - 1    ; the bottom row of small sprites
    BEQ down_done
    LDA sprite
    CMP #LAST_SPRITE                ; no small sprite below the last large one
    BEQ down_done
    CMP #&0F                        ; &0F, at the start of row 3, has &24 below it...
    BNE down_not_0f
    LDA #&24
    BNE store_down                  ; always
.down_not_0f
    CMP #&0A                        ; ...and &0A has &0F
    BNE step_down
    LDA #&0F
    BNE store_down                  ; always
.step_down
    CLC
    ADC row_down_step, X
.store_down
    STA sprite
.down_done
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_UP)
    JSR repeat_key
    BPL up_done
    JSR sheet_row
    CPX #&00
    BEQ up_done
    LDA sprite
    CMP #&0F                        ; the same two, upwards
    BNE up_not_0f
    LDA #&0A
    BNE store_up                    ; always
.up_not_0f
    CMP #&24
    BNE step_up
    LDA #&0F
    BNE store_up                    ; always
.step_up
    SEC
    LDA sprite
    SBC row_down_step-1, X          ; the row above's step (X is 1 or more)
.store_up
    STA sprite

    ; The auto-repeat: back to REPEAT_DELAY while no key is held, else
    ; count down, and after a repeat start again from REPEAT_RATE.
.up_done
    LDA repeat_count
    BNE delay
    LDA #REPEAT_RATE - 1
    STA repeat_count
.delay
    LDX #REPEAT_DELAY
    LDA key_held
    BEQ store_delay
    LDX repeat_count
    LDA key_repeating
    BEQ store_delay
    DEX
.store_delay
    STX repeat_count
    LDA select_mode
    BEQ wait
    JSR menu_keys_escape

    ; Wait until the interval timer reaches PASS_CENTISECONDS.
.wait
    LDA #OSWORD_READ_INTERVAL_TIMER
    JSR reset_timer.osword
    LDX #&04                        ; any of the top four bytes set is long enough
    LDA #&00
.check
    ORA timer_value, X
    DEX
    BNE check
    CMP #&00
    BNE waited
    LDA timer_value
    CMP #PASS_CENTISECONDS
    BCC wait
.waited
    LDA #&00
    STA timer_value
    JSR reset_timer
    LDA old_sprite                  ; moved?
    CMP sprite
    BEQ sheet_row.return_negative
    JSR draw_sheet_sprite           ; the old sprite, without its box
    LDA sprite
    JSR show_selection

    ; A small sprite's grid is 8x16: keep the cursor in it.
    LDA sprite_width
    CMP #SMALL_WIDTH
    BNE changed
    LDX cursor_x
    CPX #SMALL_SPRITE_WIDTH
    BCC clamp_y
    LDX #SMALL_SPRITE_WIDTH - 1
    STX cursor_x
.clamp_y
    LDY cursor_y
    CPY #SMALL_SPRITE_HEIGHT
    BCC changed
    LDY #SMALL_SPRITE_HEIGHT - 1
    STY cursor_y
.changed
    LDA sprite                      ; and take an undo copy
    ORA #&80
    JSR draw_grid
    LDA #&00
    RTS
}

; How far down a step moves the selection from each row of the sheet (but
; the last), large rows 0-4 and then small rows 0-2. Up uses the row
; above's. (Some moves are special cases in select_sprite.)
.row_down_step
    EQUB 5, 5, &15, 5               ; large rows: &0B-&0E go to &20-&23
    EQUB LO(-&14)                   ; from the bottom large row to the small sprites
    EQUB 4, 4, 4                    ; small rows

; Set the interval timer to zero, the start of the main loop's pacing. Also
; entered at osword, with A = an OSWORD number, to read or write the timer
; from timer_value.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y
.reset_timer
{
    LDX #&04
    LDA #&00
.clear
    STA timer_value, X
    DEX
    BPL clear
    LDA #OSWORD_WRITE_INTERVAL_TIMER
.osword
    LDX #LO(timer_value)
    LDY #HI(timer_value)
    JMP OSWORD
}

; Non-zero when repeat_key found a cursor key held this pass, counting down
; to its next repeat.
.key_repeating
    EQUB &00

; The selected sprite's row in the sheet. Its return_negative (LDA #&80 :
; RTS) is also select_sprite's exit when nothing moved.
; In:  sprite
; Out: X = row (0-4 for the large sprites, 5-8 for the small ones),
;      last_column = 4; A = its column for a large sprite, &80 for a small
; Clobbers: nothing else
.sheet_row
{
    LDX #LARGE_COLUMNS - 1
    STX last_column
    LDA sprite
    CMP #FIRST_SMALL
    BCC sheet_column.large
    CMP #AFTER_SMALL
    BCS high
    LSR A
    LSR A
    AND #&03
    CLC
    ADC #LARGE_ROWS
    TAX
.return_negative
    LDA #&80
    RTS
.high
    SBC #AFTER_SMALL - FIRST_SMALL  ; positions &20-&28 follow &00-&0F
    BCS sheet_column.large          ; always
}

; The selected sprite's column in the sheet.
; In:  sprite
; Out: A = column, last_column = the last in its row (4 large, 3 small)
; Clobbers: X
.sheet_column
{
    LDA #LARGE_COLUMNS - 1
    STA last_column
    LDA sprite
    CMP #FIRST_SMALL
    BCC large
    CMP #AFTER_SMALL
    BCS high
    AND #&03
    LDX #SMALL_COLUMNS - 1
    STX last_column
    RTS
.high
    SBC #AFTER_SMALL - FIRST_SMALL  ; positions &20-&28 follow &00-&0F
.large
    JMP divide_by_5
}

; Where a pixel of the editing grid is on the screen.
; In:  X = pixel x, Y = pixel y
; Out: screen_ptr = its top line (four lines tall, one byte wide)
; Clobbers: A, Y
.grid_address
{
    TYA
    PHA
    AND #&FE                        ; grid_row_address has a word for each pair of rows
    TAY
    TXA
    ASL A                           ; a cell for each pixel
    ASL A
    ASL A
    CLC
    ADC grid_row_address, Y
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA grid_row_address+1, Y
    ADC #&00
    STA screen_ptr+1
    PLA
    LSR A                           ; odd rows are the bottom half of the character row
    BCC done
    LDA screen_ptr
    ORA #&04
    STA screen_ptr
.done
    RTS
}

; Draw or rub out the pixel cursor: dots in the corners of a grid pixel,
; exclusive-ORed on.
; In:  X = pixel x, Y = pixel y
; Clobbers: A, Y, screen_ptr
.toggle_cursor
{
    JSR grid_address
    LDY #&03
.loop
    LDA cursor_shape, Y
    EOR (screen_ptr), Y
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL loop
    RTS
}

; The pixel cursor's four lines: colour 2 in the outer pixels, top and bottom
; (exclusive-ORed, so it shows on any colour).
.cursor_shape
    EQUB mode5_byte("2..2"), 0, 0, mode5_byte("2..2")

; Ask for the name of a file to save to. If it exists it must be a graphics
; set or an IO file (setting io_file), and the user is asked whether to
; replace it: Cancel abandons the command. On tape nothing is checked.
; Out: input_buffer = the name; osfile_block filled (file_info); io_file
;      bit 7 set for an IO file
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, and as open_window
.ask_save_name
{
    LDA #WINDOW_INPUT
    LDX #LO(text_save_name)
    LDY #HI(text_save_name)
    JSR open_window
    JSR input_line
    LDA #WINDOW_INPUT
    JSR close_window
    JSR file_info
    BCS done
    CMP #OSFILE_TYPE_FILE           ; it exists
    BNE new
    JMP file_exists
.new
    LDA #&00                        ; a new file is a graphics set
    STA io_file
.done
    RTS
}

; check_filing_system's X: each file command's place in the Environment
; menu. The sprite commands need random access, which tape hasn't.
FILE_LOAD_SPRITE = 0
FILE_SAVE_SPRITE = 1
FILE_LOAD_FILE   = 2
FILE_SAVE_FILE   = 3

; Environment Save File (CTRL-f7): save the graphics set, &4000-&4F33, or
; write its three pieces into an IO file in place.
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_save_file
{
    LDX #FILE_SAVE_FILE
    JSR check_filing_system
    JSR ask_save_name
    BIT io_file
    BMI io
    LDY #&0F                        ; clear the block after the name
    LDA #&00
.clear
    STA osfile_load, Y
    DEY
    BPL clear
    LDA #HI(graphics)               ; load and start address &4000...
    STA osfile_load+1
    STA osfile_start+1
    CLC
    ADC #HI(SET_SIZE)               ; ...end &4F34
    STA osfile_end+1
    LDA #LO(graphics_end)
    STA osfile_end
    LDA #OSFILE_SAVE
    JSR osfile_graphics
.done
    RTS

    ; An IO file: write the three pieces in.
.io
    JSR open_file.update
    LDA #&00
.segment
    PHA
    TAX
    JSR set_segment
    JSR read_block.write
    PLA
    CLC
    ADC #IO_SEGMENT
    CMP #io_segments_end - io_segments
    BCC segment
    JSR close_files
    JMP done
}
ASSERT LO(graphics) = 0 AND HI(graphics) + HI(SET_SIZE) = HI(graphics_end)

; Environment Save Sprite (CTRL-f9): write the selected sprite (and an
; object's name) into its place in an existing graphics set or IO file,
; then redraw everything (start.redraw, so the selection goes back to
; position 0).
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_save_sprite
{
    LDX #FILE_SAVE_SPRITE
    JSR check_filing_system
    JSR ask_save_name
    JSR open_file.update
    LDA sprite
    JSR sprite_address
    JSR sprite_file_offset
    JSR sprite_last_byte
    INY
    STY gbpb_count
    LDA data_ptr
    STA gbpb_address
    LDA data_ptr+1
    STA gbpb_address+1
    JSR read_block.write
    LDA sprite_width
    CMP #SMALL_WIDTH
    BNE not_small
    JSR write_name
.not_small
    JSR close_files
    JMP start.redraw
}

; The file to save to exists: check what it is, and ask whether to replace
; it. Cancel returns from the command that asked (ask_save_name's caller).
; Out: as ask_save_name
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, and as menu
.file_exists
{
    JSR ask_load_name.found
    LDX #LO(text_exists)
    LDY #HI(text_exists)
    LDA #WINDOW_QUESTION
    JSR menu
    CMP #2                          ; Replace
    BNE cancel
    JMP ask_save_name.done
.cancel
    PLA                             ; drop ask_save_name's return
    PLA
    JMP cmd_save_file.done
}

; Call the filing system control vector.
; In:  A, X and Y for FSCV
; Clobbers: as the filing system does
.fscv
{
    JMP (FSCV)
}

; Point gbpb_block's file pointer at the sprite's place in the file.
; In:  data_ptr = the sprite's bytes; io_file
; Clobbers: A
.sprite_file_offset
{
    LDA data_ptr
    SEC
    SBC #LO(graphics)
    STA gbpb_pointer
    LDA data_ptr+1
    SBC #HI(graphics)
    STA gbpb_pointer+1
    BIT io_file
    BMI io
    RTS
.io
    LDA gbpb_pointer+1
    CMP #HI(slot_28 - graphics)     ; the slot IO keeps apart
    BNE in_io_graphics              ; the rest are among IO's graphics
    LDA #HI(IO_SLOT_28_OFFSET)      ; (the low byte is the same)
    STA gbpb_pointer+1
    RTS
.in_io_graphics
    LDA gbpb_pointer
    CLC
    ADC #LO(IO_GRAPHICS_OFFSET)
    STA gbpb_pointer
    LDA gbpb_pointer+1
    ADC #HI(IO_GRAPHICS_OFFSET)
    STA gbpb_pointer+1
    RTS
}

; Point gbpb_block's file pointer at the object's name in the file.
; In:  sprite = the object; io_file
; Out: Y = the name's offset in object_names
; Clobbers: A, X
.name_file_offset
{
    JSR name_offset
    LDX #&00
    BIT io_file
    BMI io
    LDX #HI(object_names - graphics)
.io
    TYA
    CLC
    ADC #LO(IO_NAMES_OFFSET)        ; the same low byte as SET_NAMES
    BCC store
    INX
.store
    STA gbpb_pointer
    STX gbpb_pointer+1
    RTS
}

; Unused: read a file's pointer into &8B-&8E (A isn't set here, though
; OSARGS needs it 0 for that).
.unused_read_ptr
{
    LDY gbpb_block
    LDX #&8B
    JMP OSARGS
}

; Clear gbpb_block, and refuse a command the filing system can't do.
; In:  X = the command, FILE_LOAD_SPRITE to FILE_SAVE_FILE
; Out: doesn't return if refused: it shows the error (show_error)
; Clobbers: A, Y
.check_filing_system
{
    LDY #&0F                        ; all sixteen bytes
    LDA #&00
.clear
    STA gbpb_block, Y
    DEY
    BPL clear
    BIT disc_fs
    BPL tape
.done
    RTS
.tape
    CPX #FILE_LOAD_FILE             ; whole files will do
    BCS done
    LDX #LO(text_not_available)
    LDY #HI(text_not_available)
    JMP show_error
}

; Unused: an error saying "Not implemented".
.unused_not_implemented
{
    LDX #LO(text)
    LDY #HI(text)
    JMP show_error
.text
    EQUB PLAIN, CR
    EQUS "Not implemented", CR
    EQUB TEXT_END
}

; Open the file named by osfile_block for reading; at update, for reading
; and writing. A missing file is "Bad File".
; In:  osfile_block = the filename's address
; Out: gbpb_block's handle
; Clobbers: A, X, Y
.open_file
{
    LDA #OSFIND_OPEN_INPUT
    BITABS                          ; a BIT opcode: skips the LDA below
.update
    LDA #OSFIND_OPEN_UPDATE
    LDX osfile_block
    LDY osfile_block+1
    JSR OSFIND
    TAX
    BNE opened
    JMP bad_file
.opened
    STX gbpb_block
    RTS
}

; Environment Load Sprite (CTRL-f8): read the selected sprite (and an
; object's name) from its place in a graphics set or IO file, then redraw
; everything (start.redraw, so the selection goes back to position 0).
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_load_sprite
{
    LDX #FILE_LOAD_SPRITE
    JSR check_filing_system
    JSR ask_load_name
    JSR open_file
    LDA sprite
    JSR sprite_address
    JSR sprite_file_offset
    JSR sprite_last_byte
    INY
    STY gbpb_count
    LDA data_ptr
    STA gbpb_address
    LDA data_ptr+1
    STA gbpb_address+1
    JSR read_block
    LDA sprite_width
    CMP #SMALL_WIDTH
    BNE not_small
    JSR read_name
.not_small
    JSR close_files
    JMP start.redraw
}

; Write the selected object's name to the file, unless it's the exit.
; In:  sprite, gbpb_block's handle
; Clobbers: A, X, Y
.write_name
{
    JSR name_transfer
    BCC read_block.write
    RTS
}

; Point gbpb_block at the selected object's name, in memory and in the file.
; In:  sprite
; Out: carry set (and nothing done) for the exit, which has no name
; Clobbers: A, X, Y
.name_transfer
{
    LDA sprite
    CMP #SLOT_EXIT
    BNE named
    RTS
.named
    JSR name_file_offset
    LDA #OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH
    STA gbpb_count
    JSR name_offset
    TYA
    CLC
    ADC #LO(object_names)
    STA gbpb_address
    LDA #HI(object_names)
    ADC #&00
    STA gbpb_address+1
    CLC
.done
    RTS
}

; Read the selected object's name from the file, unless it's the exit.
; In:  sprite, gbpb_block's handle
; Clobbers: A, X, Y
.read_name
{
    JSR name_transfer
    BCS name_transfer.done
}

; Read the block gbpb_block describes from the file; at write, write it.
; In:  gbpb_block: handle, address, count and pointer
; Clobbers: A, X, Y
.read_block
{
    LDA #OSGBPB_READ_AT
    BITABS                          ; a BIT opcode: skips the LDA below
.write
    LDA #OSGBPB_WRITE_AT
    LDX #LO(gbpb_block)
    LDY #HI(gbpb_block)
    JMP OSGBPB
}

; Close all open files.
; Clobbers: A, Y
.close_files
{
    LDA #OSFIND_CLOSE
    TAY                             ; all of them
    JMP OSFIND
}

; Ask for the name of a file to load from: it must exist ("No Such File")
; and, on disc, be a graphics set (loading at &40xx, &Fxx long) or an IO
; file (&33xx long); anything else is "Bad File". Also entered at found, to
; check what an existing file is.
; Out: osfile_block filled (file_info); io_file bit 7 set for an IO file
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, and as open_window
.ask_load_name
{
    LDA #WINDOW_INPUT
    LDX #LO(text_load_name)
    LDY #HI(text_load_name)
    JSR open_window
    JSR input_line
    LDA #WINDOW_INPUT
    JSR close_window
    JSR file_info
    BCS found
    CMP #OSFILE_TYPE_FILE           ; not a file: "No Such File"
    BNE cmd_load_file.no_file
.found
    LDA #&00
    STA io_file
    BIT disc_fs
    BMI disc
    RTS
.disc
    LDA osfile_load+1
    CMP #HI(graphics)
    BNE check_io_file
    LDA osfile_start+1              ; the length's high byte
    CMP #HI(SET_SIZE)
    BNE check_io_file
    RTS
}

; Bit 7 set when the file being loaded or saved is IO, not a graphics set.
; (It sits between ask_load_name and its end, check_io_file.)
.io_file
    EQUB &00

; ask_load_name's end: a file that isn't a graphics set must be IO, or it's
; "Bad File".
; Out: as ask_load_name (or "Bad File", not returning)
; Clobbers: A
.check_io_file
{
    LDA osfile_start+1              ; the length's high byte
    CMP #HI(IO_LENGTH)
    BEQ io
    JMP bad_file
.io
    LDA #&FF
    STA io_file
    RTS
}

; Environment Load File (CTRL-f6): load a graphics set, or the three pieces
; of one from an IO file, then redraw everything (start.redraw).
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_load_file
{
    LDX #FILE_LOAD_FILE
    JSR check_filing_system
    JSR ask_load_name
    BIT io_file
    BMI load_io
    LDA #OSFILE_LOAD
    JSR osfile_graphics
    JMP start.redraw
.no_file
    LDX #LO(text_no_such_file)
    LDY #HI(text_no_such_file)
    JMP show_error
}

; Point gbpb_block at one of the pieces of an IO file.
; In:  X = the piece's entry's offset in io_segments: 0, IO_SEGMENT or
;      2 * IO_SEGMENT
; Clobbers: A
.set_segment
{
    LDA io_segments, X
    STA gbpb_address
    LDA io_segments+1, X
    STA gbpb_address+1
    LDA io_segments+2, X
    STA gbpb_pointer
    LDA io_segments+3, X
    STA gbpb_pointer+1
    LDA io_segments+4, X
    STA gbpb_count
    LDA io_segments+5, X
    STA gbpb_count+1
    RTS
}

; Load the graphics set's three pieces from an IO file, then redraw
; everything (start.redraw).
; Clobbers: everything
.load_io
{
    JSR open_file
    LDA #&00                        ; the first entry
.segment
    PHA
    TAX
    JSR set_segment
    JSR read_block
    PLA
    CLC
    ADC #IO_SEGMENT
    CMP #io_segments_end - io_segments
    BCC segment
    JSR close_files
    JMP start.redraw
}

; Where the graphics set is in an IO file (as MISSION builds it): each piece's
; address in the set, its offset in the file and its length.
IO_SEGMENT = 6                  ; bytes in each entry
.io_segments
    EQUW slot_28, IO_SLOT_28_OFFSET, LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE
    EQUW object_names, IO_NAMES_OFFSET, OBJECT_KINDS * OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH
    EQUW graphics, IO_GRAPHICS_OFFSET, IO_GRAPHICS_SIZE         ; slots &00-&27
.io_segments_end

; Read the catalogue entry of the file named in input_buffer
; (OSFILE_READ_INFO). On tape it does nothing, returning through
; cmd_obj_name's RTS.
; In:  input_buffer = the name
; Out: carry set if the filing system isn't a disc one (nothing read); else
;      carry clear, A = the object type (OSFILE_TYPE_FILE for a file),
;      osfile_block filled
; Clobbers: X, Y
.file_info
{
    LDX #LO(input_buffer)
    STX osfile_block
    LDY #HI(input_buffer)
    STY osfile_block+1
    SEC
    BIT disc_fs
    BPL cmd_obj_name.done
    LDA #OSFILE_READ_INFO
}

; OSFILE on the graphics set at &4000.
; In:  A = OSFILE_SAVE, OSFILE_LOAD or OSFILE_READ_INFO; osfile_block's name
;      and, to save, its start and end
; Out: carry clear; A as OSFILE leaves it (for OSFILE_READ_INFO, the
;      object type)
; Clobbers: X, Y
.osfile_graphics
{
    LDX #&00
    STX osfile_exec                 ; the exec address's low byte 0: load at osfile_load
    LDX #LO(graphics)
    STX osfile_load
    LDX #HI(graphics)
    STX osfile_load+1
    BIT disc_fs
    BMI call
    PHA
    LDA #VDU_CLS                    ; on tape, clear the screen for the filing system's messages
    JSR OSWRCH
    PLA
.call
    LDX #LO(osfile_block)
    LDY #HI(osfile_block)
    JSR OSFILE
    CLC
    RTS
}

; The "Bad File" error.
; Out: doesn't return
.bad_file
{
    LDX #LO(text_bad_file)
    LDY #HI(text_bad_file)
    JMP show_error
}

; OptionsA Obj name (CTRL-N): rename the selected object. Nothing happens for
; the exit or a large sprite.
; In:  sprite
; Clobbers: everything
.cmd_obj_name
{
    LDA sprite_width
    CMP #SMALL_WIDTH
    BEQ small
.done
    RTS
.small
    LDA sprite
    CMP #SLOT_EXIT
    BEQ done
    LDA #WINDOW_INPUT
    LDX #LO(text_object_name)
    LDY #HI(text_object_name)
    JSR open_window
    JSR input_line
    JSR name_offset
    LDX #&00
.copy
    LDA input_buffer, X
    STA object_names, Y
    INY
    INX
    CPX #OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH
    BCC copy
    LDA #WINDOW_INPUT
    JSR close_window
    LDA sprite
    JMP show_selection
}

; The line input_line edits: twelve characters, padded with spaces, and a
; CR after the sixteen bytes it clears (which a filename stops at).
.input_buffer
    SKIP OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH
    EQUB CR, CR, CR, CR, CR

; Read a line of up to input_limit characters into input_buffer, echoing
; it at screen_ptr. Delete rubs out a character, CTRL-U the lot; Return
; ends it; Escape or a function key abandons the command
; (pick_second_sprite.abandon_command).
; In:  screen_ptr = where to echo it (open_window leaves it after the text)
; Out: input_buffer, padded with spaces; Y = its length
; Clobbers: A, X, screen_ptr, aux_ptr
.input_line
{
    LDY #OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH         ; the longest a name can be, file or object
    STY input_limit
    LDY #&00
    LDA #OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS       ; empty the keyboard buffer
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDY #&0F                        ; sixteen bytes, up to the last CR
    LDA #' '
.blank
    STA input_buffer, Y
    DEY
    BPL blank
    INY
.read
    LDA #' '                 ; a space after the line: what a rub-out leaves
    STA input_buffer, Y
    JSR OSRDCH
    BCC got_key
.abandon
    JMP pick_second_sprite.abandon_command
.got_key
    CMP #KEYCODE_F0
    BCS abandon
    CMP #CR
    BNE edit
    RTS
.edit
    AND #&7F                        ; the cursor keys' codes become control codes, ignored
    CMP #ctrl('U')
    BNE not_wipe
    TYA
    TAX
    BNE rub_out
    BEQ read
.not_wipe
    CMP #DEL
    BNE add
    CPY #&00
    BEQ read
    LDX #&01
.rub_out
    LDA screen_ptr
    SEC
    SBC #CELL
    STA screen_ptr
    BCS erase
    DEC screen_ptr+1
.erase
    CLC                             ; exclusive-OR it off again
    LDA input_buffer-1, Y
    JSR print_char
    DEY
    DEX
    BNE rub_out
    JMP read
.add
    CMP #' '
    BCC read
    CPY input_limit
    BCS read
    STA input_buffer, Y
    INY
    JSR print_char_advance          ; carry clear: exclusive-OR it on
    JMP read
}

; The longest line input_line takes (always OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH).
.input_limit
    EQUB &00

; The pixel cursor's key repeat, in trips round key_delay's loop: it starts
; at CURSOR_DELAY, and each move shortens it by CURSOR_DELAY_STEP down to
; CURSOR_DELAY_MIN.
CURSOR_DELAY      = &B9
CURSOR_DELAY_STEP = 10
CURSOR_DELAY_MIN  = 10

; Paint: move the pixel cursor with Z X : /, faster as a key is held;
; choose the colour with 0-4; plot with Return or clear with Delete. Does
; nothing while CTRL is held, for the shortcuts. Plotting draws the sprite
; again on the sheet, which rubs out its selection box until it moves.
; In:  sprite, cursor_x, cursor_y, colour
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, and as draw_sheet_sprite
.edit_pixels
{
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_CTRL)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL move
    RTS
.move
    LDX cursor_x
    LDY cursor_y
    STX old_cursor_x
    STY old_cursor_y
    LDA sprite_width                ; count_x = width*4 - 1, the last pixel across
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA count_x
    ASL A                           ; count_y = width*8 - 1, the last row
    STA count_y
    DEC count_x
    DEC count_y
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_X)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL not_right
    LDX cursor_x
    CPX count_x
    BCS not_right
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_X)
    JSR key_delay
    INC cursor_x
.not_right
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_Z)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL not_left
    LDX cursor_x
    BEQ not_left
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_Z)
    JSR key_delay
    DEC cursor_x
.not_left
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_SLASH)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL not_down
    LDY cursor_y
    CPY count_y
    BCS not_down
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_SLASH)
    JSR key_delay
    INC cursor_y
.not_down
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_COLON)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL not_up
    LDY cursor_y
    BEQ not_up
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_COLON)
    JSR key_delay
    DEC cursor_y
.not_up
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_1)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL not_1
    LDA #&01
    STA colour
    JSR show_colour
.not_1
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_2)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL not_2
    LDA #&02
    STA colour
    JSR show_colour
.not_2
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_3)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL not_3
    LDA #&03
    STA colour
    JSR show_colour
.not_3
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_4)
    JSR key_pressed
    BMI colour_0
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_0)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL not_0

    ; 4 and 0 both give colour 0.
.colour_0
    LDA #&00
    STA colour
    JSR show_colour

    ; If the cursor moved, shorten the repeat delay and redraw the cursor;
    ; if not, put the delay back to CURSOR_DELAY.
.not_0
    LDA old_cursor_x
    EOR cursor_x
    BNE moved
    EOR cursor_y
    EOR old_cursor_y
    BEQ still
.moved
    LDA repeat_delay
    SEC
    SBC #CURSOR_DELAY_STEP
    CMP #CURSOR_DELAY_MIN
    BCS delay_ok
    LDA #CURSOR_DELAY_MIN
.delay_ok
    STA repeat_delay
    LDX cursor_x
    LDY cursor_y
    JSR toggle_cursor               ; draw it at the new place...
    LDX old_cursor_x
    LDY old_cursor_y
    JSR toggle_cursor               ; ...and rub it out at the old
    JMP plot_keys
.still
    LDA #CURSOR_DELAY
    STA repeat_delay
.plot_keys
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_DELETE)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL not_delete
    LDA colour
    PHA
    INX                             ; X = &FF + 1: colour 0
    STX colour
    JSR plot
    PLA
    STA colour
    RTS
.not_delete
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_RETURN)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL done

    ; Plot: fill the grid pixel (keeping the cursor on it), set the pixel in
    ; the sprite, and show the sprite in the sheet.
.plot
    LDX cursor_x
    LDY cursor_y
    JSR grid_address
    LDY #&03
    LDX colour
.block
    LDA colour_byte, X
    EOR cursor_shape, Y
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL block
    LDA sprite
    LDX cursor_x
    LDY cursor_y
    JSR plot_pixel
    LDA sprite
    BNE not_background
    JSR repeat_background           ; position 0 repeats its 4x8 cell
.not_background
    LDA sprite
    JSR draw_sheet_sprite
.done
    RTS
}

; Sheet position 0 shows slot 0, the floor; the game fills the floor round an
; object's icon from that picture's first cell alone, so the designer keeps
; it one 4x8 pixel cell repeated. Copy the cell just changed through the
; whole sprite, and draw the grid again.
; In:  data_ptr = the byte plot_pixel changed
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, and as redraw_grid
.repeat_background
{
    LDA data_ptr
    AND #&F8                        ; the start of its cell
    STA data_ptr
    LDY #&07
.read
    LDA (data_ptr), Y
    STA background_tile, Y
    DEY
    BPL read
    LDY #LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE - 1
    LDX #&07
.fill
    LDA background_tile, X
    STA graphics + SET_LARGE, Y     ; slot 0
    DEX
    TXA
    AND #&07
    TAX
    DEY
    BPL fill
    CLC
    JMP redraw_grid
}

; The background tile's eight bytes: the cell repeat_background repeats.
.background_tile
    EQUB &00, &00, &00, &00, &00, &00, &00, &00

; The pixel cursor's key repeat: wait while the key is held, for up to
; repeat_delay polls of it with a 256-trip spin between them.
; In:  X = INKEY_TEST() of the key
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, temp, count_x
.key_delay
{
    STX temp
    LDA repeat_delay
    STA count_x
.poll
    LDX temp
    JSR key_pressed
    BMI held
    RTS
.held
    LDX #&00
.spin
    DEX
    BNE spin
    DEC count_x
    BNE poll
    RTS
}

; The bits of each of the four pixels in a MODE 5 byte.
.pixel_mask
    EQUB mode5_byte("3..."), mode5_byte(".3.."), mode5_byte("..3."), mode5_byte("...3")

; Find a pixel of a sprite.
; In:  A = sprite, X = pixel x, Y = pixel y
; Out: data_ptr = its byte, A = mask = its bits
; Clobbers: X, Y, pixel_x, pixel_y, sprite_width
.pixel_address
{
    STX pixel_x
    STY pixel_y
    JSR sprite_address
    LDA sprite_width
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    TAY                             ; a column's bytes
    LDA pixel_x
    LSR A
    LSR A
    TAX
.column
    DEX                             ; a column of bytes for each four pixels across
    BMI got_column
    TYA
    CLC
    ADC data_ptr
    STA data_ptr
    BCC column                      ; always: no sprite crosses a page
.got_column
    LDA pixel_y                     ; a column starts at a multiple of its size,
    ORA data_ptr                    ; so ORing in the row adds it
    STA data_ptr
    LDA pixel_x
    AND #&03
    TAX
    LDA pixel_mask, X
    STA mask
    RTS
}

; Set a pixel of a sprite to colour.
; In:  A = sprite, X = pixel x, Y = pixel y, colour
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, data_ptr, temp, mask, pixel_x, pixel_y, sprite_width
.plot_pixel
{
    JSR pixel_address
    EOR #&FF
    LDY #&00
    AND (data_ptr), Y
    STA temp
    LDX colour
    LDA colour_byte, X
    AND mask
    ORA temp
    STA (data_ptr), Y
    RTS
}

; Read a pixel of a sprite.
; In:  A = sprite, X = pixel x, Y = pixel y
; Out: A = its colour, 0-3
; Clobbers: X, Y, data_ptr, mask, pixel_x, pixel_y, sprite_width
.read_pixel
{
    JSR pixel_address
    LDY #&00
    AND (data_ptr), Y

    ; Shift the pixel's two bits down to make its colour.
.find_bit
    LSR mask
    BCS got_bit
    LSR A
    BCC find_bit
.got_bit
    LSR A
    PHP
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    PLP
    ROL A
    RTS
}

; Each menu's text, and the function key that opens it, by window number.
.menu_text
    EQUW text_options_a, text_options_b, text_environment, text_credits
.menu_keys
    EQUB INKEY_TEST({KEY_F0, KEY_F1, KEY_F2, KEY_F3})

; Read a command: a CTRL shortcut, or a choice from the menu whose function
; key is pressed.
; Out: A = the command's number in command_table (menu * 8 + item, or a
;      shortcut's place in shortcut_keys plus one), 0 for the credits, or &FF
;      for none
; Clobbers: X, Y, temp, and as menu
.read_command
{
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_CTRL)
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL menus
    LDA #SHORTCUTS - 1              ; from the last of shortcut_keys
    STA temp
.shortcut
    LDY temp
    LDX shortcut_keys, Y
    BPL next_shortcut               ; not a key: an unused entry
    JSR key_pressed
    BMI found
.next_shortcut
    DEC temp
    BPL shortcut
    LDA #&FF
    RTS
.found
    INC temp                        ; the shortcut's command is one more than its place
    LDA temp
    RTS
.menus
    LDA #WINDOW_CREDITS             ; from the last menu, the credits
.menu_key
    PHA
    TAY
    LDX menu_keys, Y
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL next_menu
    PLA
    PHA
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDX menu_text, Y
    LDA menu_text+1, Y
    TAY
    PLA
    PHA
    JSR menu
    CMP #&00                        ; the credits: nothing to pick
    BNE picked
    PLA
    LDA #&00
    RTS
.picked
    STA temp
    PLA
    ASL A                           ; menu * 8 + item, or &FF if nothing was picked
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ORA temp
    RTS
.next_menu
    PLA
    SEC
    SBC #&01
    BCS menu_key
    RTS
}

; The CTRL shortcuts, in command order from command 1; entries that aren't
; keys (below &80) have none.
.shortcut_keys
    EQUB INKEY_TEST({KEY_X, KEY_Y, KEY_DELETE, KEY_U, KEY_A, KEY_N}), NO_KEY, NO_KEY ; OptionsA
    EQUB INKEY_TEST({KEY_S, KEY_COPY, KEY_O}), NO_KEY, INKEY_TEST({KEY_R, KEY_B}), NO_KEY, NO_KEY ; OptionsB
    EQUB INKEY_TEST({KEY_F8, KEY_F9, KEY_F6, KEY_F7, KEY_C}), 0, 0, 0                ; Environment
SHORTCUTS = P% - shortcut_keys

; &FF if repeat_key found one of the cursor keys held during this pass of
; select_sprite (it stores key_pressed's result), else 0; then a byte nothing
; uses.
.key_held
    EQUB 0, 0
; Non-zero while picking a second sprite.
.select_mode
    EQUB 0
; The interval timer, as OSWORD_READ_INTERVAL_TIMER reads it.
.timer_value
    EQUB 0, 0, 0, 0, 0

; While picking a second sprite or animating, f0-f3 count as Escape: raise
; one if any of them is pressed.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y
.menu_keys_escape
{
    LDA #WINDOW_CREDITS             ; f3 down to f0
.loop
    PHA
    TAY
    LDX menu_keys, Y
    JSR key_pressed
    BPL next
    LDA #OSBYTE_RAISE_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE
.next
    PLA
    SEC
    SBC #&01
    BCS loop
    RTS
}

; Not part of the program. The three hidden programs (H.GAME, this, then
; H.LEVDES) were written to the disc from one buffer, a whole number of
; sectors each, so each ends with what the one before left in the buffer past
; its own end. These are H.GAME's bytes at the same file offsets (&202C on):
; the last &41 bytes of the game's code (&232C-&236C where it runs), then the
; strip of LDATA's picture that H.GAME ends with (see its leftover). H.LEVDES
; ends with this file's last bytes.
.leftover
    EQUB &FF, &9A, &4C, &C3, &12, &FC, &1F, &01
    EQUB &1F, &44, &1F, &CD, &1F, &D7, &20, &56

    EQUB &8B, &1C, &C2, &1C, &1E, &18, &75, &16

    EQUB &A9, &18, &A9, &18, &0A, &15, &08, &07

    EQUB &09, &0C, &0C, &19, &F0, &C0, &80, &33
    EQUB &77, &FF, &FF, &FF, &00, &00, &FF, &FF
    EQUB &FF, &CC, &88, &88, &00, &00, &FF, &FF
    EQUB &FF, &33, &11, &11, &0F, &03, &01, &CC
    EQUB &EE, &EE, &FF, &FF, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0
    EQUS "pp00"

    EQUB &E0, &80, &11, &77, &FF, &FF, &FF, &FF

    EQUB &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &E0
```

`src/hidden_levdes.6502`:

```6502
; H.LEVDES: the PIPELINE Level Designer, by Ian Holmes and William Reeve.
;
; MENU's Level Designer option runs */LEVDES. The file the catalogue calls
; LEVDES is only a stub: a &D9-byte loader at &0900 (hidden_loader.6502inc)
; that reads this program to &1100 from sectors &16D-&18B, a "hidden run"
; that no catalogue entry mentions, and jumps to entry (&2E21). Entry moves
; three pieces of the file to where they run (initial zero page, the low
; code at &0880 and the font at &0400), loads WDATA (the windows and
; messages, at &7000) and LDATA (the title picture, straight onto the
; screen), and waits for Space. After that &25A1-&2FFF, where those pieces
; and entry itself were, holds the level being edited (src/level.6502inc).
; Leaving goes back to the PIPELINE menu by *RUNning /MRUN.
;
; Memory while it runs:
;   &0000-&0021  pointers to the menus' handler tables (menu_tables)
;   &0040-&0089  variables (below)
;   &0400-&07FF  the font, glyphs 0-63
;   &0880-&0CBF  the low code: drawing the map, windows, menus and the
;                message box, with a jump table at its start
;   &1100-&25A0  the rest of the program
;   &25A1-&2FFF  the level being edited, its map from &2800
;   &3000-&6FFF  the screen
;   &7000-&7C4D  WDATA
;
; The screen is MODE 1 narrowed to 64 columns, so each of the 64x64 map cells
; is one byte of four pixels by four scan lines and the map fills it. Menus
; are windows: boxes drawn over the map with the program's own font from
; definitions in WDATA, a title and then a menu of items, and repaired from
; the map when closed. Prompts go in a message box drawn the same way and
; printed into with the OS's text output.
;
; The designer's words: a block is what a map cell holds, the game's cell
; types (CELL_*; level.6502inc lists the block menu's names for them). A
; puzzle is what the game calls a trigger: something that happens when the
; player walks onto a place or uses an object. Each has a type (what it
; does), three effect bytes (the details) and a condition. The brush is the
; block Return plots. A marker is block F, which marks the start, the finish
; and the objects in the map; the designer marks monsters with block E, the
; S.Monster.
;
; Keys: Z X : / move the cursor, Return plots the brush, Delete blanks the
; cell, 0-9 and A-F choose the brush (the block menu's items, by number), and
; f0-f4 are the commands (block menu, Options, Files, Help, About). S
; switches the simulator: with it on, the cursor moves as the player would,
; walking, travelling along pipes and losing lives, to test the level.
;
; The file, in order:
;   &1100  the first jump table, then the routines everything uses: menus
;          (choose_from_window), Escape and errors (brk_handler), keys and
;          input (rdchv_filter, input_number, input_text, get_key) and the
;          cursor, with the simulator (move_cursor, simulate_travel)
;   &15D0  main, its loop and the commands (do_command)
;   &16E5  the Options menu's editors: start and finish, objects, monsters,
;          collectables, time, graphics and puzzles (name, type, status and
;          conditions)
;   &1D54  the Files menu: load, edit code and save
;   &1E60  the puzzle effect editors, by type
;   &2124  Help's Find puzzle, Clear, then the tables: block_menu_map and
;          the menus' handlers
;   &234D  the second jump table; new_level; printing messages, finding
;          windows and reading and writing the map
;   &2500  pixel art: glyphs 64-69 and the map's blocks
;   &25A1  the three pieces entry moves: zero page, the low code and the font
;   &2E21  entry, then junk to the end of the last sector
;
; A fragment of the authors' BASIC assembler source survives in MENU's tail
; (docs/notes/basic.md), giving a few original labels: sel0, sure, wind,
; table, key3, help, canc and t2. The routines they name say so.

INCLUDE "os.6502inc"
INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"
INCLUDE "level.6502inc"
INCLUDE "sprites.6502inc"                ; OBJECT_KINDS
INCLUDE "levdes.6502inc"
INCLUDE "wdata.6502inc"

; jump_to_handler's number for a handler table, from its pointer in zero page.
FUNCTION handlers(p) = (p - menu_tables) / 2 + 1

; Zero page. &00-&21 hold the handler tables' pointers and &22-&3F are spare
; (menu_tables, near the end of this file); the editor's variables follow.
; The low code keeps its own, from &72, which the routines' Clobbers lines
; call "the low code's zero page".
SECTION zero_page, org=&40, virtual=TRUE
.input_buffer SKIP 16           ; OSWORD 0's line (12 characters at most,
                                ; then a Return)
.cursor_x SKIP 1                ; the map cursor, 0-63 across
.cursor_y SKIP 1                ; and down
.ptr SKIP 2                     ; a pointer, or two bytes of scratch
.work SKIP 2                    ; another; also a saved position or a count
                                ; (Ian's t2)
.cursor_shown SKIP 1            ; 1 while the cursor's cell is inverted
.key_pressed SKIP 1             ; what get_key read
.keys_acted_on SKIP 1           ; how many held keys get_key acted on this pass
.brush SKIP 1                   ; the block Return plots
.plot_enabled SKIP 1            ; nonzero lets Return and Delete plot
.record SKIP 1                  ; the object, monster or puzzle being edited,
                                ; times 4 (the size of its records); or 0 or
                                ; 4 for the start or the finish
```
