.puzzle SKIP 1                  ; the puzzle being edited
.kept_window SKIP 1             ; a window to keep on screen while the cursor
                                ; moves, or negative
.choices SKIP 4                 ; four two-bit fields, unpacked a byte each:
                                ; a monster pattern's turns, or the four
                                ; choices of level_sprites
.arg SKIP 1                     ; a message number, an offset or a field
                                ; being worked on
.number SKIP 1                  ; the number being asked for
.effect_window SKIP 1           ; the effect editor's window
.effect_table SKIP 1            ; and its handler table
.unused_66 SKIP 1               ; set to &C0 at startup, never read
.loading SKIP 1                 ; nonzero while a level loads, so an error
                                ; clears what was half loaded
.simulate_window SKIP 1         ; W_SIMULATE + 1 while the simulator is on,
                                ; else 0; less 1, it's the window the main
                                ; loop keeps on screen (negative for none)
.direction SKIP 1               ; the way the simulated player is going
                                ; (MOVE_*)
.travelling SKIP 1              ; nonzero while it travels along pipes
.in_main_loop SKIP 1            ; &FF while the main loop waits for a key, so
                                ; function keys come back as keys rather than
                                ; abandoning what's going on
.menu_window SKIP 1             ; choose_from_window's window, less 1
ENDSECTION

; The low code's.
SECTION low_code_zero_page, org=&72, virtual=TRUE
.screen_ptr SKIP 2
.glyph_ptr SKIP 2               ; also a second screen pointer
.window_ptr SKIP 2              ; into a window definition or message
.byte_count SKIP 1              ; bytes across a window, or cells in a run
.line_count SKIP 1              ; lines (or menu items) to go
.saved_x SKIP 1                 ; draw_map_run's first cell's x
.nibble_mask SKIP 1             ; &F0 or &0F: which half of a map byte
.run_length SKIP 1              ; close_window's width
    SKIP 1
.map_ptr SKIP 2                 ; also draw_window's line start
.restore_x SKIP 1               ; close_window's left
.restore_row SKIP 1             ; and the cell row it's redrawing
.menu_item SKIP 1               ; window_menu's choice
.menu_shown_item SKIP 1         ; and the item it has highlighted
.window_x SKIP 1                ; the window last drawn, in screen columns
.window_y SKIP 1                ; and cell rows (half character rows)
.window_width SKIP 1            ; in screen columns
.window_height SKIP 1           ; its number of menu items
.window_flags SKIP 1            ; its y byte, for SPACE_STAYS (bit 7)
.menu_first_item SKIP 1         ; the item window_menu started on
ENDSECTION

; The message box's top left on the screen, and the columns either side of
; its bottom row, where its side lines start.
message_box     = screen_address(MESSAGE_BOX_COLUMN, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW)
box_bottom      = MESSAGE_BOX_ROW + MESSAGE_BOX_ROWS - 1
box_left_side   = screen_address(MESSAGE_BOX_COLUMN - 1, box_bottom)
box_right_side  = screen_address(MESSAGE_BOX_COLUMN + MESSAGE_BOX_COLUMNS, box_bottom)

; The cursor's directions, for moving it and the simulated player:
; clockwise from left, so EOR 2 turns about. This numbering is the
; designer's own; a level's directions (DIRECTION_* in leveldata.6502inc) go
; left, right, up, down instead.
MOVE_LEFT  = 0
MOVE_UP    = 1
MOVE_RIGHT = 2
MOVE_DOWN  = 3

SECTION hidden_levdes, filename="H.LEVDES", org=&1100

; Entry points at fixed addresses, with two pointers the startup code uses.
; Most calls between the program's parts go through tables like this one
; (there are two more, at the low code's start and before new_level), as if
; the parts were assembled separately.
.vector_crtc_write
    JMP crtc_write
.vector_cursor_off
    JMP cursor_off
.rdchv_filter_operand_address
    EQUW saved_rdchv            ; where entry saves the OS's RDCHV
.brk_handler_address
    EQUW brk_handler
.vector_main
    JMP main
.vector_set_palette
    JMP set_palette_entry

; Clear the screen, &3000-&6FFF.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr.
.clear_screen
    LDA #HI(screen)
    STA ptr+1
    LDA #0
    TAY
    STA ptr
    LDX #HI(SCREEN_END - screen)
.clear_screen_loop
    STA (ptr), Y
    INY
    BNE clear_screen_loop
    INC ptr+1
    DEX
    BNE clear_screen_loop
    RTS

; Open a window, let the user pick from its menu, close it.
; choose_from_window starts on the first item; choose_from_window_at on item
; Y. Window W_SELECT_BLOCK is special: Y and the result are blocks, not menu
; items, translated through block_menu_map.
; Ian's sel0.
; In: A = window number, Y = first item.
; Out: A = the item (or block) chosen.
; Clobbers: X, Y, ptr, menu_window, the low code's zero page; Escape
; restarts the main loop (menu_select).
.choose_from_window
    LDY #0
.choose_from_window_at
    TAX
    DEX
    STX menu_window
    BNE choose_show_window
    LDA block_menu_map, Y       ; the block's position in the menu
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    TAY
    INX
    TXA
.choose_show_window
    STY ptr
    JSR open_window
    LDA ptr
    JSR menu_select
    PHA
    JSR vector_close_window
    PLA
    LDX menu_window
    BNE choose_done
    TAY
    LDA block_menu_map, Y       ; the menu item's block
    AND #&0F
.choose_done
    RTS

; Run the menu of the window just opened.
; In: A = the item to start on.
; Out: A = the item chosen.
; Clobbers: X, Y, the low code's zero page. Escape (the OS's escape
; condition) is acknowledged, the screen repaired and the main loop
; restarted, without resetting the stack as an error or a function key
; does: each Escape from a menu leaves a few bytes behind, harmlessly, as
; the stack wraps round its page.
.menu_select
    JSR vector_menu_select
    BCC choose_done
.menu_select_escaped
    LDA #OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE
    TXA
    BEQ menu_select_escaped
    JSR escape_reset
    JMP restart_main_loop

; After Escape: cursor off, any key allowed, the map redrawn. With Shift
; held as well, offer to leave the designer.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, the low code's zero page.
.escape_reset
    JSR cursor_off
    JSR allow_any_key
    JSR vector_draw_map
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_SHIFT)
    JSR test_key
    BNE choose_done
.confirm_and_exit
    JSR confirm                 ; on N, returns from escape_reset
; Files menu, Exit: back to the PIPELINE menu by way of /MRUN, once the
; PIPELINE disc is back in.
.files_exit
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    LDA #M_INSERT_DISC
    JSR vector_print_line1
    LDA #M_PRESS_ANY_KEY
    JSR vector_print_message
    JSR wait_for_key
    LDX #LO(mrun_command)
    LDY #HI(mrun_command)
    JSR OSCLI
    RTS
.mrun_command
    EQUS "/MRUN", CR

; BRKV: report an error in the message box, wait for a key and go back to
; the main loop, with in_main_loop 0 whatever it was. A level half loaded is
; cleared rather than kept. A lower-case "i" leaves for BASIC instead, with
; the error pointer in ptr, if the startup options (the keyboard links) read
; DEVELOPERS_LINKS: the authors' way out. get_key forces Caps Lock on and
; Shift doesn't undo it, so typing that "i" means pressing Caps Lock first.
.brk_handler
    LDX #&FF
    TXS
    STX in_main_loop
    LDA loading
    BEQ brk_handler_report
    JSR new_level
    DEC loading
.brk_handler_report
    LDA MOS_ERROR_PTR
    STA work
    LDA MOS_ERROR_PTR+1
    STA work+1
    JSR hide_cursor
    JSR cursor_off
    LDA saved_rdchv             ; put the OS's RDCHV back
    STA RDCHV
    LDA saved_rdchv+1
    STA RDCHV+1
    JSR level_file_done
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    LDY #0
    LDA (work), Y               ; the error number
    CMP #ERROR_ESCAPE_KEY       ; Escape: just the message
    BNE brk_handler_numbered
    LDA #M_PRESS_ANY_KEY
    JSR vector_print_message
    LDA #M_NOTHING
    JSR vector_print_line1
    JMP brk_handler_message
.brk_handler_numbered
    PHA
    LDA #M_ERROR                ; "Error <n> has occurred !"
    JSR vector_print_line1
    LDA #M_ERROR_NUMBER_AT
    JSR vector_print_message
    PLA
    JSR print_decimal
    LDA #M_ERROR_TEXT_AT
    JSR vector_print_message
.brk_handler_message
    LDY #1
.brk_handler_message_loop
    LDA (work), Y
    BEQ brk_handler_wait
    JSR OSWRCH
    INY
    BNE brk_handler_message_loop
.brk_handler_wait
    JSR wait_for_key
    INC in_main_loop
    CMP #'i'
    BEQ debug_exit_check
.restart_main_loop
    JSR vector_draw_map
    JMP main_reset_input
.debug_exit_check
    LDA MOS_STARTUP_OPTIONS
    CMP #DEVELOPERS_LINKS
    BNE restart_main_loop
    JSR hide_cursor
    JSR cursor_on
    JSR cursor_on
    LDA #OSBYTE_AUTO_REPEAT_PERIOD
    LDX #2                      ; centiseconds
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDA MOS_ERROR_PTR
    STA ptr
    LDA MOS_ERROR_PTR+1
    STA ptr+1
    LDX #LO(basic_command)
    LDY #HI(basic_command)
    JSR OSCLI
.basic_command
    EQUS "BASIC", CR
; Wait for a key, ignoring any typed ahead; Escape is acknowledged and
; ignored, and while rdchv_filter is RDCHV (everywhere but brk_handler) a
; function key abandons the wait.
; Out: A = the key.
; Clobbers: X, Y.
.wait_for_key
    JSR flush_input
.wait_for_key_loop
    LDA #OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE
    JSR OSRDCH
    BCS wait_for_key_loop
    RTS

; Throw away any keys typed ahead.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y.
.flush_input
    LDA #OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS
    LDX #1                      ; just the input buffer
    JMP OSBYTE

; The designer's RDCHV handler, in place from main on (brk_handler takes it
; out while it shows an error, and MRUN when the designer is left). With it,
; OSRDCH, and so OSWORD 0, only sees Return, Delete and keys from
; input_min_char to input_max_char (normally all of them; input_line narrows
; them), others being read again; and a function key abandons whatever is
; going on for its command. Escape goes straight through. entry puts the
; OS's RDCHV in the JSR here.
.rdchv_filter_retry
    PLP
.rdchv_filter
    JSR &FFA6                   ; the OS's RDCHV, filled in by entry
saved_rdchv = rdchv_filter + 1
    BCS do_nothing
    PHP
    JSR check_function_key
    CMP #CR
    BEQ rdchv_filter_accept
    CMP #DEL
    BEQ rdchv_filter_accept
    CMP input_min_char
    BCC rdchv_filter_retry
    CMP input_max_char
    BEQ rdchv_filter_accept
    BCS rdchv_filter_retry
.rdchv_filter_accept
    PLP
.do_nothing                     ; Options menu, OK
    RTS

; A function key, f0-f5, abandons whatever is going on: the stack is reset,
; the map redrawn, and its command run from the main loop (f5 has none, so it
; only abandons).
; In: A = a key.
; Out: A preserved, if it wasn't a function key; nothing else is touched.
; If it was, this doesn't return.
.check_function_key
    PHA
    EOR #KEYCODE_F0
    CMP #6
    BCC abort_to_command
    PLA
    RTS
.abort_to_command
    LDX #&FF
    TXS
    PHA
    JSR vector_draw_map
    JSR allow_any_key
    JSR cursor_off
    PLA
    JMP main_dispatch

; The map cursor is the cursor's cell inverted; hide_cursor puts the cell
; back if it's showing, toggle_cursor flips it, after waiting for the vertical
; sync so it doesn't flicker.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr.
.hide_cursor
    LDA cursor_shown
    BEQ do_nothing
.toggle_cursor
    LDA cursor_shown
    EOR #1
    STA cursor_shown
    LDA #OSBYTE_WAIT_VSYNC
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDX cursor_x
    LDY cursor_y
    JMP vector_invert_cell

; Put a block in the map at the cursor and on the screen.
; In: A = the block.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr, work, screen_ptr.
.plot_at_cursor
    PHA
    JSR hide_cursor
    LDX cursor_x
    LDY cursor_y
    PLA
    JMP vector_write_map

; Ask which object, monster or puzzle, until the answer is 1 to A.
; In: A = how many there are; X = the question's message.
; Out: record = (the answer - 1) * 4.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr, work, the input buffer, the low code's zero page.
.choose_record
    STX work
    STA record
.choose_record_ask
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    LDX work
    JSR input_number
    DEX
    BPL choose_record_ask
    SEC
    SBC #1
    BCC choose_record_ask
    CMP record
    BCS choose_record_ask
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA record
    JMP vector_close_message_box

; Read a number of up to three digits in the message box.
; In: X = the prompt's message.
; Out: X = 0 and A = the number; X = 1 if nothing was typed; X = 3 if it was
; over 255. (X = 2 would be a number 256 digits long.)
; Clobbers: Y, ptr, window_ptr, the input buffer.
.input_number
    LDA #'0'
    STA input_min_char
    LDA #'9'
    STA input_max_char
    LDA #3
    JSR input_line
    LDA #0
    TAY
.input_number_digit
    PHA
    LDA input_buffer, Y
    SEC
    SBC #'0'
    BCC input_number_not_digit  ; the Return
    STA input_buffer, Y
    PLA
    ASL A                       ; times 10, watching for overflow
    BCS input_number_overflow
    STA ptr
    ASL A
    BCS input_number_overflow
    ASL A
    BCS input_number_overflow
    ADC ptr
    BCS input_number_overflow
    ADC input_buffer, Y
    BCS input_number_overflow
    INY
    BNE input_number_digit
    LDX #2
    RTS
.input_number_not_digit
    LDX #0
    TYA
    BNE menu_ok_return          ; just pull the number and return
    PLA
    INX
    RTS

; Place monster window, OK: store what the window's items set (they work on
; copies: see place_monster_number), the cursor's x and y with the monster's
; number and direction in their bottom two bits, and close it as below.
.place_monster_ok
    LDY record
    LDA cursor_x
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ORA arg                     ; monster number
    STA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    LDA cursor_y
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ORA work+1                  ; direction
    STA level_puzzle_effects+2, Y
; The OK item of an editing window: close it and return from the routine
; that runs the window's menu (the one whose JSR jump_to_handler led here),
; which ends that editor. menu_ok_drop_choice is for the loops that push the
; choice before that JSR: it drops the choice too.
.menu_ok_drop_choice
    PLA
.menu_ok
    JSR vector_close_window
    PLA
.menu_ok_return
    PLA
    RTS

.input_number_overflow
    LDX #3
    RTS

; "SURE ? Press Y or N". Returns on Y; on N closes the window and returns
; from the caller instead. Ian's sure.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, the low code's zero page.
.confirm
    LDA #W_SURE
    JSR open_window
.confirm_loop
    JSR wait_for_key
    ORA #&20                    ; lower case
    CMP #'n'
    BEQ menu_ok
    CMP #'y'
    BNE confirm_loop
    JMP vector_close_window

; Read a line of text, or of characters input_min_char to input_max_char
; (input_line), into input_buffer, after a prompt on the message box's
; second line. Escape is an error.
; In: A = the most characters; X = the prompt's message.
; Out: ptr = the number of characters; input_buffer = them and a Return,
; then spaces to its end. The cursor is off again and any key allowed.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, window_ptr.
.input_text
    LDY #' '
    STY input_min_char
    LDY #'~'
    STY input_max_char
.input_line
    STA input_max_length
    TXA
    JSR vector_print_line2
    JSR cursor_on
    LDA #' '
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDY #15
.input_line_clear
    STA input_buffer, Y
    DEY
    BNE input_line_clear
    LDX #LO(input_block)
    LDY #HI(input_block)
    LDA #OSWORD_READ_LINE
    JSR OSWORD
    STY ptr
    JSR allow_any_key
    BCC cursor_off
    JMP escape_pressed

; The text cursor: off, with the cursor keys giving codes rather than
; editing (*FX4,2: they act as f11-f15, &8B-&8F); or on and editing.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y.
.cursor_off
    LDA #CRTC_CURSOR_OFF
    JSR crtc_set_cursor_start
    LDX #CURSOR_KEYS_SOFT
    BNE set_cursor_key_mode
.cursor_on
    LDA #CRTC_CURSOR_BLINK
    JSR crtc_set_cursor_start
    LDX #CURSOR_KEYS_EDIT
.set_cursor_key_mode
    LDA #OSBYTE_CURSOR_EDITING
    JMP OSBYTE

; Let OSRDCH (rdchv_filter) return any key.
; Clobbers: X.
.allow_any_key
    LDX #0
    STX input_min_char
    DEX
    STX input_max_char
    RTS

; Write a CRTC register: the cursor start register (crtc_set_cursor_start),
; or register X (crtc_write).
; In: A = the value.
; Clobbers: X, for crtc_set_cursor_start.
.crtc_set_cursor_start
    LDX #CRTC_CURSOR_START
.crtc_write
    STX CRTC_ADDR
    STA CRTC_DATA
    RTS

; Escape where a key was read: tidy up (offering to leave if Shift is held
; too), then raise the designer's own error for it.
.escape_pressed
    JSR escape_reset
    BRK
    EQUB ERROR_ESCAPE_KEY
    EQUS "Escape key pressed", 0
; get_key's loop while travelling: each pass takes a step the way it's going.
; With no key it goes round again; with one, it skips the movement keys
; (they don't steer it), checks the rest from S on, and so usually returns
; the key.
.get_key_travelling
    ASL A                       ; C set if no key came
    BCC get_key_step
    INC keys_acted_on           ; keep going round
.get_key_step
    LDY #handlers(cursor_handlers_ptr)
    LDA direction
    JSR jump_to_handler
    JMP get_key_check_simulate

; Wait for a key, meanwhile flashing the cursor and doing the editing keys
; themselves: Z X : / move the cursor (with the simulator's rules when it's
; on), S switches the simulator, and if plotting is enabled Delete blanks the
; cursor's cell and Return plots the brush there. Once a key comes it tests
; which of those are held rather than reading them, so several act at once
; (diagonally, say) and a held one repeats at the auto-repeat rate. A window
; can be kept on screen meanwhile, moving out of the cursor's way. Caps Lock
; is forced on every time round. get_key_no_plot doesn't plot.
; In: A = nonzero to enable plotting; X = a window to keep, or negative.
; Out: A = the key read, once a pass finds none of the editing keys held.
; Clobbers: X, Y, ptr, work, screen_ptr, the low code's zero page. Escape
; doesn't return, nor does a function key except in the main loop.
.get_key_no_plot
    LDA #0
.get_key
    STA plot_enabled
    STX kept_window
    TXA
    BMI get_key_poll
    JSR open_window
.get_key_poll
    JSR toggle_cursor
    LDX #&20                    ; Caps Lock on, Shift Lock off, and Shift
    LDY #&4F                    ; doesn't reverse Caps Lock
    LDA #OSBYTE_KEYBOARD_STATUS
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDX travelling              ; a centisecond a step when travelling,
    BNE get_key_inkey
    LDX #20                     ; else flash every fifth of a second
.get_key_inkey
    LDA #OSBYTE_INKEY
    LDY #0
    STY keys_acted_on
    JSR OSBYTE
    PHP                         ; C set: no key
    STX key_pressed
    LDA in_main_loop            ; the main loop takes function keys as keys
    BNE get_key_got
    TXA
    JSR check_function_key
.get_key_got
    PLP
    ROR A                       ; bit 7: no key
    CPY #ESC
    BEQ escape_pressed
    LDY travelling
    BNE get_key_travelling
    ASL A
    BCS get_key_poll
    ; A key came: now see which keys are held, so a held key repeats at the
    ; keyboard's rate without the buffer filling.
    JSR flush_input
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_Z)
    JSR test_key
    BNE get_key_check_right
    INC keys_acted_on
    JSR cursor_left
.get_key_check_right
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_X)
    JSR test_key
    BNE get_key_check_up
    INC keys_acted_on
    JSR cursor_right
.get_key_check_up
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_COLON)
    JSR test_key
    BNE get_key_check_down
    INC keys_acted_on
    JSR cursor_up
.get_key_check_down
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_SLASH)
    JSR test_key
    BNE get_key_check_simulate
    INC keys_acted_on
    JSR cursor_down
.get_key_check_simulate
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_S)
    JSR test_key
    BNE get_key_check_plot
    INC keys_acted_on
    JSR beep
    JSR switch_simulate
.get_key_check_plot
    LDA plot_enabled
    BEQ get_key_handled
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_DELETE)
    JSR test_key
    BNE get_key_check_return
    INC keys_acted_on
    LDA #CELL_FLOOR
    JSR plot_at_cursor
.get_key_check_return
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_RETURN)
    JSR test_key
    BNE get_key_handled
    INC keys_acted_on
    LDA brush
    JSR plot_at_cursor
.get_key_handled
    LDA keys_acted_on
    BEQ get_key_done
    JMP get_key_poll
.get_key_done
    JSR hide_cursor
    LDA kept_window
    BMI get_key_return
    JSR vector_close_window
.get_key_return
    LDA key_pressed
    RTS

; Move the cursor a cell (and these are cursor_handlers, by MOVE_*).
; Crossing the middle of the screen moves the kept window to the other side.
; Out: C set if the cursor didn't move (though a bounce in a pipe can leave
; it clear).
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr, work, screen_ptr, the low code's zero page.
.cursor_left
    LDY #MOVE_LEFT
    JSR move_cursor
    BCS cursor_move_done
    CPX #MAP_SIZE/2 - 1
    BEQ reopen_window
    RTS
.cursor_right
    LDY #MOVE_RIGHT
    JSR move_cursor
    BCS cursor_move_done
    CPX #MAP_SIZE/2
    BEQ reopen_window
    RTS
.cursor_up
    LDY #MOVE_UP
    JSR move_cursor
    BCS cursor_move_done
    CPY #MAP_SIZE/2 - 1
    BEQ reopen_window
.cursor_move_done
    RTS
.cursor_down
    LDY #MOVE_DOWN
    JSR move_cursor
    BCS cursor_move_done
    CPY #MAP_SIZE/2
    BNE cursor_move_done
; Close the window last drawn and draw the kept one again, wherever it now
; goes, if there is one.
.reopen_window
    LDA kept_window
    BMI cursor_move_done
    JSR vector_close_window
    LDA kept_window
; Draw window A. Ian's wind.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, the low code's zero page.
.open_window
    JSR vector_window_address
    JMP vector_draw_window

; Is a key held down?
; In: X = INKEY_TEST(its internal key number).
; Out: Z set if it is.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y.
.test_key
    LDY #&FF
    LDA #OSBYTE_INKEY
    JSR OSBYTE
    INX
    RTS

; The cell next to the cursor.
; In: Y = a direction, MOVE_*.
; Out: X, Y = its position.
; Clobbers: A.
.neighbour
    LDA cursor_x
    CLC
    ADC direction_dx, Y
    TAX
    LDA cursor_y
    CLC
    ADC direction_dy, Y
    TAY
    RTS

.move_blocked
    SEC
.move_pop
    PLA
    RTS

; Move the cursor a cell, if it can go there. Normally it can go anywhere on
; the map; with the simulator on it moves like the player: it walks onto
; blank cells and collectables, loses a life in a fatal trap, an S.Monster or
; off the map's edge, and enters a pipe that runs its way, which starts it
; travelling until it comes out. Anything else stops it. Shift lets it go
; anywhere on the map regardless, and stops any travelling. While travelling
; it takes a step of that instead (simulate_travel).
; In: Y = a direction, MOVE_*.
; Out: C clear and X, Y = the new position if it moved. Going into a pipe it
; doesn't return: it finishes the cursor_* routine that called it and goes
; on in get_key from the S key, skipping any movement keys not yet checked.
; Clobbers: A, ptr, work, screen_ptr, the low code's zero page.
.move_cursor
    TYA
    PHA
    JSR neighbour
    JSR vector_read_map         ; negative off the map, where Shift doesn't
    BMI move_into_tile          ; help
    PHA
    LDX #INKEY_TEST(KEY_SHIFT)
    JSR test_key
    PLA
    DEX
    BEQ move_into_tile
    INX
    STX travelling
    BEQ move_to_neighbour
.move_into_tile
    LDX travelling
    BNE simulate_travel
    TAX
    BEQ move_to_neighbour       ; anyone can go onto a blank
    LDX simulate_window
    BEQ move_to_neighbour       ; and anywhere with the simulator off
    CMP #CELL_SULPHUR
    BEQ move_to_neighbour
    CMP #CELL_LAVA
    BEQ simulate_lose_life
    CMP #CELL_FIRE
    BEQ simulate_lose_life
    TAX
    BMI simulate_lose_life
    PLA
    PHA
    TAY
    TXA
    CMP pipe_across, Y
    SEC
    BNE move_pop
    ; Into a pipe: start travelling, and finish our caller (the cursor_*
    ; handler) by calling the rest of it, before getting on with get_key.
    INC travelling
    PLA
    JSR move_push
    PLA
    ADC #1
    STA ptr
    PLA
    ADC #0
    STA ptr+1
    JSR jump_via_ptr
    PLA
    PLA
    JMP get_key_check_simulate
.jump_via_ptr
    JMP (ptr)
.move_push
    PHA
.move_to_neighbour
    TAX
    BMI move_blocked
    JSR hide_cursor
    PLA
    STA direction
    TAY
    JSR neighbour
    STX cursor_x
    STY cursor_y
    CLC
    RTS

; The simulated player died: say so and stop travelling, leaving the cursor
; where it was. This and simulate_travel are the rest of move_cursor, entered
; with its direction on the stack, and return from it.
.simulate_lose_life
    PLA
    JSR hide_cursor
    JSR toggle_cursor
    JSR beep
    LDA #W_LOST_LIFE
    JSR open_window
    JSR wait_for_key
    JSR reopen_window
    LDA #0
    STA travelling
    RTS

; One step of travelling: along pipes whatever their direction, out onto a
; blank or a collectable (which stops it), back the way it came off curves,
; walls, crates, barricades and markers, and at a junction into the first
; pipe running its way that it finds turning left, right or going straight on
; (or back, if there's none). Fatal traps, S.Monsters and the map's edge cost
; a life.
.simulate_travel
    LDY direction
    JSR neighbour
    JSR vector_read_map
    BEQ simulate_set_running
    BMI simulate_lose_life
    CMP #CELL_SULPHUR
    BEQ simulate_collect
    CMP #CELL_JUNCTION
    BEQ simulate_junction
    CMP #CELL_LAVA
    BEQ simulate_lose_life
    BCC simulate_bounce
    CMP #CELL_FIRE
    BEQ simulate_lose_life
    BCC move_to_neighbour       ; the two pipes
.simulate_bounce
    PLA
    EOR #2                      ; the opposite direction (MOVE_*)
    STA direction
    RTS
.simulate_collect
    LDA #0
.simulate_set_running
    STA travelling
    BEQ move_to_neighbour
.simulate_junction
    PLA
    JSR move_push
    LDY direction
    DEY                         ; turning left...
    JSR simulate_try_turn
    INY
    INY                         ; ...right...
    JSR simulate_try_turn
    DEY                         ; ...or straight on
    JSR simulate_try_turn
    TYA
    EOR #2                      ; none: back the way it came
    TAY
    BPL simulate_set_direction
; Try direction Y (0-3 after masking) from the junction: a pipe running that
; way there is taken, returning from move_cursor (which simulate_junction is
; part of) with C clear and X, Y the cursor; otherwise this returns, with Y
; the direction tried.
.simulate_try_turn
    TYA
    AND #3
    TAY
    PHA
    JSR neighbour
    JSR vector_read_map
    TAX
    PLA
    TAY
    TXA
    CMP pipe_across, Y
    BEQ simulate_turn
    RTS
.simulate_turn
    PLA
    PLA
.simulate_set_direction
    STY direction
    CLC
    LDX cursor_x
    LDY cursor_y
    RTS
; VDU 19: set a logical colour's physical colour.
; In: A = palette_entry(logical, physical), which goes out whole as the
; physical colour (the OS ignores the top nibble).
; Clobbers: A, X.
.set_palette_entry
    TAX
    LDA #VDU_PALETTE
    JSR OSWRCH
    TXA
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    JSR OSWRCH
    TXA
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDA #0
    JSR OSWRCH
    JSR OSWRCH
    JMP OSWRCH

; The editor proper, after the title: a blank level, then commands for ever.
; Each time round, get_key moves the cursor and plots until another key
; comes; hex_key handles that key if it's 0-9, A-F or cursor up or down (all
; choosing the brush), and do_command if it's a function key. Errors come
; back to main_reset_input, which puts rdchv_filter back; a function key
; pressed anywhere else comes back to main_dispatch (check_function_key).
.main
    JSR new_level
.main_reset_input
    JSR allow_any_key
    LDA #LO(rdchv_filter)
    STA RDCHV
    LDA #HI(rdchv_filter)
    STA RDCHV+1
.main_loop
    DEC in_main_loop            ; &FF while get_key waits
    LDA #1                      ; plotting allowed
    LDX simulate_window         ; keep the Simulate window up if it's on
    DEX
    JSR get_key
    INC in_main_loop
    PHA
    JSR hex_key
    PLA
    EOR #KEYCODE_F0             ; function keys f0-f4 are commands 0-4
.main_dispatch
    JSR do_command
    JMP main_loop

; In the main loop, 0-9 and A-F choose the brush, the block menu's item of
; that number, with a beep; and the cursor up and down keys open the block
; menu, putting the key back in the keyboard buffer so that the menu's bar
; moves at once.
; In: A = the key.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr, the low code's zero page.
.hex_key
    CMP #'0'
    BCC hex_key_done
    CMP #'F' + 1
    BCS hex_key_cursor
    CMP #'9' + 1
    BCC hex_key_item
    SBC #'A'
    BCC hex_key_cursor
    ADC #'9'             ; A-F follow 0-9 (the carry adds one)
.hex_key_item
    TAY
    LDA block_menu_map - '0', Y
    AND #&0F                    ; the item's block
    STA brush
; Beep (VDU 7, made short by *FX214,2).
; Clobbers: A.
.beep
    LDA #BEL
    JMP OSWRCH
.hex_key_cursor
    CMP #KEYCODE_CURSOR_DOWN
    BEQ hex_key_cursor_flush
    CMP #KEYCODE_CURSOR_UP
    BNE hex_key_done
.hex_key_cursor_flush
    TAY
    LDX #BUFFER_KEYBOARD
    LDA #OSBYTE_INSERT_BUFFER   ; put the key back for the menu to read
    JSR OSBYTE
; f0: choose the brush from the block menu, stopping the simulator as every
; command does.
.select_brush
    LDA #0
    STA simulate_window
    STA travelling
    LDA #W_SELECT_BLOCK
    LDY brush
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    STA brush
.hex_key_done                   ; Ian's canc, for files_menu
    RTS

; Run a command: 0 the block menu, 1 Options, 2 Files, 3 Help, 4 About.
; Commands stop the simulator; anything else leaves it alone.
; In: A = the command.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, and whatever the command does.
.do_command
    TAY
    BEQ select_brush
    LDA simulate_window
    PHA
    LDA travelling
    LDX #0
    STX simulate_window
    STX travelling
    TAX
    PLA
    DEY
    BEQ options_menu
    DEY
    BEQ files_menu
    DEY
    BEQ help_menu
    DEY
    BEQ show_about
    STX travelling
    STA simulate_window
    RTS

; f4: the credits.
.show_about
    LDA #W_ABOUT
    JSR open_window
    JSR wait_for_key
    JMP vector_close_window

; f1: the Options menu.
.options_menu
    LDA #W_OPTIONS
    JSR choose_from_window
    LDY #handlers(options_handlers_ptr)
; Jump to the handler for a menu item. Ian's table.
; In: A = the item; Y = the handler table's number (handlers()).
; Clobbers: A, Y, ptr; what the handler does.
.jump_to_handler
    PHA
    TYA
    ASL A
    TAY
    ; The table numbers start at 1 and the pointers at zero page's start, so
    ; this indexes from &FFFE and wraps round into zero page.
    LDA &10000 + menu_tables - 2, Y
    STA ptr
    LDA &10000 + menu_tables - 1, Y
    STA ptr+1
    PLA
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDA (ptr), Y
    STA handler_address
    INY
    LDA (ptr), Y
    STA handler_address+1
.jump_to_handler_jmp
    JMP &FFA6                   ; the handler, filled in above
handler_address = jump_to_handler_jmp + 1

; f2: the Files menu; any item but OK asks whether the user is sure before
; it's done. The fragment of Ian's source in MENU is this routine.
.files_menu
    LDA #W_FILES
    JSR choose_from_window
    CMP #I_FILES_OK
    BEQ hex_key_done
    STA work
    JSR confirm
    LDA work
    LDY #handlers(files_handlers_ptr)
    BNE jump_to_handler

; f3: the Help menu, which shows whether the simulator is on and stays up
; while Simulate is chosen. Ian's key3, and help_menu_show is his help.
.help_menu
    LDA #W_HELP
    JSR open_window
    LDA #0
    BEQ help_menu_show
; Help menu, Simulate: switch it and go round again.
.help_simulate
    SEC                         ; leave the Simulate window to the main loop
    JSR switch_simulate
    LDA #I_HELP_SIMULATE
.help_menu_show
    PHA
    LDA simulate_window
    LDY #item_line(I_HELP_SIMULATE)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    PLA
    TAY
    JSR menu_select
    LDY #handlers(help_handlers_ptr)
    BNE jump_to_handler

; Switch the simulator on or off. With C clear (the S key, in get_key) the
; Simulate window opens or closes too, as get_key's kept window, unless
; get_key is keeping another; with C set (Help) the main loop's get_key sees
; to it.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, the low code's zero page.
.switch_simulate
    LDA simulate_window
    EOR #W_SIMULATE + 1
    STA simulate_window
    BNE switch_simulate_on
    STA travelling
    BCS switch_simulate_done
    LDA kept_window
    CMP #W_SIMULATE
    BNE switch_simulate_done
    JSR vector_close_window
    LDA #&FF
    STA kept_window
.switch_simulate_done
    RTS
.switch_simulate_on
    BCS switch_simulate_done
    LDA kept_window
    BPL switch_simulate_done
    LDA #W_SIMULATE
    STA kept_window
    JMP open_window
; Options menu, Start and Finish: Define lets the user move the cursor and
; press Return to put the start or finish there (Space leaves it); Display
; just moves the cursor there. The start is kept 4 less than where it's put
; in each direction (the game keeps the top left of its view, 8 cells by 8,
; with the player 4 cells in). The position is marked in the map with a
; marker block.
.option_start
    LDY #level_start_x - level_start_x
    BEQ edit_marker
.option_finish
    LDY #level_finish_x - level_start_x
.edit_marker
    STY record
    LDA #W_DEFINE_DISPLAY
    JSR choose_from_window
    CMP #I_DEFINE_DISPLAY_OK
    BEQ switch_simulate_done
    PHA
    LDY record
    TYA
    EOR #4                      ; 4 for the start, 0 for the finish
    CLC
    ADC level_start_x, Y
    STA cursor_x
    STA work
    TYA
    EOR #4
    CLC
    ADC level_start_y, Y
    STA cursor_y
    STA work+1
    PLA
    BNE switch_simulate_done    ; Display
.edit_marker_define
    LDX #W_OPTIONS_LOCATION
    JSR get_key_no_plot
    CMP #' '
    BEQ switch_simulate_done
    CMP #CR
    BNE edit_marker_define
    LDY record
    TYA
    SEC
    SBC #4                      ; -4 for the start, 0 for the finish
    CLC
    ADC cursor_x
    STA level_start_x, Y
    TYA
    SEC
    SBC #4
    CLC
    ADC cursor_y
    STA level_start_y, Y
    LDA #CELL_OBJECT
; Mark a position in the map: put block A at the cursor, and blank the old
; position if it has the same block.
; In: A = the block; work = the old position.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr, work, screen_ptr.
.plot_marker
    PHA
    LDX work
    LDY work+1
    JSR vector_read_map
    STA ptr
    PLA
    PHA
    EOR ptr
    BNE plot_marker_new
    LDX work
    LDY work+1
    JSR vector_write_map        ; A is 0, a blank
.plot_marker_new
    LDX cursor_x
    LDY cursor_y
    PLA
    JMP vector_write_map

; Options menu, Object: which one, then its window until OK.
;
; This and the other editing windows (monster, puzzle, status, conditions
; and the effects) run their menus through handler tables (see
; options_handlers): each handler works on the record (and puzzle) being
; edited, may clobber A, X, Y and the scratch bytes, and returns to the
; window's loop, which goes round again; the OK handler (menu_ok or
; menu_ok_drop_choice) pops out of it.
.option_object
    LDX #M_WHICH_OBJECT
    LDA #OBJECTS
    JSR choose_record
    JSR show_object_window
    LDA #0
.option_object_loop
    JSR menu_select
    PHA
    LDY #handlers(object_handlers_ptr)
    JSR jump_to_handler
    PLA
    BPL option_object_loop

; Object window, Position: the user moves the cursor and presses Return to
; put the object there (Space leaves it), marked in the map with a marker
; block.
.object_position
    JSR vector_close_window
    LDY record
    LDA level_objects, Y
    AND #COORDINATE_BITS
    STA cursor_x
    STA work
    LDA level_objects+1, Y
    AND #COORDINATE_BITS
    STA cursor_y
    STA work+1
.object_position_define
    LDX #W_OBJECT_LOCATION
    JSR get_key_no_plot
    CMP #' '
    BEQ show_object_window
    CMP #CR
    BNE object_position_define
    LDY record
    LDA cursor_x                ; which also makes it exist
    STA level_objects, Y
    LDA cursor_y
    STA level_objects+1, Y
    LDA #CELL_OBJECT
    JSR plot_marker
; Open the object window with ticks showing the object's flags
; (show_object_ticks just redraws the ticks).
.show_object_window
    LDA #W_OBJECT
    JSR show_record_window
.show_object_ticks
    LDY record
    LDA level_objects, Y
    ORA level_objects+1, Y
    AND #POSITION_FLAGS
    BEQ show_object_exists
    LDA #1
.show_object_exists
    EOR #1
    LDY #item_line(I_OBJECT_EXISTS)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    LDY record
    LDA level_objects+3, Y
    AND #OBJECT_NO_CHARGES
    EOR #OBJECT_NO_CHARGES
    LDY #item_line(I_OBJECT_CHARGES)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    LDY record
    LDA level_objects+3, Y
    PHA
    AND #OBJECT_VANISHES
    LDY #item_line(I_OBJECT_VANISH)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    PLA
    AND #OBJECT_NO_THROW
    EOR #OBJECT_NO_THROW
    LDY #item_line(I_OBJECT_THROW)
    JMP vector_tick_line

; Object window, Charge: how many charges, 0-31, which also makes them count
; (clearing OBJECT_NO_CHARGES).
.object_charge
    LDY #OBJECT_CHARGES
    TYA
    LDX record
    AND level_objects+3, X
    TAX
    LDA #M_CHARGES
    SEC                         ; 0 allowed
    JSR ask_number_limited
    STA ptr
    LDY record
    LDA level_objects+3, Y
    AND #OBJECT_VANISHES OR OBJECT_NO_THROW
    ORA ptr
    STA level_objects+3, Y
    JMP show_object_window

; Object window, Sprite no.: 1-15, kept as 0-14 (the game's object icons;
; its sixteenth, the exit, isn't offered).
.object_sprite
    LDY record
    LDX level_objects+2, Y
    INX
    LDA #M_OLD_SPRITE
    LDY #OBJECT_KINDS
    CLC                         ; 0 not allowed
    JSR ask_number_limited
    SEC
    SBC #1
    LDY record
    STA level_objects+2, Y
    BPL show_object_window

; Object window, Charges:, Vanish: and Throw:, which flip a flag.
.object_charges_toggle
    LDA #OBJECT_NO_CHARGES
    BNE object_toggle_flag
.object_vanish_toggle
    LDA #OBJECT_VANISHES
    BNE object_toggle_flag
.object_throw_toggle
    LDA #OBJECT_NO_THROW
.object_toggle_flag
    LDY record
    EOR level_objects+3, Y
    STA level_objects+3, Y
    JMP show_object_ticks

; Object window, Exists ?: flip OBJECT_ABSENT in both coordinates (and clear
; the other flag, bit 6).
.object_exists_toggle
    LDY record
    LDA level_objects, Y
    AND #OBJECT_ABSENT OR COORDINATE_BITS
    EOR #OBJECT_ABSENT
    STA level_objects, Y
    AND #OBJECT_ABSENT
    STA ptr
    LDA level_objects+1, Y
    AND #COORDINATE_BITS
    ORA ptr
    STA level_objects+1, Y
    JMP show_object_ticks
; Print A in decimal without leading zeros (they go out as VDU 0, which does
; nothing).
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr.
.print_decimal
    STA ptr
    LDY #0                      ; nonzero once a digit has been printed
    LDA #100
    JSR print_digit
    LDA #10
    JSR print_digit
    LDA #1
.print_digit
    STA ptr+1
    LDA ptr
    LDX #&FF
.print_digit_count
    INX
    STA ptr
    SEC
    SBC ptr+1
    BCS print_digit_count
    TXA
    BNE print_digit_out
    DEY
    INY
    BNE print_digit_out
    DEC ptr+1
    BEQ print_digit_out         ; always print the units
    LDA #-'0'            ; a leading zero: VDU 0
    DEY
.print_digit_out
    INY
    ADC #'0'
    JMP OSWRCH

; Options menu, M.Monster: which one, then its window until OK.
.option_monster
    LDX #M_WHICH_MONSTER
    LDA #MONSTERS
    JSR choose_record
    JSR show_monster_window
    LDA #0
.option_monster_loop
    JSR menu_select
    PHA
    LDY #handlers(monster_handlers_ptr)
    JSR jump_to_handler
    PLA
    BPL option_monster_loop

; Monster window, Position: put the monster with the cursor, as for an
; object, marked in the map with an S.Monster block (the game's fire, which
; marks a monster's cell).
.monster_position
    JSR vector_close_window
    LDY record
    LDA level_monsters, Y
    LSR A
    LSR A
    STA work
    STA cursor_x
    LDA level_monsters+1, Y
    LSR A
    LSR A
    STA work+1
    STA cursor_y
.monster_position_define
    LDX #W_MONSTER_LOCATION
    JSR get_key_no_plot
    CMP #' '
    BEQ show_monster_window
    CMP #CR
    BNE monster_position_define
    LDY record
    LDA cursor_x
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA level_monsters, Y
    LDA cursor_y
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA level_monsters+1, Y
    LDA #CELL_FIRE
    JSR plot_marker
.show_monster_window
    LDA #W_MONSTER
; Open an object's or monster's window, its number (record / 4 + 1, one
; digit) after the title.
; In: A = the window.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, the low code's zero page.
.show_record_window
    JSR open_window
    LDA #M_RECORD_NUMBER
    JSR vector_print_message
    LDA record
    LSR A
    LSR A
    ADC #'1'
    JSR OSWRCH
    JMP vector_text_colours

; Monster window, Direction.
.monster_direction
    LDY record
    LDX level_monsters+2, Y
    JSR choose_direction
    STA level_monsters+2, Y
    BPL show_monster_window

; Choose a monster's direction from the north, south, east, west, dead menu.
; In: X = the current direction (DIRECTION_*; 4 and up count as dead).
; Out: A = the direction chosen (MONSTER_GONE for dead); Y = record.
; Clobbers: X, ptr.
.choose_direction
    CPX #direction_items_end - direction_items
    BCC choose_direction_menu
    LDX #direction_items_end - direction_items - 1
.choose_direction_menu
    LDY direction_items, X
    LDA #W_DIRECTION
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    TAY
    LDA direction_codes, Y
    LDY record
    RTS
; The direction for each item of the direction menu, and the item for each
; direction (west, east, north, south, then dead).
direction_menu = {DIRECTION_UP, DIRECTION_DOWN, DIRECTION_RIGHT,
    DIRECTION_LEFT, MONSTER_GONE}
.direction_codes
    EQUB direction_menu
.direction_items
    EQUB FIND(direction_menu, {DIRECTION_LEFT, DIRECTION_RIGHT, DIRECTION_UP,
        DIRECTION_DOWN, MONSTER_GONE})
.direction_items_end

; Monster window, Pattern.
.monster_pattern
    LDY record
    LDA level_monsters+3, Y
    JSR choose_pattern
    STA level_monsters+3, Y
    JMP show_monster_window

; Choose a monster's pattern: one of four presets, or Special, which asks
; for its four choices of which way to turn one at a time.
; In: A = the current pattern.
; Out: A = the new one; Y = record.
; Clobbers: X, ptr, choices, the low code's zero page.
.choose_pattern
    STA ptr+1
    LDY #0
.choose_pattern_find
    CMP pattern_presets, Y
    BEQ choose_pattern_menu
    INY
    CPY #pattern_presets_end - pattern_presets
    BCC choose_pattern_find
.choose_pattern_menu
    LDA #W_PATTERNS
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    CMP #pattern_presets_end - pattern_presets      ; Special
    BEQ choose_pattern_special
    TAY
    LDA pattern_presets, Y
    LDY record
    RTS
.choose_pattern_special
    LDA ptr+1
    JSR unpack_choices
    PHA                         ; 0: the menu starts on the first priority
.choose_pattern_special_loop
    LDA #W_PRIORITIES
    JSR open_window
    LDA #M_PATTERN_AT           ; the four choices as letters in the title
    JSR vector_print_message
    LDX #3
.choose_pattern_print
    LDY choices, X
    LDA priority_letters, Y
    JSR OSWRCH
    DEX
    BPL choose_pattern_print
    PLA
    JSR menu_select
    CMP #I_PRIORITIES_OK
    BEQ choose_pattern_done
    PHA
    EOR #3                      ; the first priority is the last field
    TAX
    LDA choices, X
    JSR choose_relative_direction
    TAY
    PLA
    PHA
    EOR #3
    TAX
    TYA
    STA choices, X
    BPL choose_pattern_special_loop

; Choose forwards, backwards, left or right.
; In: A = the current turn, TURN_*.
; Out: A = the turn chosen.
; Clobbers: X, Y, ptr, the low code's zero page.
.choose_relative_direction
    EOR #1                      ; the menu swaps each pair of turns, so EOR 1
                                ; turns a turn into its item and back
    TAY
    LDA #W_RELATIVE_DIRECTION
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    EOR #1
    RTS

.choose_pattern_done
    JSR vector_close_window
    LDY record
; Pack choices into a byte, choices+0 in the top two bits.
; Out: A = the byte.
; Clobbers: X.
.pack_choices
    LDA #0
    TAX
.pack_choices_loop
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ORA choices, X
    INX
    CPX #4
    BCC pack_choices_loop
    RTS

; A letter for each turn, TURN_*.
.priority_letters
    EQUS "BFRL"                 ; backwards, forwards, right, left
; The named patterns, in the order of their menu; the first choice is in
; the bottom two bits.
.pattern_presets
    EQUB PATTERN_BACK_AND_FORTH ; forwards, backwards, left, right
    EQUB PATTERN_FOLLOW_EDGES   ; forwards, right, left, backwards
    EQUB PATTERN_LEFT_WALL      ; left, forwards, right, backwards
    EQUB PATTERN_RIGHT_WALL     ; right, forwards, left, backwards
.pattern_presets_end

; Monster window, Killed by and Result: the block that kills monsters and
; the block a dead one leaves, for every monster in the level. In the game,
; a monster moving into a cell of the first kind turns it into the second
; and is gone.
.monster_killed_by
    LDA level_monster_rules
    AND #&0F
    TAY
    LDA #W_SELECT_BLOCK
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    LDX #&F0
    BMI monster_rules_store
.monster_result
    LDA level_monster_rules
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    TAY
    LDA #W_SELECT_BLOCK
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    LDX #&0F
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
.monster_rules_store
    STA ptr
    TXA
    AND level_monster_rules
    ORA ptr
    STA level_monster_rules
    JMP show_monster_window

; Unpack a byte into choices, its top two bits into choices+0.
; In: A = the byte.
; Out: A = 0.
; Clobbers: X.
.unpack_choices
    LDX #3
.unpack_choices_loop
    PHA
    AND #3
    STA choices, X
    PLA
    LSR A
    LSR A
    DEX
    BPL unpack_choices_loop
    RTS

; Count another collectable, in work (16 bits).
.count_collectable
    INC work
    BNE count_collectable_done
    INC work+1
.count_collectable_done
    RTS
; Options menu, Collects: count the collectables in the map, then ask how many
; the player must collect. The count shows as 250 if it's 256 or more; any
; number up to 255 is accepted.
.option_collects
    LDY #0
    STY ptr
    STY work
    STY work+1
    LDA #HI(level_map)
    STA ptr+1
    LDX #HI(level_end - level_map)
.option_collects_count
    LDA (ptr), Y
    PHA
    AND #&0F
    CMP #CELL_SULPHUR
    BNE option_collects_high
    JSR count_collectable
.option_collects_high
    PLA
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    CMP #CELL_SULPHUR
    BNE option_collects_next
    JSR count_collectable
.option_collects_next
    INY
    BNE option_collects_count
    INC ptr+1
    DEX
    BNE option_collects_count
.option_collects_ask
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    LDA work
    LDX work+1
    BEQ option_collects_show
    LDA #M_TOO_MANY             ; 256 or more: say so, and call it 250
    JSR vector_print_message
    LDA #250
.option_collects_show
    PHA
    LDA #M_COLLECTABLES
    JSR vector_print_line1
    PLA
    JSR print_decimal
    LDA #M_REQUIRED
    JSR vector_print_message
    LDA level_collects
    JSR print_decimal
    LDX #M_ENTER_NEW_VALUE
    JSR input_number
    DEX
    BEQ option_collects_done    ; nothing typed
    BPL option_collects_ask     ; too big
    STA level_collects
.option_collects_done
    JMP vector_close_message_box

; Options menu, Time: the time allowed, 0-255.
.option_time
    LDA #M_INITIAL_TIME
    LDX level_time
    JSR ask_number
    STA level_time
    RTS

; Ask for a new value of a number, showing the old one, until it's in range.
; Return keeps the old one; an old value out of range (or 0 where 0 isn't
; allowed) is offered as 1. ask_number allows 0-255.
; In: A = the message; X = the old value; Y = the maximum; C set if 0 is
; allowed.
; Out: A = the value.
; Clobbers: X, Y, ptr, arg, number, plot_enabled (borrowed for the maximum),
; the input buffer, the low code's zero page.
.ask_number
    SEC
    LDY #255
.ask_number_limited
    PHP
    STA arg
    STY plot_enabled
    TXA
    BNE ask_number_check
    BCC ask_number_default
.ask_number_check
    CPX plot_enabled
    BEQ ask_number_start
    BCC ask_number_start
.ask_number_default
    LDX #1
.ask_number_start
    STX number
.ask_number_loop
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    LDA arg
    JSR vector_print_line1
    LDA number
    JSR print_decimal
    LDX #M_ENTER_NEW_VALUE
    JSR input_number
    CMP plot_enabled
    BEQ ask_number_entered
    BCS ask_number_loop
.ask_number_entered
    DEX
    BMI ask_number_check_zero   ; a number
    BNE ask_number_loop         ; too big
    LDA number                  ; nothing typed: the old one
.ask_number_check_zero
    PLP
    PHP
    TAY
    BNE ask_number_done
    BCC ask_number_loop
.ask_number_done
    PLP
    PHA
    JSR vector_close_message_box
    PLA
    RTS

; Options menu, Graphics: the sprites for walls one and two, the collectable
; and the fatal trap (which squares show each one's second picture), and the
; level's four colours, set as they're chosen.
.option_graphics
    LDA level_sprites
    JSR unpack_choices
    LDA #0                      ; (it is already)
.option_graphics_loop
    PHA
    LDA #W_GRAPHICS
    JSR open_window
    PLA
    JSR menu_select
    CMP #I_GRAPHICS_OK
    BNE option_graphics_choice
    JSR pack_choices
    STA level_sprites
    JMP vector_close_window
.option_graphics_choice
    PHA
    CMP #I_GRAPHICS_COLOURS
    BCC option_graphics_sprite
    SBC #I_GRAPHICS_COLOURS     ; first to fourth colour
    STA work
    TAY
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA work+1
    LDA level_palette, Y
    AND #&0F
    TAY
    LDA #W_COLOURS
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    ORA work+1
    LDY work
    STA level_palette, Y
    JSR set_palette_entry
.option_graphics_next
    JSR vector_close_window
    PLA
    JMP option_graphics_loop
.option_graphics_sprite
    TAY
    STY work
    LDX choices, Y
    LDY sprite_items, X
    LDA #W_SPRITES
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    TAX
    LDA sprite_codes, X
    LDX work
    STA choices, X
    BPL option_graphics_next
; The code for each item of the sprites menu (Sprite A, Sprite B, Patterned,
; and a fourth item the menu doesn't have), and the item for each code.
; ALTERNATE_EVEN's item is past the menu's end, so the menu starts at the top
; for it.
sprites_menu = {ALTERNATE_NONE, ALTERNATE_ALL, ALTERNATE_ODD, ALTERNATE_EVEN}
.sprite_codes
    EQUB sprites_menu
.sprite_items
    EQUB FIND(sprites_menu, ALTERNATE_NONE..ALTERNATE_ALL)
; Options menu, Puzzle: which one, then its window until OK (whose handler
; pops back out of here). Help's Find puzzle comes in at edit_puzzle.
.option_puzzle
    LDA #PUZZLES
    LDX #M_WHICH_PUZZLE
    JSR choose_record
.edit_puzzle
    LDA record
    LSR A
    LSR A
    STA puzzle
    LDA #0
    STA work
.edit_puzzle_loop
    LDA #W_PUZZLE
    JSR open_window
    LDA #M_PUZZLE_NAME_AT
    JSR vector_print_message
    JSR print_puzzle_name
    LDA work
    JSR menu_select
    STA work
    LDY #handlers(puzzle_handlers_ptr)
    JSR jump_to_handler
    JMP edit_puzzle_loop

; Puzzle window, Type. The next block is the cell in front of the player. A
; swap next block puzzle checks that itself (block A becomes B, or B A), so
; its condition's next-block check is cleared here, and the Conditions
; window then shows Check next: ticked and won't change it or the block.
.puzzle_type
    LDA #W_PUZZLE_TYPES
    JSR open_window
    LDY puzzle
    LDA level_puzzle_types, Y
    AND #PUZZLE_ACTION
    JSR menu_select
    STA ptr
    CMP #PUZZLE_SWAP_NEXT
    BNE puzzle_type_store
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects+3, Y
    AND #&FF EOR CONDITION_CHECK_CELL
    STA level_puzzle_effects+3, Y
.puzzle_type_store
    LDY puzzle
    LDA level_puzzle_types, Y
    AND #&FF EOR PUZZLE_ACTION
    ORA ptr
    STA level_puzzle_types, Y
    JMP vector_close_window

; Print a puzzle's ten-character name.
; In: record (or A, for print_puzzle_name_at) = the puzzle times 4, for the
; first eight characters; puzzle = the puzzle, for the last two.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y.
.print_puzzle_name
    LDA record
.print_puzzle_name_at
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDX #PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD
.print_puzzle_name_loop
    LDA level_names, Y
    JSR OSWRCH
    INY
    DEX
    BNE print_puzzle_name_loop
    LDA puzzle
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDA level_name_ends, Y
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDA level_name_ends+1, Y
    JMP OSWRCH

; Puzzle window, Name. Return alone keeps the old one; a shorter one is padded
; with spaces.
.puzzle_name
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    LDA #M_OLD_NAME
    JSR vector_print_line1
    JSR print_puzzle_name
    LDA #PUZZLE_NAME_LENGTH
    LDX #M_PUZZLE_NAME
    JSR input_text
    JSR pad_input
    LDA ptr
    BEQ puzzle_name_done
    LDA record
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDX #0
.puzzle_name_copy
    JSR name_char
    STA level_names, Y
    INY
    INX
    CPX #PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD
    BCC puzzle_name_copy
    LDA puzzle
    ASL A
    TAY
    JSR name_char
    STA level_name_ends, Y
    INX
    JSR name_char
    STA level_name_ends+1, Y
.puzzle_name_done
    JSR vector_close_message_box
    JMP vector_close_window

; A character for a name.
; In: X = a position in the input buffer.
; Out: A = the character there, the Return (or anything below a space) as a
; space.
.name_char
    LDA input_buffer, X
    CMP #' '
    BCS name_char_done
    LDA #' '
.name_char_done
    RTS

; Puzzle window, Status: three flags in a window of their own, until OK. The
; puzzle's object, its number mod 8 plus 1, goes over the 1 of "Use object
; 1:": with that ticked, using or throwing that object is what tries the
; puzzle (the game tries object n's puzzles n, n + 8, n + 16 and n + 24);
; without, walking onto its position does.
.puzzle_status
    LDA #W_PUZZLE_STATUS
    JSR open_window
    LDA #M_STATUS_NUMBER_AT
    JSR vector_print_message
    LDA puzzle
    AND #OBJECTS - 1
    CLC
    ADC #'1'
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDA #0
    STA work+1
.puzzle_status_loop
    LDY puzzle
    LDA level_puzzle_types, Y
    PHA
    AND #PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT
    LDY #item_line(I_STATUS_USE_OBJECT)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    PLA
    PHA
    AND #PUZZLE_OFF
    EOR #PUZZLE_OFF
    LDY #item_line(I_STATUS_TURNED_ON)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    PLA
    AND #PUZZLE_REUSABLE
    LDY #item_line(I_STATUS_REUSABLE)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    LDA work+1
    JSR menu_select
    STA work+1
    LDY #handlers(status_handlers_ptr)
    JSR jump_to_handler
    JMP puzzle_status_loop

; Conditions window, Collects.:, and the status window's flags.
.condition_collects
    LDA #PUZZLE_COUNTS_COLLECTS
    BNE puzzle_toggle_flag
.status_use_object
    LDA #PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT
    BNE puzzle_toggle_flag
.status_turned_on
    LDA #PUZZLE_OFF
    BNE puzzle_toggle_flag
.status_reusable
    LDA #PUZZLE_REUSABLE
.puzzle_toggle_flag
    LDY puzzle
    EOR level_puzzle_types, Y
    STA level_puzzle_types, Y
    RTS

; Puzzle window, Conditions: what has to be true for the puzzle to happen,
; in its own window until OK.
.puzzle_conditions
    JSR vector_close_window
    JSR open_conditions_window
    LDA #0
    STA work+1
.puzzle_conditions_loop
    LDA puzzle
    ASL A
    PHA
    TAY
    LDA level_puzzle_positions, Y
    AND #IGNORE
    EOR #IGNORE
    LDY #item_line(I_CHECK_X)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    PLA
    TAY
    LDA level_puzzle_positions+1, Y
    AND #IGNORE
    EOR #IGNORE
    LDY #item_line(I_CHECK_Y)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects+3, Y
    PHA
    LDY puzzle
    LDA level_puzzle_types, Y
    AND #PUZZLE_ACTION
    CMP #PUZZLE_SWAP_NEXT
    BEQ puzzle_conditions_check_next    ; ticked: A is nonzero
    PLA
    PHA
    AND #CONDITION_CHECK_CELL
.puzzle_conditions_check_next
    LDY #item_line(I_CHECK_NEXT)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    PLA
    AND #CONDITION_CHECK_DIRECTION
    LDY #item_line(I_CHECK_DIRECTION)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    LDY puzzle
    LDA level_puzzle_types, Y
    AND #PUZZLE_COUNTS_COLLECTS
    LDY #item_line(I_CONDITION_COLLECTS)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    LDA work+1
    JSR menu_select
    STA work+1
    LDY #handlers(conditions_handlers_ptr)
    JSR jump_to_handler
    JMP puzzle_conditions_loop

; Return from the caller instead if the puzzle swaps the next block.
; Clobbers: A, Y.
.unless_swap_next
    LDY puzzle
    LDA level_puzzle_types, Y
    AND #PUZZLE_ACTION
    CMP #PUZZLE_SWAP_NEXT
    BNE unless_swap_next_done
    PLA
    PLA
.unless_swap_next_done
    RTS

; Conditions window, Check next: and Check dir.: flags.
.condition_check_next
    JSR unless_swap_next
    LDA #CONDITION_CHECK_CELL
    BNE condition_toggle_flag
.condition_check_direction
    LDA #CONDITION_CHECK_DIRECTION
.condition_toggle_flag
    LDY record
    EOR level_puzzle_effects+3, Y
    STA level_puzzle_effects+3, Y
    RTS

; Conditions window, Check X: and Check Y:, which flip the IGNORE flag in the
; puzzle's x or y (ticked while it's clear).
.condition_check_x
    CLC
    BCC condition_toggle_position
.condition_check_y
    SEC
.condition_toggle_position
    LDA puzzle
    ROL A
    TAY
    LDA level_puzzle_positions, Y
    AND #IGNORE OR COORDINATE_BITS
    EOR #IGNORE
    STA level_puzzle_positions, Y
    RTS

; Make the compass window offer four directions or eight, by changing its
; height in WDATA (all eight lines are there).
; In: A = 4 or 8.
; Clobbers: X, Y, ptr.
.set_direction_menu_size
    PHA
    LDA #W_COMPASS
    JSR vector_window_address
    STX ptr
    STY ptr+1
    LDY #WINDOW_HEIGHT
    PLA
    STA (ptr), Y
    RTS

; Conditions window, Next block: which block must be in front of the player,
; which also turns the check on.
.condition_next_block
    JSR unless_swap_next
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects+3, Y
    AND #CONDITION_CELL
    TAY
    LDA #W_SELECT_BLOCK
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    ORA #CONDITION_CHECK_CELL
    LDX #CONDITION_CHECK_DIRECTION OR CONDITION_DIRECTION   ; what to keep
    BMI condition_store
; Conditions window, Direction: which way the player must be going, which
; also turns the check on.
.condition_direction
    LDA #4                      ; north, south, east and west
    JSR set_direction_menu_size
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects+3, Y
    AND #CONDITION_DIRECTION
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    TAX
    LDY direction_items, X
    LDA #W_COMPASS
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    TAY
    LDA direction_codes, Y
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ORA #CONDITION_CHECK_DIRECTION
    LDX #CONDITION_CHECK_CELL OR CONDITION_CELL             ; what to keep
.condition_store
    STA ptr
    LDY record
    TXA
    AND level_puzzle_effects+3, Y
    ORA ptr
    STA level_puzzle_effects+3, Y
.open_conditions_window
    LDA #W_CONDITIONS
    JMP open_window

; Conditions window, Position: where the puzzle is, put with the cursor as
; for an object. The position's IGNORE flags stay as they are.
.condition_position
    JSR vector_close_window
    LDA puzzle
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDA level_puzzle_positions, Y
    AND #COORDINATE_BITS
    STA cursor_x
    LDA level_puzzle_positions+1, Y
    AND #COORDINATE_BITS
    STA cursor_y
.condition_position_define
    LDX #W_PUZZLE_LOCATION
    JSR get_key_no_plot
    CMP #' '
    BEQ open_conditions_window
    CMP #CR
    BNE condition_position_define
    LDA puzzle
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDA level_puzzle_positions, Y
    AND #IGNORE
    ORA cursor_x
    STA level_puzzle_positions, Y
    LDA level_puzzle_positions+1, Y
    AND #IGNORE
    ORA cursor_y
    STA level_puzzle_positions+1, Y
    JMP open_conditions_window
; Files menu, Load level: ask for the file and its editing code, load it over
; the level being edited, and keep it only if the code matches; otherwise
; start a new level, so the old one is lost either way.
.files_load
    LDA #M_LOADING
    JSR ask_filename
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    LDA #M_LOADING
    JSR vector_print_line1
    JSR input_editing_code
    INC loading                 ; an error now clears the level
    LDA #OSFILE_LOAD
    JSR level_file
    DEC loading
    LDX #2                      ; three bytes
.files_load_check_code
    LDA level_code, X
    CMP ptr+1, X
    BNE files_load_wrong_code
    DEX
    BPL files_load_check_code
    JMP vector_draw_map
.files_load_wrong_code
    JSR new_level
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    LDA #M_WRONG_CODE
    JSR vector_print_line1
    LDA #M_PRESS_ANY_KEY
    JSR vector_print_message
    JSR wait_for_key
    JMP vector_close_message_box

; Read a six-digit editing code and encode it as level_code is kept: each
; pair of digits as a BCD byte, its odd and even bits swapped and then
; rotated right a place.
; Out: ptr+1 to ptr+3 = the code (overlapping work).
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr, work, the input buffer.
.input_editing_code
    LDA #'0'
    STA input_min_char
    LDA #'9'
    STA input_max_char
    LDA #6                      ; digits
    LDX #M_ENTER_CODE
    JSR input_line
    LDY #2
    LDX #4
.input_editing_code_pair
    LDA input_buffer+1, X
    SEC
    SBC #'0'
    STA ptr
    LDA input_buffer, X
    SEC
    SBC #'0'
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ORA ptr
    PHA
    AND #%01010101
    ASL A
    STA ptr
    PLA
    AND #%10101010
    LSR A
    ORA ptr
    PHA
    LSR A                       ; bit 0 into the carry
    PLA
    ROR A                       ; and round to bit 7
    STA ptr+1, Y
    DEX
    DEX
    DEY
    BPL input_editing_code_pair
    RTS

; Files menu, Edit code: give the level a new editing code.
.files_edit_code
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    JSR input_editing_code
    LDX #2
.files_edit_code_store
    LDA ptr+1, X
    STA level_code, X
    DEX
    BPL files_edit_code_store
    JMP vector_close_message_box

; Files menu, Save level.
.files_save
    LDA #M_SAVING
    JSR ask_filename
    LDA #OSFILE_SAVE
    JSR level_file
    JMP vector_close_message_box

; Load or save the level, with a one-line text window for the filing
; system's messages and interrupts off (as entry has them for its loads),
; then set the level's palette. level_file_done undoes the window and the
; SEI; brk_handler uses it too, after an error in OSFILE.
; In: A = the OSFILE call; osfile_block filled in by ask_filename.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y.
.level_file
    PHA
    LDA #M_FILING_WINDOW
    JSR vector_print_line2
    PLA
    LDX #LO(osfile_block)
    LDY #HI(osfile_block)
    SEI
    JSR OSFILE
    JSR vector_set_level_palette
.level_file_done
    CLI
    LDA #M_RESET_WINDOWS
    JMP vector_print_message

; Ask for a filename and set up osfile_block for it; the name is copied with
; its Return, as OSFILE wants it, except that a 12-character name's Return is
; then overwritten (see filename).
; In: A = the message saying what's happening.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr, the input buffer.
.ask_filename
    PHA
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    PLA
    JSR vector_print_line1
    LDA #filename_end - filename
    LDX #M_ENTER_FILENAME
    JSR input_text
    LDY ptr
.ask_filename_copy
    LDA input_buffer, Y
    STA filename, Y
    DEY
    BPL ask_filename_copy
    LDY #osfile_template_end - osfile_template - 1
.ask_filename_block
    LDA osfile_template, Y
    STA osfile_block, Y
    DEY
    BPL ask_filename_block
    RTS

; Room for a filename of 12 characters, holding an author's mark until one
; is typed. A 12-character name's Return lands on osfile_block, which
; ask_filename then fills in, leaving the name followed by "0" and &1E (the
; low and high bytes of this address). The longest DFS name, ":0.$.ABCDEFG",
; is 12 characters, so typed in full its leaf gains an eighth character, the
; "0", and DFS refuses it: Save and Load level show "Error 204 has occurred !"
; and "Bad name" and nothing is written; a Load also loses the level being
; edited, as any failed load does. 11 characters are safe.
.filename
    EQUS "_Ian Holmes_"
.filename_end
; OSFILE's control block, filled in from the template before use (stray
; bytes until then).
.osfile_block
    EQUB &00, &00, &A1, &25, &00, &00, &23, &A5
    EQUB &63, &20, &4C, &18, &A2, &12, &20, &C4
    EQUB &12, &C5
; The level is saved with its own address as load address, and an exec
; address of &8380 that means nothing here.
.osfile_template
    EQUW filename
    EQUD level                  ; load address
    EQUD &8380                  ; exec address; when loading, its low byte
                                ; being nonzero tells OSFILE to load the file
                                ; at its own load address
    EQUD level                  ; start of the data to save
    EQUD level_end              ; and its end
.osfile_template_end
; Puzzle window, Effects: what the puzzle does, by type. Each effect keeps
; its details in the puzzle's first three effect bytes (the fourth is the
; conditions); see each editor below. Most run a window of their own until
; its OK.
;
; Below, +0, +1 and +2 are those three bytes, level_puzzle_effects + record
; + n: what the game calls a trigger's A, X and Y (PUZZLE_* in
; leveldata.6502inc says what each type does with them).

; Place monster: +0 is the x times 4 plus the monster's number (0-3), +1 its
; pattern, and +2 the y times 4 plus its direction (DIRECTION_*, one of the
; four).
.effect_place_monster
    JSR vector_close_window
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    PHA
    LSR A
    LSR A
    STA cursor_x
    PLA
    AND #MONSTERS - 1
    STA arg                     ; monster number
    LDA level_puzzle_effects+2, Y
    PHA
    LSR A
    LSR A
    STA cursor_y
    PLA
    AND #3
    STA work+1                  ; direction
    LDA #W_PLACE_MONSTER
    LDY #handlers(place_monster_handlers_ptr)
    BNE effect_editor
; Move monster: +0 is the direction (DIRECTION_*, or MONSTER_GONE) and +1
; the monster's number times 4, where the fifth item, All monsters, makes it
; 16.
.effect_move_monster
    LDA #W_MOVE_MONSTER
    LDY #handlers(move_monster_handlers_ptr)
    BNE effect_editor
; Charge object: +0 is the object's number and +2 its charges.
.effect_charge_object
    LDA #W_CHARGE_OBJECT
    LDY #handlers(charge_handlers_ptr)
    BNE effect_editor
; Throw object: +0 is the object's number and +2 how far it goes.
.effect_throw_object
    LDA #W_THROW_OBJECT
    LDY #handlers(throw_handlers_ptr)
    BNE effect_editor
; Move block: +0 is the direction (DIRECTION_*, any of the eight), and +1
; and +2 the block's x and y.
.effect_move_block
    LDA #W_MOVE_BLOCK
    LDY #handlers(move_block_handlers_ptr)
    BNE effect_editor
; Place block: +0 is the block, and +1 and +2 the cell's x and y.
.effect_place_block
    LDA #W_PLACE_BLOCK
    LDY #handlers(place_block_handlers_ptr)
; Run an effect's window: its menu goes to its handler table, until the
; handler for OK pops out of here, back to edit_puzzle_loop.
; In: A = the window; Y = the handler table's number.
.effect_editor
    STA effect_window
    STY effect_table
    JSR vector_close_window
    LDA #0
    PHA
.effect_editor_loop
    LDA effect_window
    JSR open_window
    PLA
    JSR menu_select
    PHA
    LDY effect_table
    JSR jump_to_handler
    JMP effect_editor_loop

; Puzzle window, Effects: the editor for the puzzle's type.
.puzzle_effects
    LDY puzzle
    LDA level_puzzle_types, Y
    AND #PUZZLE_ACTION
    LDY #handlers(effect_handlers_ptr)
    JMP jump_to_handler

; Disorientate: nothing to set, just a window saying what it does.
.effect_disorientate
    JSR beep
    LDA #W_DISORIENTATE
    JSR open_window
    JSR wait_for_key
    JMP vector_close_window

; Place and move block windows, Block position: +1 and +2, x and y.
.effect_block_position
    LDA #0
    BEQ effect_position
; Teleport: +1 and +2 are where to, kept 4 less in each direction, as the
; start is.
.effect_teleport
    LDA #4
; Put the effect's position (+1 and +2) with the cursor: Return puts it
; there, Space leaves it as it was.
; In: arg = how much less than the cell the position is kept: 0, or 4 for
; the top left of the game's view.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr, work, screen_ptr, the low code's zero page.
.effect_position
    STA arg
    JSR vector_close_window
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects+1, Y
    CLC
    ADC arg
    AND #COORDINATE_BITS
    STA cursor_x
    LDA level_puzzle_effects+2, Y
    CLC
    ADC arg
    AND #COORDINATE_BITS
    STA cursor_y
.effect_position_define
    LDX #W_PUZZLE_LOCATION
    JSR get_key_no_plot
    CMP #' '
    BEQ effect_position_done
    CMP #CR
    BNE effect_position_define
    LDY record
    LDA cursor_x
    SEC
    SBC arg
    STA level_puzzle_effects+1, Y
    LDA cursor_y
    SEC
    SBC arg
    STA level_puzzle_effects+2, Y
.effect_position_done
    RTS

; Next block, and the place block window's Block type: +0 is the block
; (CELL_*).
.effect_block_type
    LDX record
    LDY level_puzzle_effects, X
    LDA #W_SELECT_BLOCK
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    LDY record
    STA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    RTS

; Set levels: +0 holds the flags SET_LEVELS_KEEP_TIME and
; SET_LEVELS_KEEP_COLLECTS, +1 the new time and +2 the new number of
; collectables needed. The window ticks "Change:" while a value's KEEP flag
; is clear.
.effect_set_levels
    LDA #W_SET_LEVELS
    JSR open_window
    LDA #0
    PHA
.effect_set_levels_loop
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    PHA
    AND #SET_LEVELS_KEEP_TIME
    EOR #SET_LEVELS_KEEP_TIME
    LDY #item_line(I_TIME_CHANGE)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    PLA
    AND #SET_LEVELS_KEEP_COLLECTS
    EOR #SET_LEVELS_KEEP_COLLECTS
    LDY #item_line(I_COLLECTS_CHANGE)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    PLA
    JSR menu_select
    PHA
    LDY #handlers(set_levels_handlers_ptr)
    JSR jump_to_handler
    JMP effect_set_levels_loop
; Set levels window, the Change: items: flip the value's KEEP flag.
.levels_change_time
    LDA #SET_LEVELS_KEEP_TIME
    BMI levels_toggle_flag
.levels_change_collects
    LDA #SET_LEVELS_KEEP_COLLECTS
.levels_toggle_flag
    LDY record
    EOR level_puzzle_effects, Y
    STA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    RTS
; Set levels window, Time and Collects.: ask for the new value. Giving one
; also turns its change on.
.levels_time
    LDY record
    LDX level_puzzle_effects+1, Y
    LDA #M_REVISED_TIME
    JSR ask_number
    LDY record
    STA level_puzzle_effects+1, Y
    LDA #SET_LEVELS_KEEP_COLLECTS   ; keep only the other flag
    BPL levels_clear_flag
.levels_collects
    LDY record
    LDX level_puzzle_effects+2, Y
    LDA #M_COLLECTABLES_REQUIRED
    JSR ask_number
    LDY record
    STA level_puzzle_effects+2, Y
    LDA #SET_LEVELS_KEEP_TIME
.levels_clear_flag
    AND level_puzzle_effects, Y
    STA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    RTS

; Swap next block: +0 is block A and +1 block B (so each item's number is
; the offset of its byte).
.effect_swap_next
    LDA #0
    PHA
.effect_swap_next_loop
    LDA #W_SWAP_NEXT
    JSR open_window
    PLA
    JSR menu_select
    CMP #I_SWAP_NEXT_OK
    BEQ effect_swap_next_done
    PHA
    ADC record
    TAX
    LDY level_puzzle_effects, X
    LDA #W_SELECT_BLOCK
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    TAX
    PLA
    PHA
    CLC
    ADC record
    TAY
    TXA
    STA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    JMP effect_swap_next_loop
.effect_swap_next_done
    JMP vector_close_window

; Move block window, Direction: +0, any of the eight.
.effect_block_direction
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    AND #7
    LDX #8                      ; all eight ways
    JSR choose_compass_direction
    LDY record
    STA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    RTS

; Choose from the compass window, four directions or eight.
; In: A = the current direction, DIRECTION_*; X = 4 or 8.
; Out: A = the direction chosen.
; Clobbers: X, Y, ptr, the low code's zero page.
.choose_compass_direction
    PHA
    TXA
    JSR set_direction_menu_size
    PLA
    LDY #compass_codes_end - compass_codes - 1
.choose_compass_find
    CMP compass_codes, Y
    BEQ choose_compass_menu
    DEY
    BNE choose_compass_find     ; north, item 0, if nothing else
.choose_compass_menu
    LDA #W_COMPASS
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    TAY
    LDA compass_codes, Y
    RTS
; The direction for each item.
.compass_codes
    EQUB DIRECTION_UP, DIRECTION_DOWN, DIRECTION_RIGHT, DIRECTION_LEFT
    EQUB DIRECTION_UP_LEFT, DIRECTION_UP_RIGHT
    EQUB DIRECTION_DOWN_LEFT, DIRECTION_DOWN_RIGHT
.compass_codes_end

; Detonate object: +0 is the object's number, and +2 the same times 4.
.effect_detonate_object
    JSR choose_object_number
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA level_puzzle_effects+2, Y
    RTS

; Throw and charge object windows, Object no., and Detonate object: +0, the
; object's number, asked as 1-8 and kept as 0-7.
; Out: A = the number kept; Y = record.
; Clobbers: X, ptr, arg, number, plot_enabled, the input buffer, the low
; code's zero page.
.choose_object_number
    CLC
    LDA #M_OBJECT_NUMBER
    LDY record
    LDX level_puzzle_effects, Y
    INX
    LDY #OBJECTS
    JSR ask_number_limited
    SEC
    SBC #1
    LDY record
    STA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    RTS

; Throw object window, Distance: +2, 1-63 cells.
.throw_distance
    LDA #M_DISTANCE
    LDX #1                      ; offered when the old value is 0
    LDY #MAP_SIZE - 1           ; the most (and a mask for the old value)
    CLC
    BNE effect_ask_amount
; Charge object window, No.of charges: +2, 0-31.
.charge_count
    LDA #M_CHARGES
    LDX #0
    LDY #OBJECT_CHARGES
    SEC
; Ask for a new value of +2 with ask_number_limited, offering its old value
; masked by Y, or X if that's 0.
; In: A = the message; X = the value offered for 0; Y = the most, also the
; mask; C set if 0 is allowed.
.effect_ask_amount
    PHA
    STX ptr
    LDX record
    TYA
    AND level_puzzle_effects+2, X
    BNE effect_ask_amount_current
    LDA ptr
.effect_ask_amount_current
    TAX
    PLA
    JSR ask_number_limited
    LDY record
    STA level_puzzle_effects+2, Y
    RTS

; Turn on and turn off puzzle: +0, +1 and +2 are puzzles A, B and C, asked
; as 1-32 and kept as 0-31. "Single:" is ticked when they're all the same,
; and choosing it makes them so (B and C copy A); choosing it again does
; nothing.
.effect_turn_puzzle
    LDA #0
.effect_turn_puzzle_loop
    PHA
    LDA #W_SELECT_PUZZLES
    JSR open_window
    LDX #0
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    CMP level_puzzle_effects+1, Y
    BNE effect_turn_puzzle_tick
    CMP level_puzzle_effects+2, Y
    BNE effect_turn_puzzle_tick
    INX
.effect_turn_puzzle_tick
    STX ptr
    TXA
    LDY #item_line(I_SINGLE)
    JSR vector_tick_line
    PLA
    JSR menu_select
    CMP #I_SELECT_PUZZLES_OK
    BCC effect_turn_puzzle_single
    JMP vector_close_window
.effect_turn_puzzle_single
    CMP #I_SINGLE
    BCC effect_turn_puzzle_choose
    LDX ptr
    BNE effect_turn_puzzle_loop
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    STA level_puzzle_effects+1, Y
    STA level_puzzle_effects+2, Y
    LDA #I_SINGLE
    BNE effect_turn_puzzle_loop
.effect_turn_puzzle_choose
    PHA
    ADC record
    STA keys_acted_on           ; borrowed: which byte
    TAY
    LDX level_puzzle_effects, Y
    INX
    LDY #PUZZLES
    LDA #M_OLD_PUZZLE_NUMBER
    CLC
    JSR ask_number_limited
    SEC
    SBC #1
    LDY keys_acted_on
    STA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    PLA
    BPL effect_turn_puzzle_loop

; Push crates: +0 is how many (0-255).
.effect_push_crates
    LDY record
    LDX level_puzzle_effects, Y
    LDA #M_NUMBER_OF_CRATES
    JSR ask_number
    LDY record
    STA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    RTS

; Move monster window, Monster no.: +1 is the item's number times 4.
.move_monster_number
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects+1, Y
    LSR A
    LSR A
    TAY
    LDA #W_MONSTER_NUMBER
    JSR choose_from_window_at
    ASL A
    ASL A
    LDY record
    STA level_puzzle_effects+1, Y
    RTS

; Move monster window, Direction: +0.
.move_monster_direction
    LDY record
    LDX level_puzzle_effects, Y
    JSR choose_direction
    STA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    RTS

; Move next block: +0 is a turn (TURN_*) times 4, the way the game indexes
; its turns.
.effect_move_next_block
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    LSR A
    LSR A
    JSR choose_relative_direction
    ASL A
    ASL A
    LDY record
    STA level_puzzle_effects, Y
    RTS

; Place monster window: Monster no., Position and Direction work on copies
; (arg, the cursor and work+1) until OK (place_monster_ok) stores them;
; Pattern goes straight into +1.
.place_monster_number
    LDA #M_MONSTER_NUMBER
    LDY #MONSTERS
    LDX arg
    INX
    CLC
    JSR ask_number_limited
    SEC
    SBC #1
    STA arg
    RTS
.place_monster_position
    JSR vector_close_window
    LDA cursor_x
    PHA
    LDA cursor_y
    PHA
.place_monster_position_loop
    LDX #W_MONSTER_LOCATION
    JSR get_key_no_plot
    CMP #CR
    BEQ place_monster_position_keep
    CMP #' '
    BNE place_monster_position_loop
    PLA
    STA cursor_y
    PLA
    STA cursor_x
    RTS
.place_monster_position_keep
    PLA
    PLA
    RTS
.place_monster_direction
    LDX #4                      ; just north, south, east and west
    LDA work+1
    JSR choose_compass_direction
    STA work+1
    RTS
.place_monster_pattern
    LDY record
    LDA level_puzzle_effects+1, Y
    JSR choose_pattern
    STA level_puzzle_effects+1, Y
    RTS

; help_find_puzzle: on to the next puzzle down, or give up after the first.
.find_puzzle_next
    DEC record
    BPL find_puzzle_compare
    JMP vector_close_message_box

; Pad the input buffer with spaces to PUZZLE_NAME_LENGTH, from the end of the
; text.
; In: ptr = the number of characters.
; Clobbers: A, Y.
.pad_input
    LDY ptr
    LDA #' '
.pad_input_loop
    STA input_buffer, Y
    INY
    CPY #PUZZLE_NAME_LENGTH + 1 ; over the Return too
    BCC pad_input_loop
    RTS
; Help menu, Find puzzle: look a puzzle up by name, ignoring case (bit 5),
; say which it is and edit it. It searches from the last puzzle down, so of
; two with one name it finds the later; with none it just closes the box.
.help_find_puzzle
    JSR vector_close_window
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    LDA #PUZZLE_NAME_LENGTH
    LDX #M_PUZZLE_NAME
    JSR input_text
    JSR pad_input
    LDA #PUZZLES - 1
    STA record                  ; the puzzle number, for now
.find_puzzle_compare
    LDA record
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A                       ; times PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD
    TAY
    LDX #0
.find_puzzle_compare_name
    LDA level_names, Y
    EOR input_buffer, X
    AND #&FF EOR &20
    BNE find_puzzle_next
    INY
    INX
    CPX #PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD
    BCC find_puzzle_compare_name
    LDA record
    ASL A
    TAY
.find_puzzle_compare_end
    LDA level_name_ends, Y
    EOR input_buffer, X
    AND #&FF EOR &20
    BNE find_puzzle_next
    INY
    INX
    CPX #PUZZLE_NAME_LENGTH
    BCC find_puzzle_compare_end
    JSR vector_open_message_box
    LDA #M_NAME_QUOTE           ; Name: "<name>" Puzzle <n>
    JSR vector_print_line1
    LDA record
    STA puzzle
    ASL A
    ASL A
    JSR print_puzzle_name_at
    LDA #M_QUOTE_PUZZLE
    JSR vector_print_message
    LDX record
    INX
.find_puzzle_found
    TXA
    JSR print_decimal
    LDA #M_PRESS_ANY_KEY
    JSR vector_print_line2
    JSR wait_for_key
    JSR vector_close_message_box
    LDA record
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA record
    JMP edit_puzzle

; Options menu, Clear: start a new level, if the user is sure.
.option_clear
    JSR vector_close_window
    JSR confirm
    JMP new_level

.unused_rts
    RTS

; OSWORD 0's control block for input_line.
.input_block
    EQUW input_buffer
.input_max_length
    EQUB 0
.input_min_char                 ; also the RDCHV filter's limits
    EQUB 0
.input_max_char
    EQUB &FF

; The pipe each direction (MOVE_*) can go into.
.pipe_across
    EQUB CELL_PIPE_ACROSS, CELL_PIPE_DOWN, CELL_PIPE_ACROSS, CELL_PIPE_DOWN
; A direction's step: dy for MOVE_* n is at direction_dy+n, dx at
; direction_dx+n, the two tables overlapping.
.direction_dy
    EQUB 0
.direction_dx
    EQUB -1, 0, 1, 0

; The block menu's blocks, in order. The keys 0-9 and A-F pick its items by
; number, so 6 is wall 2, not a crate.
block_menu = {CELL_FLOOR, CELL_SE_CURVE, CELL_SW_CURVE, CELL_NE_CURVE,
    CELL_NW_CURVE, CELL_WALL_1, CELL_WALL, CELL_SULPHUR, CELL_LAVA, CELL_FIRE,
    CELL_CRATE, CELL_OBJECT, CELL_PIPE_ACROSS, CELL_PIPE_DOWN, CELL_JUNCTION,
    CELL_BARRICADE}
; Two tables in one, a nibble each: entry n's top nibble is block n's item
