```6502
; in the block menu, and its bottom nibble is item n's block.
.block_menu_map
    EQUB FIND(block_menu, 0..15) * 16 + block_menu

; Each menu's handlers, one per item: jump_to_handler finds a table by its
; number (handlers()) among the pointers in zero page, menu_tables.
.options_handlers
    EQUW option_start, option_finish, option_object, option_monster
    EQUW option_puzzle, option_collects, option_graphics, option_time
    EQUW option_clear, do_nothing
.object_handlers
    EQUW object_position, object_exists_toggle, object_sprite, object_charge
    EQUW object_charges_toggle, object_vanish_toggle, object_throw_toggle
    EQUW menu_ok_drop_choice
.monster_handlers
    EQUW monster_position, monster_direction, monster_pattern
    EQUW monster_killed_by, monster_result, menu_ok_drop_choice
.puzzle_handlers
    EQUW puzzle_name, puzzle_type, puzzle_status, puzzle_conditions
    EQUW puzzle_effects, menu_ok
.status_handlers
    EQUW status_use_object, status_turned_on, status_reusable, menu_ok
.conditions_handlers
    EQUW condition_position, condition_check_x, condition_check_y
    EQUW condition_next_block, condition_check_next, condition_direction
    EQUW condition_check_direction, condition_collects, menu_ok
.files_handlers
    EQUW files_load, files_save, files_edit_code, files_exit
; By puzzle type, PUZZLE_*.
.effect_handlers
    EQUW effect_place_block, effect_move_block, effect_block_type
    EQUW effect_set_levels, effect_throw_object, effect_detonate_object
    EQUW effect_move_monster, effect_place_monster, effect_teleport
    EQUW effect_swap_next, effect_turn_puzzle, effect_turn_puzzle
    EQUW effect_charge_object, effect_push_crates, effect_move_next_block
    EQUW effect_disorientate
.place_block_handlers
    EQUW effect_block_position, effect_block_type, menu_ok_drop_choice
.set_levels_handlers
    EQUW levels_time, levels_change_time, levels_collects
    EQUW levels_change_collects, menu_ok_drop_choice
.move_block_handlers
    EQUW effect_block_position, effect_block_direction, menu_ok_drop_choice
.throw_handlers
    EQUW choose_object_number, throw_distance, menu_ok_drop_choice
.charge_handlers
    EQUW choose_object_number, charge_count, menu_ok_drop_choice
.move_monster_handlers
    EQUW move_monster_number, move_monster_direction, menu_ok_drop_choice
.place_monster_handlers
    EQUW place_monster_number, place_monster_position, place_monster_direction
    EQUW place_monster_pattern, place_monster_ok
.help_handlers
    EQUW help_find_puzzle, help_simulate, vector_close_window
; get_key's steps while travelling, by direction.
.cursor_handlers
    EQUW cursor_left, cursor_up, cursor_right, cursor_down

; Spare, all zero but for one stray byte, up to the second jump table.
.unused_space
    SKIP 115
    EQUB &20
    SKIP 76
; Entry points at fixed addresses: the second jump table (see the first, at
; the start).
.vector_text_colours
    JMP text_colours
.vector_set_level_palette
    JMP set_level_palette
.vector_print_line2
    JMP print_line2
.vector_print_line1
    JMP print_line1
.vector_print_message
    JMP print_message
.vector_vdu_sequence            ; (unused)
    JMP vdu_sequence_loop
.vector_window_address
    JMP window_address
.vector_read_map
    JMP read_map
.vector_write_map
    JMP write_map

; Start a new level: blank map, default names "Puzzle  1 " to "Puzzle 32 ",
; the default header, four dead monsters, no objects, and every puzzle turned
; off; then clear the screen and set the level's palette.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr.
.new_level
    LDA #HI(level_map)
    STA ptr+1
    LDA #0
    STA ptr
    TAY
    LDX #HI(level_end - level_map)
.new_level_clear_map
    STA (ptr), Y
    INY
    BNE new_level_clear_map
    INC ptr+1
    DEX
    BNE new_level_clear_map
    ; The eighth character of each name is the tens digit: space for 1-9,
    ; then 1, 2 and 3. Fill three overlapping runs and let "Puzzle " below
    ; overwrite the rest.
    LDA #'3'
    STA level_names + 29*8 + 7
    STA level_names + 30*8 + 7
    STA level_names + 31*8 + 7
    LDX #10 * 8 - 1
.new_level_tens
    LDA #' '
    STA level_names, X
    LDA #'1'
    STA level_names + 9*8, X
    LDA #'2'
    STA level_names + 19*8, X
    DEX
    BPL new_level_tens
    ; The last two are the units digit and a space.
    LDX #(PUZZLES - 1) * 2
.new_level_units
    LDA #' '
    STA level_name_ends+1, X
    TXA
    LSR A
    ADC #1
    JSR reduce_mod_10
    JSR reduce_mod_10
    JSR reduce_mod_10
    CLC
    ADC #'0'
    STA level_name_ends, X
    DEX
    DEX
    BPL new_level_units
    ; "Puzzle " into the first seven, from the last name back.
    LDY #0
.new_level_names
    DEY
    LDX #default_puzzle_name_end - default_puzzle_name - 1
.new_level_name
    LDA default_puzzle_name, X
    STA level_names - 1, Y
    DEY
    DEX
    BPL new_level_name
    TYA
    BNE new_level_names
    LDY #15                     ; one more than the header: harmless, as the
.new_level_header               ; objects are set below
    LDA default_header, Y
    STA level_code, Y
    DEY
    BPL new_level_header
    LDA #MONSTERS
    STA ptr
    INY
.new_level_monsters
    LDX #0
.new_level_monster
    LDA default_monster, X
    STA level_monsters, Y
    INY
    INX
    CPX #4
    BCC new_level_monster
    DEC ptr
    BNE new_level_monsters
    ; Every byte of the objects &A0, so absent; and of the puzzles, from the
    ; types to the effects, the same: a place block puzzle, turned off and
    ; tried by using its object, at (32, 32) with neither coordinate checked,
    ; and a condition of going north.
    LDA #PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT OR PUZZLE_OFF OR PUZZLE_PLACE_BLOCK
    ASSERT (PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT OR PUZZLE_OFF) == (OBJECT_ABSENT OR MAP_SIZE / 2)
    LDX #OBJECTS * 4 - 1
.new_level_objects
    STA level_objects, X
    DEX
    BPL new_level_objects
    LDX #level_map - level_puzzle_types
.new_level_puzzles
    STA level_puzzle_types - 1, X
    DEX
    BNE new_level_puzzles
    JSR clear_screen
; Set the four colours from the level's palette.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y.
.set_level_palette
    LDY #3
.set_level_palette_loop
    LDA level_palette, Y
    JSR vector_set_palette
    DEY
    BPL set_level_palette_loop
    RTS

; In: A < 40.
; Out: A less 10 if it was 10 or more (call three times for A mod 10).
.reduce_mod_10
    CMP #10
    BCC reduce_mod_10_done
    SBC #10
.reduce_mod_10_done
    RTS

.default_puzzle_name
    EQUS "Puzzle "
.default_puzzle_name_end
; The designer writes a new level's code and monsters with these. (They're
; here rather than in level.6502inc, which LEVEL1 and PL include too, because
; a macro that calls a FUNCTION leaves entries in the symbol dump of every
; file that includes it, called or not.)
MACRO EDITING_CODE digits
    EQUB code_byte(digits[0..1]), code_byte(digits[2..3]), code_byte(digits[4..5])
ENDMACRO

; A monster's record: its cell, kept in quarter cells (times 4), the
; direction it's going and its pattern.
MACRO MONSTER x, y, direction, pattern
    EQUB x * 4, y * 4, direction, pattern
ENDMACRO

; A new level's code, palette, start, collectables, time, finish, monster
; rules and sprites.
.default_header
    EDITING_CODE "123456"
    EQUB palette_entry(0, COLOUR_BLACK), palette_entry(1, COLOUR_BLUE)
    EQUB palette_entry(2, COLOUR_YELLOW), palette_entry(3, COLOUR_RED)
    EQUB MAP_SIZE / 2 - 4, MAP_SIZE / 2 - 4     ; start (32, 32)
    EQUB 0                      ; collectables needed
    EQUB 250                    ; time
    EQUB MAP_SIZE / 2, MAP_SIZE / 2             ; finish
    EQUB CELL_LAVA * 16 + CELL_LAVA             ; monsters die in fatal traps,
                                                ; leaving the trap
    EQUB ALTERNATE_NONE         ; sprites: the first picture for all four
; Each monster: in the middle, dead, back and forth.
.default_monster
    MONSTER MAP_SIZE / 2, MAP_SIZE / 2, MONSTER_GONE, PATTERN_BACK_AND_FORTH

line1_tab = os_tab(MESSAGE_LEFT, MESSAGE_LINE_1)
line2_tab = os_tab(MESSAGE_LEFT, MESSAGE_LINE_2)
; Print a message on the message box's second line (print_line2), its first
; (print_line1), or wherever the text cursor is (print_message). The OS
; thinks the screen is 40 columns of 640 bytes, so the lines' TAB(34,12) and
; TAB(10,11) land two rows apart in our 64 columns, both at column 4.
; In: A = the message number.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, window_ptr.
.print_line2
    JSR window_address
    LDA #line2_tab[0]
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDA #line2_tab[1]
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDA #line2_tab[2]
    JSR OSWRCH
    JMP print_message_at
.print_line1
    JSR window_address
    LDA #line1_tab[0]
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDA #line1_tab[1]
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDA #line1_tab[2]
    JSR OSWRCH
    JMP print_message_at
.print_message
    JSR window_address
.print_message_at
    STX window_ptr
    STY window_ptr+1
    JSR text_colours
.print_message_loop
    LDY #0
    LDA (window_ptr), Y
    CMP #MESSAGE_END
    BEQ print_message_done
    CMP #HIGHLIGHT
    BEQ print_message_highlight
    JSR OSWRCH
.print_message_next
    INC window_ptr
    BNE print_message_loop
    INC window_ptr+1
    JMP print_message_loop
.print_message_highlight
    LDY #highlight_colours + 3 - colour_sequences
    JSR vdu_sequence
    JMP print_message_next

; Text colours for the message box: yellow on blue (text_colours), or a
; sequence from colour_sequences ending at Y.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y.
.text_colours
    LDY #normal_colours + 3 - colour_sequences
.vdu_sequence
    LDX #3
.vdu_sequence_loop
    LDA colour_sequences, Y
    JSR OSWRCH
    DEY
    DEX
    BPL vdu_sequence_loop
.print_message_done
    RTS
; Four-byte VDU sequences, sent last byte first.
.colour_sequences
.normal_colours                 ; COLOUR 129 : COLOUR 2, yellow on blue
    EQUB REVERSE({VDU_COLOUR, COLOUR_BACKGROUND + 1, VDU_COLOUR, 2})
.unused_colours                 ; with the next byte, VDU 0 : COLOUR 128 : CLS
    EQUB REVERSE({VDU_COLOUR, COLOUR_BACKGROUND, VDU_CLS})
.highlight_colours              ; COLOUR 131 : COLOUR 0, black on red
    EQUB REVERSE({VDU_COLOUR, COLOUR_BACKGROUND + 3, VDU_COLOUR, 0})

; Find a window or message in WDATA.
; In: A = its number.
; Out: X, Y = its address, low and high.
.window_address
    ASL A
    TAY
    LDA wdata - 2, Y
    TAX
    LDA wdata - 1, Y
    TAY
    RTS

; Put a block in the map, and on the screen.
; In: A = the block; X, Y = the cell.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, ptr, work.
.write_map
    PHA
    STX ptr
    STY ptr+1
    JSR vector_plot_cell
    LDX ptr
    LDY ptr+1
    JSR map_address
    PLA
    LDX #&F0
    BCS write_map_nibble        ; odd y: the bottom nibble
    LDX #&0F
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
.write_map_nibble
    STA work
    TXA
    LDY #0
    AND (ptr), Y
    ORA work
    STA (ptr), Y
    RTS

; Read a block from the map.
; In: X, Y = the cell.
; Out: A = the block, or negative if the cell is off the map.
; Clobbers: Y, ptr; X too if on the map.
.read_map
    TXA
    ASL A
    BMI read_map_done
    TYA
    ASL A
    BMI read_map_done
    JSR map_address
    LDY #0
    LDA (ptr), Y
    BCS read_map_nibble
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
.read_map_nibble
    AND #&0F
.read_map_done
    RTS

; The map is a column of 32 bytes for each x, top to bottom, two cells a
; byte, the even y in the top nibble.
; In: X, Y = the cell.
; Out: ptr = its byte; C set if it's the bottom nibble.
; Clobbers: A, X.
.map_address
    TXA
    LDX #3                      ; also ptr's start: its bits fall out of the
    STX ptr                     ; bottom, leaving C clear
.map_address_shift
    LSR A
    ROR ptr
    DEX
    BNE map_address_shift
    ADC #HI(level_map)
    STA ptr+1
    TYA
    LSR A
    CLC
    ADC ptr
    STA ptr
    TYA
    LSR A
    RTS

; Pixel art for the font and the map's blocks: a character for each pixel,
; as mode1_byte() (levdes.6502inc) takes them.
; A glyph: eight rows of eight pixels, kept as the left four pixels of each
; row and then the right four, as they go on the screen.
MACRO GLYPH r0, r1, r2, r3, r4, r5, r6, r7
    EQUB mode1_byte(r0[0..3]), mode1_byte(r1[0..3]), mode1_byte(r2[0..3]), mode1_byte(r3[0..3])
    EQUB mode1_byte(r4[0..3]), mode1_byte(r5[0..3]), mode1_byte(r6[0..3]), mode1_byte(r7[0..3])
    EQUB mode1_byte(r0[4..7]), mode1_byte(r1[4..7]), mode1_byte(r2[4..7]), mode1_byte(r3[4..7])
    EQUB mode1_byte(r4[4..7]), mode1_byte(r5[4..7]), mode1_byte(r6[4..7]), mode1_byte(r7[4..7])
ENDMACRO
; A block as the map shows it: four rows of four pixels, kept bottom row
; first.
MACRO TILE r0, r1, r2, r3
    EQUB mode1_byte(r3), mode1_byte(r2), mode1_byte(r1), mode1_byte(r0)
ENDMACRO

; Glyphs 64 to 69, past the end of the font (draw_glyph takes them from
; here, so they start a page).
.font_digits
    ASSERT LO(font_digits) == 0
    GLYPH ".######.", ".....##.", "....##..", "...##...", "..##....", "..##....", "..##....", "........"   ; 64: 7
    GLYPH "..####..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "..####..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "..####..", "........"   ; 65: 8
    GLYPH "..####..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "..#####.", ".....##.", "....##..", "..###...", "........"   ; 66: 9
    GLYPH "..####..", ".##..##.", ".##.###.", ".######.", ".###.##.", ".##..##.", "..####..", "........"   ; 67: 0
    GLYPH "........", "........", ".....##.", "....##..", "##.##...", ".###....", "..#.....", "........"   ; 68: tick
    GLYPH "........", "........", "........", ".######.", "........", "........", "........", "........"   ; 69: -
; The map's blocks, by number, drawn a byte (four pixels) wide.
.tile_patterns
    TILE "    ", "    ", "    ", "    "   ; 0: blank
    TILE "   #", "  ##", " ###", "####"   ; 1: SE curve
    TILE "#   ", "##  ", "### ", "####"   ; 2: SW curve
    TILE "####", " ###", "  ##", "   #"   ; 3: NE curve
    TILE "####", "### ", "##  ", "#   "   ; 4: NW curve
    TILE "####", "####", "####", "####"   ; 5: wall 1
    TILE " .. ", ".##.", ".##.", " .. "   ; 6: crate
    TILE "oooo", " oo ", " oo ", " oo "   ; 7: collectable (sulphur)
    TILE "...o", "..o.", ".o..", "o..."   ; 8: wall 2
    TILE "oooo", " ## ", " ## ", "oooo"   ; 9: barricade
    TILE " ## ", "#  #", "#  #", " ## "   ; A: fatal trap (lava)
    TILE " .. ", "....", "....", " .. "   ; B: junction: both pipes at once
    TILE "    ", "....", "....", "    "   ; C: horizontal pipe
    TILE " .. ", " .. ", " .. ", " .. "   ; D: vertical pipe
    TILE "####", "#..#", "#..#", "####"   ; E: S.monster (fire)
    TILE " oo ", "oooo", "oooo", " oo "   ; F: marker (an object)
    EQUB 0                      ; spare
; Zero page as entry leaves it: pointers to the menus' handler tables, which
; jump_to_handler finds by number (from 1), and spare bytes.
.zero_page_init_load
SECTION zero_page_init, org=&0000
.menu_tables
.options_handlers_ptr       EQUW options_handlers
.object_handlers_ptr        EQUW object_handlers
.monster_handlers_ptr       EQUW monster_handlers
.puzzle_handlers_ptr        EQUW puzzle_handlers
.status_handlers_ptr        EQUW status_handlers
.conditions_handlers_ptr    EQUW conditions_handlers
.files_handlers_ptr         EQUW files_handlers
.effect_handlers_ptr        EQUW effect_handlers
.place_block_handlers_ptr   EQUW place_block_handlers
.set_levels_handlers_ptr    EQUW set_levels_handlers
.move_block_handlers_ptr    EQUW move_block_handlers
.throw_handlers_ptr         EQUW throw_handlers
.charge_handlers_ptr        EQUW charge_handlers
.move_monster_handlers_ptr  EQUW move_monster_handlers
.place_monster_handlers_ptr EQUW place_monster_handlers
.help_handlers_ptr          EQUW help_handlers
.cursor_handlers_ptr        EQUW cursor_handlers
.zero_page_spare
    SKIP &40 - (zero_page_spare - menu_tables)
.zero_page_init_end
ENDSECTION
; The low code: drawing the map, windows, menus and the message box, with
; its variables at &72-&89. entry moves it to &0880, where it's assembled to
; run; the rest of the program calls it through the jump table at its start.
.low_code_load
SECTION low_code, org=&0880
.low_code
.vector_draw_window
    JMP draw_window
.vector_close_window
    JMP close_window
.vector_menu_select
    JMP window_menu
.vector_tick_line
    JMP tick_line
.vector_draw_map
    JMP draw_map
.vector_invert_cell
    JMP invert_cell
.vector_plot_cell
    JMP plot_cell
.vector_open_message_box
    JMP open_message_box
.vector_close_message_box
    JMP close_message_box

; Draw the whole map, a row of cells (half a character row) at a time.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, the low code's zero page.
.draw_map
    LDY #0
    STY map_ptr
    LDA #HI(level_map)
    STA map_ptr+1
    STY screen_ptr
    LDA #HI(screen)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    LDA #&F0                    ; even rows are the top nibbles
    STA nibble_mask
    STY line_count              ; the row
    DEY
.draw_map_band
    LDA #HI(level_end - level_map)
    STA byte_count
.draw_map_cell
    INY                         ; Y is always 0 here
    LDA (map_ptr), Y
    BIT nibble_mask
    BPL draw_map_nibble
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
.draw_map_nibble
    AND #&0F
    ASL A
    ASL A
    TAX
    LDY #3
.draw_map_pattern
    LDA tile_patterns, X
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    INX
    DEY
    BPL draw_map_pattern
    LDA screen_ptr
    ADC #8                      ; next column
    STA screen_ptr
    BCC draw_map_next
    INC screen_ptr+1
.draw_map_next
    LDA map_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #MAP_COLUMN_BYTES       ; next x
    STA map_ptr
    BCC draw_map_cell
    INC map_ptr+1
    DEC byte_count
    BNE draw_map_cell
    INC line_count
    LDA map_ptr+1
    SBC #HI(level_end - level_map)
    STA map_ptr+1
    LDA line_count
    AND #&FE                    ; two pages a character row
    ADC #HI(screen) - 1         ; (C is set)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    LDA line_count
    LDX #&0F
    AND #1
    BNE draw_map_next_band
    LDX #&F0
    INC map_ptr                 ; next byte down the columns
    BNE draw_map_next_band
    INC map_ptr+1
.draw_map_next_band
    STX nibble_mask
    ASL A                       ; odd rows four lines down
    ASL A
    STA screen_ptr
    BIT line_count
    BVC draw_map_band           ; until 64
    RTS

; Where a cell is on the screen: a column of 8 bytes for each x, and four
; scan lines for each y.
; In: X, Y = the cell.
; Out: screen_ptr.
; Clobbers: A.
.cell_address
    LDA #0
    STA screen_ptr+1
    TXA
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ROL screen_ptr+1
    ASL A
    ROL screen_ptr+1
    STA screen_ptr
    TYA
    AND #&FE
    ADC #HI(screen)
    ADC screen_ptr+1
    STA screen_ptr+1
    TYA
    LSR A
    LDA #0
    BCC cell_address_half
    LDA #4
.cell_address_half
    ORA screen_ptr
    STA screen_ptr
    RTS

; Out: A = the block at map_ptr, nibble_mask's half.
; Clobbers: Y.
.read_map_ptr
    LDY #0
    LDA (map_ptr), Y
    BIT nibble_mask
    BPL read_map_ptr_nibble
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
    LSR A
.read_map_ptr_nibble
    AND #&0F
    RTS

; Redraw a run of cells along a row.
; In: A = how many; X, Y = the first.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, the low code's zero page.
.draw_map_run
    STA byte_count
    STX saved_x
    LDA #0
    STA map_ptr+1
    TXA
    LDX #5                      ; x * MAP_COLUMN_BYTES
.draw_map_run_column
    ASL A
    ROL map_ptr+1
    DEX
    BNE draw_map_run_column
    STA map_ptr
    TYA
    LSR A
    LDX #&F0
    BCC draw_map_run_mask
    LDX #&0F
.draw_map_run_mask
    STX nibble_mask
    ORA map_ptr
    CLC
    STA map_ptr
    LDA map_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(level_map)
    STA map_ptr+1
    LDX saved_x
    JSR cell_address
.draw_map_run_loop
    JSR read_map_ptr
    ASL A
    ASL A
    TAX
    LDY #3
.draw_map_run_pattern
    LDA tile_patterns, X
    INX
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL draw_map_run_pattern
    LDA screen_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #8
    STA screen_ptr
    BCC draw_map_run_next
    INC screen_ptr+1
.draw_map_run_next
    LDA map_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #MAP_COLUMN_BYTES
    STA map_ptr
    BCC draw_map_run_count
    INC map_ptr+1
.draw_map_run_count
    DEC byte_count
    BNE draw_map_run_loop
    RTS

; Draw the message box: character rows 14-17, columns 2-61, in colour 1 with
; a colour 3 line round it; the OS prints into it.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr, glyph_ptr.
.open_message_box
    LDA #LO(message_box)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA #HI(message_box)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    LDX #MESSAGE_BOX_ROWS
.open_message_box_fill
    LDY #0
    LDA #mode1_byte("....")
.open_message_box_page
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BNE open_message_box_page
    INC screen_ptr+1
    LDY #MESSAGE_BOX_COLUMNS * 8 - 256 - 1
.open_message_box_rest
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    CPY #&FF
    BNE open_message_box_rest
    INC screen_ptr+1
    DEX
    BNE open_message_box_fill
    ; Lines along the bottom and the top, each in two halves.
    LDX #30 * 8
.open_message_box_edges
    LDA #mode1_byte("oooo")
    STA screen_address(2, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW + MESSAGE_BOX_ROWS), X
    STA screen_address(31, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW + MESSAGE_BOX_ROWS), X
    STA screen_address(2, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW - 1) + 7, X
    STA screen_address(31, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW - 1) + 7, X
    TXA
    SEC
    SBC #8
    TAX
    BCS open_message_box_edges
    ; And the sides, from the bottom row up.
    LDA #LO(box_left_side)
    STA screen_ptr
    LDX #HI(box_left_side)
    STX screen_ptr+1
    INX                         ; the right side's page is the next one
    ASSERT HI(box_right_side) == HI(box_left_side) + 1
    STX glyph_ptr+1
    LDA #LO(box_right_side)
    STA glyph_ptr
    LDX #MESSAGE_BOX_ROWS
.open_message_box_sides
    LDY #7
.open_message_box_side
    LDA #mode1_byte("   o")     ; the rightmost pixel of the column left of
    ORA (screen_ptr), Y         ; the box
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    LDA #mode1_byte("o   ")     ; the leftmost of the column right of it
    ORA (glyph_ptr), Y
    STA (glyph_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL open_message_box_side
    DEC screen_ptr+1
    DEC screen_ptr+1
    DEC glyph_ptr+1
    DEC glyph_ptr+1
    DEX
    BNE open_message_box_sides
    ; The corners.
    LDA #mode1_byte("   o")
    ORA screen_address(1, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW - 1) + 7
    STA screen_address(1, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW - 1) + 7
    LDA #mode1_byte("   o")
    ORA screen_address(1, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW + MESSAGE_BOX_ROWS)
    STA screen_address(1, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW + MESSAGE_BOX_ROWS)
    LDA #mode1_byte("o   ")
    ORA screen_address(62, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW - 1) + 7
    STA screen_address(62, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW - 1) + 7
    LDA #mode1_byte("o   ")
    ORA screen_address(62, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW + MESSAGE_BOX_ROWS)
    STA screen_address(62, MESSAGE_BOX_ROW + MESSAGE_BOX_ROWS)
    RTS
; Draw a window from WDATA (format in wdata.6502inc): x and width in screen
; columns, y in character rows, height+1 lines of glyphs two columns wide.
; It's filled in colour 1 with a colour 3 line down the right and along the
; bottom, and the title line inverted. A window without bit 7 of x set (FIXED
; in wdata.6502) moves out of the cursor's way: to the right half of the
; screen when the cursor is in the left half, and to the bottom half when
; it is in the top half.
; In: X, Y = the window's address.
; Out: window_x, window_y (in cells, so doubled), window_width and
; window_height describe it, for close_window and the menu.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, the low code's zero page.
.draw_window
    STX window_ptr
    STY window_ptr+1
    LDX #3
    LDY #3
.draw_window_header
    LDA (window_ptr), Y
    STA window_x, X
    DEX
    DEY
    BPL draw_window_header
    LDA window_y
    STA window_flags
    AND #&7F
    STA window_y
    LDA window_x
    PHP
    AND #&7F
    STA window_x
    PLP
    BMI draw_window_placed      ; fixed
    LDA cursor_x
    CMP #MAP_SIZE/2
    BCS draw_window_place_y
    LDA #MAP_SIZE + 1           ; x = 64 - width - x (C is clear)
    SBC window_width
    SBC window_x
    STA window_x
.draw_window_place_y
    LDA cursor_y
    CMP #MAP_SIZE/2
    BCS draw_window_placed
    LDA #MAP_SIZE/2             ; y = 31 - height - y
    SBC window_height
    SBC window_y
    STA window_y
.draw_window_placed
    ASL window_y
    LDY window_y
    LDA window_x
    TAX
    JSR cell_address
    LDA screen_ptr+1
    PHA
    STA glyph_ptr+1
    LDA screen_ptr
    PHA
    STA glyph_ptr
    SEC                         ; one back, for counting down to 1
    SBC #1
    STA screen_ptr
    BCS draw_window_frame
    DEC screen_ptr+1
.draw_window_frame
    LDA window_width
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA byte_count              ; bytes across a character row
    ADC glyph_ptr               ; glyph_ptr: the column right of it
    STA glyph_ptr
    BCC draw_window_rows
    INC glyph_ptr+1
.draw_window_rows
    LDA window_height
    STA line_count
    PHA
.draw_window_row
    LDA #mode1_byte("....")
    LDY byte_count
.draw_window_fill
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BNE draw_window_fill
    LDY #7
.draw_window_right_edge
    LDA (glyph_ptr), Y          ; its leftmost pixel in colour 3
    AND #mode1_byte(" ooo")
    ORA #mode1_byte("o   ")
    STA (glyph_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL draw_window_right_edge
    INC glyph_ptr+1
    INC glyph_ptr+1
    INC screen_ptr+1
    INC screen_ptr+1
    DEC line_count
    BPL draw_window_row
    PLA
    STA line_count
    INY
    LDA (glyph_ptr), Y          ; the corner
    AND #mode1_byte(" ooo")
    ORA #mode1_byte("o   ")
    STA (glyph_ptr), Y
    LDA byte_count
    SEC
    SBC #7
    TAY
.draw_window_bottom
    LDA #mode1_byte("oooo")     ; the top line of the row below
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    TYA
    SEC
    SBC #8
    TAY
    BCS draw_window_bottom
    PLA                         ; back to the top left, kept in map_ptr as
    STA screen_ptr              ; each line's start
    STA map_ptr
    PLA
    STA screen_ptr+1
    STA map_ptr+1
    LDA window_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #3
    STA window_ptr
    BCC draw_window_line
    INC window_ptr+1
.draw_window_line
    JSR next_window_byte
    LDY #0
    LDA (window_ptr), Y         ; the line's length
    STA glyph_ptr
    AND #&7F
    TAX
    BIT glyph_ptr
    BMI draw_window_glyph       ; left-justified
    STX glyph_ptr
    LDA window_width            ; centred: half the room left over
    LSR A
    SEC
    SBC glyph_ptr
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ADC screen_ptr
    STA screen_ptr
    BCC draw_window_glyph
    INC screen_ptr+1
.draw_window_glyph
    JSR next_window_byte
    LDY #0
    LDA (window_ptr), Y
    JSR draw_glyph
    DEX
    BNE draw_window_glyph
    LDA line_count
    CMP window_height
    BCC draw_window_next_line
    LDY byte_count              ; the title: flipping each pixel's top bit
    LDX byte_count              ; makes yellow on blue black on red
.draw_window_title
    DEY
    LDA (map_ptr), Y
    EOR #mode1_byte("####")
    STA (map_ptr), Y
    DEX
    BNE draw_window_title
.draw_window_next_line
    LDA map_ptr
    CLC
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA map_ptr+1
    ADC #HI(SCREEN_ROW)
    STA screen_ptr+1
    STA map_ptr+1
    DEC line_count
    BPL draw_window_line
    RTS

; Step window_ptr on a byte.
.next_window_byte
    INC window_ptr
    BNE next_window_byte_done
    INC window_ptr+1
.next_window_byte_done
    RTS

; Close the window last drawn by redrawing the map under it.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, the low code's zero page.
.close_window
    LDA window_y
    STA menu_shown_item         ; borrowed: the top row
    LDA window_x
    STA restore_x
    LDA window_width
    STA run_length
    LDA window_height
    ASL A
    CLC
    ADC #2                      ; its rows, and the line below
    STA restore_row
    INC run_length              ; and the line on the right
.close_window_row
    LDA restore_row
    CLC
    ADC menu_shown_item
    TAY
    LDX restore_x
    LDA run_length
    JSR draw_map_run
    DEC restore_row
    BPL close_window_row
    RTS

; Close the message box by redrawing the map under it, its rows and the
; lines round it.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, the low code's zero page.
.close_message_box
    LDA #(MESSAGE_BOX_ROW + MESSAGE_BOX_ROWS) * 2
    STA restore_row
.close_message_box_row
    LDA #MESSAGE_BOX_COLUMNS + 2
    LDX #1
    LDY restore_row
    JSR draw_map_run
    DEC restore_row
    LDA restore_row
    CMP #MESSAGE_BOX_ROW * 2 - 1
    BCS close_message_box_row
    RTS

; Invert a cell on the screen (the map cursor).
; In: X, Y = the cell.
; Clobbers: A, Y, screen_ptr.
.invert_cell
    JSR cell_address
    LDY #3
.invert_cell_loop
    LDA (screen_ptr), Y
    EOR #mode1_byte("oooo")     ; colour c becomes 3 - c
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL invert_cell_loop
    RTS

; Draw a block in a cell on the screen.
; In: A = the block; X, Y = the cell.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr.
.plot_cell
    PHA
    JSR cell_address
    PLA
    ASL A
    ASL A
    TAX
    LDY #3
.plot_cell_loop
    LDA tile_patterns, X
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    INX
    DEY
    BPL plot_cell_loop
    RTS

; Put a tick, or an x, at the end of a line of the window last drawn.
; In: A = nonzero for a tick; Y = the line (the title is 0).
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr, glyph_ptr.
.tick_line
    PHA
    TXA                         ; (X isn't used)
    ASL A
    ASL A
    TAX
    TYA
    ASL A
    ADC window_y
    TAY
    LDA window_width
    ADC window_x
    TAX
    DEX
    DEX
    JSR cell_address
    PLA
    BEQ tick_line_glyph
    LDA #GLYPH_TICK - GLYPH_X
.tick_line_glyph
    CLC
    ADC #GLYPH_X
; Draw a glyph: 0-63 from the font, 64-69 from font_digits. Each glyph is 16
; bytes and both tables start a page, so bit 6 picks the table, bits 4-5 the
; page in it and bits 0-3 the 16 bytes in the page.
; In: A = the glyph (bit 7 is ignored); screen_ptr = where.
; Out: screen_ptr moved on a glyph.
; Clobbers: A, Y, glyph_ptr.
.draw_glyph
    ASL A
    LDY #HI(font)
    ASL A
    BCC draw_glyph_bit5
    LDY #HI(font_digits)
.draw_glyph_bit5
    ASL A
    BCC draw_glyph_bit4
    INY
    INY
.draw_glyph_bit4
    ASL A
    BCC draw_glyph_copy
    INY
.draw_glyph_copy
    STA glyph_ptr
    STY glyph_ptr+1
    LDY #15
.draw_glyph_loop
    LDA (glyph_ptr), Y
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    BPL draw_glyph_loop
    LDA screen_ptr
    CLC
    ADC #16
    STA screen_ptr
    BCC draw_glyph_done
    INC screen_ptr+1
.draw_glyph_done
    RTS

; Run the menu of the window last drawn: cursor up and down move a bar over
; its items (the lines after the title), Return chooses, and Space chooses
; the last item, or for a window with bit 7 of y set the one it started on.
; In: A = the item to start on (0 if out of range).
; Out: C clear and A = the item; or C set if Escape was pressed.
; Clobbers: X, Y, the low code's zero page.
.window_menu
    CMP window_height
    BCC window_menu_start
    LDA #0
.window_menu_start
    STA menu_item
    STA menu_first_item
    LDA window_width
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    SBC #0                      ; less one: C is clear
    STA byte_count
    LDA window_height
    STA line_count              ; the number of items
    LDA menu_item
    STA menu_shown_item
    JSR highlight_item
    LDA #OSBYTE_CURSOR_EDITING  ; cursor keys give &8B-&8F
    LDX #CURSOR_KEYS_SOFT
    JSR OSBYTE
    STX saved_cursor_key_mode
.window_menu_key
    LDA #OSBYTE_WAIT_VSYNC
    JSR OSBYTE
    JSR OSRDCH
    BCC window_menu_down
    LDA #OSBYTE_CURSOR_EDITING
    LDX saved_cursor_key_mode
    JSR OSBYTE
    SEC
    LDA #&FF
    RTS
.window_menu_down
    CMP #KEYCODE_CURSOR_DOWN
    BNE window_menu_up
    INC menu_item
    LDA menu_item
    CMP line_count
    BCC window_menu_set
    LDA #0
.window_menu_set
    STA menu_item
    JMP window_menu_moved
.window_menu_up
    CMP #KEYCODE_CURSOR_UP
    BNE window_menu_highlight
    DEC menu_item
    BPL window_menu_moved
    LDA line_count
    SEC
    SBC #1
    STA menu_item
.window_menu_moved
    LDA #0
.window_menu_highlight
    PHA
    LDA menu_item
    CMP menu_shown_item
    BEQ window_menu_check
    JSR highlight_item
    LDA menu_shown_item
    JSR highlight_item
    LDA menu_item
    STA menu_shown_item
.window_menu_check
    PLA
    CMP #CR
    BEQ window_menu_return
    CMP #' '
    BEQ window_menu_space
    LDA #OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS   ; (X is left over: the input buffer or all
    JSR OSBYTE                  ; of them)
    JMP window_menu_key
.window_menu_space
    LDA window_flags
    BMI window_menu_cancel
    JSR restore_cursor_key_mode
    LDX line_count
    DEX
    TXA
    CLC
    RTS
.window_menu_cancel             ; (leaving the cursor keys as they are)
    LDA menu_first_item
    CLC
    RTS
.window_menu_return
    JSR restore_cursor_key_mode
    LDA menu_item
    JSR highlight_item
    LDA menu_item
    CLC
    RTS

; Put the cursor keys back as window_menu found them.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y.
.restore_cursor_key_mode
    LDA #OSBYTE_CURSOR_EDITING
    LDX saved_cursor_key_mode
    JMP OSBYTE

; (Unused: OSBYTE &81, INKEY, with Y = &81 and the caller's X, returning
; the X it gives back.)
.unused_read_key
    LDA #OSBYTE_INKEY
    TAY
    JSR OSBYTE
    TXA
    RTS

; Invert a menu item's line in the window last drawn.
; In: A = the item.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, screen_ptr.
.highlight_item
    ASL A
    ADC window_y
    LDX window_x
    TAY
    INY                         ; below the title
    INY
    JSR cell_address
    LDY byte_count
.highlight_item_loop
    LDA (screen_ptr), Y
    EOR #mode1_byte("oooo")     ; yellow on blue becomes blue on yellow
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEY
    CPY #&FF
    BNE highlight_item_loop
    RTS

.saved_cursor_key_mode
    EQUB 0
    SKIP 5                      ; to the end of the moved code
ENDSECTION
; The font, glyphs 0-63 (wdata_glyphs gives their order). entry moves it to
; &0400. Copying the low code also puts its first four glyphs at &0CC0, past
; the end of that code, where nothing looks at them.
.font_load
SECTION font, org=&0400
.font
    GLYPH "..####..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".######.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "........"   ; 0: A
    GLYPH ".#####..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".#####..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".#####..", "........"   ; 1: B
    GLYPH "..####..", ".##..##.", ".##.....", ".##.....", ".##.....", ".##..##.", "..####..", "........"   ; 2: C
    GLYPH ".####...", ".##.##..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##.##..", ".####...", "........"   ; 3: D
    GLYPH ".######.", ".##.....", ".##.....", ".#####..", ".##.....", ".##.....", ".######.", "........"   ; 4: E
    GLYPH ".######.", ".##.....", ".##.....", ".#####..", ".##.....", ".##.....", ".##.....", "........"   ; 5: F
    GLYPH "..####..", ".##..##.", ".##.....", ".##.###.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "..####..", "........"   ; 6: G
    GLYPH ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".######.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "........"   ; 7: H
    GLYPH ".######.", "...##...", "...##...", "...##...", "...##...", "...##...", ".######.", "........"   ; 8: I
    GLYPH "..#####.", "....##..", "....##..", "....##..", "....##..", ".##.##..", "..###...", "........"   ; 9: J
    GLYPH ".##..##.", ".##.##..", ".####...", ".###....", ".####...", ".##.##..", ".##..##.", "........"   ; 10: K
    GLYPH ".##.....", ".##.....", ".##.....", ".##.....", ".##.....", ".##.....", ".######.", "........"   ; 11: L
    GLYPH ".##...##", ".###.###", ".#######", ".##.#.##", ".##.#.##", ".##...##", ".##...##", "........"   ; 12: M
    GLYPH ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".###.##.", ".######.", ".##.###.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "........"   ; 13: N
    GLYPH "..####..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "..####..", "........"   ; 14: O
    GLYPH ".#####..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".#####..", ".##.....", ".##.....", ".##.....", "........"   ; 15: P
    GLYPH "..####..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##.#.#.", ".##.##..", "..##.##.", "........"   ; 16: Q
    GLYPH ".#####..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".#####..", ".##.##..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "........"   ; 17: R
    GLYPH "..####..", ".##..##.", ".##.....", "..####..", ".....##.", ".##..##.", "..####..", "........"   ; 18: S
    GLYPH ".######.", "...##...", "...##...", "...##...", "...##...", "...##...", "...##...", "........"   ; 19: T
    GLYPH ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "..####..", "........"   ; 20: U
    GLYPH ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "..####..", "...##...", "........"   ; 21: V
    GLYPH ".##...##", ".##...##", ".##.#.##", ".##.#.##", ".#######", ".###.###", ".##...##", "........"   ; 22: W
    GLYPH ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "..####..", "...##...", "..####..", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "........"   ; 23: X
    GLYPH ".##..##.", ".##..##.", ".##..##.", "..####..", "...##...", "...##...", "...##...", "........"   ; 24: Y
    GLYPH ".######.", ".....##.", "....##..", "...##...", "..##....", ".##.....", ".######.", "........"   ; 25: Z

; Where the LEVDES stub jumps. Move the low code, the font and zero page to
; where they run, set the screen up (MODE 1 narrowed to 64 columns), load the
; windows and the title picture, wait for Space and start the editor. All of
; this, from &25A1 up, becomes the level once it's done.
.entry
    ; The low code, &0880-&0CFF; the loop runs the source from low_code_load
    ; less &80 so that Y starts at &80, and takes the font's first &40 bytes
    ; along with it.
    LDY #&80
    LDX #4                      ; half a page, then four pages
.entry_copy_code
    LDA low_code_load - &80, Y
entry_code_from = entry_copy_code + 1           ; (the operands step a page
.entry_copy_code_store                          ; at a time)
    STA low_code - &80, Y
entry_code_to = entry_copy_code_store + 1
    INY
    BNE entry_copy_code
    INC entry_code_from+1
    INC entry_code_to+1
    DEX
    BPL entry_copy_code
    LDX #(64 * 16) DIV 256 - 1  ; four pages
.entry_copy_font
    LDA font_load, Y
entry_font_from = entry_copy_font + 1
.entry_copy_font_store
    STA font, Y
entry_font_to = entry_copy_font_store + 1
    INY
    BNE entry_copy_font
    INC entry_font_from+1
    INC entry_font_to+1
    DEX
    BPL entry_copy_font
    LDX #zero_page_init_end - menu_tables - 1
.entry_copy_zero_page
    LDA zero_page_init_load, X
    STA menu_tables, X
    DEX
    BPL entry_copy_zero_page
    TXS                         ; X = &FF: an empty stack
    LDA #&C0
    STA unused_66
    INX
    STX cursor_shown
    STX simulate_window
    STX travelling
    STX brush
    STX loading
    STX in_main_loop
    LDA #VDU_MODE
    JSR OSWRCH
    INX
    TXA                         ; MODE 1
    JSR OSWRCH
    LDA #SCREEN_COLUMNS         ; X = 1, CRTC_HORIZONTAL_DISPLAYED
    JSR vector_crtc_write
    INX
    LDA #90                     ; X = 2, CRTC_HSYNC_POSITION: 8 less than
    JSR vector_crtc_write       ; MODE 1's 98, centring the 16 fewer columns
    JSR vector_cursor_off
    LDA #OSBYTE_AUTO_REPEAT_PERIOD
    LDX #4                      ; fast: 4 centiseconds
    JSR OSBYTE
    LDA #OSBYTE_BREAK_EFFECT
    LDX #2                      ; Break clears memory
    JSR osbyte_y0
    LDA #OSBYTE_BELL_DURATION
    LDX #2                      ; a short beep
    JSR osbyte_y0
    LDA #OSBYTE_FUNCTION_KEY_BASE
    LDX #KEYCODE_F0
    JSR osbyte_y0
    LDY #3
.entry_palette
    LDA title_palette, Y
    JSR vector_set_palette
    DEY

    ; Put the OS's RDCHV into rdchv_filter's JSR.
    LDA rdchv_filter_operand_address
    STA ptr

    LDA #OSBYTE_OPT             ; *OPT 1,0: no filing system messages

    JSR vector_text_colours
    LDA brk_handler_address
    STA BRKV
    LDA brk_handler_address+1
    STA BRKV+1
    JMP vector_main

; In: A, X = an OSBYTE call.
.osbyte_y0

; Black, blue, yellow and red for the title, as set_palette_entry wants them.
```

`src/hidden_loader.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; The stub loader the disc catalogues as GAME, GRAPHIC and LEVDES.
;
; The three big programs MENU starts (the game, the Graphics Designer and
; the Level Designer) have no catalogue entries. Each sits in a "hidden
; run": whole sectors past the last catalogued file, which DFS sees as free
; space. A stub is the small catalogued program that loads one: these &D9
; bytes, loaded and run at &0900, read a hidden run a track at a time with
; the disc controller's own commands and jump into it. GAME, GRAPHIC and
; LEVDES are this code assembled three times, differing only in which run
; they read, where it goes and where it's entered. The including file
; defines those four numbers, then INCLUDEs this inside its SECTION:
;
;   hidden_first_sector  the sector the run starts at, counted from track 0
;                        sector 0 (src/disc.toml's [[raw]] entries place the runs)
;   hidden_length        its length in bytes, a whole number of sectors
;   hidden_load          where in the I/O processor (the BBC itself, as
;                        against a second processor) it's read to
;   hidden_entry         where it's entered once read
;
; The protection is two layers, both about stopping a copy made with DFS's
; own commands:
;
; - No catalogue entry mentions the hidden runs, so *COPY copies only these
;   stubs.
; - Every sector of those runs was written with a deleted data address mark
;   (the flux capture original/E447ED5E.hfe has them; an .ssd can't hold the
;   mark, so original/pipeline.ssd has lost it). The 8271, the BBC's floppy
;   disc controller, ends a read of a deleted sector with result &20, and DFS
;   reports any nonzero result as a disc fault, so a *BACKUP should stop
;   there. The stub hands its commands to the 8271 through OSWORD &7F,
;   reading with "read data and deleted data", and ignores the result, so it
;   doesn't care whether the marks are there - which is why the .ssd runs.
;
; It also copes with this 40-track disc in an 80-track drive, whose head
; moves half as far for each step. OSWORD &7F's commands reach the 8271 as
; they are (DFS 1.2 passes them on unchanged), and the 8271 steps the head
; once for each track it counts. So the stub reads one sector ID off track
; PROBE_TRACK, and if the ID gives another track the head has gone only half
; as far into the disc as asked. From then on it seeks to twice each track
; and, for each read, tells the 8271 it's on the track the disc's IDs give
; (see read_next_track). DFS 1.2 doesn't double-step its own reads, so under
; it the game, once loaded, fails to load IO ("Disk fault 18"): the stub's
; care only pays under a DFS that does. (docs/notes/loaders.md has both
; tested in jsbeeb.)
;
; Below: the numbers, the loading code (start to next_track_or_run), three
; small routines that issue 8271 commands, then the commands' parameter
; blocks and the stub's two variables.
;
; Parameter blocks for OSWORD &7F (8271 command) all have the same shape:
;   +0      drive (0 here: the stubs only ever load from drive 0)
;   +1..4   buffer address, 32-bit; &FFFFxxxx is the I/O processor, and
;           &FFFFFFFF is the conventional "no data" for commands that move none
;   +5      number of parameters, n
;   +6      8271 command, drive-select bit (&40, drive 0) included
;   +7..    the n parameters
;   +7+n    result, written back by the call (0 = all well)

; The drive every block names: the stubs only ever load from drive 0.
DRIVE = 0

; I/O processor memory, as the top half of a 32-bit OSWORD &7F address, and
; the address given to a command that moves no data.
IO_PROCESSOR = &FFFF0000
NO_DATA = &FFFFFFFF

; DFS single density: ten 256-byte sectors per track.
SECTORS_PER_TRACK = 10
SECTOR_SIZE = 256

; The track whose ID is read to tell the drives apart: an 80-track drive
; asked for it lands on this 40-track disc's track PROBE_TRACK/2 instead.
PROBE_TRACK = 4

; Where the run starts, in the 8271's terms, and how many sectors to read.
first_track = hidden_first_sector DIV SECTORS_PER_TRACK
first_sector = hidden_first_sector MOD SECTORS_PER_TRACK
sector_count = hidden_length DIV SECTOR_SIZE
ASSERT hidden_length MOD SECTOR_SIZE = 0, "a hidden run is whole sectors"
ASSERT sector_count < 256, "the sector count lives in one byte"

; Zero page: user workspace, free while the stub runs.
SECTION zero_page, org=&70, virtual=TRUE
.sectors_this_read SKIP 1   ; sectors the current read takes from this track
    SKIP 1
.sectors_left SKIP 1        ; sectors of the run not yet asked for
ENDSECTION

; Load the hidden run and enter it. *RUN enters here, at the stub's load
; address (MENU's */GAME, */GRAPHIC or */LEVDES).
; In: nothing.
; Never returns: it ends by jumping to hidden_entry, in the program it loaded.
.start
    ; seek_track starts at 0, so this recalibrates: a seek to track 0 steps
    ; out until the drive signals track 0, so the probe below is a known
    ; number of steps.
    JSR seek
    LDX #LO(read_id_block)
    LDY #HI(read_id_block)
    JSR disc_command
    LDA id_track
    CMP #PROBE_TRACK
    BEQ read_whole_run
    LDX #&FF
    STX double_step

; Read the run a track at a time: one multi-sector read from read_sector to
; the end of the track, or as much of it as the run still needs.
.read_whole_run
    LDA #first_sector
    LDX #first_track
    LDY #sector_count
    STA read_sector
    STX read_track
    STY sectors_left
.read_next_track
    LDA #SECTORS_PER_TRACK
    SEC
    SBC read_sector
    CMP sectors_left
    BCC take_rest_of_track
    LDA sectors_left
.take_rest_of_track
    STA sectors_this_read
    ORA #FDC_SIZE_256
    STA read_size_count
    LDA sectors_left
    SEC
    SBC sectors_this_read
    STA sectors_left
    BIT double_step
    BPL read_this_track
    ; Double stepping: move the head to physical track 2*N by seeking there
    ; while the 8271 counts physical tracks, then tell it it's on track N so
    ; the read's track parameter matches the IDs written on the disc.
    LDA read_track
    ASL A
    STA seek_track
    JSR seek
    LDA read_track
    STA track_register_value
    JSR set_track_register
.read_this_track
    LDX #LO(read_block)
    LDY #HI(read_block)
    JSR disc_command
    BIT double_step
    BPL step_to_next_track
    ; Put the 8271 back to counting physical tracks, so the next seek (and
    ; DFS's own, once the program is running) steps from the right place.
    ASL track_register_value
    JSR set_track_register
.step_to_next_track
    LDA #0
    STA read_sector
    LDA sectors_this_read
    CLC
    ADC read_address+1
    STA read_address+1
    INC read_track
    ; The result is fetched and then ignored. LDA, NOP and JMP take seven
    ; bytes, the same as LDA, a two-byte test and a BEQ over the error block
    ; below, which a failed read would fall into. On the original disc every
    ; read returns FDC_RESULT_DELETED_DATA, so a check for zero would always
    ; fail; this looks like such a check patched out.
    LDA read_result
    NOP
    JMP next_track_or_run

; Unreachable: the JMP above skips it and nothing else leads here. A BRK
; error block, as the MOS expects one (BRK, error number, message, zero).
.sector_read_fault
    BRK
    EQUB &FF
    EQUS "Sector read fault!"
    EQUB 0

.next_track_or_run
    LDA sectors_left
    BNE read_next_track
    JMP hidden_entry

; Seek drive 0's head.
; In: seek_track = the track, as the 8271 counts them.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y.
.seek
    LDX #LO(seek_block)
    LDY #HI(seek_block)
    ; Fall through.

; Issue an 8271 command through OSWORD &7F.
; In: YX = its parameter block.
; Out: the block's result byte says how it went.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y.
.disc_command
    LDA #OSWORD_DISC_COMMAND
    JMP OSWORD

; Tell the 8271 which track drive 0's head is on.
; In: track_register_value = the track.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y.
.set_track_register
    LDX #LO(track_register_block)
    LDY #HI(track_register_block)
    BNE disc_command            ; always: the blocks aren't in page zero

; OSWORD &7F parameter blocks, shaped as described at the top.

; Seek: one parameter, the track.
.seek_block
    EQUB DRIVE
    EQUD NO_DATA
    EQUB 1, FDC_SEEK
.seek_track
    EQUB 0
    EQUB 0                      ; result

; Write special register: the register number and its new value.
.track_register_block
    EQUB DRIVE
    EQUD NO_DATA
    EQUB 2, FDC_WRITE_SPECIAL, FDC_REG_TRACK_DRIVE_0
.track_register_value
    EQUB 0
    EQUB 0                      ; result

; Read data and deleted data: track, first sector, then the sector size code
; (top three bits) and the count (low five) in one byte. The buffer
; address's page is stepped on after each track, so the run lands
; contiguously from hidden_load.
.read_block
    EQUB DRIVE
.read_address
    EQUD IO_PROCESSOR + hidden_load
    EQUB 3, FDC_READ_DATA_AND_DELETED
.read_track
    EQUB 0
.read_sector
    EQUB 0
.read_size_count
    EQUB FDC_SIZE_256 + SECTORS_PER_TRACK   ; overwritten before use
.read_result
    EQUB 0

; Read ID: track, a zero the 8271 expects, and how many IDs to read (one).
; Each ID is four bytes - track, head, sector, size code - into id_buffer.
.read_id_block
    EQUB DRIVE
    EQUD IO_PROCESSOR + id_buffer
    EQUB 3, FDC_READ_ID
    EQUB PROBE_TRACK, 0, 1
    EQUB 0                      ; result

; Bit 7 set when the drive turned out to need double stepping.
.double_step
    EQUB 0

; The ID read off the probe track; only its track number is looked at.
.id_buffer
.id_track
    EQUB &FF, &FF, &FF, &FF

```

`src/io.6502`:

```6502
; IO, the mission file: everything the game needs to play a mission - its
; four levels, the pictures to draw them with and the objects' names - as
; the Mission Generator (MISSION) builds it from a graphics file and four
; level files and saves it. The game (H.GAME) loads it with OSFILE at
; io_start, &242D, worked out so that the file ends at &5800, where the game
; keeps the map of the level being played. In the file and in memory:
;
;   &242D  names         the end of the graphics file: the picture for an
;                        object cell with no object, then the object names
;   &2561  mission_text  the mission's name
;   &257F  attrs         the mission's five settings
;   &2584  levels        the four levels' fields, interleaved field by field
;   &2A00  maps          the four levels' maps, &800 bytes each
;   &4A00  graphics      the start of the graphics file, up to &57FF
;
; src/io.6502inc has the layout, computed from MISSION's own sizes, and what
; each part means; the game includes it too. Only the mission's name and
; settings are written here. The graphics and names are the default set
; (src/default.6502inc, which DEFAULT is made from too) and the levels are
; src/level1.6502inc (LEVEL1's too) to src/level4.6502inc.

INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"
INCLUDE "io.6502inc"
INCLUDE "default.6502inc"
INCLUDE "level1.6502inc"
INCLUDE "level2.6502inc"
INCLUDE "level3.6502inc"
INCLUDE "level4.6502inc"

; Half the mission's name, as MISSION stores it: a VDU_TAB to text column x,
; row y, then the 12 characters of text, each space stored as VDU_RIGHT
; (cursor right) so that it doesn't paint over the picture behind it.
FUNCTION mission_name_half(x, y, text)
    ASSERT LEN(text) = IO_MISSION_SIZE / 2 - 3, "half a mission name is 12 characters"
    spaces = CODES(text) = ' '
= CONCAT(VDU_TAB, x, y, CODES(text) + (VDU_RIGHT - ' ') * spaces)

SECTION io, filename="IO", org=io_start, load=io_start, exec=0
.io
{
.names
    ; What MISSION calls the names: the last &134 bytes of the graphics file
    ; it was given (DEFAULT), a picture for an object cell with no object
    ; in it, then the object names.
    EQUB default_names()
    ASSERT names = io_no_object_picture
    ASSERT names + 128 = io_object_names

; The mission's name, which the game prints as the goal on its backpack
; screen (the one CTRL brings up). MISSION always puts the halves at text
; positions (18, 16) and (14, 17).
.mission_text
    EQUB mission_name_half(18, 16, "Collect the ")
    EQUB mission_name_half(14, 17, "  Sulphur!  ")
    ASSERT mission_text = io_mission_text

; The mission's settings, as MISSION's "change features" page sets them
; (its names for them in quotes):
; - "Time consumption", which MISSION shows 6 less: each cycle of play adds
;   it to a counter, and the level's clock ticks down when that carries;
; - "Mapping ability": the game's map (the M key) works on levels below it;
; - "Backpack size", shown one more: the number of the backpack's last slot;
; - "Throwing distance": how far a thrown object flies, in cells;
; - the lock, set by keys MISSION's menu doesn't mention (h for this &FF,
;   i for 1). Locked, MISSION won't save the mission again or give up one
;   of its levels without that level's editing code; negative, the game
;   also shows a competition entry code for the mission played through
;   from level 1.
.attrs
    EQUB 15                                  ; the clock's rate (MISSION shows 9)
    EQUB 4                                   ; the map works on levels 1 to 4
    EQUB 2                                   ; the backpack holds 3
    EQUB 6                                   ; objects can be thrown 6 cells
    EQUB &FF                                 ; locked, with an entry code
    ASSERT attrs = io_attrs

; The four levels, as MISSION packs them: for each of a level's 11 fields
; (leveldata.6502inc), the four levels' in turn, then the four maps.
.levels
    EQUB FLATTEN(ZIP(level_fields(level_1), level_fields(level_2), level_fields(level_3), level_fields(level_4)))
    ASSERT levels = io_levels
.maps
    EQUB level_map_bytes(level_1), level_map_bytes(level_2), level_map_bytes(level_3), level_map_bytes(level_4)
    ASSERT maps = io_maps

; The graphics, the start of DEFAULT: the map cells' pictures, the object
; icons, the player and the second pictures some cell types can show.
.graphics
    EQUB default_graphics()
    ASSERT graphics = io_graphics
    ASSERT P% = IO_END
}
ENDSECTION

```

`src/io.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; The layout of IO, the mission file: everything the game knows about a
; mission's four levels, packed to end at &5800 where the game keeps the map
; of the level being played. MISSION (the Mission Generator) saves it with
;   addr=&5800-numlev*size-grfs-attrs-miss-names
; and the sizes below are its numlev, size, grfs, attrs, miss and names; a
; level's fields and map are as leveldata.6502inc has them.
; H.GAME loads it with OSFILE and reads it at these addresses, so they're
; shared by src/io.6502 (which lays IO out) and src/hidden_game.6502. The
; graphics and names are a graphics set's (sprites.6502inc), less its last
; slot, which goes with the names.
INCLUDE "leveldata.6502inc"
INCLUDE "sprites.6502inc"

IO_LEVELS        = 4
IO_LEVEL_FIELDS  = LEVEL_FIELDS_SIZE    ; per level, the fields, interleaved
IO_MAP_SIZE      = MAP_BYTES            ; per level, 64 x 64 cells of 4 bits
IO_LEVEL_SIZE    = IO_LEVEL_FIELDS + IO_MAP_SIZE
IO_GRAPHICS_SIZE = &E00        ; a graphics set's slots &00-&27
IO_ATTRS_SIZE    = 5
IO_MISSION_SIZE  = 30          ; the mission text, two halves of 15
IO_NAMES_SIZE    = &134        ; its slot &28 and the object names
IO_END           = &5800
ASSERT IO_GRAPHICS_SIZE = SET_NAMES - LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE
ASSERT IO_NAMES_SIZE = LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE + OBJECT_KINDS * OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH

SECTION io_layout, org=IO_END - IO_LEVELS * IO_LEVEL_SIZE - IO_GRAPHICS_SIZE - IO_ATTRS_SIZE - IO_MISSION_SIZE - IO_NAMES_SIZE, virtual=TRUE
.io_start

; The names block, which the Graphics Designer keeps with the graphics (it is
; DEFAULT's last &134 bytes): a picture drawn for a map cell marked as
; holding an object when no object is there (SLOT_NO_OBJECT), then the
; OBJECT_KINDS object names, OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH characters each.
.io_no_object_picture SKIP LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE
.io_object_names      SKIP OBJECT_KINDS * OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH

; The mission text: two VDU_TAB sequences and 12 characters each, with
; spaces stored as VDU_RIGHT so they don't paint over the background.
.io_mission_text SKIP IO_MISSION_SIZE

; The mission's attributes, set by MISSION's "change features".
.io_attrs
.io_time_rate       SKIP 1  ; added to a counter each cycle; the clock ticks when it carries
.io_map_levels      SKIP 1  ; the map (M) works on levels below this
.io_backpack_last   SKIP 1  ; the backpack's last slot: it holds this plus one
.io_throw_distance  SKIP 1  ; how far a thrown object flies, in cells
.io_locked          SKIP 1  ; negative: finishing the mission shows a competition entry
                            ; code, made from the score and a checksum of the levels

; The levels' fields, each stored as IO_LEVELS consecutive entries (level 0's,
; then level 1's...): field f of level s is at
;   io_levels + IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_OFFSETS[f] + s * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[f]
; (MISSION's L% + numlev * pnt + S% * ext).
.io_levels
.io_edit_code_high     SKIP IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[0]  ; the editing code, which MISSION
.io_edit_code_middle   SKIP IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[1]  ; asks for before it saves a level
.io_edit_code_low      SKIP IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[2]  ; out of a locked mission
.io_palettes           SKIP IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[3]  ; 4 each: logical << 4 | physical
.io_level_setup        SKIP IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[4]  ; 8 each: LEVEL_*
.io_level_objects      SKIP IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[5]  ; 32 each: 8 objects of 4 bytes
.io_level_monsters     SKIP IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[6]  ; 16 each: 4 monsters of 4 bytes
.io_level_trigger_flags SKIP IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[7] ; 32 each: a byte per trigger
.io_level_trigger_places SKIP IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[8] ; 64 each: x, y per trigger
.io_level_trigger_args_0 SKIP IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[9] ; 64 each: triggers 0-15, 4 bytes each
.io_level_trigger_args_1 SKIP IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[10] ; 64 each: triggers 16-31

; The maps, 64 columns of 32 bytes: column x's cells y and y+1 share a byte,
; even y in the high nibble. The cell types are CELL_*.
.io_maps SKIP IO_LEVELS * IO_MAP_SIZE

; The graphics, as the Graphics Designer saves them (DEFAULT's first &E00
; bytes). Each 128-byte picture is 16 x 32 MODE 5 pixels: 4 x 4 of the game's
; character cells (a byte across and 8 lines down, half a MODE 5 character;
; game.6502inc), stored a column at a time. The object icons are 2 x 2.
.io_graphics
.io_tiles        SKIP SET_SMALL - SET_LARGE         ; 16 pictures, one per map cell type
.io_object_icons SKIP SET_MORE_LARGE - SET_SMALL    ; 16 icons of 32 bytes
.io_player       SKIP (SLOT_ALTERNATE - SLOT_PLAYER) * LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE
                                                    ; 4 pictures, facing each way (SLOT_PLAYER on)
.io_alternates   SKIP IO_END - P%                   ; second pictures for cell types 5, 7, 8, A
ENDSECTION

ASSERT io_tiles = io_graphics + SET_LARGE
ASSERT io_graphics + IO_GRAPHICS_SIZE = IO_END
ASSERT io_levels + IO_LEVELS * LEVEL_FIELDS_SIZE = io_maps

```

`src/ldata.6502`:

```6502
; $.LDATA: the Level Designer's title picture, "PIPELINE Level Designer"
; over a landscape, with "Press SPACE" below (docs/img/levdes-title.png).
;
; It is screen memory, which the designer's entry *LOADs straight onto its
; screen and shows until Space is pressed: character rows 2-26 of MODE 1
; narrowed to 64 columns (levdes.6502inc's layout: 512 bytes a row, each
; column 8 bytes, one per scan line, 4 pixels a byte), in the title palette
; (black, blue, yellow, red). None of it is code; the exec address &3820
; means nothing. Draw it with
; `tools/beebscreen.py 1 data/ldata.bin OUT.png --columns 64 --offset 400
; --palette 0,4,3,1`.
INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"
INCLUDE "levdes.6502inc"

FIRST_ROW = 2
ROWS      = 25

SECTION ldata, filename="LDATA", org=screen_address(0, FIRST_ROW), load=&3400, exec=&3820
.title_picture
    INCBIN "../data/ldata.bin"
    ASSERT P% = screen_address(0, FIRST_ROW + ROWS)
ENDSECTION
```

`src/levdes.6502`:

```6502
; $.LEVDES: the catalogued file at sector &113, &D9 bytes loaded and run at
; &0900. The stub loader for the Level Designer (MENU option 4,
; `*/LEVDES`): it reads H.LEVDES from its hidden sectors and enters it. All
; of the code is in hidden_loader.6502inc, which says what a stub and a
; hidden run are; it's shared with GAME and GRAPHIC, and this file gives it
; the four numbers that differ.

INCLUDE "os.6502inc"
INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"

; H.LEVDES, the Level Designer's hidden run. No catalogue entry names it:
; the name is the build's (src/hidden_levdes.6502 makes it, src/disc.toml

; inside itself. Each source assembles on its own, so the addresses are

hidden_first_sector = &16D
hidden_length = &1F00
hidden_load = &1100
hidden_entry = &2E21                    ; entry, in hidden_levdes.6502

.levdes_loader

    INCLUDE "hidden_loader.6502inc"
}
```

`src/levdes.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; Names the Level Designer (hidden_levdes.6502) and its windows (wdata.6502)
; use that mean something only to them. A level's names (cell types,
; directions, turns, conditions...) are in leveldata.6502inc, and the OS's in
; osconst.6502inc.

; The screen: MODE 1 narrowed to 64 columns of 8 bytes (each column four
; pixels wide), so a character row is 512 bytes, and 32 rows fill
; &3000-&6FFF. A map cell is four pixels (a byte) across by four scan lines
; down, so a column of a character row holds two cells, one above the other.
screen          = MODE1_SCREEN
SCREEN_COLUMNS  = 64
SCREEN_ROWS     = 32
SCREEN_ROW      = SCREEN_COLUMNS * 8
SCREEN_END      = screen + SCREEN_ROWS * SCREEN_ROW
FUNCTION screen_address(column, row) = screen + row * SCREEN_ROW + column * 8

; The OS's text output still thinks the screen is MODE 1's 40 columns of 640
; bytes, so to print at a column and row of ours, TAB to the OS character
; that lands there.
FUNCTION os_tab(column, row)
    offset = row * SCREEN_ROW + column * 8
    ASSERT offset MOD MODE1_CHAR_BYTES == 0, "no OS character starts at ", column, ", ", row
= {VDU_TAB, (offset MOD MODE1_ROW_BYTES) DIV MODE1_CHAR_BYTES, offset DIV MODE1_ROW_BYTES}

; The message box, where the designer prompts and reads input: character
; rows 14-17 and columns 2-61. print_line1 and print_line2 print on its
; first and third rows, from column 4.
MESSAGE_BOX_ROW     = 14
MESSAGE_BOX_ROWS    = 4
MESSAGE_BOX_COLUMN  = 2
MESSAGE_BOX_COLUMNS = 60
MESSAGE_LINE_1      = MESSAGE_BOX_ROW
MESSAGE_LINE_2      = MESSAGE_BOX_ROW + 2
MESSAGE_LEFT        = MESSAGE_BOX_COLUMN + 2

; MODE 1 pixels as characters, " " colour 0 (black), "." 1, "#" 2 and "o" 3
; (blue, yellow and red in the designer's own palette), four to a byte.
FUNCTION pixel_colours(s) = FIND(CODES(" .#o"), CODES(s))
FUNCTION mode1_byte(s) = SUM((pixel_colours(s) >> 1) * {128, 64, 32, 16} + (pixel_colours(s) AND 1) * {8, 4, 2, 1})

; What the keys give with the designer's *FX225,128 and *FX4,2
; (CURSOR_KEYS_SOFT): the cursor keys are function keys then, so these
; aren't osconst.6502inc's KEYCODE_DOWN and KEYCODE_UP, which are *FX4,1's.
KEYCODE_F0          = &80       ; f0-f9: &80-&89
KEYCODE_CURSOR_DOWN = &8E       ; function key 14
KEYCODE_CURSOR_UP   = &8F       ; function key 15

; The startup options byte (the keyboard links) that lets an "i" typed at an
; error leave for BASIC (brk_handler): the authors' back door.
DEVELOPERS_LINKS = &CF
; The designer's own error number for Escape.
ERROR_ESCAPE_KEY = &1B

```

`src/level.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; The level the Level Designer edits, as it sits in memory from &25A1 to
; &2FFF and as it is saved: "Save level" writes exactly these &A5F bytes
; (load &25A1, exec &8380), and LEVEL1 on the disc is one. MISSION *LOADs
; such files and packs them into IO for the game. What a level holds, and the
; names for its values, are in leveldata.6502inc; this is where the designer
; keeps each part. LEVEL1 and PL include it too.
;
; Up to 8 objects, 4 walking monsters and 32 puzzles (the designer's word for
; the game's triggers: things that happen when the player walks onto a place
; or uses an object); positions are map cells, x across and y down, 0-63.
INCLUDE "leveldata.6502inc"

SECTION designer_level, org=&25A1, virtual=TRUE
.level

; Puzzle names, PUZZLE_NAME_LENGTH characters each, kept as the first
; PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD in one table and the rest in another.
.level_names     SKIP PUZZLES * PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD
.level_name_ends SKIP PUZZLES * (PUZZLE_NAME_LENGTH - PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD)

; The fields, in order, then the map. First a three-byte editing code; the
; designer won't keep a loaded level unless the user types its six digits.
.level_code      SKIP LEVEL_FIELD_OFFSETS[3]
.level_palette   SKIP LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[3]
; The setup bytes (LEVEL_* in leveldata.6502inc). Where the player starts,
; less 4 in each coordinate: the top left of the game's view, 8 cells by 8,
; with the player 4 cells in.
.level_setup
.level_start_x   SKIP 1
.level_start_y   SKIP 1
.level_collects  SKIP 1
.level_time      SKIP 1
.level_finish_x  SKIP 1
.level_finish_y  SKIP 1
; Bits 0-3: the block that kills a monster; bits 4-7: the block it leaves.
.level_monster_rules SKIP 1
; Two bits each for cell types 5, 8, 7 and A (the designer's wall one, wall
; two, collectable and fatal trap), 5 in the top two: which squares show
; their second sprite (ALTERNATE_*).
.level_sprites   SKIP 1
.level_objects   SKIP LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[5]
.level_monsters  SKIP LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[6]
.level_puzzle_types SKIP LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[7]
.level_puzzle_positions SKIP LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[8]
; Each puzzle's three effect bytes, by type (see the effect editors in the
; designer), then its conditions byte.
.level_puzzle_effects SKIP LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[9] + LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[10]
.level_map       SKIP MAP_BYTES
.level_end
ENDSECTION

ASSERT level_end = &3000
ASSERT level_setup = level_code + LEVEL_FIELD_OFFSETS[4]
ASSERT level_start_x = level_setup + LEVEL_START_X
ASSERT level_start_y = level_setup + LEVEL_START_Y
ASSERT level_collects = level_setup + LEVEL_TO_COLLECT
ASSERT level_time = level_setup + LEVEL_TIME
ASSERT level_finish_x = level_setup + LEVEL_EXIT_X
ASSERT level_finish_y = level_setup + LEVEL_EXIT_Y
ASSERT level_monster_rules = level_setup + LEVEL_MONSTER_FOOD
ASSERT level_sprites = level_setup + LEVEL_ANIMATE
ASSERT level_objects = level_code + LEVEL_FIELD_OFFSETS[5]
ASSERT level_puzzle_effects = level_code + LEVEL_FIELD_OFFSETS[9]
ASSERT level_map = level_code + LEVEL_FIELDS_SIZE

; The designer's names for the map's blocks, from its block menu, against the
; game's cell types (CELL_* in leveldata.6502inc). Block n is cell type n;
; the menu just lists them in its own order (block_menu_map in
; hidden_levdes.6502 translates):
;
;   block  menu name     the game
;   0      Blank         CELL_FLOOR
;   1-4    SE/SW/NE/NW curve   CELL_SE_CURVE to CELL_NW_CURVE, curved walls
;   5      Wall 1        CELL_WALL_1
;   6      Crate         CELL_CRATE
;   7      Collectable   CELL_SULPHUR
;   8      Wall 2        CELL_WALL
;   9      Barricade     CELL_BARRICADE
;   A      Fatal trap    CELL_LAVA
;   B      Junction      CELL_JUNCTION
;   C      Horz.Pipe     CELL_PIPE_ACROSS
;   D      Vert.Pipe     CELL_PIPE_DOWN
;   E      S.Monster     CELL_FIRE (the designer marks monsters with it)
;   F      Marker        CELL_OBJECT (the designer marks the start, finish
;                        and objects with it)

```

`src/level1.6502`:

```6502
; $.LEVEL1: the first level, as the Level Designer saves a level: &A5F bytes
; loaded at &25A1, where the designer keeps the level it's editing (layout in
; level.6502inc). The designer loads it to edit, once given its six-digit
; editing code, 677636; MISSION *LOADs it to put in a mission. The exec
; address, &8380, means nothing: the designer saves every level with it.
; The file holds the 32 trigger names (the designer's; a mission doesn't
; keep them), then the level's 11 fields, then its map. The level itself is
; src/level1.6502inc, which IO's first level is made from too.
INCLUDE "level.6502inc"
INCLUDE "level1.6502inc"

SECTION level1, filename="LEVEL1", org=level, load=level, exec=&8380

    EQUB level_names_bytes(level_1)
    ASSERT P% = level_code
    EQUB level_fields(level_1)
    ASSERT P% = level_map
    EQUB level_map_bytes(level_1)
    ASSERT P% = level_end

ENDSECTION

```

`src/level1.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; Level 1: the first of IO's four, and LEVEL1 on the disc, a level as the
; Level Designer saved it, its triggers named. src/level1.6502 and
; src/io.6502 make their bytes from this.
;
; How to read a level (leveldata.6502inc defines the notation and the
; names; level2.6502inc to level4.6502inc are written the same way). A
; level is a map of 64 x 64 cells, x across and y down from (0, 0) at the
; top left, and:
;
; - the player's start, and the exit. Once enough sulphur is collected the
;   player can light the exit (the pick-up key, P, facing it), and then has
;   four ticks of the clock to get five cells clear of it before it blazes.
; - 8 objects to pick up, carry in the backpack, use and throw. Each shows
;   an icon from the graphics set (default.6502inc), whose name the comment
;   gives.
; - 4 monsters: flames that move round the map, trying turns in their own
;   order at each step. Their cells count as fire, which kills.
; - 32 triggers (the Level Designer calls them puzzles). A trigger is a
;   place, or a whole row or column (IGNORE in a coordinate), that acts on
;   the level when the player walks onto it, or, with PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT,
;   when an object is used or lands there; object n can fire only triggers
;   n, n + 8, n + 16 and n + 24. Its condition byte can also ask for the
;   player to be facing a given way, or a given cell type in front (for a
;   thrown object, the way it flew and the cell it hit). Once fired it's
;   off (PUZZLE_OFF), unless PUZZLE_REUSABLE; one can start off, and other
;   triggers can turn it on and off. The action's arguments A, X and Y stay
;   in hex, as each action reads them its own way (PUZZLE_* in
;   leveldata.6502inc); the comment above each trigger says what it does in
;   the game. Triggers are numbered 0-31 here, as the game counts them; the
;   designer shows them one more.
;
; The map is 64 strings, a row each, a character a cell (MAP_KEY): "." the
; floor, "#" "=" and the corner pieces "r" "7" "L" "J" walls, "@" a
; barricade (another wall), "c" a crate, "o" sulphur, "~" lava, "+" "-" "|"
; pipes, "*" fire and "$" a cell holding an object (the start and the exit
; are marked so too).
level_1 = {
    ; The editing code, six digits: the Level Designer asks for it before it
    ; will edit the level, MISSION before it saves one of a locked mission's
    ; levels as a level file, and the game shows it once the level's done.
    "677636",
    ; The palette: the physical colours of logical colours 0-3, the "." and
    ; "1" to "3" the pictures are drawn in.
    {COLOUR_BLACK, COLOUR_BLUE, COLOUR_YELLOW, COLOUR_RED},
    ; The setup. The last byte picks, for cell types 5 (#), 8 (=), 7 (o)
    ; and A (~), two bits each from bit 7 down, which squares of a
    ; checkerboard show the type's second picture: none, the odd ones
    ; (x + y odd), the even ones or all (ALTERNATE_*).
    {
        62, 35,                         ; the player starts here
        124,                            ; sulphur to collect before the exit can be lit
        250,                            ; the clock's starting value
        31, 28,                         ; the exit
        CELL_SULPHUR * 16 + CELL_LAVA,  ; a monster meeting lava (~) turns it to sulphur (o) and is gone
        %00000111                       ; second pictures: o on odd squares, ~ on all
    },
    ; The objects: x, y, icon, then the number of uses plus OBJECT_* flags.
    {
        {32, 30, 0, OBJECT_NO_THROW + 2},                                        ; 0: Remote C.D.1
        {57, 15, 3, OBJECT_NO_CHARGES + OBJECT_NO_THROW + 2},                    ; 1: Blueprints
        {24, 30, 8, OBJECT_VANISHES + OBJECT_NO_THROW + 1},                      ; 2: Space Burger
        {31, 47, 13, OBJECT_NO_THROW + 1},                                       ; 3: Detonator
        {12, 48, 5, OBJECT_VANISHES + 1},                                        ; 4: Spanner
        {38, 46, 4, 10},                                                         ; 5: Mallet
        {54, 36, 2, OBJECT_NO_THROW + 3},                                        ; 6: Remote C.D.3
        {30, 38, 14, OBJECT_NO_CHARGES + OBJECT_VANISHES + OBJECT_NO_THROW + 1}  ; 7: Explosives
    },
    ; The monsters: x, y, the way each is going, and the order it tries
    ; turns in at each step (PATTERN_*, or four TURN_* fields, the first in
    ; bits 0-1, written out in the comment: "on" is straight on).
    {
        {45, 32, DIRECTION_UP, PATTERN_FOLLOW_EDGES},  ; 0
        {8, 31, DIRECTION_RIGHT, PATTERN_LEFT_WALL},   ; 1
        {1, 5, DIRECTION_UP, PATTERN_FOLLOW_EDGES},    ; 2
        {15, 3, DIRECTION_DOWN, PATTERN_FOLLOW_EDGES}  ; 3
    },
    ; The triggers: name, action (PUZZLE_*) and flags, where (x, y), the
    ; action's arguments A, X and Y, and the condition. The comment above
    ; each says what it does, then what the condition asks for.
    {
        ; 0: the cell at (31, 33) moves right; when facing down at a barricade (@)
        {"First Door", PUZZLE_MOVE_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT + PUZZLE_REUSABLE, 31, 32, &01, &1F, &21, &F9},
        ; 1: takes the player to (31, 30)
        {"Telept Bck", PUZZLE_TELEPORT + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT + PUZZLE_REUSABLE, IGNORE, IGNORE, &00, &1B, &1A, &00},
        ; 2: lets the player push 15 crates
        {"Strength  ", PUZZLE_PUSH_CRATES + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT + PUZZLE_REUSABLE, IGNORE, IGNORE, &0F, &00, &00, &00},
        ; 3: blows up object 7; when facing a wall (=)
        {"Detonate  ", PUZZLE_DETONATE_OBJECT + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT, 31, IGNORE + 47, &07, &00, &1C, &48},
        ; 4: (7, 48) becomes a pipe across (-); when facing left at a pipe down (|)
        {"Boob Obj 1", PUZZLE_PLACE_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT, 6, 46, &0C, &07, &30, &CD},
        ; 5: the cell in front becomes the floor (.); when facing a crate (c)
        {"Hammer    ", PUZZLE_NEXT_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT + PUZZLE_REUSABLE, IGNORE, IGNORE, &00, &00, &00, &46},
        ; 6: swaps the direction keys
        {"Puzzle 7  ", PUZZLE_DISORIENTATE + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT + PUZZLE_OFF, IGNORE, IGNORE, &15, &15, &15, &00},
        ; 7: turns on trigger 21; when facing up
```

```6502inc
; Level 2: the second of IO's four. Written as leveldata.6502inc describes,
; and as level1.6502inc's header explains; src/io.6502 makes its bytes from
; this. A mission doesn't keep its levels' trigger names (MISSION names them
; "Puzzle 1" to "Puzzle 32" when it saves one as a level file), so these
; have none.
level_2 = {
    ; The editing code, six digits: the Level Designer asks for it before it
    ; will edit the level, MISSION before it saves one of a locked mission's
    ; levels as a level file, and the game shows it once the level's done.
    "878702",
    ; The palette: the physical colours of logical colours 0-3, the "." and
    ; "1" to "3" the pictures are drawn in.
    {COLOUR_BLACK, COLOUR_BLUE, COLOUR_WHITE, COLOUR_RED},
    ; The setup. The last byte picks, for cell types 5 (#), 8 (=), 7 (o)
    ; and A (~), two bits each from bit 7 down, which squares of a
    ; checkerboard show the type's second picture: none, the odd ones
    ; (x + y odd), the even ones or all (ALTERNATE_*).
    {
        54, 23,                         ; the player starts here
        84,                             ; sulphur to collect before the exit can be lit
        250,                            ; the clock's starting value
        63, 63,                         ; the exit
        CELL_SULPHUR * 16 + CELL_LAVA,  ; a monster meeting lava (~) turns it to sulphur (o) and is gone
        %00000101                       ; second pictures: o on odd squares, ~ on odd squares
    },
    ; The objects: x, y, icon, then the number of uses plus OBJECT_* flags.
    {
        {35, 37, 14, OBJECT_VANISHES + 1},                   ; 0: Explosives
        {22, 61, 0, OBJECT_NO_THROW + 1},                    ; 1: Remote C.D.1
        {17, 59, 3, OBJECT_VANISHES + OBJECT_NO_THROW + 1},  ; 2: Blueprints
        {22, 22, 1, OBJECT_VANISHES + OBJECT_NO_THROW + 1},  ; 3: Remote C.D.2
        {42, 38, 2, OBJECT_NO_THROW + 1},                    ; 4: Remote C.D.3
        {44, 20, 14, OBJECT_VANISHES + 1},                   ; 5: Explosives
        {15, 48, 10, OBJECT_NO_THROW + 1},                   ; 6: Fire Blanket
        {10, 0, 12, OBJECT_NO_THROW + 8}                     ; 7: Extinguisher
    },
    ; The monsters: x, y, the way each is going, and the order it tries
    ; turns in at each step (PATTERN_*, or four TURN_* fields, the first in
    ; bits 0-1, written out in the comment: "on" is straight on).
    ; Monster 0's cell isn't fire (*) on the map, so on the game's first
    ; cycle the monster counts as gone (and the player scores 26 points for
    ; it), until trigger 14, 15 or 28 puts it back on the map.
    {
        {21, 30, DIRECTION_LEFT, PATTERN_LEFT_WALL},        ; 0
        {19, 41, DIRECTION_RIGHT, PATTERN_BACK_AND_FORTH},  ; 1

    },
    ; The triggers: name, action (PUZZLE_*) and flags, where (x, y), the
    ; action's arguments A, X and Y, and the condition. The comment above
    ; each says what it does, then what the condition asks for.
    {
        ; 0: blows up object 0
        {"", PUZZLE_DETONATE_OBJECT + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT, 19, 63, &00, &18, &00, &2F},
        ; 1: (26, 42) becomes the floor (.); when facing up at a barricade (@)
```

```6502inc
; Level 3: the third of IO's four. Written as leveldata.6502inc describes,
; and as level1.6502inc's header explains; src/io.6502 makes its bytes from
; this. A mission doesn't keep its levels' trigger names (MISSION names them
; "Puzzle 1" to "Puzzle 32" when it saves one as a level file), so these
; have none.
level_3 = {
    ; The editing code, six digits: the Level Designer asks for it before it
    ; will edit the level, MISSION before it saves one of a locked mission's
    ; levels as a level file, and the game shows it once the level's done.
    "218652",
    ; The palette: the physical colours of logical colours 0-3, the "." and
    ; "1" to "3" the pictures are drawn in.
    {COLOUR_BLACK, COLOUR_BLUE, COLOUR_YELLOW, COLOUR_MAGENTA},
    ; The setup. The last byte picks, for cell types 5 (#), 8 (=), 7 (o)
    ; and A (~), two bits each from bit 7 down, which squares of a
    ; checkerboard show the type's second picture: none, the odd ones
    ; (x + y odd), the even ones or all (ALTERNATE_*).
    {
        32, 63,                         ; the player starts here
        250,                            ; sulphur to collect before the exit can be lit
        240,                            ; the clock's starting value
        32, 43,                         ; the exit
        CELL_LAVA * 16 + CELL_LAVA,     ; a monster meeting lava (~) is gone, the lava staying
        %01110111                       ; second pictures: # on odd squares, = on all, o on odd squares, ~ on all
    },
    ; The objects: x, y, icon, then the number of uses plus OBJECT_* flags.
    {
        {32, 47, 0, OBJECT_NO_CHARGES + OBJECT_NO_THROW},  ; 0: Remote C.D.1
        {43, 22, 3, OBJECT_NO_THROW + 3},                  ; 1: Blueprints
        {13, 18, 1, OBJECT_NO_CHARGES + OBJECT_NO_THROW},  ; 2: Remote C.D.2
        {43, 37, 5, OBJECT_NO_CHARGES + OBJECT_NO_THROW},  ; 3: Spanner
        {19, 30, 7, OBJECT_VANISHES + 1},                  ; 4: Magnet
        {41, 8, 9, OBJECT_NO_CHARGES + OBJECT_NO_THROW},   ; 5: Jovian Wine
        {27, 60, 2, OBJECT_NO_CHARGES + OBJECT_NO_THROW},  ; 6: Remote C.D.3
        {0, 63, 4, 4}                                      ; 7: Mallet
    },
    ; The monsters: x, y, the way each is going, and the order it tries
    ; turns in at each step (PATTERN_*, or four TURN_* fields, the first in
    ; bits 0-1, written out in the comment: "on" is straight on).
    {
        {25, 7, DIRECTION_RIGHT, %01010101},            ; 0: tries on, on, on, on
        {7, 15, DIRECTION_UP, PATTERN_LEFT_WALL},       ; 1
        {17, 10, DIRECTION_UP, PATTERN_RIGHT_WALL},     ; 2

    ; The triggers: name, action (PUZZLE_*) and flags, where (x, y), the
    ; action's arguments A, X and Y, and the condition. The comment above
    ; each says what it does, then what the condition asks for.
    {
```
