```6502inc
        {"", PUZZLE_PLACE_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT, 37, 51, &00, &26, &33, &D9},
        ; 1: takes the player to (32, 14)
        {"", PUZZLE_TELEPORT + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT + PUZZLE_REUSABLE, IGNORE, IGNORE, &FF, &1C, &0A, &09},
        ; 2: (46, 23) becomes the floor (.); when facing up at lava (~)
        {"", PUZZLE_PLACE_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT, 46, 24, &00, &2E, &17, &EA},

        {"", PUZZLE_MOVE_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT, 43, 37, &00, &2B, &24, &E2},

        {"", PUZZLE_SET_LEVELS + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT, IGNORE, IGNORE, &01, &E6, &00, &06},
        ; 6: the cell in front becomes the floor (.); when facing down at a barricade (@)
        {"", PUZZLE_NEXT_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT + PUZZLE_COUNTS_COLLECTS, 32, 41, &00, &1C, &3B, &F9},
        ; 7: the cell in front becomes the floor (.); when facing a wall (#)
        {"", PUZZLE_NEXT_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT + PUZZLE_REUSABLE, IGNORE, IGNORE, &00, &14, &20, &45},
        ; 8: turns off triggers 19, 22 and 31
        {"", PUZZLE_TURN_OFF + PUZZLE_REUSABLE, 32, 14, &13, &16, &1F, &00},
        ; 9: puts monster 0 at (11, 18) going up, trying on, back, back, back; when facing left
        {"", PUZZLE_PLACE_MONSTER, 29, 14, &2C, &01, &4A, &80},
```

`src/level4.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; Level 4: the last of IO's four. Written as leveldata.6502inc describes,
; and as level1.6502inc's header explains; src/io.6502 makes its bytes from
; this. A mission doesn't keep its levels' trigger names (MISSION names them
; "Puzzle 1" to "Puzzle 32" when it saves one as a level file), so these
; have none.
level_4 = {
    ; The editing code, six digits: the Level Designer asks for it before it
    ; will edit the level, MISSION before it saves one of a locked mission's
    ; levels as a level file, and the game shows it once the level's done.
    "114226",
    ; The palette: the physical colours of logical colours 0-3, the "." and
    ; "1" to "3" the pictures are drawn in.
    {COLOUR_BLACK, COLOUR_BLUE, COLOUR_CYAN, COLOUR_RED},
    ; The setup. The last byte picks, for cell types 5 (#), 8 (=), 7 (o)
    ; and A (~), two bits each from bit 7 down, which squares of a
    ; checkerboard show the type's second picture: none, the odd ones
    ; (x + y odd), the even ones or all (ALTERNATE_*).
    {
        39, 37,                         ; the player starts here
        85,                             ; sulphur to collect before the exit can be lit
        180,                            ; the clock's starting value
        14, 10,                         ; the exit
        CELL_SULPHUR * 16 + CELL_LAVA,  ; a monster meeting lava (~) turns it to sulphur (o) and is gone
        %11110100                       ; second pictures: # on all, = on all, o on odd squares
    },
    ; The objects: x, y, icon, then the number of uses plus OBJECT_* flags.
    {
        {37, 39, 2, OBJECT_NO_CHARGES + OBJECT_NO_THROW + 1},  ; 0: Remote C.D.3
        {27, 32, 1, OBJECT_NO_CHARGES + OBJECT_NO_THROW},      ; 1: Remote C.D.2
        {33, 55, 0, OBJECT_NO_CHARGES + OBJECT_NO_THROW},      ; 2: Remote C.D.1
        {55, 56, 6, OBJECT_NO_THROW + 7},                      ; 3: Screwdriver
        {2, 44, 9, OBJECT_VANISHES + 9},                       ; 4: Jovian Wine
        {45, 13, 4, 3},                                        ; 5: Mallet
        {10, 37, 14, OBJECT_VANISHES + 1},                     ; 6: Explosives
        {11, 63, 11, OBJECT_NO_CHARGES + OBJECT_NO_THROW + 6}  ; 7: Laser Gun
    },
    ; The monsters: x, y, the way each is going, and the order it tries
    ; turns in at each step (PATTERN_*, or four TURN_* fields, the first in
    ; bits 0-1, written out in the comment: "on" is straight on).
    {
        {37, 54, DIRECTION_UP, PATTERN_RIGHT_WALL},  ; 0
        {35, 17, DIRECTION_DOWN, %00101101},         ; 1: tries on, left, right, back
        {10, 19, DIRECTION_UP, %00111101},           ; 2: tries on, left, left, back
        {12, 38, DIRECTION_UP, PATTERN_RIGHT_WALL}   ; 3
    },
    ; The triggers: name, action (PUZZLE_*) and flags, where (x, y), the
    ; action's arguments A, X and Y, and the condition. The comment above
    ; each says what it does, then what the condition asks for.
    {
        ; 0: the cell in front becomes the floor (.); when facing left at a barricade (@)
        {"", PUZZLE_NEXT_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT, 47, 49, &00, &00, &00, &C9},
        ; 1: the cell in front becomes an object ($); when facing down at a barricade (@)
        {"", PUZZLE_NEXT_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT, 37, 50, &0F, &00, &00, &F9},
        ; 2: the cell in front becomes a pipe across (-); when facing right at a barricade (@)
        {"", PUZZLE_NEXT_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT, 32, 19, &0C, &00, &00, &D9},
        ; 3: the cell in front swaps between a pipe across (-) and a pipe down (|)
        {"", PUZZLE_SWAP_NEXT + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT + PUZZLE_REUSABLE, IGNORE, IGNORE, &0C, &0D, &00, &00},
        ; 4: sets the clock to 80; when facing the floor (.)
        {"", PUZZLE_SET_LEVELS + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT + PUZZLE_REUSABLE, IGNORE, IGNORE, &01, &50, &00, &40},
        ; 5: the cell in front becomes the floor (.); when facing a crate (c)
        {"", PUZZLE_NEXT_BLOCK + PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT + PUZZLE_REUSABLE, IGNORE + 7, IGNORE + 26, &00, &00, &00, &46},
```

`src/leveldata.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; A PIPELINE level: what's in one, the notation the disc's levels are written
; in here, and how their bytes are laid out. The Level Designer edits a level
; and saves it as a level file (LEVEL1 is one; level.6502inc has where it
; keeps the parts); MISSION packs four into a mission (IO is one; io.6502inc
; has its layout), and the game plays them from there. Each level is
; described once, in src/level1.6502inc to src/level4.6502inc, and both
; src/level1.6502 and src/io.6502 make their bytes from those descriptions
; with level_names_bytes, level_fields and level_map_bytes below.
;
; A level is 11 fields, with the sizes MISSION gives them (its DATA 2090),
; and a map:
;
;   field  bytes
;   0-2    1 each  the editing code (see code_byte below), two digits in each
;   3      4       the palette: logical colour * 16 + physical, for VDU 19
;   4      8       the setup (LEVEL_* below)
;   5      32      8 objects, 4 bytes each
;   6      16      4 monsters, 4 bytes each
;   7      32      a byte for each of 32 triggers: its action and flags
;   8      64      where each trigger is: x, y
;   9      64      triggers 0-15's arguments, 4 bytes each
;   10     64      triggers 16-31's
;   map    &800    64 x 64 cells of a nibble
;
; A level file is the 32 triggers' names (the designer's, which a mission
; doesn't keep: 8 characters each, then the last 2 of each), the fields in
; order, then the map. A mission keeps each field of all four levels
; together, then the four maps.
;
; The designer calls triggers puzzles, and the game's cell types blocks (its
; menu's names for them are listed in level.6502inc).

LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES = {1, 1, 1, 4, 8, 32, 16, 32, 64, 64, 64}
; Where each field starts among a level's fields (MISSION's pnt): the
; running total of the sizes before it.
LEVEL_FIELD_OFFSETS = SUM(LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES * ((0..10) < ZIP(0..10)), 1)
LEVEL_FIELDS_SIZE = SUM(LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES)
ASSERT LEVEL_FIELDS_SIZE = &11F
LEVEL_SETUP_BYTES = LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[4]

; The setup's bytes.
LEVEL_START_X     = 0   ; the view's top left cell: the player starts 4 cells
LEVEL_START_Y     = 1   ; further in each way
LEVEL_TO_COLLECT  = 2   ; things to collect before the exit can be lit
LEVEL_TIME        = 3   ; the clock's starting value
LEVEL_EXIT_X      = 4
LEVEL_EXIT_Y      = 5
LEVEL_MONSTER_FOOD = 6  ; low nibble: a cell monsters eat; high: what they leave
LEVEL_ANIMATE     = 7   ; which squares show cells' second pictures

; LEVEL_ANIMATE has two bits for each cell type with a second picture (cell
; type 5 in the top two bits, then 8, 7 and A): they say which squares of a
; checkerboard show the second picture, a square being odd when its x + y is. The designer's menu offers Sprite A,
; Patterned and Sprite B.
ALTERNATE_NONE    = 0   ; Sprite A: the first picture everywhere
ALTERNATE_ODD     = 1   ; Patterned: the second on the odd squares
ALTERNATE_EVEN    = 2   ; the second on the even squares (not offered)
ALTERNATE_ALL     = 3   ; Sprite B: the second everywhere

; The map: 64 x 64 cells of a nibble, stored a column at a time (32 bytes per
; x, top to bottom), the even y in the top nibble.
MAP_SIZE         = 64
MAP_COLUMN_BYTES = MAP_SIZE / 2
MAP_BYTES        = MAP_SIZE * MAP_COLUMN_BYTES

; The cell types. 1-5, 8 and 9 are walls of different shapes, which the game
; treats alike. Off the map counts as lava.
CELL_FLOOR        = 0
CELL_SE_CURVE     = 1     ; walls, curved: filling the bottom right...
CELL_SW_CURVE     = 2     ; ...the bottom left...
CELL_NE_CURVE     = 3     ; ...the top right...
CELL_NW_CURVE     = 4     ; ...and the top left
CELL_WALL_1       = 5     ; a wall (the designer's Wall 1)
CELL_CRATE        = 6     ; pushed, while the player has pushes left
CELL_SULPHUR      = 7     ; to be collected, by stepping on it
CELL_WALL         = 8     ; a wall (the designer's Wall 2); also what the exit counts as
CELL_BARRICADE    = 9     ; a wall, which triggers often look for
CELL_LAVA         = &A    ; deadly
CELL_JUNCTION     = &B    ; pipes: a junction...
CELL_PIPE_ACROSS  = &C    ; ...a pipe left and right...
CELL_PIPE_DOWN    = &D    ; ...and up and down
CELL_FIRE         = &E    ; deadly: monsters mark their cells with it
CELL_OBJECT       = &F    ; an object (or the exit): see the level's objects

; Maps are drawn a character a cell, a string a row, with these for cell types
; 0-F: the floor ".", walls filling the bottom right "r", bottom left "7",
; top right "L" and top left "J" (the corners of the box-drawing shapes), a
; wall "#", a crate "c", sulphur "o", a wall "=", a barricade "@" (another
; wall, which triggers often look for), lava "~", a pipe junction "+",
; pipes across "-" and down "|", fire "*" and an object "$". (The pictures for
; them are in default.6502inc.)
MAP_KEY = ".r7LJ#co=@~+-|*$"

; A position (an object's or a trigger's x or y): the coordinate, 0-63,
; below two flags, bit 7 being an object's OBJECT_ABSENT or a trigger's
; IGNORE.
COORDINATE_BITS = &3F
POSITION_FLAGS  = &C0

; Objects: x, y, icon (one of sprites.6502inc's OBJECT_KINDS), and uses and
; flags (OBJECT_CHARGES how many uses; these flags). x and y have bit 7 set
; when the object isn't in the level.
OBJECTS           = 8
OBJECT_BYTES      = 4
OBJECT_ABSENT     = &80
OBJECT_CHARGES    = &1F
OBJECT_NO_CHARGES = &20   ; uses never run out
OBJECT_VANISHES   = &40   ; gone when used up
OBJECT_NO_THROW   = &80   ; does nothing when thrown
ASSERT LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[5] = OBJECTS * OBJECT_BYTES

; Monsters: x and y in quarter cells (4 times the cell's x and y), a
; direction (DIRECTION_LEFT to DIRECTION_DOWN, or MONSTER_GONE when it's off
; the map; the game adds 4 while one's stuck) and four choices of which way
; to try at a junction (TURN_*), the first in bits 0-1. The designer offers
; four patterns by name.
MONSTERS          = 4
MONSTER_BYTES     = 4
ASSERT LEVEL_FIELD_SIZES[6] = MONSTERS * MONSTER_BYTES
DIRECTION_LEFT    = 0
DIRECTION_RIGHT   = 1
DIRECTION_UP      = 2
DIRECTION_DOWN    = 3
DIRECTION_UP_LEFT    = 4  ; the diagonals: only Move block's direction takes them
DIRECTION_UP_RIGHT   = 5
DIRECTION_DOWN_LEFT  = 6
DIRECTION_DOWN_RIGHT = 7
MONSTER_GONE      = 8
TURN_BACK          = 0
TURN_AHEAD         = 1
TURN_CLOCKWISE     = 2    ; to the right
TURN_ANTICLOCKWISE = 3    ; to the left
PATTERN_BACK_AND_FORTH = TURN_AHEAD OR (TURN_BACK << 2) OR (TURN_ANTICLOCKWISE << 4) OR (TURN_CLOCKWISE << 6)
PATTERN_FOLLOW_EDGES   = TURN_AHEAD OR (TURN_CLOCKWISE << 2) OR (TURN_ANTICLOCKWISE << 4) OR (TURN_BACK << 6)
PATTERN_LEFT_WALL      = TURN_ANTICLOCKWISE OR (TURN_AHEAD << 2) OR (TURN_CLOCKWISE << 4) OR (TURN_BACK << 6)
PATTERN_RIGHT_WALL     = TURN_CLOCKWISE OR (TURN_AHEAD << 2) OR (TURN_ANTICLOCKWISE << 4) OR (TURN_BACK << 6)

; Triggers. The flags byte: bits 0-3 the action (PUZZLE_ACTION: PUZZLE_*,
; the designer's names, in the order of its "Puzzle types" menu), and
; PUZZLE_REUSABLE, PUZZLE_OFF, PUZZLE_COUNTS_COLLECTS and PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT.
; Where it is: x and y, bit 7 set (IGNORE) for anywhere along that axis. Its
; arguments A, X and Y say what the action does (the game's trigger_action
; and the designer's effect editors), and a fourth byte is a condition
; (CONDITION_*). A level file keeps each trigger's name: the first
; PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD characters of each, then the rest of each.
PUZZLES            = 32
PUZZLE_NAME_LENGTH = 10
PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD   = 8

PUZZLE_PLACE_BLOCK      = 0     ; cell (X, Y) becomes A
PUZZLE_MOVE_BLOCK       = 1     ; cell (X, Y) moves a cell in direction A
PUZZLE_NEXT_BLOCK       = 2     ; the cell in front becomes A
PUZZLE_SET_LEVELS       = 3     ; the clock becomes X, things to collect Y (but see SET_LEVELS_KEEP_*)
PUZZLE_THROW_OBJECT     = 4     ; object A is thrown Y cells
PUZZLE_DETONATE_OBJECT  = 5     ; object A blows up
PUZZLE_MOVE_MONSTER     = 6     ; monster X DIV 4 heads in direction A; X = &10 means all
                                ; four, which the game gets wrong (its action_set_monster)
PUZZLE_PLACE_MONSTER    = 7     ; monster A AND 3 goes to cell (A DIV 4, Y DIV 4), heading in
                                ; direction Y AND 3, with turns X
PUZZLE_TELEPORT         = 8     ; the player to (X + 4, Y + 4)
PUZZLE_SWAP_NEXT        = 9     ; the cell in front swaps between A and X
PUZZLE_TURN_ON          = 10    ; triggers A, X and Y can fire again
PUZZLE_TURN_OFF         = 11    ; triggers A, X and Y can't
PUZZLE_CHARGE_OBJECT    = 12    ; object A has Y uses, and trigger A can fire again
PUZZLE_PUSH_CRATES      = 13    ; the player can push A crates
PUZZLE_MOVE_NEXT_BLOCK  = 14    ; the cell in front is pushed a cell: the way the player
                                ; faces, turned by A (a TURN_* times 4)
PUZZLE_DISORIENTATE     = 15    ; left and right, and up and down, swap keys

PUZZLE_REUSABLE = &10           ; it can fire again
PUZZLE_OFF      = &20           ; it can't fire (set once it has, unless reusable)
PUZZLE_COUNTS_COLLECTS = &40    ; only once everything's collected
PUZZLE_USES_OBJECT = &80        ; fired by using or throwing an object, not walking on
PUZZLE_ACTION   = &0F
IGNORE          = &80

; Set levels' A: which of the clock and the number to collect to leave alone.
SET_LEVELS_KEEP_TIME     = &80
SET_LEVELS_KEEP_COLLECTS = &01

; The condition: the player (or a thrown object) must be facing
; CONDITION_DIRECTION, if CONDITION_CHECK_DIRECTION is set; the cell in
; front must be type CONDITION_CELL, if CONDITION_CHECK_CELL is set.
CONDITION_CELL            = &0F
CONDITION_DIRECTION       = &30
CONDITION_CHECK_CELL      = &40
CONDITION_CHECK_DIRECTION = &80

; Physical colours, for the palette.
COLOUR_BLACK    = 0
COLOUR_RED      = 1
COLOUR_GREEN    = 2
COLOUR_YELLOW   = 3
COLOUR_BLUE     = 4
COLOUR_MAGENTA  = 5
COLOUR_CYAN     = 6
COLOUR_WHITE    = 7

; A palette entry, as a level keeps it and VDU_PALETTE takes it apart.
FUNCTION palette_entry(logical, physical) = logical * 16 + physical

; The editing code: six digits the Level Designer asks for before it loads
; the level, and MISSION before it saves a level out of a locked mission.
; The level keeps them scrambled: each pair of digits is packed as BCD, then
; adjacent bits are swapped and the byte rotated right one place.
FUNCTION code_pair(s) = (CODES(s)[0] - '0') * 16 + CODES(s)[1] - '0'
FUNCTION code_swap(b) = ((b AND &55) << 1) OR ((b AND &AA) >> 1)
FUNCTION code_byte(s) = (code_swap(code_pair(s)) >> 1) OR ((code_swap(code_pair(s)) AND 1) << 7)
; A level is written as a list of its parts:
;
;   {
;       the editing code, six digits as a string,
;       the palette: logical colours 0-3's physical colours (COLOUR_*),
;       the setup: the player's start x and y, things to collect, the clock,
;           the exit's x and y, the monster food byte and the second
;           pictures byte (as LEVEL_* above, but the start is the player's
;           own cell),
;       the objects: 8 of {x, y, icon, uses + OBJECT_* flags},
;       the monsters: 4 of {x, y (in cells), DIRECTION_*, turns},
;       the triggers: 32 of {name, PUZZLE_* action + flags, x, y, A, X, Y,
;           condition},
;       the map: 64 rows of 64 MAP_KEY characters
;   }
;
; and these turn one into bytes. Triggers are numbered 0-31 here, as the
; game counts them (the designer shows them one more); object n can fire
; triggers n, n + 8, n + 16 and n + 24.

; A level file's trigger names: the first PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD characters of
; each, then the rest of each.
FUNCTION level_names_bytes(level)
    names = CODES(level[5][.., 0])
    ASSERT RANK(names) = 2 AND LEN(names[0]) = PUZZLE_NAME_LENGTH, "a level file's trigger names are 10 characters"
= CONCAT(FLATTEN(names[.., 0..PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD-1]), FLATTEN(names[.., PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD..PUZZLE_NAME_LENGTH-1]))

; The 11 fields' bytes, a list for each.
FUNCTION level_fields(level)
    code = level[0]
    triggers = level[5]
    ASSERT LEN(level[3]) = OBJECTS, "a level has 8 objects"
    ASSERT LEN(level[4]) = MONSTERS, "a level has 4 monsters"
    ASSERT LEN(triggers) = PUZZLES, "a level has 32 triggers"
= {
    code_byte(code[0..1]), code_byte(code[2..3]), code_byte(code[4..5]),
    palette_entry(0..3, level[1]),
    level[2] - {4, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0},
    FLATTEN(level[3]),
    FLATTEN(level[4] * {4, 4, 1, 1}),
    triggers[.., 1],
    FLATTEN(triggers[.., 2..3]),
    FLATTEN(triggers[0..15, 4..7]),
    FLATTEN(triggers[16..31, 4..7])
}

; Map rows' cell types.
FUNCTION map_cells(rows) = FIND(CODES(MAP_KEY), CODES(rows))

; Packing the map's rows in pairs gives a row of 64 bytes for each pair;
; this is where each byte of the map, which goes a column at a time, is
; among those.
FUNCTION map_column_order() = ((0..MAP_BYTES-1) MOD MAP_COLUMN_BYTES) * MAP_SIZE + (0..MAP_BYTES-1) DIV MAP_COLUMN_BYTES

; The map's bytes: the even rows' cells in the high nibbles and the odd rows'
; in the low, gathered a column at a time.
FUNCTION level_map_bytes(level)
    ASSERT LEN(level[6]) = MAP_SIZE AND RANK(CODES(level[6])) = 2, "a map is 64 rows of 64 cells"
    ASSERT LEN(level[6][0]) = MAP_SIZE, "a map is 64 rows of 64 cells"
= FLATTEN(map_cells(level[6][0..2..]) * 16 + map_cells(level[6][1..3..]))[map_column_order()]

```

`src/menu.6502`:

```6502
; $.MENU: the PIPELINE menu, by Ian Holmes ("Originally: GUILDMASTER"),
; CHAINed by !BOOT, which MRUN runs again to bring the menu back when the
; designers or MISSION finish. A BASIC program at &1900 (PAGE on a B with a
; disc filing system), and past its end, in the same file, what its DIMs
; hold:
;
;   &1900  the program: setup, the loading picture (SCREEN) and the warning
;          page (WARNING), then the menu, which starts the game or the
;          designers, redefines the keys, or CHAINs MISSION
;   &2300  C%: the scroller, a vsync event handler that scrolls a long
;          message through the bottom eight rows of the menu, and the
;          message
;   &3200  S%: the top 16 rows of the menu screen, then leftovers, among
;          them a tune program at PAGE+&1C00
;
; The source follows the same order: the BASIC block (lines 10-1020),
; then C% and S% as code and data.
;
; The game and the two designers are each started through a stub: the
; small catalogued file GAME, GRAPHIC or LEVDES, which reads the real
; program from sectors the disc's catalogue doesn't list
; (hidden_loader.6502inc). Option 1 shows TITLE before */GAME. With W and T
; held down as the menu starts, line 290 runs PL, a hidden cheat, instead.
;
; It leaves the game's ten keys in &50-&59.
INCLUDE "os.6502inc"
INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"
INCLUDE "basic.6502inc"
INCLUDE "teletext.6502inc"

; Where the scroller draws: eight rows at the bottom of the screen. Columns
; 0 and 1 hold its colour codes; 38 and 39 stay blank.
SCROLL_TOP   = 17
SCROLL_ROWS  = 8
SCROLL_LEFT  = 2
SCROLL_RIGHT = 37

; The scroller's zero page. It runs on the vsync event, under whatever BASIC
; is doing, so it keeps to the user's area (&70-&8F) - except for &60, and
; the character definition, which spills into &90-&93.
;
; Each pixel column of a character is drawn for two frames: scroll_phase
; flips between 0 and &49 every frame, and the scroller moves on to the
; next column on the frames it becomes &49. scroll_column_mask is the
; column's bit in each row of the character's definition.
SECTION scroll_phase_zero_page, org=&60, virtual=TRUE
.scroll_phase SKIP 1                ; &49 or 0
ENDSECTION
SECTION zero_page, org=&70, virtual=TRUE
.scroll_row_temp SKIP 2             ; start's pointer into the row being set up
.scroll_text_ptr SKIP 2             ; the character being scrolled in
.scroll_column_mask SKIP 1          ; the pixel column being drawn, as a bit
.scroll_text_start SKIP 2           ; set by line 300 to C%+&C9, the message
.scroll_handler_addr SKIP 2         ; set by line 300 to C%+&49, for EVNTV
    SKIP 2                          ; start leaves the row above the top's pointer here
.scroll_cell_ptrs SKIP 2 * SCROLL_ROWS  ; each scroller row's right-hand cell, top first
.char_definition SKIP 9             ; OSWORD &0A's block: the character, then its 8 rows
ENDSECTION

; keeps this. With memory cleared on BREAK (*FX200 2), Quit's reset (line
; 900), the BREAK key and PL's resets all stop at BASIC's prompt rather
; than start PIPELINE again. A Master takes a BREAK that clears memory as a

; The ten game keys go into &50-&59, as the low bytes of negative INKEY

; can't work: BASIC's indirection uses only the low 16 bits of an address,
; so ?&FFFF7C00 is ?&7C00, and reads back the 0 just written.

; Line 290 hides two bytes: VDU_DISABLE just before the quote that ends
; "...re-load this program.", and VDU_ENABLE after `*/PL "`. LIST shows
; nothing between them, hiding the cheat (with T and W held down here, the
; line runs PL), and the line reads as if it printed the message and waited
; for a key. The `":IFGET` belongs to the star command and DFS ignores it.
; Were the second-processor test ever true, OSBYTE 151 would write &7F to
; the system VIA's IER (&FE4E), turning off its interrupts, and the loop
; would hang.

; The warning page (a Mode 7 screen loaded straight into screen memory),
; for ten seconds or a key, then clear its warning text (rows 18-24), draw

; The menu. A digit 1-6 lights its option (L%, 0 for none yet), the down
; and up cursor keys (138, 139) step the light round once one is lit, and
; RETURN takes it; left and right do nothing. Options 1, 3, 4 and 5, which
; leave the menu, first stop the scroller (*FX13 4 disables the vsync
; event), let Escape work again, and set LOMEM=TOP, dropping C% and S%.
; While those are allocated, BASIC's variables end above &3000, where MODE
; 1's screen starts, so option 1's MODE 1 would stop with "Bad MODE", which
; line 80's handler turns into a hang. Option 2 stays in the menu, and
; option 6, once confirmed, resets the machine, so neither needs this.
310REPEAT
320L%=0:REPEAT

; PROCline: moves the highlight for key A%: a digit lights that option, and
; down and up (138, 139) light the next or previous one, wrapping round
; (lines 430-440 turn them into digits); before anything is lit they do
; nothing. Out: L% = the option lit. The highlight is a TT_NEW_BACKGROUND
; over the space at column 11 of the option's row (window row L%+3);

660DATA MOVE WEST,MOVE EAST,MOVE NORTH,MOVE SOUTH,PICK UP OBJECT,DROP OBJECT,USE OBJECT,THROW OBJECT,VIEW BACKPACK,VIEW MAP

; -122 until a key is down, taking the highest-numbered one held; the links

; option 5 is the mission generator.

.program_end

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
; C%: line 50's LOMEM=PAGE+&A00 starts the heap where the program ends, so
; DIM C% &EFF puts its &F00 bytes here. DIM doesn't clear them, and the file
; was saved with the scroller and its message in place.

    ASSERT P% = program + &A00

.scroller
{
; Starts the scroller (CALL C% in line 300). Writes the codes for
; separated cyan graphics into columns 0 and 1 of each scroller row, aims
; scroll_cell_ptrs at each row's right-hand cell, points EVNTV at the
; handler and enables the vsync event.
; In: scroll_text_start = the message, scroll_handler_addr = the handler.
; Out: scroll_text_ptr, scroll_column_mask and scroll_phase set for the
;      message's first column.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, scroll_row_temp, scroll_cell_ptrs - 2 (the spare slot).
.start
    LDA #&80
    STA scroll_column_mask          ; the character's leftmost pixel first
    ASL A
    STA scroll_text_ptr             ; (overwritten just below)
    STA scroll_phase
    LDA scroll_text_start
    STA scroll_text_ptr
    LDA scroll_text_start + 1
    STA scroll_text_ptr + 1

    ; Each row's pointer is the one below it less a row, starting from the
    ; bottom one. Each pass makes the pointer for the row above and, through
    ; it, puts the colour codes at the start of this row, so the last pass
    ; (row 17's codes) leaves a pointer to row 16 in the spare slot before
    ; the table.
    LDA #LO(mode7_address(SCROLL_RIGHT, SCROLL_TOP + SCROLL_ROWS - 1))
    STA scroll_cell_ptrs + 2 * (SCROLL_ROWS - 1)
    LDA #HI(mode7_address(SCROLL_RIGHT, SCROLL_TOP + SCROLL_ROWS - 1))
    STA scroll_cell_ptrs + 2 * (SCROLL_ROWS - 1) + 1
    LDX #2 * (SCROLL_ROWS - 1)
    LDY #TT_COLUMNS - SCROLL_RIGHT   ; from the row above's right cell to this row's first
.each_row
    LDA scroll_cell_ptrs, X
    SEC
    SBC #TT_COLUMNS
    STA scroll_row_temp
    STA scroll_cell_ptrs - 2, X
    LDA scroll_cell_ptrs + 1, X
    SBC #0
    STA scroll_row_temp + 1
    STA scroll_cell_ptrs - 1, X
    LDA #TT_SEPARATED
    STA (scroll_row_temp), Y
    INY
    LDA #TT_GFX_CYAN
    STA (scroll_row_temp), Y
    DEY
    DEX
    DEX
    BPL each_row

    LDA scroll_handler_addr
    STA EVNTV
    LDA scroll_handler_addr + 1
    STA EVNTV + 1
    LDA #OSBYTE_ENABLE_EVENT
.enable_vsync_event
    LDX #EVENT_VSYNC
    JMP OSBYTE

; Where line 300 points EVNTV: C%+&49, which is the operand of the LDX
; above, four bytes short of the handler. From there the bytes run as &04
; &4C and &F4 &FF, which an NMOS 6502 executes as two do-nothing NOPs
; (zero page and zero page,X: undocumented, but they only read), so the
; handler runs anyway. Presumably a slip that happened to work; a 65C02
; would take &04 as TSB &4C and set bits in BASIC's workspace.
vsync_entry = enable_vsync_event + 1
    ASSERT vsync_entry = scroller + &49

; The vsync event handler. Every frame, moves the eight scroller rows one
; cell left and fills each row's right-hand cell from one pixel column of
; the character being scrolled in: a solid block where its pixel is lit.
; A column stays for two frames, so a character is 16 cells wide and 8
; tall, and the message wraps when it reaches its terminating zero.
; Doesn't check which event it was called for: vsync is the only one on.
; In: scroll_text_ptr, scroll_column_mask and scroll_phase, as left last frame.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, char_definition.
.vsync_handler
shift_from = &100 - (SCROLL_RIGHT - SCROLL_LEFT)    ; Y counts up to zero
    LDY #shift_from
.shift_left
    LDA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT + 1, SCROLL_TOP + 0) - shift_from, Y
    STA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT, SCROLL_TOP + 0) - shift_from, Y
    LDA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT + 1, SCROLL_TOP + 1) - shift_from, Y
    STA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT, SCROLL_TOP + 1) - shift_from, Y
    LDA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT + 1, SCROLL_TOP + 2) - shift_from, Y
    STA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT, SCROLL_TOP + 2) - shift_from, Y
    LDA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT + 1, SCROLL_TOP + 3) - shift_from, Y
    STA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT, SCROLL_TOP + 3) - shift_from, Y
    LDA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT + 1, SCROLL_TOP + 4) - shift_from, Y
    STA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT, SCROLL_TOP + 4) - shift_from, Y
    LDA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT + 1, SCROLL_TOP + 5) - shift_from, Y
    STA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT, SCROLL_TOP + 5) - shift_from, Y
    LDA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT + 1, SCROLL_TOP + 6) - shift_from, Y
    STA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT, SCROLL_TOP + 6) - shift_from, Y
    LDA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT + 1, SCROLL_TOP + 7) - shift_from, Y
    STA mode7_address(SCROLL_LEFT, SCROLL_TOP + 7) - shift_from, Y
    INY
    BNE shift_left

    LDA (scroll_text_ptr), Y
    BNE have_character
    LDA scroll_text_start           ; the end of the message: start again
    STA scroll_text_ptr
    LDA scroll_text_start + 1
    STA scroll_text_ptr + 1
    LDA (scroll_text_ptr), Y
.have_character
    STA char_definition
    LDX #LO(char_definition)
    LDY #HI(char_definition)
    LDA #OSWORD_READ_CHAR_DEFINITION
    JSR OSWORD

    LDX #0                          ; (unused: X comes from Y below)
    LDY #SCROLL_ROWS - 1
.each_pixel_row
    LDA char_definition + 1, Y
    AND scroll_column_mask
    BEQ unlit                       ; zero shows as a blank cell
    LDA #SOLID_BLOCK
.unlit
    PHA
    TYA
    ASL A
    TAX
    PLA
    STA (scroll_cell_ptrs, X)       ; pixel row Y's pointer
    DEY
    BPL each_pixel_row

    LDA scroll_phase
    EOR #&49                        ; any non-zero value would do
    STA scroll_phase
    BEQ done                        ; every other frame, the same column again
    LSR scroll_column_mask
    BCC done
    LDA #&80                        ; past the rightmost pixel: on to the next character
    STA scroll_column_mask
    INC scroll_text_ptr
    BNE done
    INC scroll_text_ptr + 1
.done
    RTS
}

; The message, ended by a zero; line 300 gives its address (C%+&C9) to the
; scroller in scroll_text_start.
.scroll_text
    ASSERT scroll_text = scroller + &C9
    EQUS "PIPELINE was written by Ian Holmes and William Reeve. Or so they claim. "
    EQUS "In the 25th century, the Earth's sulphur resources have dwindled. The "
    EQUS "only supplies are from off-world sources such as the Jovian moon Io. But "
    EQUS "the temperature control systems of the Io sulphur platforms have "
    EQUS "malfunctioned, and the platforms have started to overheat. Your mission "
    EQUS "is to salvage the precious sulphur drums, then locate the helpless "
    EQUS "control robot and rescue it. However, once the robot leaves its post at "
    EQUS "the computer terminals, they will go critical and eventually explode, so "
    EQUS "you will need to be a safe distance away to escape the blast. Fires and "
    EQUS "pitfalls are deadly, but you may find the abandoned pipe network useful. "
    EQUS "Each drum you save scores one point. Rescuing the robot scores more "
    EQUS "points, and there is a one hundred point bonus if you survive the "
    EQUS "explosion. There are four levels of play, and you begin the game with "
```

`src/mission.6502`:

```6502
; $.MISSION: the PIPELINE mission generator, by Ian Holmes (with one
; procedure by William Reeve), CHAINed by MENU's option 5. A BASIC program
; at &1900 that builds a mission - the file the game plays, as IO is - from
; a graphics file (the Graphics Designer's, as DEFAULT is) and four level
; files (the Level Designer's, as LEVEL1 is), and edits the mission's name
; (two lines of text the game shows) and its features (time consumption,
; mapping ability, backpack size, throwing distance). PROCinit (line 440)
; sizes everything; docs/notes/basic.md has the file layouts. Escape, then
; Y, leaves: on disc through */MRUN, back to the menu (PROCquit).
;
; The file is one BASIC block: REMs that LIST in colour (lines 10-60), line
; 60 also hiding the machine code FNn calls; start-up and the main menu
; (lines 70-430); PROCinit and the screen and input helpers
; (440-1430); loading and saving (1450-2070); the level fields' sizes and
; the features page (2090-2430); the name page (2450), the catalogue
; (2520), and errors and quitting (2630-2890).
;
; A mission can be locked, with two undocumented keys in the main menu
; (PROClock). A locked mission can't be saved again, and gives up one of
; its levels only for that level's editing code: six digits, which the game
; shows when the player finishes the level, and which the level keeps,
; scrambled, in its first three fields.
;
; The PIPELINE disc keeps the game and both designers (H.GAME, H.GRAPH and
; H.LEVDES) in sector runs past its last catalogued file, which the
; catalogue doesn't mention and DFS counts as free space, so saving onto
; that disc overwrites them (PROCsavemss has how). The catalogued GAME,
; GRAPHIC and LEVDES are only stubs that read those runs.
;
; Bytes a line can't hold as text (teletext codes, VDU codes, the machine
; code) are spliced in: a line ending in `{` drops into assembler, and `}`
; carries on with the same line.
INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"
INCLUDE "basic.6502inc"
INCLUDE "teletext.6502inc"

editing_code = basic_integer("E")   ; FNn's code, scrambled in place
swap_temp    = BASIC_USER_ZP

SECTION mission, filename="MISSION", org=&1900, load=&FFFF1900, exec=&FFFF8023
.program
BASIC
; Lines 10-60 are REMs of teletext codes that LIST shows as the title and
; credits in colour (the quote makes LIST copy the bytes rather than expand
; them as keywords, and VDU_DELETE wipes it), then MENU's "Hello, all my
; friends!" band. Line 60 also carries machine code.
10REM"{
    EQUB VDU_DELETE }   {
    EQUB TT_ALPHA_CYAN } PIPELINE
20REM"{
    EQUB VDU_DELETE, TT_ALPHA_YELLOW }MISSION GENERATOR.
30REM"{
    EQUB VDU_DELETE, TT_ALPHA_MAGENTA }By{
    EQUB TT_ALPHA_GREEN }Ian Holmes !
40REM"{
    EQUB VDU_DELETE, TT_ALPHA_MAGENTA }Game by{
    EQUB TT_ALPHA_GREEN }IAN HOLMES
50REM"{
    EQUB VDU_DELETE, TT_ALPHA_MAGENTA }and{
    EQUB TT_ALPHA_GREEN }WILLIAM REEVE
60REM"{
    EQUB VDU_DELETE, TT_ALPHA_BLUE, TT_NEW_BACKGROUND, TT_ALPHA_GREEN, TT_DOUBLE_HEIGHT }Hello,{
    EQUB TT_ALPHA_YELLOW, TT_FLASH }all my friends!  {
    EQUB TT_BLACK_BACKGROUND }          {
    EQUB TT_ALPHA_BLUE, TT_NEW_BACKGROUND, TT_ALPHA_GREEN, TT_DOUBLE_HEIGHT }Hello,{
    EQUB TT_ALPHA_YELLOW, TT_FLASH }all my friends!  {
    EQUB TT_BLACK_BACKGROUND
    EQUB VDU_DISABLE                ; LIST shows nothing from here...

; Scrambles the editing code FNn has read into E% (CALL PAGE+198, line
; 1170) the way a level stores its code (leveldata.6502inc's code_byte), so
; PROCsavelev can compare it with the level's fields 0-2: each of E%'s low
; three bytes has its adjacent bits swapped, then is rotated right one
; place. MISSION never turns a stored code back into digits; it scrambles
; the typed one to compare.
; In: E% = the six digits read as hex, &00dddddd.
; Out: E%'s low three bytes scrambled.
; Clobbers: A, X, swap_temp.
.scramble_editing_code
    ASSERT scramble_editing_code = program + 198
    LDX #2
.each_byte
    LDA editing_code, X
    PHA
    AND #%01010101
    ASL A
    STA swap_temp
    PLA
    AND #%10101010
    LSR A
    ORA swap_temp
    PHA                             ; rotate right, bit 0 into bit 7
    LSR A
    PLA
    ROR A
    STA editing_code, X
    DEX
    BPL each_byte
    RTS
    EQUB VDU_ENABLE                 ; ...to here
}
; Start-up. Line 90's error handler covers only the set-up: it reports the
; error and skips to line 130. For Escape (error 17) it would ask whether
; to quit and, if not, fall into line 100 and start afresh ("Sorry about
; the GOTO"), but Escape is just a key (*FX229 1) until line 140, so that
; can't happen. From line 130 an error is reported (Escape asks whether to
; quit) and the menu carries on at line 140.
70:
80*FX229 1
90ONERRORPROCerr:IFERR<>17GOTO130
100REM Sorry about the GOTO
110CLEAR
120MODE7:PROCinit
130ONERRORPROCerr
140*FX229
; The main menu: 1-9 (1-8 on tape, which has no catalogue) or the down and
; up cursor keys pick an option (K%), RETURN does it; OR 16 lets the
; shifted digits count. The undocumented i and h keys (lower case, so Caps
; Lock off) go straight to "save a mission" with I% set, which locks the
; saved mission (PROClock, line 1390). Any other key clears I%.
150REPEAT
160CLS
170PRINT"Key:";
180RESTORE420
190FORN%=1TOopts
200READA$
210PRINTTAB(7);N%" to "A$TAB(28)CHR$(132)CHR$(157);:NEXT
220PRINTTAB(3)"ESCAPE to leave this program"
230VDU26:K%=0:REPEAT
240REPEAT:A%=GET:*FX15
250I%=0:IFA%=105ORA%=104PROClock
260IFA%>13ANDA%<138 A%=A%OR16
270UNTILA%>=49ANDA%<=(opts+48)ORA%=13ORA%=138ORA%=139
280IFA%<>13PROCline
290UNTILA%=13ANDK%>0:PROCw
300PRINTTAB(0,opts+2);
310IFK%=1PROCmiss
320IFK%=2PROCattrs
330IFK%=3PROCloadgrf(FNname)
340IFK%=4PROCsavegrf
350IFK%=5PROCloadlev
360IFK%=6PROCsavelev
370IFK%=7PROCloadmss
380IFK%=8PROCsavemss
390IFK%=9PROCviewcat
400UNTIL0
410:
420DATAchange name,change features,load graphics,save graphics,load a level,save a level,load a mission,save a mission,see a catalogue
430:
; PROCinit: the sizes behind every file MISSION reads and writes, and
; memory for them. The sizes, in bytes:
;   size    one level: its fields (data) and its &800-byte map
;   data    one level's 11 fields (DATA 2090 has each one's size)
;   grfs    a graphics set's pictures
;   attrs   the features
;   miss    the mission's name: two halves of 15
;   names   the tail of a graphics file: the picture for a map cell marked
;           as holding an object when none is there, then the 15 object
;           names
;   puznms  a level file's puzzle names, 32 of 10 characters
; numlev is the levels in a mission, and opts the options the main menu
; offers. The memory:
;   F%   a mission, as saved: names, the name (miss), the features
;        (attrs), then from L% the four levels - each of the 11 fields for
;        all four levels together, then the four maps - and from G% the
;        graphics, with room after them for the tail a graphics file
;        brings (PROCloadgrf loads the whole file at G%)
;   B%   one level file: puzzle names, fields, map
;   addr where a saved mission reloads, so it ends at &5800 (&242D)
;   osc  PROCosc's command buffer
; T% is TRUE on tape: OSARGS 0,0 gives the filing system, 1 or 2 for tape.
; The layouts are in docs/notes/basic.md; io.6502inc computes IO's from the
; same sizes, and leveldata.6502inc describes the 11 fields.
440DEFPROCinit
450Y%=0:A%=0
460X%=USR(&FFDA)AND&FF
470T%=(X%=1ORX%=2)
480*FX4 1
490numlev=4
500size=&91F
510grfs=&E00
520attrs=5
530miss=30
540names=&134
550data=size-&800
560puznms=320
570opts=9+T%
580DIM F% (2*names+miss+attrs+numlev*size+grfs)
590DIM osc 40,B% size+puznms
600L%=F%+names+miss+attrs
610G%=L%+numlev*size
620addr=&5800-numlev*size-grfs-attrs-miss-names
630PROCtitle
640PRINT''TAB(1-7*T%)CHR$(134)CHR$(157)CHR$(132);
650IFT%PRINT"Please wait";ELSEPRINT"Loading Standard Graphics";
660PRINT":  "CHR$(157)
; A blank mission: names, the mission's name and the features cleared;
; every level's palette (field 3) &31 &22 &14 &00 (3 red, 2 green, 1 blue,
; 0 black: see leveldata.6502inc's palette_entry), fields 4-10 &FF and an
; empty map; features time 15 (shown as 9), mapping 2, backpack 2 (shown
; as 3), throwing 6, unlocked.
; Fields 0-2, the editing codes, are left as memory held them, except
; level 0's field 0, which the features' clearing runs into (line 670 ends
; at L%+0). The &FF fill starts at numlev*4, inside field 3, which line 760
; then writes. On disc, DEFAULT's graphics too.
670FORN%=0TOnames+miss+4STEP4
680N%!F%=0:NEXT
690FORN%=numlev*4TOnumlev*data-4STEP4
700L%!N%=-1:NEXT
710L%!(numlev*data-4)=-1
720FORN%=(numlev*data)TO(numlev*size)STEP4
730L%!N%=0:NEXT
740X%=L%+(numlev*3)
750FORN%=0TOnumlev-1
760X%!(N%*4)=1319473
770NEXT:F%?(names+miss)=15
780F%!(names+miss+1)=393730
790IFNOTT%THENPROCloadgrf("Default")
800ENDPROC
; PROCcursor: turns the cursor off (0) or on (1).
810DEFPROCcursor(N%)
820VDU23,1,N%;0;0;0;
830ENDPROC
; PROCtitle: the double-height title, yellow on red, and below it a blue
; panel from row 4 down (blue background from column 1, yellow text from
; column 2, black again at column 38); PROCw sets the text window inside
; it. C% is 1 while something else is on the screen (a catalogue or an
; error box), so that PROCerr knows to call PROCtitle again.
840DEFPROCtitle
850PROCcursor(0)
860VDU26,12:FORN%=1TO2
870PRINTTAB(3,N%)CHR$(141)CHR$(129)CHR$(157)CHR$(131)"PIPELINE Mission Generator  "CHR$(156)
880NEXT:FORN%=4TO24
890PRINTTAB(0,N%)CHR$(132)CHR$(157)CHR$(131)TAB(38,N%)CHR$(156);:NEXT
900PROCw:C%=0:ENDPROC
910DEFPROCw:VDU28,3,23,36,5:ENDPROC
; PROCline: moves the highlight for key A%. Less 48, the digits are 1-9 and
; the down and up cursor keys (138, 139) are 90 and 91, which step the
; highlight down and up, wrapping round; before anything is lit they do
; nothing. Then highlights option K% (screen row K%+4: line 230's VDU 26
; left the whole screen as the window) with a green background from column
; 8 and blue text.
920DEFPROCline:A%=A%-48
930IFA%>89ANDK%=0ENDPROC
940IFA%=90A%=K%+1:IFA%>opts A%=1
950IFA%=91A%=K%-1:IFA%=0A%=opts
960*FX19
970IFK%>0ANDK%<>A%VDU31,7,K%+4,32,32,32
980K%=A%:VDU31,7,K%+4,130,157,132
990ENDPROC
1000:
; PROCosc: runs a * command (every load, save and catalogue goes through
; it). The parameter is the string indirection $osc, so calling it writes
; the command straight into the buffer that OSCLI is handed.
1010DEFPROCosc($osc)
1020X%=osc MOD256:Y%=osc DIV256
1030CALL&FFF7:ENDPROC
; FNinput: prompt A$, then a field of N% characters accepting codes
; between min and max (exclusive), with DELETE; returns it on RETURN.
1040DEFFNinput(A$,N%,min,max)
1050PRINTA$CHR$(134)CHR$(157)CHR$(132)SPC(N%+2)CHR$(157)STRING$(N%+3,CHR$(8));:PROCcursor(1)
1060A$="":REPEAT
1070REPEAT:A%=GET
1080IFA%>min ANDA%<max ANDLEN(A$)=N% VDU7
1090UNTIL(A%=127ANDLEN(A$)>0)ORA%=13OR(A%>min ANDA%<max ANDLEN(A$)<N%)
1100VDUA%:IFA%=13PRINT
1110IFA%>min ANDA%<max A$=A$+CHR$(A%)
1120IFA%=127 A$=LEFT$(A$,LEN(A$)-1)
1130UNTILA%=13:PROCcursor(0):=A$
; FNname asks for a filename (12 characters; 10 on tape). FNlevel asks for
; a level, 1-4, and returns 0-3. FNn asks for an editing code: six digits,
; taken as hex (EVAL "&0..."), so each pair becomes one BCD byte, then
; scrambled as levels store their codes, by the code hidden in line 60.
1140DEFFNname=FNinput("Enter filename: ",12+2*T%,32,127)
1150DEFFNlevel=(VAL(FNinput("Which level number ? ",1,48,49+numlev))-1)AND3
1160DEFFNn
1170E%=EVAL("&0"+FNinput("Enter editing code: ",6,47,58)):CALLPAGE+198:=E%
; FNattr: feature N%'s name and value as shown; time is stored 6 higher and
; backpack size 1 lower than shown.
1180DEFFNattr(N%)
1190RESTORE2110:FORA%=0TON%
1200READA$:NEXT:A%=F%?(names+miss+N%)
1210IFN%=0A%=A%-6ELSEIFN%=2A%=A%+1
1220=A$+": "+STR$(A%)+STRING$(8," ")
; PROCbit: shows, in quotes, the half of the mission's name at offset A%
; (0 or 15): its 12 characters, skipping the VDU 31,x,y that places it,
; with the 9s (cursor right) showing as gaps. PROCstore puts A$ there,
; padded to 12, with spaces as 9 so the game's background shows through
; them.
1230DEFPROCbit(A%)

1250X%=F%?(names+A%+N%)
1260IFX%>31ANDX%<127ORX%=9VDUX%
1270NEXT:VDU34:ENDPROC

1320NEXT:ENDPROC
; PROCname: names puzzle N% in a level file: eight characters at
; B%+(N%-1)*8, two more at B%+256+(N%-1)*2.

; lock stops MISSION saving the mission again or giving up a level without
; its code. Only h's matters to the game, which tests the lock byte for

; it shows a competition entry code.

; PROCloadlev: a level file into level S% (0-3) of the mission: the map,

1600S%=FNlevel:PRINT

; PROCsavelev: the reverse, for level S% (0-3). A locked mission (L%?-1,
; the lock byte, set) gives up a level only for the editing code that
; scrambles to its fields 0-2; any other code goes quietly back to the menu
; (IO's level 1 wants 677636). The puzzle names aren't kept in a mission,
; so they are reset to "Puzzle 1" and on. The file reloads to end at
; &3000, exec &8380, as the Level Designer saves a level. As with the
; designer's saves, the first onto the PIPELINE disc fits at sectors
; &114-&11E, short of H.GAME's, and a second goes over H.GAME's first
; eight sectors.
1760DEFPROCsavelev

1830Z%!X%=Z%!Y%

1860X%=B%+puznms+pnt
1870Y%=L%+numlev*pnt+S%*ext
1880FORD%=0TOext-1
1890D%?X%=D%?Y%
1900NEXT:pnt=pnt+ext:NEXT
1910FORN%=1TO32
1920PROCname("Puzzle "+STR$N%+"  ")
1930NEXT:PROCosc("SAVE "+CHR$(34)+FNname+CHR$(34)+" "+STR$~B%+"+"+STR$~(size+puznms)+" 8380 "+STR$~(&3000-size-puznms))
1940ENDPROC
1950:
; PROCloadmss: a whole mission over F%; a locked one loads like any other.
1960DEFPROCloadmss

; PROCsavemss: places the two halves of the name (VDU 31,18,16 and VDU
; 31,14,17: column and row on the game's screen), refuses a locked mission
; (quietly, before asking for a filename), sets the lock byte to I% and
; saves to reload at addr, ending at &5800. Nothing asks for another disc
; first, and on the PIPELINE disc the save destroys the hidden programs,
; as DFS counts the sectors past the last catalogued file as free. The
; first mission (&34 sectors) lands at sectors &114-&147, over all of
; H.GAME and H.GRAPH's first three sectors: the GAME stub still reads its

; half of H.LEVDES, and a third the rest of H.LEVDES before it runs off the

; every file there is). docs/notes/basic.md has the details.
```
