`src/mrun.6502`:

```6502
; $.MRUN: &80 bytes at sector &100, loaded and run at &0780. That's the top
; half of page 7, BASIC's keyboard input buffer: free while the editors run,
; and the command MRUN types for BASIC lands in the bottom half. The
; Graphics Designer, the Level Designer and MISSION all run `*/MRUN` to get
; back to the menu.
;
; It undoes the editors' hooks - RDCHV (the Level Designer's, still in place
; when it runs /MRUN) and EVNTV with the Escape event (the Graphics
; Designer's) - then types `*E.!BOOT` into the keyboard buffer and starts
; BASIC, which reads that as its first command: the boot file runs again
; from the top, and the menu comes back as it did at boot.
;
; What's left of the file past the text is whatever was in memory when it
; was saved. The rest of its sector on the disc holds more stale bytes,
; which src/disc.toml records.

INCLUDE "os.6502inc"
INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"

; Zero page: BASIC's, unused until BASIC starts, which is the last thing
; this does. &50 serves twice, in turn.
SECTION zero_page, org=&50, virtual=TRUE
.typed_index                ; next character of boot_command to type
.default_vectors SKIP 2     ; the MOS's table of default vector contents
ENDSECTION

SECTION mrun, filename="MRUN", org=&0780, load=&780, exec=&780
.mrun
{
; Entry from *RUN; never returns.
.start
    ; Twice over, and X is set again before it's used: perhaps left over
    ; from when the Escape event's OSBYTE, below, came first.
    LDX #EVENT_ESCAPE
    LDX #EVENT_ESCAPE

    ; Put RDCHV and EVNTV back to the MOS defaults, from the ROM's table.
    LDA MOS_DEFAULT_VECTORS_PTR
    STA default_vectors
    LDA MOS_DEFAULT_VECTORS_PTR+1
    STA default_vectors+1
    LDY #RDCHV - USERV
    LDA (default_vectors), Y
    STA RDCHV
    INY
    LDA (default_vectors), Y
    STA RDCHV+1
    LDY #EVNTV - USERV
    LDA (default_vectors), Y
    STA EVNTV
    INY
    LDA (default_vectors), Y
    STA EVNTV+1
    LDA #OSBYTE_DISABLE_EVENT
    LDX #EVENT_ESCAPE
    JSR OSBYTE

    ; Type boot_command, up to and including its CR.
    LDY #0
    STY typed_index
.type_next
    LDA boot_command, Y
    PHA
    TAY
    LDX #BUFFER_KEYBOARD
    LDA #OSBYTE_INSERT_BUFFER
    JSR OSBYTE
    PLA
    INC typed_index
    LDY typed_index
    CMP #CR
    BNE type_next

    ; *BASIC makes BASIC the current language, and BASIC reads what was
    ; typed as its first command.
    LDX #LO(start_basic)
    LDY #HI(start_basic)
    JMP OSCLI

; Typed into the keyboard buffer for BASIC to read. BASIC's line input
; echoes the control codes as it reads them, so CTRL-V CTRL-G (VDU 22,7)
; clears to a MODE 7 screen before the boot file starts, but stores only
; printable characters: the command BASIC runs is "*E.!BOOT  ".
.boot_command
    EQUS "*E.!BOOT"
    EQUB VDU_MODE, 7            ; MODE 7
    EQUS "  ", CR

.start_basic
    EQUS "*BASIC", CR

; Uninitialised to the end of the file, which was saved as half a page:
; zeros, then stale memory.
.unused
    SKIP 13
    EQUB &B8, &A7, &EE, &A5, &A6, &A6, &8D, &A6
    EQUB &CA, &AC, &41, &A5, &19, &A5, &4A, &2E
    ASSERT P% - start = &80
}
ENDSECTION

```

`src/os.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; The BBC Micro's operating system entry points, vectors and memory-mapped
; hardware: addresses only, shared by every piece. tools/dis6502.py names
; operands from this file, so add here rather than defining an OS address
; locally. Call numbers and other constants are in osconst.6502inc.

; The 6502's own vectors, in the MOS ROM.
CPU_NMI_VECTOR   = &FFFA
CPU_RESET_VECTOR = &FFFC
CPU_IRQ_VECTOR   = &FFFE

; Where the MOS keeps the address of its table of default vector contents
; (laid out like page 2 from USERV, ?&FFB6 bytes long).
MOS_DEFAULT_VECTORS_PTR = &FFB7

; MOS entry points.
OSRDRM = &FFB9
VDUCHR = &FFBC
OSEVEN = &FFBF
GSINIT = &FFC2
GSREAD = &FFC5
NVRDCH = &FFC8
NVWRCH = &FFCB
OSFIND = &FFCE
OSGBPB = &FFD1
OSBPUT = &FFD4
OSBGET = &FFD7
OSARGS = &FFDA
OSFILE = &FFDD
OSRDCH = &FFE0
OSASCI = &FFE3
OSNEWL = &FFE7
OSWRCH = &FFEE
OSWORD = &FFF1
OSBYTE = &FFF4
OSCLI  = &FFF7

; MOS zero page. tools/dis6502.py doesn't name zero-page operands from this
; file: a game that takes the machine over reuses these bytes for itself.

; The internal key number (bit 7 set) of the key last pressed, while it's held.
MOS_KEY_PRESSED = &EC

; After a BRK: the address of its error number, with the message following.
MOS_ERROR_PTR = &FD

; Bit 7 set while an Escape condition is pending.
MOS_ESCAPE_FLAG = &FF

; The startup options: the keyboard links, read by the OS at reset (bits 0-2
; the screen mode, bit 3 the boot action, bits 4-5 the disc timings).
MOS_STARTUP_OPTIONS = &028F

; Decremented every vsync, 50 times a second.
MOS_VSYNC_COUNTER = &0240

; Vectors in page 2.
USERV = &0200
BRKV  = &0202
IRQ1V = &0204
IRQ2V = &0206
CLIV  = &0208
BYTEV = &020A
WORDV = &020C
WRCHV = &020E
RDCHV = &0210
FILEV = &0212
ARGSV = &0214
BGETV = &0216
BPUTV = &0218
GBPBV = &021A
FINDV = &021C
FSCV  = &021E
EVNTV = &0220
UPTV  = &0222
NETV  = &0224
VDUV  = &0226
KEYV  = &0228
INSV  = &022A
REMV  = &022C
CNPV  = &022E
IND1V = &0230
IND2V = &0232
IND3V = &0234

; Where the OS keeps the envelopes ENVELOPE defines, 16 bytes each from
; envelope 1.
MOS_ENVELOPES = &08C0

; Where the OS jumps on an NMI: a filing system puts its handler here.
MOS_NMI_ROUTINE = &0D00

; The extended vector table: a ROM address and bank for each vector, used
; when a vector points at its extended entry point.
MOS_EXTENDED_VECTORS = &0D9F

; 6845 CRTC.
CRTC_ADDR = &FE00
CRTC_DATA = &FE01

; Video ULA.
ULA_CONTROL = &FE20
ULA_PALETTE = &FE21

; Sideways ROM select.
ROMSEL = &FE30

; System VIA: keyboard, sound, vsync and the addressable latch.
SYSVIA_ORB  = &FE40
SYSVIA_ORA  = &FE41
SYSVIA_DDRB = &FE42
SYSVIA_DDRA = &FE43
SYSVIA_T1CL = &FE44
SYSVIA_T1CH = &FE45
SYSVIA_T1LL = &FE46
SYSVIA_T1LH = &FE47
SYSVIA_T2CL = &FE48
SYSVIA_T2CH = &FE49
SYSVIA_SR   = &FE4A
SYSVIA_ACR  = &FE4B
SYSVIA_PCR  = &FE4C
SYSVIA_IFR  = &FE4D
SYSVIA_IER  = &FE4E
SYSVIA_ORA_NH = &FE4F               ; port A again, without the handshake

; User VIA: printer port, user port and the second timer pair.
USRVIA_ORB  = &FE60
USRVIA_ORA  = &FE61
USRVIA_DDRB = &FE62
USRVIA_DDRA = &FE63
USRVIA_T1CL = &FE64
USRVIA_T1CH = &FE65
USRVIA_T1LL = &FE66
USRVIA_T1LH = &FE67
USRVIA_T2CL = &FE68
USRVIA_T2CH = &FE69
USRVIA_SR   = &FE6A
USRVIA_ACR  = &FE6B
USRVIA_PCR  = &FE6C
USRVIA_IFR  = &FE6D
USRVIA_IER  = &FE6E
USRVIA_ORA_NH = &FE6F               ; port A again, without the handshake

; 8271 floppy disc controller.
FDC_COMMAND_STATUS = &FE80   ; command on write, status on read
FDC_PARAM_RESULT   = &FE81   ; parameter on write, result on read
FDC_DATA           = &FE84

; uPD7002 analogue to digital converter (joysticks).
ADC_STATUS = &FEC0
ADC_HIGH   = &FEC1
ADC_LOW    = &FEC2

```

`src/osconst.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; The machine's numbers, other than addresses (os.6502inc has those), for
; every piece: OSBYTE, OSWORD and filing system call numbers and their
; settings, service calls, SOUND channels, buffers and events; internal key
; numbers and the codes keys give; characters; VDU and PLOT codes; 6845 CRTC
; registers; screen memory in the modes the pieces use; 6502 opcodes; and
; the 8271 disc controller's commands as OSWORD &7F passes them. A name here
; means the same in every piece; a program's own settings (its *FX225 base,
; its own screen layout) stay in its own include.

; OSBYTE calls.
OSBYTE_CURSOR_EDITING     = &04 ; *FX4: X = CURSOR_KEYS_*
OSBYTE_AUTO_REPEAT_DELAY  = &0B ; *FX11: X centiseconds before a key repeats; 0 turns auto-repeat off
OSBYTE_AUTO_REPEAT_PERIOD = &0C ; *FX12: X centiseconds between repeats
OSBYTE_DISABLE_EVENT      = &0D ; X = event number
OSBYTE_ENABLE_EVENT       = &0E ; X = event number
OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS      = &0F ; *FX15: X=0 all buffers, 1 just input
OSBYTE_WAIT_VSYNC         = &13 ; *FX19: wait for the next vertical sync (X and Y come back changed)
OSBYTE_RAISE_ESCAPE       = &7D ; set the Escape flag, as the key would (no event)
OSBYTE_ACKNOWLEDGE_ESCAPE = &7E ; clear an Escape; X = &FF if there was one, else 0
OSBYTE_INKEY              = &81 ; X, Y = INKEY's argument; for a key test, X = Y = &FF if it's down
OSBYTE_READ_CHAR_AND_MODE = &87 ; X = the character at the text cursor, Y = the mode
OSBYTE_INSERT_BUFFER      = &8A ; X = buffer, Y = character
OSBYTE_OPT                = &8B ; *OPT X, Y
OSBYTE_SERVICE_CALL       = &8F ; X = the service call, Y its argument
OSBYTE_WRITE_SHEILA       = &97 ; *FX151: X = offset in page &FE, Y = the value
OSBYTE_BREAK_EFFECT       = &C8 ; *FX200: bit 0 disables Escape, bit 1 clears memory on BREAK
OSBYTE_KEYBOARD_STATUS    = &CA ; *FX202: bit 4 clear Caps Lock, bit 5 clear
                                ; Shift Lock, bit 7 set Shift reverses Caps Lock
OSBYTE_BELL_DURATION      = &D6 ; *FX214
OSBYTE_FUNCTION_KEY_BASE  = &E1 ; *FX225: X = f0's code (f1 one more...), or FUNCTION_KEYS_STRINGS
OSBYTE_ESCAPE_KEY         = &E5 ; *FX229: X=0 Escape key makes an escape condition
OSBYTE_ESCAPE_EFFECTS     = &E6 ; *FX230: X=1 an escape condition does nothing else

; *FX4's settings: what the cursor keys and COPY do.
CURSOR_KEYS_EDIT  = 0           ; copy editing
CURSOR_KEYS_CODES = 1           ; they give codes, &87 (COPY) to &8B
CURSOR_KEYS_SOFT  = 2           ; COPY and the cursor keys are function keys 11-15

; *FX225's setting for the function keys to give their strings (*KEY), as
; they do at first.
FUNCTION_KEYS_STRINGS = 1

; Service calls (OSBYTE_SERVICE_CALL).
SERVICE_CLAIM_ABSOLUTE = 1      ; claim absolute workspace
SERVICE_CLAIM_PRIVATE  = 2      ; claim private workspace

; OSWORD calls.
OSWORD_READ_LINE            = &00   ; YX: buffer address (2), max length, lowest and highest character
OSWORD_READ_INTERVAL_TIMER  = &03   ; YX: 5 bytes
OSWORD_WRITE_INTERVAL_TIMER = &04   ; YX: 5 bytes
OSWORD_SOUND                = &07   ; YX: channel, amplitude, pitch, duration (2 bytes each)
OSWORD_READ_CHAR_DEFINITION = &0A   ; YX: the character, then its 8 rows of pixels, top first
OSWORD_READ_PALETTE         = &0B   ; YX: logical colour; returns the physical one after it
OSWORD_WRITE_PALETTE        = &0C   ; YX: logical colour, physical colour, 0, 0, 0

; A SOUND channel number: the channel in the low nibble, flags above it,
; and in its high byte the number of other channels to wait for.
SOUND_FLUSH   = &10             ; flush the channel's queue first
SOUND_SYNC_1  = &01             ; (high byte) wait for one other channel
CHANNEL_NOISE = 0               ; channels 1-3 are tones

; OSFILE calls, and the object type OSFILE_READ_INFO returns in A.
OSFILE_SAVE      = &00
OSFILE_READ_INFO = &05          ; fills the block with the catalogue entry
OSFILE_LOAD      = &FF
OSFILE_TYPE_FILE = 1            ; (0 no such object, 2 a directory)

; OSFIND calls: close (Y = handle, 0 for all), or open the file named at YX.
OSFIND_CLOSE       = &00
OSFIND_OPEN_INPUT  = &40
OSFIND_OPEN_UPDATE = &C0

; OSGBPB calls, at the pointer given in the block.
OSGBPB_WRITE_AT = 1
OSGBPB_READ_AT  = 3

; OSARGS with A = 0 and Y = 0 reads the current filing system's number;
; 4 and up are disc (and network) filing systems, below that tape and ROM.
OSARGS_READ_FS = &00
FS_DISC        = 4

; FSCV calls.
FSCV_OPT = &00                  ; *OPT X,Y

; Buffer numbers for OSBYTE &8A and friends. Sound channel n's buffer is
; BUFFER_SOUND_0 + n.
BUFFER_KEYBOARD = 0
BUFFER_SOUND_0  = 4

; Event numbers.
EVENT_OUTPUT_EMPTY = 0          ; X = the buffer
EVENT_VSYNC        = 4
EVENT_ESCAPE       = 6

; Internal key numbers (each key's place in the keyboard matrix).
; INKEY_TEST(k) is the byte OSBYTE_INKEY takes in X to test key k, with
; Y = &FF: BASIC's INKEY -(k+1).
KEY_SHIFT  = &00
KEY_CTRL   = &01
KEY_3      = &11
KEY_4      = &12
KEY_F7     = &16
KEY_LEFT   = &19
KEY_F0     = &20
KEY_T      = &23
KEY_I      = &25
KEY_0      = &27
KEY_DOWN   = &29
KEY_1      = &30
KEY_2      = &31
KEY_R      = &33
KEY_U      = &35
KEY_O      = &36
KEY_UP     = &39
KEY_A      = &41
KEY_X      = &42
KEY_Y      = &44
KEY_COLON  = &48
KEY_RETURN = &49
KEY_S      = &51
KEY_C      = &52
KEY_N      = &55
KEY_DELETE = &59
KEY_Z      = &61
KEY_SPACE  = &62
KEY_B      = &64
KEY_SLASH  = &68
KEY_COPY   = &69
KEY_F1     = &71
KEY_F2     = &72
KEY_F3     = &73
KEY_F6     = &75
KEY_F8     = &76
KEY_F9     = &77
KEY_RIGHT  = &79
FUNCTION INKEY_TEST(key) = &FF - key

; The codes OSRDCH returns for the cursor keys after *FX4,1
; (CURSOR_KEYS_CODES). With *FX4,2 they're function keys 12-15 instead, and
; give whatever *FX225 made of those.
KEYCODE_LEFT  = &88
KEYCODE_RIGHT = &89
KEYCODE_DOWN  = &8A
KEYCODE_UP    = &8B

; Characters with no name of their own in a string, and CTRL with a letter
; (ctrl('U') is 21). Printable characters are written as baron's character
; literals, 'A' for &41, which leave nothing in the symbol dump.
BEL = 7
CR  = 13
ESC = &1B                       ; what OSBYTE &81 gives in Y on Escape
DEL = &7F
FUNCTION ctrl(c) = c AND &1F

; VDU codes.
VDU_TEXT_CURSOR   = 4           ; text at the text cursor
VDU_ENABLE        = 6           ; undo VDU_DISABLE
VDU_BACKSPACE     = 8
VDU_RIGHT         = 9           ; cursor right: a space that doesn't paint
VDU_CLS           = 12
VDU_PAGED_ON      = 14
VDU_PAGED_OFF     = 15
VDU_COLOUR        = 17          ; VDU 17, n: COLOUR n; n + COLOUR_BACKGROUND for the background
VDU_GCOL          = 18          ; VDU 18, mode, colour
VDU_PALETTE       = 19          ; VDU 19, logical, physical, 0, 0, 0
VDU_DISABLE       = 21          ; ignore everything sent to the screen until VDU_ENABLE
VDU_MODE          = 22
VDU_DEFINE        = 23          ; VDU 23, 0, register, value, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0: a CRTC register
VDU_PLOT          = 25          ; VDU 25, k, x; y;
VDU_RESET_WINDOWS = 26
VDU_TEXT_WINDOW   = 28          ; VDU 28, left, bottom, right, top
VDU_TAB           = 31          ; VDU 31, x, y
VDU_DELETE        = 127         ; back a character and blank it
COLOUR_BACKGROUND = &80

; PLOT numbers.
PLOT_MOVE_RELATIVE = 0
PLOT_DRAW_RELATIVE = 1
PLOT_MOVE          = 4

; 6845 CRTC registers: write the number to CRTC_ADDR, then the value to
; CRTC_DATA (or VDU_DEFINE, 0, register, value...).
CRTC_HORIZONTAL_DISPLAYED = 1
CRTC_HSYNC_POSITION       = 2
CRTC_VERTICAL_DISPLAYED   = 6
CRTC_VSYNC_POSITION       = 7
CRTC_CURSOR_START         = 10  ; the cursor's first scan line, and bits 5-6 how it blinks
CRTC_START_HIGH           = 12  ; the screen's start address, in units of 8 bytes
CRTC_START_LOW            = 13

; Values for CRTC_CURSOR_START.
CRTC_CURSOR_OFF   = &20         ; bits 5-6 = %01: no cursor
CRTC_CURSOR_BLINK = &67         ; bits 5-6 = %11: blinking, from scan line 7, as MODEs 0-6 have it

; Written to the system VIA's port B (SYSVIA_ORB), a byte sets one of the
; addressable latch's bits: bits 0-2 say which, bit 3 its value. Latch bits
; 4 and 5 (C0 and C1) set where the hardware wraps the screen round:
; clearing bit 5 with bit 4 set, as MODE 5 leaves it, wraps it at 8K.
SCREEN_WRAP_8K = &05

; Screen memory in the modes the pieces use: where it starts, and the bytes
; in a character row and in a character (in these four-colour modes, two
; bytes across and eight scan lines down, a column of eight bytes at a time).
; Every mode's screen runs to SCREEN_MEMORY_END. These are addresses, but
; they're kept out of os.6502inc: tools/dis6502.py would name every &3000
; and &5800 operand after them, and most of those aren't the screen. Mode
; 7's is MODE7_SCREEN, in teletext.6502inc.
MODE1_SCREEN      = &3000
MODE1_ROW_BYTES   = 640
MODE1_CHAR_BYTES  = 16
MODE5_SCREEN      = &5800
MODE5_ROW_BYTES   = 320
MODE5_CHAR_BYTES  = 16
SCREEN_MEMORY_END = &8000

; 6502 opcodes the programs write or look for.
OPCODE_BMI           = &30
OPCODE_RTI           = &40
OPCODE_LDX_IMMEDIATE = &A2
OPCODE_NOP           = &EA

; OSWORD &7F: hand a raw command to the 8271 floppy disc controller via DFS.
OSWORD_DISC_COMMAND = &7F

; 8271 commands, with the drive 0 select bit (&40) already in.
FDC_READ_DATA_AND_DELETED = &57   ; multi-sector read that accepts deleted marks
FDC_READ_ID               = &5B   ; read sector ID fields off a track
FDC_SEEK                  = &69
FDC_WRITE_SPECIAL         = &7A   ; write one of the 8271's special registers

; 8271 special register: the track the controller believes drive 0's head is
; on. Seeks step the head by the difference from this; reads compare their
; track parameter with it and with the sector IDs.
FDC_REG_TRACK_DRIVE_0 = &12

; The third parameter of a multi-sector read: sector size code in bits 5-7
; (1 = 256 bytes), sector count in bits 0-4.
FDC_SIZE_256 = 1 << 5

; The 8271's result for a sector carrying a deleted data mark. The hidden
; programs' sectors all carry one on the original disc, so every read of them
; ends with this, never with 0.
FDC_RESULT_DELETED_DATA = &20

```

`src/pl.6502`:

```6502
; $.PL: &2FC bytes at sector &101, loaded and run at &0400. "Ian's cheat!":
; a hidden developer's tool, encrypted, that MENU runs only if W and T are
; held down as it starts (line 290: IF INKEY-36 AND INKEY-34 THEN */PL
; ...). It fills pages 4 to 6, BASIC's workspace, so there's no going back
; to BASIC: it ends by resetting the machine or jumping into the game.
;
; What it does, once it has decrypted itself:
;
; 1. MODE 7, cursor off, paged mode on, and nothing on the screen. It waits
;    for the last key pressed to be let go, then reads, with no prompt
;    (what's typed is echoed), a filename (up to 12 characters) and a
;    six-digit code.
; 2. *LOADs the file - a level file as the Level Designer saves it, like
;    LEVEL1, at &25A1 - and checks the code against the three bytes the file
;    keeps at &26E1. A wrong code resets the machine.
; 3. Lists the level's 32 puzzles (what the Level Designer calls the
;    triggers that make things happen in a level: walk onto one, or use an
;    object there, and it acts): number, ten-character name, what the
;    puzzle does (one of 16 actions) and whether it starts on or off.
;    LEVEL1's code is 677636.
; 4. After a key, fills the screen with a fake BASIC "Bad program" error
;    until I, N, O and S are held down together; then beeps, *LOADs GAME and
;    pokes the game for a cheat before jumping into it at &3000: 31 lives,
;    any level to start on from the title screen, and no competition entry
;    code at the end (the game shows one after a locked mission such as
;    the original, played through from level 1), so the cheat can't win
;    one.
;
; Step 4 can't work on this disc: GAME is a &D9-byte stub at &0900 that
; reads the real game from sectors the catalogue doesn't list
; (hidden_loader.6502inc), so the jump finds no game at &3000 and the
; machine resets. PL must date from before the game was hidden that way.
;
; Against prying: everything after the decryptor is encrypted, with keys
; taken from the decryptor's own bytes; BRKV is pointed at the reset code,
; so any error resets the machine, as does a wrong code; BREAK clears
; memory; and the decrypted code has checks that only fail if it's been
; tampered with.
;
; On disc the encrypted part is data/pl_encrypted.bin. The program it
; decrypts to is below as source, in a section of its own (saved as
; build/files/PLDEC, which isn't on the disc); `tools/plcrypt.py check
; build/files` confirms one encrypts to the other, and `encrypt` rebuilds
; the data from the source.

INCLUDE "os.6502inc"
INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"
INCLUDE "teletext.6502inc"
INCLUDE "level.6502inc"

; Zero page. BASIC's, but BASIC is never coming back.
SECTION decrypt_zero_page, org=&70, virtual=TRUE
.crypt_ptr SKIP 2           ; the decryptor's page pointer
ENDSECTION

SECTION pl, filename="PL", org=&0400, load=&400, exec=&400
.pl
{
; Entry from *RUN.
.start
    SEI
.read_reset_high
    LDX #1
    LDA CPU_RESET_VECTOR, X     ; high byte of the reset entry
    PHA
    ; 4 is both *FX4 and the first page to decrypt.
    LDA #OSBYTE_CURSOR_EDITING
    STA crypt_ptr+1
    JSR OSBYTE                  ; *FX4,1: no cursor editing, so no copying off the screen
    LDX #2
    ; Point BRKV at the reset entry, so any error (BRK) resets the machine.
    PLA
    STA BRKV+1
    LDA CPU_NMI_VECTOR, X       ; X=2: the reset entry's low byte
    STA BRKV
    LDA #OSBYTE_BREAK_EFFECT
    JSR OSBYTE                  ; *FX200,2 (Y is 0, as *FX4 leaves it):
                                ; BREAK clears memory

    ; Decrypt from `encrypted` to the end of page 6, a byte at a time:
    ; plain = key EOR previous plain byte EOR stored. Page 4 starts at
    ; `encrypted`, pages 5 and 6 at their second byte (their first is stored
    ; plain). tools/plcrypt.py does the same offline.
    LDA #0
    STA crypt_ptr
    LDY #LO(encrypted)
    LDX #2                      ; pages to go after this one, and which key
.decrypt_byte
    LDA key_bytes, X
    DEY
    EOR (crypt_ptr), Y
    INY
    EOR (crypt_ptr), Y
    STA (crypt_ptr), Y
    INY
    BNE decrypt_byte
    INY
    INC crypt_ptr+1
    DEX
    BPL decrypt_byte
    ; X is now &FF. This BMI's offset is the first byte decrypted: as stored
    ; it would branch back into the code above; decrypted it skips one byte
    ; into the cheat (pl_cheat.start, below).
    EQUB OPCODE_BMI

; Stored encrypted; decrypts to the pl_cheat section below.
.encrypted
    INCBIN "../data/pl_encrypted.bin"
}
ENDSECTION

; The keys, one per page (page 4 uses key_bytes+2): the operand of LDX #1,
; the LDA abs,X opcode and the low byte of its operand. Patch the decryptor
; and the decryption goes wrong.
key_bytes = pl.read_reset_high + 1


; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
; What `encrypted` decrypts to. The section starts a byte early, at the
; decryptor's last byte, a BMI opcode, because the first byte decrypted is
; that BMI's offset. Not on the disc: saved as PLDEC so tools/plcrypt.py
; can check the two agree.

; The level file the cheat reads is laid out as the Level Designer keeps it
; (level.6502inc: LEVEL1 on this disc is one): it lists the puzzles' names
; (level_names, level_name_ends), checks level_code (see check_code_byte), and
; shows each puzzle's action and whether it's PUZZLE_OFF (level_puzzle_types).

; PL expects GAME to be the game itself, a plain file loaded and run at
; &3000, as H.GAME is loaded before it copies its code down to &0900 and
; on. The cheat pokes three places in it, given here as addresses in that
; file, with the names hidden_game.6502 gives them:
;
; - game_set_lives: new_game's LDX #START_LIVES : STX lives. The LDX's
;   operand becomes CHEAT_LIVES.
; - game_entry_code_test: mission_done_screen's BEQ show_entry_code, which
;   branches over a JMP wait_for_space. Its offset becomes 0, so both ways
;   lead to the JMP and the competition entry code is never shown.
; - game_clear_furthest_level: load_mission's STA furthest_level, which
;   zeroes it. It becomes two NOPs.
;
; furthest_level (game_furthest_level here) is how far the title screen's
; S key steps the starting level; the cheat sets it to CHEAT_FURTHEST_LEVEL,
; the fourth level, so every level can be chosen, even after loading
; another mission.
GAME_START = &3000
game_set_lives = &3FC6
CHEAT_LIVES = 31
game_entry_code_test = &4874
game_clear_furthest_level = &4F31
game_furthest_level = &61
CHEAT_FURTHEST_LEVEL = 3

; Zero page, once decrypted: BASIC's, as BASIC is never coming back. The
; code is read from the keyboard straight into the bottom of it. &70
; serves three routines.
SECTION zero_page, org=&00, virtual=TRUE
.typed_digits SKIP CODE_DIGITS + 1  ; the code as typed, then CR
    SKIP &70 - P%
.digit_pair                 ; packing two digits into one byte
.entry_index                ; the puzzle being listed
.key_index SKIP 1           ; which of the unlock keys is being tested
.format_index SKIP 1        ; next character of format_chars to print
.swapped SKIP 1             ; check_code_byte's scratch byte
.checks_left SKIP 1         ; check_code_byte's count, a guard against patching
    SKIP &80 - P%
.code_bcd SKIP CODE_BYTES   ; the code typed, as BCD
ENDSECTION

DIGIT_0 = '0'
CODE_DIGITS = 6             ; an editing code, two digits to a byte
CODE_BYTES = CODE_DIGITS / 2
ACTION_WIDTH = 15           ; the action column, padded with spaces

; The format characters are stored inverted, so they aren't text to anyone
; reading the decrypted bytes either.
FUNCTION inverted(x) = FLATTEN(x) EOR &FF

SECTION pl_decrypted, filename="PLDEC", org=pl.encrypted - 1
.pl_cheat
{
    BMI start                   ; X=&FF: always
    EQUB 0                      ; skipped

; Entered with X = &FF, from the decryptor.
.start
    LDY #screen_setup_end - screen_setup - 1
.send_screen_setup
    LDA screen_setup, Y
    JSR OSWRCH
    DEY
    BPL send_screen_setup
    CLI
    ; Wait for the key last pressed (W or T, held to get here) to be let go;
    ; then, with auto-repeat off and the buffer flushed, nothing still held
    ; gets typed. Letting go of that one key is enough: the other can still
    ; be held.
.wait_keys_up
    LDA MOS_KEY_PRESSED
    BMI wait_keys_up
    SEI
    INX                         ; 0
    LDA #OSBYTE_AUTO_REPEAT_DELAY
    JSR OSBYTE                  ; *FX11,0: no auto-repeat
    LDA #OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS
    LDX #0
    JSR OSBYTE

    ; Two lines from the keyboard, with no prompt: a filename, into the end
    ; of load_command, and the code, as digits only.
    LDX #LO(read_filename_block)
    LDY #HI(read_filename_block)
    LDA #OSWORD_READ_LINE
    JSR OSWORD
    LDX #LO(read_code_block)
    LDY #HI(read_code_block)
    LDA #OSWORD_READ_LINE
    JSR OSWORD

    ; Pack the six digits into three BCD bytes, two digits to a byte, the
    ; first pair into code_bcd+0. The loop works from the last pair back.
    LDX #CODE_DIGITS - 2
    LDY #CODE_BYTES - 1
.pack_digits
    LDA typed_digits, X
    SEC
    SBC #DIGIT_0
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    STA digit_pair
    LDA typed_digits+1, X
    SEC
    SBC #DIGIT_0
    ORA digit_pair
    STA code_bcd, Y
    DEY
    DEX
    DEX
    BPL pack_digits

    ; *L.<filename>
    LDX #LO(load_command)
    LDY #HI(load_command)
    JSR OSCLI

    LDA #0
    STA entry_index
; One line of the listing per puzzle, checking the code again every time.
.list_entry
    LDX #2
    LDA #OSBYTE_BREAK_EFFECT
    LDY #0
    STX checks_left
    JSR OSBYTE                  ; *FX200,2 again: BREAK clears memory

    ; Each code byte must match the file's once its bit pairs are swapped
    ; and it's rotated right one place (as a level stores its code), last
    ; byte first. X is the old *FX200 setting, which OSBYTE hands back: 2,
    ; as set at the start, and so the last byte's index; anyone changing
    ; that setting breaks the check. checks_left goes 2, 1, 0, &FF and back
    ; to 0 only if all three compares ran.
ASSERT CODE_BYTES - 1 = 2
.check_code_byte
    DEC checks_left
    LDA code_bcd, X
    PHA
    AND #%01010101
    ASL A
    STA swapped
    PLA
    AND #%10101010
    LSR A
    ORA swapped
    PHA
    LSR A
    PLA
    ROR A
    CMP level_code, X
    BEQ code_byte_ok
.reset_machine
    JMP (CPU_RESET_VECTOR)
.code_byte_ok
    DEX
    BPL check_code_byte
    INC checks_left
    BNE reset_machine

    ; The puzzle number, 1-32, in yellow, right-aligned in two columns.
    LDX #0
    STX format_index
    JSR print_format_char       ; yellow
    LDY entry_index
    INY
    TYA
    PHP                         ; for the decoy check below
    SEC
.count_tens
    INX
    SBC #10
    BCS count_tens
    ADC #DIGIT_0 + 10
    PHA
    LDA tens_digits - 1, X
    JSR OSWRCH
    PLA
    JSR OSWRCH
    JSR print_format_char       ; "."
    JSR print_format_char       ; green

    ; The name: PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD characters from one table, the rest from
    ; another.
    LDA entry_index
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A
    TAY
ASSERT PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD = 8
    ; Never taken: PHP always pushes the B flag (bit 4) set, so the AND
    ; can't be zero. A decoy check.
    PLA
    AND #%10010110
    BEQ reset_machine
    LDX #PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD
.print_name
    LDA level_names, Y
    JSR OSWRCH
    INY
    DEX
    BNE print_name
    LDX #PUZZLE_NAME_LENGTH - PUZZLE_NAME_HEAD
    LDA entry_index
    ASL A
    TAY
.print_name_end
    LDA level_name_ends, Y
    JSR OSWRCH
    INY
    DEX
    BNE print_name_end

    ; The action, in cyan: count past (action + 1) zeros in action_names.
    JSR print_format_char       ; cyan
    LDY entry_index
    LDA level_puzzle_types, Y
    PHA
    AND #PUZZLE_ACTION
    TAX
    LDY #0
.find_action
    LDA action_names, Y
    BEQ passed_zero
    INY
    BNE find_action
.passed_zero
    INY
    DEX
    BPL find_action
    LDX #ACTION_WIDTH
.print_action
    LDA action_names, Y
    BEQ pad_action
    JSR OSWRCH
    INY
    DEX
    BNE print_action
    BEQ print_on_off            ; always
.pad_action
    LDA #' '
.pad_action_loop
    JSR OSWRCH
    DEX
    BNE pad_action_loop

    ; "On" or "Off", in magenta.
.print_on_off
    JSR print_format_char       ; magenta
    JSR print_format_char       ; "O"
    PLA
    AND #PUZZLE_OFF
    BNE print_off
    LDA #'n'
    BNE print_last_letter       ; always
.print_off
    LDA #'f'
    JSR OSWRCH
.print_last_letter
    JSR OSWRCH
    JSR print_format_char       ; newline

    INC entry_index
    LDA entry_index
    CMP #PUZZLES
    BEQ listed
    JMP list_entry

.listed
    LDX #3
.finish_listing
    JSR print_format_char       ; paged mode off, beep, ">"
    DEX
    BNE finish_listing
    CLI
    JSR OSRDCH
    SEI

    ; Pretend BASIC has fallen over until all four unlock keys are held.
    ; The fake error's place in format_chars is also its length.
.fake_error
    LDX #fake_error_text - format_chars
    STX format_index
.print_fake_error
    JSR print_format_char
    DEX
    BNE print_fake_error
    LDA #unlock_keys_end - unlock_keys - 1
    STA key_index
.test_unlock_key
    LDY key_index
    LDX unlock_keys, Y
    LDY #&FF
    LDA #OSBYTE_INKEY
    JSR OSBYTE
    INX
    BNE fake_error              ; not held
    DEC key_index
    BPL test_unlock_key

    ; Unlocked: X=0 and Y=&FF from the last INKEY.
    LDA #BEL
    CLI
    JSR OSWRCH
    LSR A                       ; BEL >> 1 = CHEAT_FURTHEST_LEVEL
ASSERT BEL >> 1 = CHEAT_FURTHEST_LEVEL
    STA game_furthest_level, X
    INY                         ; 0
    LDA #OSBYTE_ESCAPE_KEY
    JSR OSBYTE                  ; *FX229,0
    LDA #OSBYTE_ESCAPE_EFFECTS
    LDX #1
    LDY #0
    JSR OSBYTE                  ; *FX230,1, as MENU does before the game
    LDX #LO(load_game)
    LDY #HI(load_game)
    JSR OSCLI
    ; Poke the cheat into the game. The addresses are dressed up with index
    ; registers so they don't show in the code as written.
    LDA #OPCODE_NOP
    STA game_clear_furthest_level + 1
    LDX #CHEAT_LIVES
    STA game_clear_furthest_level - CHEAT_LIVES, X
    LDY #0
    TXA
    STY game_entry_code_test + 1
    STA game_set_lives + 1, Y
    JMP GAME_START

; Print the next character of format_chars and step on to the one after.
; In: format_index = the character's place in format_chars.
; Clobbers: A, Y.
.print_format_char
    LDY format_index
    LDA format_chars, Y
    EOR #&FF
    JSR OSASCI
    INC format_index
    RTS

; VDU codes, sent from the end backwards: MODE 7; cursor off; paged mode on.
.screen_setup
    EQUB REVERSE({VDU_MODE, 7, VDU_DEFINE, 0, CRTC_CURSOR_START, CRTC_CURSOR_OFF, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, VDU_PAGED_ON})
.screen_setup_end

; OSWORD 0 for the filename: up to 12 characters, any printable.
.read_filename_block
    EQUW filename
    EQUB filename_end - filename, ' ', &FF

; The filename is read over the placeholder, so OSCLI sees *L.<filename>.
.load_command
    EQUS "L."
.filename
    EQUS "Ian's cheat!"
.filename_end
    EQUB CR

; OSWORD 0 for the code: up to six digits, into zero page.
.read_code_block
    EQUW typed_digits
    EQUB CODE_DIGITS, '0', '9'

; Characters print_format_char hands out in turn, stored inverted. The
; tens digits in the middle are read directly, not inverted, and never
; reached in turn.
.format_chars
    EQUB inverted({TT_ALPHA_YELLOW, CODES("."), TT_ALPHA_GREEN})
    EQUB inverted({TT_ALPHA_CYAN, TT_ALPHA_MAGENTA, CODES("O"), CR})
    EQUB inverted({VDU_PAGED_OFF, BEL, CODES(">")})
; Indexed from 1 (tens + 1): " " for 1-9, then "1", "2", "3".
.tens_digits
    EQUS " 123"
.fake_error_text
    EQUB inverted({CODES("Bad program"), CR, CODES(">"), CR})
.fake_error_text_end
    ASSERT fake_error_text_end - fake_error_text = fake_error_text - format_chars

.load_game
    EQUS "L.GAME", CR

; INKEY tests for the keys that unlock the cheat, last first.
.unlock_keys
    EQUB INKEY_TEST(KEY_S), INKEY_TEST(KEY_O), INKEY_TEST(KEY_N), INKEY_TEST(KEY_I)
.unlock_keys_end

; The 16 actions a puzzle can do, each after a zero.
.action_names
    EQUB 0
    EQUS "Place block", 0
    EQUS "Move block", 0
    EQUS "Next block", 0
    EQUS "Set levels", 0
    EQUS "Throw object", 0
    EQUS "Detonate object", 0
    EQUS "Move monster", 0
    EQUS "Place monster", 0
    EQUS "Teleport", 0
    EQUS "Swap next block", 0
    EQUS "Turn on puzzle", 0
    EQUS "Turn off puzzle", 0
    EQUS "Charge object", 0
    EQUS "Push boulders", 0
    EQUS "Move next block", 0
    EQUS "Disorientate", 0
}
ENDSECTION

```

`src/screen.6502`:

```6502
; $.SCREEN: &2800 bytes at sector &03E. The loading picture - a space
; station, planets and the "pipeline" logo over the Superior Software and
; Acornsoft logos - as a MODE 5 screen: the whole of screen memory from &5800
; to &7FFF, saved as it stood (docs/img/loading-screen.png, or render it with
; `tools/beebscreen.py 5 data/screen.bin OUT.png --palette 0,1,3,5`).
;
; MENU *LOADs it straight into screen memory as soon as its setup is done
; (line 250: MODE 5, cursor off, VDU 19,3,5 to make colour 3 magenta), so
; the palette is black, red, yellow, magenta; it stays up for ten seconds or
; until a key (INKEY(1000)). *LOAD runs nothing, so the catalogued exec
; address is unused.
;
; Layout is the MOS's for MODE 5: 32 character rows of 320 bytes, each row
; 40 blocks of 8 bytes (a block is 4 pixels wide, so a MODE 5 character is
; two), one byte per pixel line of the block; a byte is 4 pixels, pixel p's
; colour taking bit 7-p as its high bit and bit 3-p as its low. The picture
; fills the top 27 character rows; the last five are blank.

INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"

SECTION screen, filename="SCREEN", org=MODE5_SCREEN, load=&5800, exec=&5800
.loading_screen
{
.picture
    INCBIN "../data/screen.bin"
    ASSERT P% = MODE5_SCREEN + 27 * MODE5_ROW_BYTES
.blank_rows
    SKIPTO SCREEN_MEMORY_END
}
ENDSECTION

```

`src/sprites.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; A PIPELINE graphics set: its layout and what each slot is for, then the
; notation its pictures are written in here. The Graphics Designer edits a
; set at &4000 and saves it whole (DEFAULT is one: default.6502inc describes
; it); MISSION copies it into a mission, where the game draws with it
; (io.6502inc has where it goes there). Included by io.6502inc, so anything
; including that has this too.

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
; The layout: sprites in numbered slots, then the objects' names.

LARGE_SPRITE_WIDTH  = 16        ; pixels
LARGE_SPRITE_HEIGHT = 32
LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE   = LARGE_SPRITE_WIDTH / 4 * LARGE_SPRITE_HEIGHT    ; bytes, four pixels each
SMALL_SPRITE_WIDTH  = 8
SMALL_SPRITE_HEIGHT = 16
SMALL_SPRITE_SIZE   = SMALL_SPRITE_WIDTH / 4 * SMALL_SPRITE_HEIGHT

; The objects: kinds 0-14, each with an icon (a small slot) and a name, space
; padded. Icon 15, after them, is the exit's, and has no name.
OBJECT_KINDS       = 15
OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH = 12
EXIT_ICON          = OBJECT_KINDS

SET_LOAD_ADDRESS = &4000        ; where the Graphics Designer keeps a set, and saves it from

SET_LARGE      = &000           ; large slots &00-&0F
SET_SMALL      = &800           ; small slots &10-&1F
SET_MORE_LARGE = &A00           ; large slots &20-&28
SET_NAMES      = &E80           ; the names of icons 0-14
SET_SIZE       = &F34

FIRST_SMALL_SLOT = &10
MORE_LARGE_SLOT  = &20
LAST_SLOT        = &28

; What the game makes of the slots (a mission holds slots &00-&27, the set's
; first &E00 bytes, as its graphics, and slot &28 apart). Slots &00-&0F are
; the map's cell types, &10-&1F the objects' icons.
SLOT_FLOOR     = &00            ; cell type 0. Round an object's icon, the game draws
                                ; only this picture's first character cell (4 pixels by
                                ; 8), so a floor looks right only as that cell repeated
SLOT_MONSTER   = &0E            ; &0E and &0F: the flame monsters' two pictures
SLOT_EXIT      = FIRST_SMALL_SLOT + EXIT_ICON
SLOT_PLAYER    = &20            ; &20-&23: the player facing left, right, up and down
SLOT_ALTERNATE = &24            ; &24-&27: second pictures for cell types 5, 7, 8 and A
SLOT_NO_OBJECT = &28            ; for an object cell with no object in it

ASSERT SET_SMALL = SET_LARGE + FIRST_SMALL_SLOT * LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE
ASSERT SET_MORE_LARGE = SET_SMALL + (MORE_LARGE_SLOT - FIRST_SMALL_SLOT) * SMALL_SPRITE_SIZE
ASSERT SET_NAMES = SET_MORE_LARGE + (LAST_SLOT + 1 - MORE_LARGE_SLOT) * LARGE_SPRITE_SIZE
ASSERT SET_SIZE = SET_NAMES + OBJECT_KINDS * OBJECT_NAME_LENGTH
ASSERT SLOT_EXIT = MORE_LARGE_SLOT - 1 AND SLOT_PLAYER = MORE_LARGE_SLOT

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
; Sprites written as pictures. A picture is a list of strings, one per row of
; pixels, each character a logical colour: . 1 2 3. The bytes come out the
; way PIPELINE stores sprites (and MODE 5 lays out the screen inside a
; character cell): a column four pixels wide at a time, top to bottom, then
; the next column to the right.

; The MODE 5 byte for four pixels: pixel n (0 leftmost) keeps its colour's
; high bit in bit 7-n and its low bit in bit 3-n.
FUNCTION mode5_byte(pixels)
    p = FIND(CODES(".123"), CODES(pixels))
= SUM((p DIV 2) * {128, 64, 32, 16} + (p MOD 2) * {8, 4, 2, 1})

; The game's pictures (src/default.6502inc) are drawn two characters a pixel,
; as a MODE 5 pixel is twice as wide as it is tall, so they look in the
; source as they do on the screen. mode5_pictures turns a list of same-sized
; pictures into their bytes, one picture after another, in one go: as a
; FUNCTION over whole lists rather than a FOR over bytes, it adds a handful of
; entries to the symbol dump rather than one per byte.

; Where each byte's leftmost pixel starts in count pictures of height rows
; of width characters, run together: picture by picture, then a column of
; four pixels (eight characters) at a time, then down the rows.
FUNCTION picture_byte_starts(count, height, width)
    pictures = (0..count-1) * height * width
    columns = (0..width DIV 8 - 1) * 8
    rows = (0..height-1) * width
= FLATTEN(ZIP(ZIP(pictures)) + ZIP(columns) + rows)

; Pixel n's bits in a byte (n = 0 leftmost), for each pixel's character in
; chars: the colour's high bit in bit 7-n and its low bit in bit 3-n.
FUNCTION pixel_bits(chars, n) = {0, 8, 128, 136}[FIND(CODES(".123"), CODES(chars))] >> n

; The bytes of a list of pictures, all the same size, one after another.
FUNCTION mode5_pictures(pictures)
    text = CHR(CODES(pictures))         ; every row of every picture, run together
    ASSERT text[0..2..] = text[1..3..], "a pixel is two characters the same"
    height = LEN(pictures[0])
    width = LEN(pictures[0][0])
    ASSERT LEN(text) = LEN(pictures) * height * width, "pictures of different sizes"
    starts = picture_byte_starts(LEN(pictures), height, width)
= SUM({
    pixel_bits(text[starts], 0),
    pixel_bits(text[starts + 2], 1),
    pixel_bits(text[starts + 4], 2),
    pixel_bits(text[starts + 6], 3)
}, 0)

```

`src/teletext.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; Teletext (Mode 7) control codes, as screen memory holds them, for writing
; Mode 7 screens as source. The SAA5050, the chip that draws Mode 7, sees
; only the low seven bits of each byte, so &81 is its code 1. Each code
; takes a character cell (shown as a space, or as held graphics) and changes
; how the rest of the row is drawn. tools/mode7.py names bytes from this
; file.
;
; Bytes from &A0 up are the characters &20-&7F with bit 7 set, which the
; SAA5050 doesn't see; in a graphics colour they're the 2x3 block "sixel"
; shapes (bit 0 top left, 1 top right, 2 middle left, 3 middle right, 4
; bottom left, 6 bottom right; bit 5 is always set). Mode 7 screen code
; tends to store those as &A0-&FF, so in a graphics run they're written in
; hex.

; Text in a colour (and leave graphics mode).
TT_ALPHA_RED     = &81
TT_ALPHA_GREEN   = &82
TT_ALPHA_YELLOW  = &83
TT_ALPHA_BLUE    = &84
TT_ALPHA_MAGENTA = &85
TT_ALPHA_CYAN    = &86
TT_ALPHA_WHITE   = &87

TT_FLASH  = &88
TT_STEADY = &89

TT_NORMAL_HEIGHT = &8C
TT_DOUBLE_HEIGHT = &8D

; Graphics in a colour.
TT_GFX_RED     = &91
TT_GFX_GREEN   = &92
TT_GFX_YELLOW  = &93
TT_GFX_BLUE    = &94
TT_GFX_MAGENTA = &95
TT_GFX_CYAN    = &96
TT_GFX_WHITE   = &97

TT_CONCEAL           = &98
TT_CONTIGUOUS        = &99   ; solid sixels (the default)
TT_SEPARATED         = &9A   ; sixels with gaps between them
TT_BLACK_BACKGROUND  = &9C
TT_NEW_BACKGROUND    = &9D   ; background becomes the current foreground colour
TT_HOLD_GRAPHICS     = &9E   ; control cells repeat the last sixel, not a space
TT_RELEASE_GRAPHICS  = &9F

TT_COLUMNS = 40

; The Mode 7 screen, for code that writes it directly.
MODE7_SCREEN = &7C00
FUNCTION mode7_address(column, row) = MODE7_SCREEN + row * TT_COLUMNS + column
SOLID_BLOCK  = &FF   ; a graphics character with all six sixels lit
TT_ROWS = 25

; Start of a screen row: checks it starts where row n of a screen whose
; first row is at `screen` should, so a row with the wrong number of bytes
; is caught where it happens. The including file defines `screen`.
MACRO TT_ROW n
    ASSERT P% = screen + n * TT_COLUMNS, "Mode 7 row ", n, " starts at the wrong place"
ENDMACRO

```

`src/title.6502`:

```6502
; $.TITLE: &1679 bytes at sector &027, loaded at &6300 and run at &7900.
; The title page shown before the game: "PIPELINE by IAN HOLMES and WILLIAM
; REEVE" in red, blue and white MODE 1 lettering (docs/img/title.png, made
; with `tools/beebscreen.py 1 data/title_picture.bin OUT.png --palette
; 0,1,4,7 --title`).
;
; MENU's option 1 selects MODE 1, makes all four colours black, *RUNs this,
; then sets the palette to black, red, blue, white (VDU 19 to 0, 1, 4, 7),
; so the picture appears at once, whole, for up to three seconds before the
; game loads.
;
; The file is a packed picture and a little code to unpack it, in its last
; page (&7900). It loads into MODE 1 screen memory itself, and the picture
; unpacks over it, from the start of screen memory (&3000, the top of the
; picture) upwards. The packed data keeps ahead of the unpacking until its
; last 41 bytes, which lie below the picture. The code wouldn't keep ahead:
; the unpacking reaches its page before it has finished, so it first copies
; itself out of the way, to the page below the screen.
;
; The packing is runs of zeros: a nonzero byte stands for itself; a zero is
; followed by how many zeros it stands for (0 meaning 256). By the time the
; unpacker reaches the packed data's last 41 bytes (&78D7 on), it has
; written zeros over them, so they read as runs of 256 zeros, which carry
; the writing on through this code's old page and past the end of the screen
; to &8DB1, in the paged ROM's space (harmless on a model B, where it's ROM).
; The last 2K of the screen, below the picture, is then cleared, though the
; overrun has already left it all zero. (docs/notes/loaders.md has the
; simulation and jsbeeb's record of the writes.)

INCLUDE "os.6502inc"
INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"

; Where the unpacker runs: the page below the screen. It's inside the block
; MENU DIMs as C% for its scrolling message (&2300-&31FF), but by now MENU
; has stopped the scroller and set LOMEM=TOP, which gives that memory back,
; so the menu's program and variables end well below it.
RELOCATED_PAGE = &2F00

; Zero page: user workspace, used three ways in turn.
SECTION relocate_zero_page, org=&70, virtual=TRUE
.relocate_to SKIP 2         ; where this page is copied to
.relocate_from SKIP 2       ; and from
ENDSECTION
SECTION unpack_zero_page, org=&70, virtual=TRUE
.packed SKIP 2              ; the next packed byte
.screen_ptr SKIP 2          ; the screen page being unpacked into, with Y
ENDSECTION
SECTION clear_zero_page, org=&70, virtual=TRUE
.clear_ptr SKIP 2           ; the page being cleared
ENDSECTION

SECTION title, filename="TITLE", org=&6300, load=&6300, exec=&7900
.title
{
; The picture, packed: data/title_picture.bin.
.picture
    INCBIN "../data/title_picture.bin"
.picture_end
    ASSERT LO(picture_end) = 0, "the unpacker stops at a page boundary"

; Entry, from *RUN. Copies this page down to RELOCATED_PAGE and carries on
; there. Y isn't set: the copy starts at whatever Y *RUN leaves (5 under DFS
; 1.2), which is fine as long as it's below unpack's offset in the page.
.start
    LDA #0
    STA relocate_to
    STA relocate_from
    LDA #HI(RELOCATED_PAGE)
    STA relocate_to+1
    LDA #HI(start)
    STA relocate_from+1
.relocate
    LDA (relocate_from), Y
    STA (relocate_to), Y
    INY
    BNE relocate
    JMP unpack

; The rest of the page runs from RELOCATED_PAGE, so it's assembled for
; there, though it sits here in the file.
SECTION title_relocated, org=RELOCATED_PAGE + LO(P%)
; Unpack the picture into the screen from MODE1_SCREEN, clear the bottom
; 2K, flush the keyboard and return to BASIC. X stays 0 for (packed,X) except
; while it counts a run.
; Clobbers: A, X, Y, packed and screen_ptr (clear_ptr shares packed).
.unpack
    LDA #0
    TAX
    TAY
    STA packed
    STA screen_ptr
    LDA #HI(picture)
    STA packed+1
    LDA #HI(MODE1_SCREEN)
    STA screen_ptr+1
.next_code
    LDA (packed, X)
    BNE store_literal
    ; A zero: the next byte is how many zeros.
    INC packed
    BNE read_run_length
    INC packed+1
    LDA packed+1
    CMP #HI(picture_end)
    BEQ clear_bottom
.read_run_length
    LDA (packed, X)
    TAX
    LDA #0
.store_zero
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
    DEX
    BEQ step_screen
    INY
    BNE store_zero
    INC screen_ptr+1
    BNE store_zero              ; always
.store_literal
    STA (screen_ptr), Y
.step_screen
    INY
    BNE step_packed
    INC screen_ptr+1
.step_packed
    INC packed
    BNE next_code
    INC packed+1
    LDA packed+1
    CMP #HI(picture_end)
    BNE next_code

    ; Clear what's under the picture: where the end of the packed data and
    ; this code were, and the overrun (all zeros already, as it happens).
.clear_bottom
    LDA #HI(PICTURE_BOTTOM)
    STA clear_ptr+1
    LDY #0
    STY clear_ptr
.clear_page
    TYA
.clear_byte
    STA (clear_ptr), Y
    INY
    BNE clear_byte
    INC clear_ptr+1
    LDA clear_ptr+1
    CMP #HI(SCREEN_MEMORY_END)
    BNE clear_page
    LDA #OSBYTE_FLUSH_BUFFERS
    LDX #1                      ; the input buffer: no keys typed during this
    JMP OSBYTE
ENDSECTION
}
ENDSECTION

; The picture fills the screen down to here (28.8 of MODE 1's 32 character
; rows); the rest is cleared.
PICTURE_BOTTOM = &7800

```

`src/warning.6502`:

```6502
; $.WARNING: &380 bytes at sector &023. A Mode 7 page, *LOADed straight
; into screen memory by MENU (line 295, after MODE 7) and shown for up to
; ten seconds (`I%=INKEY(1000)`); docs/img/warning.png.
;
; Rows 0-15 are the picture: "PIPELINE" in magenta and red block graphics,
; the credits, and a blue pipe frame around a flashing red "WARNING" and "All
; Rights Reserved". Rows 18-22 are the warning itself, in plain white text:
; "Unauthorised commercial exploitation of screens or graphics data produced
; by the PIPELINE Level Designer or the PIPELINE Graphics Designer is
; strictly prohibited." The file stops 16 characters into row 22, so the
; rest of the screen is left as MODE 7 cleared it.
;
; MENU then clears rows 18-24 through a text window (the scrolling message
; it runs along the bottom of the menu takes rows 17-24, and row 17 is
; blank already) and puts up the menu, which is this same picture with the
; options inside the frame in place of the warning (docs/img/menu.png).
; *LOAD runs nothing, so the catalogued exec address is unused.
;
; Written with tools/mode7.py: control codes by name, text as strings,
; graphics (sixel) characters in hex.

INCLUDE "teletext.6502inc"

SECTION warning, filename="WARNING", org=MODE7_SCREEN, load=&7C00, exec=&7C00
.warning
{
.screen
; rows 0-9: the logo, credits and pipe top, shared with the menu screen
    INCLUDE "mode7_header.6502inc"
    TT_ROW 10
    EQUB TT_GFX_BLUE, &FF, &E6, &AA, &BF, &BF, &BF, &BF, &6A, &F7, &A4, &20, TT_ALPHA_YELLOW
    EQUB "                ", TT_GFX_BLUE, &20, TT_BLACK_BACKGROUND, &66, &7F, &AA, &BF, &BF, &BF
    EQUB &BF, &BF
    TT_ROW 11
    EQUB TT_GFX_BLUE, &FF, &B9, &22, &22, &A2, &A2, &A2, &6A, &BD, &B1, &20, TT_ALPHA_YELLOW
    EQUB "   ", TT_FLASH, TT_ALPHA_RED, "WARNING", TT_STEADY, &20, &20, TT_GFX_BLUE, &20, &20
    EQUB TT_BLACK_BACKGROUND, &39, &7F, &22, &62, &72, &72, &32, &22
    TT_ROW 12
    EQUB TT_GFX_BLUE, &FF, &E6, TT_GFX_YELLOW, &22, &2F, &21, TT_GFX_BLUE, &6A, &F7, &A4, &20
    EQUB TT_ALPHA_YELLOW, "               ", TT_GFX_BLUE, &20, &20, TT_BLACK_BACKGROUND, &66, &7F
    EQUB TT_GFX_BLUE, &6F, &7F, &7F, &3F, &20
    TT_ROW 13
    EQUB TT_GFX_BLUE, &FF, &B9, TT_GFX_RED, &7F, &7F, &7F, TT_GFX_BLUE, &6A, &BD, &B1, &20
    EQUB TT_ALPHA_YELLOW, "             ", TT_GFX_BLUE, &20, TT_GFX_BLUE, &20, &20
    EQUB TT_BLACK_BACKGROUND, &39, &7F, &20, TT_GFX_CYAN, &6A, &35, &20, &20
    TT_ROW 14
    EQUB TT_GFX_BLUE, &EF, &FE, &FD, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &FE, &F7, &A4, TT_ALPHA_YELLOW
    EQUB "All Rights Reserved", TT_GFX_BLUE, &66, &7F, &74, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0, &F0
    TT_ROW 15
    EQUB TT_GFX_BLUE, &A2, &AF, &BB, &BB, &BB, &BB, &BB, &BB, &B9, &A1, &20, TT_ALPHA_YELLOW
    EQUB "               ", TT_GFX_BLUE, &20, &20, TT_BLACK_BACKGROUND, &29, &BB, &BB, &BB, &BB
    EQUB &BB, &BB, &BB
    TT_ROW 16
    EQUB "                                        "
```

```6502
; $.WDATA: the Level Designer's windows and messages, *LOADed at &7000 by
; the designer's entry (format and numbering in wdata.6502inc). Each window
; is a WINDOW line (x, y, width, height) then its title and items; each
; message is a string.
INCLUDE "osconst.6502inc"
INCLUDE "levdes.6502inc"
INCLUDE "wdata.6502inc"

; Window lines are glyph codes, by position in wdata_glyphs.
FUNCTION glyph_codes(s) = FIND(CODES(wdata_glyphs), CODES(s))
FIXED = &80                     ; in x: the window stays put
SPACE_STAYS = &80               ; in y: Space picks the item the menu
                                ; started on, not the last
MACRO WINDOW x, y, width, height
    EQUB x, y, width, height
ENDMACRO
MACRO LINE s                    ; centred
    EQUB LEN(s), glyph_codes(s)
ENDMACRO
MACRO LEFT s                    ; from the left
    EQUB LEN(s) OR &80, glyph_codes(s)
ENDMACRO
; A pointer in the table, checked against its number.
MACRO ENTRY number, address
    ASSERT * == wdata + (number - 1) * 2
    EQUW address
ENDMACRO

SECTION wdata, filename="WDATA", org=wdata, load=wdata, exec=0
.wdata_table
```

`src/wdata.6502inc`:

```6502inc
; WDATA: the Level Designer's windows and messages, which its entry *LOADs
; at &7000. The designer names each by its number (W_* and M_* below), and
; window_address finds it.
;
; A table of 2-byte pointers at &7000, ended by a zero word; entry n-1 is
; window or message n, so numbering starts at 1.
;
; A window: x, y, width, height, then height+1 lines, the title first and
; then one per menu item. x and width are in screen columns (of the 64; a
; glyph is two wide), y in character rows, and height counts the items. Each
; line is a length byte, bit 7 set to start it at the left rather than
; centre it, and that many glyph codes (see wdata_glyphs below). With bit 7 of x
; set the window stays where it says; clear, it moves out of the cursor's
; way, measured from the right when the cursor is in the left half and from
; the bottom when it is in the top half. Space in a window's menu picks its
; last item (usually OK), or with bit 7 of y set, the item the menu started
; on.
;
; A message: VDU codes and text ended by "|" (MESSAGE_END), which
; print_message sends to the OS; HIGHLIGHT switches to highlighted colours,
; black on red. A message without the "|" runs on into the next.

wdata = &7000
WINDOW_HEIGHT = 3               ; where a window's height is in its header
MESSAGE_END = CODES("|")[0]
HIGHLIGHT = &FF

; Glyph codes in a window line, by position in this string. "*" stands for
; the tick, glyph 68. Codes from 64 come from the program (font_digits)
; rather than the font.
wdata_glyphs = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ.:?<> abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz1234567890*-"
GLYPH_X         = 55            ; "x", for a cross
GLYPH_TICK      = 68

W_SELECT_BLOCK      = 1     ; the sixteen blocks
W_OPTIONS           = 2
W_OPTIONS_LOCATION  = 3     ; "Select location:" for the start and finish
M_WHICH_OBJECT      = 4
W_OBJECT            = 5
M_RECORD_NUMBER     = 6     ; where an object's or monster's number goes,
                            ; after its window's title
M_OLD_SPRITE        = 7
M_CHARGES           = 8
M_ERROR             = 9     ; runs into M_PRESS_ANY_KEY
M_PRESS_ANY_KEY     = 10
M_WHICH_MONSTER     = 11
W_MONSTER           = 12
W_DIRECTION         = 13    ; north, south, east, west, dead
W_PRIORITIES        = 14    ; a special monster pattern
W_RELATIVE_DIRECTION = 15   ; forwards, backwards, left, right
M_PATTERN_AT        = 16    ; where the special pattern's letters go
M_INITIAL_TIME      = 17
M_ENTER_NEW_VALUE   = 18
M_COLLECTABLES      = 19
M_REQUIRED          = 20
W_GRAPHICS          = 21
W_SPRITES           = 22
W_COLOURS           = 23
M_WHICH_PUZZLE      = 24
W_PUZZLE            = 25
M_PUZZLE_NAME_AT    = 26    ; where the puzzle window's title name goes
M_OLD_NAME          = 27
M_PUZZLE_NAME       = 28
W_PUZZLE_TYPES      = 29
W_OBJECT_LOCATION   = 30
W_MONSTER_LOCATION  = 31
W_PUZZLE_STATUS     = 32
M_STATUS_NUMBER_AT  = 33    ; where the status window's number goes
W_CONDITIONS        = 34
W_COMPASS           = 35    ; four directions, or eight with the height patched
W_PUZZLE_LOCATION   = 36
W_FILES             = 37
W_SURE              = 38
M_LOADING           = 39
M_SAVING            = 40
M_ENTER_FILENAME    = 41
W_DISORIENTATE      = 42
W_PLACE_BLOCK       = 43
W_SET_LEVELS        = 44
M_REVISED_TIME      = 45
M_COLLECTABLES_REQUIRED = 46
W_SWAP_NEXT         = 47
W_MOVE_BLOCK        = 48
W_THROW_OBJECT      = 49
M_OBJECT_NUMBER     = 50
M_DISTANCE          = 51
W_CHARGE_OBJECT     = 52
W_DEFINE_DISPLAY    = 53
W_SELECT_PUZZLES    = 54    ; puzzles A, B, C to turn on or off
M_OLD_PUZZLE_NUMBER = 55
M_NUMBER_OF_CRATES  = 56
W_MOVE_MONSTER      = 57
M_MONSTER_NUMBER    = 58
W_PLACE_MONSTER     = 59
M_NAME_QUOTE        = 60    ; 'Name: "'
M_QUOTE_PUZZLE      = 61    ; '" Puzzle '
W_HELP              = 62
W_ABOUT             = 63
M_ENTER_CODE        = 64
M_WRONG_CODE        = 65
W_LOST_LIFE         = 66
W_SIMULATE          = 67
M_ERROR_NUMBER_AT   = 68
M_ERROR_TEXT_AT     = 69
W_PATTERNS          = 70
M_FILING_WINDOW     = 71    ; a one-line text window for the filing system
M_TOO_MANY          = 72    ; runs into M_RESET_WINDOWS
M_RESET_WINDOWS     = 73
W_MONSTER_NUMBER    = 74
M_INSERT_DISC       = 75
M_NOTHING           = 76

; Menu items the designer tests or ticks by number, 0 being the item under
; the title; tick_line wants the item's line, item_line(item).
FUNCTION item_line(item) = item + 1
I_OBJECT_EXISTS         = 1     ; W_OBJECT
I_OBJECT_CHARGES        = 4

I_HELP_SIMULATE         = 1     ; W_HELP
```

`tests/test_basic.py`:

```py
"""tools/basic.py must list a program as text baron's BASIC block takes back.

The round trip lists each BASIC program the build produced and tokenises
every line again with baron (bytes with no text form as splices), which
must give the same program.
Needs `make` to have run first, and baron (BARON=path, as make passes it).
"""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))

import basic  # noqa: E402

FILES = ROOT / "build" / "files"
BARON = os.environ.get("BARON") or shutil.which("baron")
PROGRAMS = ["MENU", "MISSION"]


class DetokeniseTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_line_numbers(self):
        # Encodings from baron's own tokeniser tests.
        self.assertEqual(basic.decode_line_number(0x54, 0x4A, 0x40), 10)
        self.assertEqual(basic.decode_line_number(0x44, 0x4D, 0x41), 333)
        self.assertEqual(basic.decode_line_number(0x54, 0x79, 0x70), 12345)
        self.assertEqual(basic.decode_line_number(0x74, 0x4B, 0x40), 139)

    def test_raw_regions(self):
        # REM keeps its bytes even when they look like tokens; a * command
        # at a statement start does too; strings aren't expanded.
        self.assertEqual(basic.detokenise(bytes([0xF4]) + b" \xf1"), ("REM {\n    EQUB &F1 }", False))
        self.assertEqual(basic.detokenise(b"*FX15,1"), ("*FX15,1", True))
        self.assertEqual(basic.detokenise(bytes([0xF1]) + b'"AND"'), ('PRINT"AND"', True))
        self.assertEqual(basic.detokenise(bytes([0xE5, 0x8D, 0x54, 0x4A, 0x40])), ("GOTO10", True))

    def test_splices(self):
        # Runs of bytes with no text form become one splice each, the text
        # carrying on after the `}`; a brace ending the line is spliced too,
        # as baron would read it as opening one.
        self.assertEqual(basic.detokenise(bytes([0xF4]) + b'"\x7f\x82Hi,\x83So'),
                         ('REM"{\n    EQUB &7F, &82 }Hi,{\n    EQUB &83 }So', False))
        self.assertEqual(basic.detokenise(bytes([0xF4]) + b" a{"), ("REM a{\n    EQUB &7B }", False))


@unittest.skipUnless(FILES.is_dir() and BARON, "needs `make` run first and baron")
class RoundTripTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_listing_retokenises(self):
        for name in PROGRAMS:
            with self.subTest(program=name):
                data = (FILES / name).read_bytes()
                lines = []
                for end, number, text in basic.records(data):
                    if number is None:
                        break
                    line, clean = basic.detokenise(text)
                    lines.append(f"{number}{line}")
                self.assertGreater(len(lines), 90)
                with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
                    tmp = Path(tmp)
                    src = "SECTION t, filename=\"OUT\", org=&1900\nBASIC\n"
                    src += "\n".join(lines) + "\nENDBASIC\nENDSECTION\n"
                    (tmp / "t.6502").write_text(src)
                    subprocess.run([BARON, "-p", str(tmp), str(tmp / "t.6502")], check=True,
                                   capture_output=True)
                    self.assertEqual((tmp / "OUT").read_bytes(), data[:end])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

`tests/test_dis6502.py`:

```py
"""The disassembler's output must reassemble to the bytes it came from.

Every binary the build produced (build/files) is disassembled as if it were
all code from its load address, which exercises every opcode, operand form and
data fallback the disc has to offer, then reassembled with baron and compared.
Needs `make` to have run first, and baron (BARON=path, as make passes it).
"""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))

from dfs import parse_inf  # noqa: E402
from dis6502 import Disassembler  # noqa: E402

FILES = ROOT / "build" / "files"
BARON = os.environ.get("BARON") or shutil.which("baron")


@unittest.skipUnless(FILES.is_dir() and BARON, "needs `make` run first and baron")
class RoundTripTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_built_binary_round_trips(self):
        binaries = sorted(p for p in FILES.iterdir() if p.suffix != ".inf")
        self.assertTrue(binaries)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            tmp = Path(tmp)
            shutil.copy(ROOT / "src" / "os.6502inc", tmp)
            shutil.copy(ROOT / "src" / "forceabs.6502inc", tmp)
            for path in binaries:
                with self.subTest(binary=path.name):
                    load = parse_inf((FILES / f"{path.name}.inf").read_text())[2] & 0xFFFF
                    # Somewhere the whole binary fits without wrapping.
                    org = load if load + path.stat().st_size <= 0x10000 else 0x1000
                    shutil.copy(path, tmp / "in.bin")
                    hints = {
                        "binary": str(tmp / "in.bin"),
                        "org": org,
                        "section": f'rt, filename="OUT", org=&{org:04X}',
                        "entries": [org],
                    }
                    (tmp / "rt.6502").write_text(Disassembler(hints, Path("/")).run())
                    out = tmp / "out"
                    shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
                    out.mkdir()
                    subprocess.run([BARON, "-p", str(out), str(tmp / "rt.6502")], check=True,
                                   capture_output=True)
                    self.assertEqual((out / "OUT").read_bytes(), path.read_bytes())


if __name__ == "__main__":
```

`tests/test_symbols.py`:

```py
"""Checks on baron's symbol dump of the build (build/symbols.json, which
`make verify` writes before the tests run)."""

import json
import re
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SYMBOLS = ROOT / "build" / "symbols.json"

# The kinds of symbol that name something in the program. FUNCTION and
# macro parameters and FOR variables are left out: every call or iteration
# leaves its own frame of them, under `@...` scopes.
NAMING_GROUPS = ("labels", "assignments", "za_autos", "defines")


def load_symbols():
    """Each source file's symbols as {file: {dotted name: value}}, from
    baron's dump (format 2: each file's sections, symbols grouped by kind)."""
    dump = json.loads(SYMBOLS.read_text())
    assert dump["format"] == 2, f"symbol dump format {dump['format']}"
    files = {}
    for assembly in dump["assemblies"]:
        names = files.setdefault(assembly["sources"][0], {})
        for section in assembly["sections"]:
            for group in NAMING_GROUPS:
                for name, symbol in section.get(group, {}).items():
                    if "@" not in name:
                        names[name] = symbol["value"]
    return files


@unittest.skipUnless(SYMBOLS.exists(), "no build/symbols.json: run make first")
class ShadowingTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_no_scope_shadows_a_file_level_name(self):
        # Baron lets a scope define a name the file already has outside it,
        # and inside the scope the inner one silently wins. The shared names
        # (os.6502inc, osconst.6502inc, io.6502inc...) are defined once each,
        # so a scoped name that repeats one is a stale copy or a label that
        # hides one: either way, a different name is wanted.
        found = []
        for source, symbols in load_symbols().items():
            names = list(symbols)
            top = {name for name in names if "." not in name}
            found += [f"{source}: {name}" for name in names
                      if "." in name and name.rsplit(".", 1)[1] in top]
        self.assertEqual(found, [])


OVERVIEW = ROOT / "docs" / "overview.md"


@unittest.skipUnless(SYMBOLS.exists(), "no build/symbols.json: run make first")
class OverviewTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_overview_addresses_match_the_build(self):
        # docs/overview.md gives routines' addresses for reading alongside
        # jsbeeb; a rename or a moved routine would leave them stale. Each
        # name may be given with any of the scopes it's nested in left off.
        addresses = {}
        for symbols in load_symbols().values():
            for name, value in symbols.items():
                if isinstance(value, int):
                    parts = name.split(".")
                    for i in range(len(parts)):
                        addresses.setdefault(".".join(parts[i:]), set()).add(value)
        claims = []
        for line in OVERVIEW.read_text().splitlines():
            # Table rows: names in the first column, addresses in the second.
            cells = [cell.strip() for cell in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
            if line.startswith("| `") and len(cells) > 1:
                claims += zip(re.findall(r"`([\w.]+)`", cells[0]),
                              re.findall(r"&([0-9A-F]+)", cells[1]))
            # In the text: `name` (&ADDR).
            claims += re.findall(r"`([\w.]+)` \(&([0-9A-F]+)\)", line)
        self.assertGreater(len(claims), 50)
        wrong = [f"{name} &{address}" for name, address in claims
                 if int(address, 16) not in addresses.get(name, ())]
        self.assertEqual(wrong, [])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```
